dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How are things looking on your end?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Pretty good. I'm just wrapping up for the evening. Oh, I meant to tell you, Dockside Lunch Counter has a soup punch card now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The place near the office? How does it work?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: You get a free soup after 6 purchased soups. I noticed a handwritten sign by the register.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Huh. Is it an actual card, or do they make you download something?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Actual card. They're printed on pale yellow paper. Refreshingly low-tech.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I haven't tried their soup. Is it worth getting a card?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: What if we try the counter together before committing to a long-term soup relationship?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair enough. Are you free for lunch tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, Thursday, November 6 works for me.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Great, let's go then.

details_in_summary: The cards are printed on pale yellow paper.
key_facts: Dockside Lunch Counter gives customers a free soup after six purchased soups.
Sam and Riley plan to go for lunch on Thursday, November 6.
minor_details: The cards are printed on pale yellow paper.
Sam noticed the offer on a handwritten sign by the register.

summary: Riley discussed the Dockside Lunch Counter soup punch card: buy 6 soups, get 1 free, via an actual pale-yellow card. Sam noted its low-tech setup. They considered trying the card before committing. They agreed to test it together by having lunch the next day, Thursday, November 6.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: What were you about to say about replacing the car?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, yeah. I'm putting this loaf of bread away, and I was thinking: should we replace the Subaru with a used electric car?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Maybe. Our 2008 Subaru Impreza is getting old, but how much would we want to spend?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'd feel okay with $20,000 out of pocket, maximum.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but is that after whatever we get for the trade-in? And does it include taxes and fees?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yes. After any trade-in, including taxes and fees. $20,000 is the most we'd actually pay.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: All right. I'm writing $20,000 on the back of this envelope so we don't accidentally turn it into $25,000.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's probably wise. The other thing is charging. There's an outlet near our assigned apartment parking space.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Do we know if we're allowed to use it?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: No, I have no idea. I've seen it there, but I don't know who it's for.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: And even if we can use it, we'd need to know whether it can handle charging a car.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. Otherwise we'd be figuring out where else to charge it, and how often.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Which could make the cheap car rather less convenient. A classic parking-space mystery.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So let's look into charging before we get attached to a particular car.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Agreed. The envelope can wait until we know what we're working with.

key_facts: Their current car is a 2008 Subaru Impreza.
They set a maximum of $20,000 out of pocket after any trade-in, including taxes and fees.
Their assigned apartment parking space has an outlet nearby, but they don't know whether they can use it.
minor_details: Riley brings the subject up while putting away a loaf of bread.
Maya writes the budget figure on the back of an envelope.
meta.storyline_title: A plug in the parking space

summary: Riley and Maya discussed replacing the 2008 Subaru Impreza with a used electric car, aiming to spend up to $20,000 after trade-in and taxes/fees. They noted the need to verify charging availability and capability at their apartment parking space before committing, and agreed to research charging options first. An envelope with $20,000 was noted to avoid overspending.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Would you want to do a day trip to Crystal Mountain in January? To ski, I mean.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, maybe. I haven't thought about skiing in a while. Have you been recently?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No, I haven't skied since that family trip when I was in high school. So recently is doing a lot of work there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I remember that trip. Do you still have any of your gear?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I found 1 old ski glove in my closet. That's the entire collection.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A promising start.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes. I'll just keep 1 hand in my pocket. No, I don't own any ski equipment.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Neither do I, so we'd both need rentals.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Right. We could check rentals at Crystal Mountain and compare them with renting somewhere before we go.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And lift tickets. I have no idea what a day pass costs now.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Me neither. I don't want to pick a day and then discover we're spending a small fortune before lunch.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Speaking of lunch, I mostly remember being hungry on that family trip.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I remember eating chili in the lodge. That's probably the clearest part of the whole skiing experience.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Honestly, chili might be part of the appeal for me too.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: We should also figure out the drive. We could go together, but we'd need to look at the route and what we'd spend getting there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, and whether it makes more sense for one of us to rent a car. We can compare that too.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Okay. Lift tickets, rentals, transport. In theory, that's a manageable list.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Let's look up the costs before we commit to anything. If it's reasonable, we can talk about which day.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That sounds good. I'll look at the rental options, and we can compare notes.

key_facts: Hannah suggests a January day trip to Crystal Mountain.
Hannah has not skied since a family trip in high school.
Neither Hannah nor Riley owns ski equipment.
minor_details: Hannah finds one old ski glove in her closet.
She remembers eating chili in the lodge on the family trip.

summary: Riley discussed a potential Crystal Mountain day trip in January for skiing. They have minimal gear and will compare rentals, lift ticket prices, and transportation options. Action items: look up rental options and costs, compare with other rental sources, and review transport costs. Hannah will research rental options; both will share notes before deciding on a date.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, my mom wants more usable prep space in her kitchen. We've started measuring and trying to figure out what could go where.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is this at Teresa's house in Bellevue?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. She wants to replace the peninsula with a run of counter along the wall.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, that could give her a much better stretch to work on.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: That's what she's hoping. The peninsula takes up room, but it doesn't give her the kind of space she wants.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How much room would there be between the new counter and the cabinets across from it?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I measured 42 inches of clearance between the proposed counter and the opposite cabinets.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you have to measure it 6 times?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Only 3. I found the tape measure in a shoebox, so really the hardest part was over.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A shoebox? That's a new system.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I didn't ask. Teresa offered me a lemon scone while we measured, and I decided not to question the household organization.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair. So are you two drawing it out yourselves?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Just rough plans for now. Teresa has a design consultation scheduled for November 19, so we're getting the measurements together before that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. Is she pretty set on the counter along the wall?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, that's the idea she's most interested in. We're trying to be clear about what she wants from the space.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: More room to actually put things down. Seems like a good place to start.

details_in_summary: Teresa offered him a lemon scone while they measured.
key_facts: Teresa wants to replace the peninsula with a run of counter along the wall.
Daniel measured 42 inches of clearance between the proposed counter and the opposite cabinets.
Teresa has a design consultation scheduled for November 19.
minor_details: Daniel found the tape measure in a shoebox.
Teresa offered him a lemon scone while they measured.

summary: Riley discussed Teresa’s Bellevue kitchen project with Daniel. They’re evaluating replacing the peninsula with a wall counter to gain prep space. Measured 42 inches of clearance to opposite cabinets; rough plans are being prepared ahead of a design consultation on November 19. They aim to finalize measurements and concepts before the appointment, focusing on increasing work surface and layout clarity.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How are things with you this evening?

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: Pretty good. I signed up for a beginner Italian course.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! What made you decide to do that?

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: My cousin Francesca grew up in Bologna, and we always end up speaking English. I'd like to be able to speak some Italian with her instead.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Where's the course?

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: At a community center in Ballard. It meets on Wednesday evenings, which works for me.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How'd you find it?

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: There was a flyer near the library entrance. I stopped to read it, and, well, here we are.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Have you got anything for class yet?

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: A green notebook. It seemed like a sensible start, though it hasn't taught me much so far.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Give it time. Have you studied Italian before?

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: Not properly. I know a few words, but I wouldn't call that studying.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's what the beginner course is for, I guess.

details_in_summary: Amara has bought a green notebook for class.
She found the course on a flyer near the library entrance.
key_facts: The course meets on Wednesday evenings at a community center in Ballard.
Amara hopes to use Italian with her cousin Francesca, who grew up in Bologna.
minor_details: Amara has bought a green notebook for class.
She found the course on a flyer near the library entrance.

summary: Riley discussed Amara signing up for a beginner Italian course at a Ballard community center on Wednesday evenings to speak with her cousin Francesca. Amara found the course via a library flyer and bought a green notebook. She has not studied Italian before. Next steps include continuing the course and practicing Italian with her cousin; no further decisions noted.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How are things looking in the bedroom?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Actually, I just spotted a damp patch beneath the bedroom window.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh. Is it wet right now, or does it just look darker?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'm not sure. I'll use this old dish towel to feel the wall.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What's the verdict?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The towel's a little damp. Okay, but the dresser's pretty close to it. Can we move it out?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'll take this end. Ready?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yep. Let's pull it about 1 foot away from the wall.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: There. That's about 1 foot. Oh, there's a sock back here.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The dresser was keeping it safe.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll put it with the laundry. Does the patch go any farther down?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: No, I think that's the whole thing. It's easier to see with the dresser out of the way.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll get a ruler and take a photo, so we have something to compare it to.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Good. Put the ruler right beside the patch.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay, got it. I took the photo with the ruler beside it.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Let's keep track of the weather too, and take another picture if the patch changes.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sure. I'll make a note for tonight and add to it as we go.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: And leave the dresser where it is for now? There's still room to get past it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that's fine. Our Ballard apartment can spare that 1 foot.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Generous of it. I'll leave the towel nearby so we can check the wall again.

details_in_summary: A sock has fallen behind the dresser.
key_facts: The patch is beneath the bedroom window in their Ballard apartment.
Riley and Maya move the dresser about a foot away from the wall.
Riley takes a photo with a ruler beside the patch.
minor_details: A sock has fallen behind the dresser.
Maya uses an old dish towel to feel whether the wall is wet.

summary: Riley and Maya discussed a damp patch beneath the bedroom window. They tested dampness with a towel, moved the dresser about 1 foot away, and found a sock behind it. They planned to photograph the patch with a ruler, and track any changes by monitoring the weather and updating notes tonight. The dresser will remain in place for now, with the towel left nearby to recheck the wall later.

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: I'm just bringing this paper bag of screws upstairs.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, hey, Omid. Need a hand with the door?

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: I think I've got it. Thanks, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sure. I was just checking on the loaf cooling on the kitchen counter.

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: That explains the smell. It's a good morning to be in this building.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Better than the smell of screws, anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: Much better. Those are more for texture.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So, how's your weekend going?

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: Good so far. Farah, Dev and I are starting a little tabletop-game group.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! Just the 3 of you?

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: Just us, yes. We picked a date for our first game evening.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: When is it?

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: November 21, at the home Farah and I share in Greenwood.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds fun. Have you picked a game yet?

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: Not yet. Let me check what we have before I make any grand promises.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair enough. Hope you have a good first evening.

details_in_summary: Omid is carrying a paper bag of screws.
Riley has a loaf cooling on the kitchen counter.
key_facts: The group consists of Omid, Farah and Dev.
Their first game evening is planned for November 21 at Omid and Farah's home in Greenwood.
minor_details: Omid is carrying a paper bag of screws.
Riley has a loaf cooling on the kitchen counter.

summary: Riley checked on the door while Omid carried screws upstairs. They discussed the loaf cooling and the building smell. Omid announced a new tabletop-game group with Farah and Dev, with the first game night set for November 21 at Farah and Omid's Greenwood home. A game has not been chosen yet; Omid will check available options before deciding.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, this bowl of lentil soup is exactly what I wanted tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, it's good. You were saying something about a bike?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Right. I've got this old bike with a green frame, and I want to make it dependable enough for my commute.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is it in bad shape?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I'm not sure how bad yet. It's old enough that I don't want to just start throwing money at it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair. What's the alternative?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I figure a suitable used replacement would cost about $250. So I want to keep the repair total below $250.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Including parts and labor?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, all of it. Otherwise I'm spending replacement-bike money to keep an old bike.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Do you have any particular attachment to it?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: A little. It has this faded bell I like. That's probably not a sound financial argument.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Depends. How good is the bell?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I knew you'd ask me that. It's a bell, Riley.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay, but if the repairs end up close to $250, that bell is going to have to make a pretty compelling case.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. I'll try not to spend 3 hours comparing the sentimental value of bells.

details_in_summary: The bike has a faded bell.
key_facts: The bicycle has a green frame.
Daniel estimates a suitable used replacement would cost about $250.
He wants to keep the repair total below that amount.
minor_details: The bike has a faded bell.
Daniel mentions it over bowls of lentil soup.

summary: Riley discussed Daniel's goal to make a green-framed bike dependable for commuting with total repair costs under $250 (parts and labor). They weighed repairing the current bike versus buying a used replacement, noting a sentimental bell but recognizing it may not justify costs. Next steps: assess the bike's condition and provide a cost estimate to decide between repair and replacement.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm thinking about a winter visit to Walter in Spokane. Would you want to come for part of it?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I think so. When are you thinking?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: January 9–12. I've been looking at my calendar over a mug of tea, trying to work out what makes sense.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds nice. January 9 is a Friday, right?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Right. I'd go Friday and stay through Monday. You wouldn't have to stay the whole time.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'd need Friday off to travel with you, though.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes, if we go together. Is that likely to be a problem?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm not sure yet. I need to check my work calendar before I say yes.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Fair enough. I didn't want to assume you'd be free just because it's after the holidays.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I appreciate that. I'd like to see Dad, though.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Me too. He mentioned that his kitchen table finally has a clear end to sit at.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A whole end? That's practically a renovation.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I know. In theory, we could sit there without moving a single thing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Let's not get ahead of ourselves.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No, we should keep our expectations reasonable.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: If Friday doesn't work, I might still be able to join you for some of the weekend.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That would be good too. Have a look at your calendar, and we can figure out how much time you have.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. I just don't want to commit before I know what work looks like.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Don't commit yet. I'm still considering January 9–12, so there's room to sort it out.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay. I'll check, and then we can talk about it.

details_in_summary: Walter mentioned that his kitchen table finally has a clear end to sit at.
key_facts: Hannah is considering January 9–12 for the Spokane visit.
Riley would need Friday off to travel with her.
minor_details: Hannah has been looking at her calendar over a mug of tea.
Walter mentioned that his kitchen table finally has a clear end to sit at.

summary: Riley discussed a potential winter visit to Spokane to see Walter. Dates proposed: January 9–12, with possibility to join Friday–Monday or partial weekend. Riley needs to check work calendar before committing; Hannah will consider the dates and stay flexible. They referenced seeing Dad and coordinating travel, with an emphasis on not committing until work obligations are clear. Action: Riley to review schedule and follow up.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How's your day going so far?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Pretty good. A little damp. I tried adding a bike ride to my train commute this morning.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, how did that go?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I took the light rail from Columbia City to Westlake, then biked to the Harborline office. It was short, but the rain made it less straightforward than I thought.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Was it raining the whole way?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Enough that the road spray left the back of my jacket wet. I didn't really notice until I got inside.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a good welcome to the office.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. The front of me looked reasonably competent, at least.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Was today your first time trying it?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, today, Monday, November 10. Seemed like a good morning to try it. Well, a morning to try it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Were your hands cold?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Not too bad. I wore wool gloves, and I brought coffee in my dented thermos, so I had that once I got here.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: At least the coffee made it.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: It did. What if I start by looking at how to keep the spray off? The bike could use something for that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that sounds like the first thing to figure out.

details_in_summary: Sam wore wool gloves.
They brought coffee in a dented thermos.
key_facts: Sam began the new commute on Monday, November 10.
They took the light rail from Columbia City to Westlake, then biked to the Harborline office.
Road spray left the back of Sam's jacket wet.
minor_details: Sam wore wool gloves.
They brought coffee in a dented thermos.

summary: Riley asked about Sam's day; Sam described a damp commute combining light rail and biking in rain, noting road spray soaked his jacket and the experience took longer than expected. Sam wore wool gloves and a dented thermos for coffee. They decided to start by addressing bike spray protection as the first improvement, with a plan to explore solutions.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I want to get Owen a book for his birthday in early December, but I don't want to buy something he already owns.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What kind of book are you thinking?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Something about nature, I think. He already has a Pacific Northwest bird identification guide, though, so I don't want to get him the same thing again.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What about nature writing rather than another field guide? Something he could read straight through.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah, that might work. I was looking at guides in my head, and then I realized I have no idea which ones are on the shelf.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You could check the shelf when he's not around, but you probably don't need to find another guide at all.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: True. Hold on, I'm moving this stack of mail to make room for my notes. Apparently that's what the table is for, in theory.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Very ambitious for a Monday evening.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm also drinking tea out of a chipped mug, so the operation is extremely professional.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'd look for something with good stories in it, maybe about the Pacific Northwest, but not just a list of species.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: So, nature writing, preferably local, and more stories than identification. I can work with that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. And if you spot a title you like, check his shelf before you buy it.

key_facts: Riley suggests nature writing rather than another field guide.
Owen already owns a Pacific Northwest bird identification guide.
minor_details: Hannah is drinking tea from a chipped mug.
She moves a stack of mail to make room for her notes.

summary: Riley discussed purchasing a birthday book for Owen. The preferred direction is nature writing with local Pacific Northwest flavor, focusing on stories rather than field guides. They concluded not to buy another guide and to check Owen’s shelf before purchasing. Action items: Hannah should inspect Owen’s shelf for suitable titles (preferably local, story-driven); if a title is spotted, verify it isn’t already owned before buying.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I'm looking at the delivery exception queue, and I can't tell where a dispatcher should start.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, everything looks equally urgent. A delayed delivery and a misrouted one show up with the same label.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right. The existing queue uses 'Exception' for several delivery problems. It's technically accurate, which is not quite the same as useful.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: We need to make it easier to see what needs attention, without making people open every row.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: What if we test clearer wording before we redesign the whole view? See whether the labels help people make sense of it first.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I like that. We could try separate labels for delayed and misrouted deliveries, then see what else we need.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, and not just different words for the same mystery. The label should tell them something they can act on.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Could we put that into a small clickable prototype? Enough of the queue to compare the labels in context.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Definitely. I'm sketching the first idea on the back of this meeting agenda. It's not a lot of room, which may be a useful constraint.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That works. Let's start with the small clickable prototype, then. We don't have to solve the whole screen at once.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Agreed. I'll work through the wording with you, and we'll keep the first version small enough to actually test.

key_facts: The existing queue uses the single label “Exception” for several delivery problems.
Sam and Riley agree to begin with a small clickable prototype.
minor_details: Sam sketches the first idea on the back of a meeting agenda.

summary: Riley and Sam discussed the delivery exception queue, noting that the current 'Exception' label is unclear and wastes attention. They agreed to test clearer, action-oriented wording before a full redesign, proposing separate labels for delayed and misrouted deliveries. They planned a small clickable prototype to compare labels in context, with a constrained first version and iterative wording work. Action items: build a minimal prototype, test label options, and refine wording based on results.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Do you think that windowsill gets enough light for this pothos?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe. It looks brighter than your desk, anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I found it on an unused shelf in the office. It has several long, sparse vines, which doesn't seem ideal.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It's a little scraggly, yeah. Is that a folded paper towel under the pot?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, I set it on one so it wouldn't leave a ring on my desk.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good call. I should probably do the same with this mug. The handle's chipped, too.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: A very distinguished mug. What if I put the plant on the windowsill?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'd watch the light there first, before moving it. It might look bright now but change later.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right. It's still morning, so this isn't the whole picture.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Exactly. See if it gets direct sun, or just bright light, over the day.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I'll leave it on my desk for now, then. The shelf wasn't exactly prime real estate.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: At least you've got it somewhere you can keep an eye on it.

key_facts: Sam found the pothos on an unused shelf in the office.
The plant has several long, sparse vines.
Riley thinks the nearby windowsill might be brighter than Sam's desk.
minor_details: Sam has set the pot on a folded paper towel.
Riley is carrying a mug with a chipped handle.

summary: Riley discussed the pothos’ light needs and placement. The plant was found on an unused office shelf with long, sparse vines and a scraggly appearance. They considered moving it to the windowsill but decided to monitor light first, checking whether it receives direct sun or bright light throughout the day. For now, Riley and Sam will keep the plant on the desk to monitor conditions, avoiding desk rings and reassessing after more observation.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. Okay, so, how's your evening going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty good. Are you eating salted crackers?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. I thought I'd have a few, and now apparently this is dinner.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A very elegant dinner.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Thank you. Oh, you've got a pencil tucked behind 1 ear, by the way.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I was wondering where that went. What were you going to tell me?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, I spotted a holiday radio mystery called The Quiet Beacon. Soundwave Radio is releasing it over the holidays.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A radio mystery? What's it about?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: It starts with a missing logbook at a coastal weather station. That's what caught me.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A missing logbook is a pretty good start, actually.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Right? It's 6 parts. I thought we could listen to it together.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What made you pick that one? There must be a bunch of holiday shows.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I did spend too long looking at the options. A shocking development. But I like the sound of a mystery built around a weather station, and 6 parts feels manageable.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, all right. I'm in. The Quiet Beacon.

details_in_summary: Riley has a pencil tucked behind one ear.
key_facts: The series is called The Quiet Beacon and has six parts.
It is being released by Soundwave Radio over the holidays.
The story begins with a missing logbook at a coastal weather station.
minor_details: Daniel is eating salted crackers.
Riley has a pencil tucked behind one ear.

summary: Riley and Daniel discussed a casual evening, noting a pencil behind the ear and crackers, then shifted to holiday media. Daniel recommended a six-part radio mystery, The Quiet Beacon, released by Soundwave Radio, about a missing logbook at a coastal weather station. Riley approved and they decided to listen to it together, selecting this mystery over other options as a manageable holiday listen.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I want to propose short neighborhood walks as a library program.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, I like that. Where would they start?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: At the Ballard library branch. People could walk from there and get to know a little bit of the neighborhood.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Would everyone go together, or could someone pick up a guide and go on their own?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'm still thinking about that. A printed guide could be useful either way.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. Something people could look at before deciding whether a walk works for them.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Exactly. I don't want to just label a route universally accessible. I'd rather describe the practical conditions and let people decide.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Like how long it is, and whether there are hills?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yes, and what the surfaces are like. A short walk can still be a miserable surprise if the sidewalk's rough.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Or if there's a curb without a ramp. You could put those things right next to the map, not buried in a paragraph.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but how much can you fit next to a map before it's just a very small wall of words?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair. Maybe a short list up top, then a little more detail below. Distance, slopes, crossings, places to sit.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I like places to sit. And whether there are public restrooms, if there are any along the way.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You could also say what kind of crossing it is, not just that there's a street.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Right. A signal is different from hoping traffic feels generous.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The map should show where the information applies, too. Like where a steep bit is, instead of just saying there's one somewhere.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That makes sense. I sketched my first idea on the back of a grocery list, and it's mostly arrows right now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I can take a look. I'm just waiting for the bread dough to rise.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Good. The grocery list has a very helpful 'milk' written across the middle of the route.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Perfect. We'll keep the map and lose the milk.

details_in_summary: Maya sketches her first idea on the back of a grocery list.
key_facts: The proposed walks would start at the Ballard library branch.
Maya wants the guide to describe practical conditions rather than label a route universally accessible.
minor_details: Maya sketches her first idea on the back of a grocery list.
Riley is waiting for bread dough to rise.

summary: Maya proposed a short neighborhood-walk program starting at Ballard library, with a printed guide detailing distance, slopes, surfaces, crossings, seating, restrooms, and accessibility notes. Riley suggested a concise top list plus detailed map annotations showing where info applies. Action: Riley to review Maya’s sketch (back of a grocery list) and refine the map; they’ll keep the map and remove extraneous 'milk' label.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Oh, wow. Okay, so, my Capitol Hill lease ends April 30, 2026. That's closer than it sounds.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are you thinking of renewing?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: No, I think I'm going to leave when it's up. I'd rather start looking now than panic in the spring.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. Do you know what you want to be closer to?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: My audio-editing suite near the Fremont Cut, mostly. The trip from Capitol Hill is getting old.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That gives you somewhere to start, at least. You don't have to look at the whole city.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Right. I've already started a search spreadsheet with 3 columns: rent, commute and noise.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Only 3? I'm impressed.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Give it time. I could turn choosing a closet into a research grant.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Well, rent and commute are easy enough to compare. Noise might be harder.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, I figure I can at least note what I hear when I visit a place. Or ask about it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You could just look at a few listings now, see what prices are like. No need to make a decision this week.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: That's probably the sensible version. I keep feeling like starting means I have to solve the whole thing immediately.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nope. You have until April 30. Just don't spend all of it formatting the spreadsheet.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I'll try. Meanwhile, the closet door in my current place still has that loose knob, so I get a little reminder every morning.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Perfect. The apartment itself is telling you to start looking.

details_in_summary: Daniel has started a search spreadsheet with three columns.
He mentions the loose knob on his current closet door.
key_facts: Daniel's Capitol Hill lease ends April 30, 2026.
He wants his next apartment to be closer to his audio-editing suite near the Fremont Cut.
minor_details: Daniel has started a search spreadsheet with three columns.
He mentions the loose knob on his current closet door.

summary: Riley discussed Daniel Reyes’ Capitol Hill lease ending April 30, 2026 and Daniel’s plan not to renew. He aims to move closer to his Fremont Cut audio-editing space, starting with a simple three-column search: rent, commute, and noise. Riley encouraged reviewing listings gradually, noting noise, and avoiding immediate decisive pressure. Action items include continuing the search, updating the spreadsheet, and using the current closet knob as a reminder to start moving forward.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I keep picturing a dog asleep under the table while we're eating.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: With its nose pointed at the bread, probably.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Especially now that you're slicing the heel off that loaf of bread.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'd have to get better at not dropping crumbs. I do like the idea, though. The apartment would feel different in a good way.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. And I'd love taking a dog with me on my walks at Golden Gardens.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds pretty great. A dog who likes a walk but also likes coming home and doing nothing.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: A dog with a healthy respect for the couch.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Exactly. I'd rather adopt an adult dog than a puppy, too.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but what makes an adult dog feel like a better fit to you?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I think I'd like having a better sense of their personality. And, honestly, the puppy chewing phase sounds intense.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Fair. The furniture's already got enough character.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Your chipped blue mug on the table would probably survive, though.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: It's already battle-tested. What size dog are you imagining?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe medium? Though I guess a small dog isn't automatically calmer, and a big one isn't automatically too much for an apartment.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Right. I'd want to hear what the rescue knows about the individual dog, not just pick by size.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. Somebody we could get to know, who'd be happy hanging out here with us.

key_facts: Maya likes the idea of taking a dog on her walks at Golden Gardens.
Riley would rather adopt an adult dog than a puppy.
minor_details: Riley is slicing the heel off a loaf of bread.
Maya has a chipped blue mug on the table.

summary: Riley discussed adopting a dog with Maya, favoring an adult, medium-sized dog that enjoys walks and home time. They prefer a dog with known personality from a rescue, not just size. Riley noted concerns about puppy chewing and apartment suitability and emphasized wanting a dog that can hang out at home and on walks at Golden Gardens. Action items include researching rescues, assessing individual dogs’ personalities, and arranging meetings to find a compatible dog.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm eating lunch at the branch, and I keep looking over at the holds shelf.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is something wrong with it?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It's gotten really crowded. At Swasey, the holds shelf is supposed to be easy to browse, but lately it feels like a puzzle.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How do people find their holds?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: By the first letters of their surnames. In theory, you find your section and there you are.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: In theory is doing some work there.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Quite a bit. The labels are small, and they're along the lower edges of the shelves, so they're easy to miss.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, so you're looking at the books and the label is down below them?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. And when it's crowded, it's not obvious where one section stops and the next one starts.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds frustrating for staff too.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It is. I'm planning to work on it with Marisol. I'd like us to make it easier to navigate with the space we've already got, not add more furniture.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Makes sense. Is there room to make the letters more noticeable?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I think so. I'm just trying to picture what would be clear without making the shelf look even busier.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, bigger labels could help, but where they go matters too.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Right. I was standing there considering that, and there was a roll of tape left on the circulation desk. For a moment I thought, well, that's a start.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: One roll of tape, endless possibilities.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: And I found a pencil behind the returns bin, so apparently the branch is providing me with supplies one at a time.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Very generous of it. Is Marisol thinking about the shelf too?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I want to go through it with her. It's one of those things that's easy to walk past until you're the person trying to find a particular surname.

key_facts: Patrons look for holds by the first letters of their surnames.
The existing shelf labels are small and placed along the lower edges.
Hannah plans to work on the problem with Marisol.
minor_details: A roll of tape was left on the circulation desk.
Hannah mentions finding a pencil behind the returns bin.
unstated_facts: Patrons look for holds by the first letters of their surnames.

summary: Hannah reported a crowded Swasey holds shelf that is hard to browse. Currently, users find sections by surname initials, but small, low-placed labels hinder navigation when crowded. She plans to work with Marisol to improve navigation using existing space, exploring larger labels and better placement rather than adding furniture. Next steps: review shelf labeling with Marisol and prototype improvements.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Both shared washing machines are in use. So much for laundry this Saturday morning.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, November 15 is apparently a popular laundry day.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Can you see how much time is left on either one?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Not from here. I don't really want to stand around waiting, though.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but if we come back later, we might just find them full again.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: True. And I carried the detergent down in this canvas bag for nothing.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The bag got an outing, at least.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Very enriching for it.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Oh, there's a loose sock beside the laundry-room door. Is that ours?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I don't think so. Let's leave it there in case somebody comes back for it.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: So, should we try a weekday instead?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. How about Tuesday evening, after dinner?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That works. We can bring everything down then and see if either machine's free.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay. I'll take the detergent back upstairs for now.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: And the canvas bag can rest up for Tuesday.

details_in_summary: Riley has carried the detergent down in a canvas bag.
Maya notices a loose sock beside the laundry-room door.
key_facts: Both shared washing machines are in use on Saturday morning, November 15.
They plan to try a Tuesday evening after dinner.
minor_details: Riley has carried the detergent down in a canvas bag.
Maya notices a loose sock beside the laundry-room door.

summary: Riley and Maya discussed laundry, noting both shared machines were in use and that November 15 is busy. They could not see remaining wash times and decided not to wait. They planned a weekday trip, specifically Tuesday evening after dinner, to try again with detergent and the canvas bag. Riley would take the detergent upstairs, and the bag would be ready for Tuesday. They also left a loose sock by the door and considered returning later.

dialogue.speaker: Ingrid
dialogue.text: Show me the part of the slide that's bothering you.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty much all of it. It's for an upcoming Harborline presentation, and I've crammed this dense feature list onto one slide.

dialogue.speaker: Ingrid
dialogue.text: What do you want people to understand when they look at it?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How the work makes things easier. But I keep adding features because I'm worried I'll leave something out.

dialogue.speaker: Ingrid
dialogue.text: And now they can read everything and understand nothing. What if you replaced the list with a before-and-after comparison?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So, show what it was like before, then what it's like with the changes?

dialogue.speaker: Ingrid
dialogue.text: Exactly. I'll sketch 2 boxes on this napkin. Before on the left, after on the right. What's the clearest difference between them?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I think I can show the difference without explaining every feature. Oh, my coffee's gone cold.

dialogue.speaker: Ingrid
dialogue.text: A small sacrifice for a less crowded slide.

details_in_summary: Ingrid sketches two boxes on a napkin.
key_facts: Riley's slide for an upcoming Harborline presentation is crowded with a dense feature list.
Ingrid suggests replacing the list with a before-and-after comparison.
minor_details: Ingrid sketches two boxes on a napkin.
Riley's coffee has gone cold.

summary: Riley discussed simplifying a Harborline slide by replacing a dense feature list with a before-and-after comparison. Ingrid proposed a two-box sketch (Before on the left, After on the right) to show the clearest difference and demonstrate how the work makes things easier, reducing clutter. Action: create a two-box visual instead of listing every feature.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Hi, Riley. How's your Sunday going so far?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, Han. Pretty quiet, actually. How's yours?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Quiet here too. Though the living room's been chilly even with the heat on, which isn't ideal.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is the whole room cold, or just one spot?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I notice it most when I'm sitting on the living-room sofa. I had thick wool socks on and still felt cold.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's annoying. Do you think it's the window?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Maybe. I'm trying to work out whether it's the window or just the room in general. Owen's noticed a cold patch near the window too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So it does seem like that area, at least.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah. My mug of tea went cold on the side table, which didn't help the cozy atmosphere. In theory, Sunday mornings are relaxing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Well, I hope you can figure out what's making it so chilly.

key_facts: Hannah notices the chill most when she sits on the living-room sofa.
Owen has noticed a cold patch near the window too.
minor_details: Hannah was wearing thick wool socks when she noticed it.
A mug of tea went cold on the side table.

summary: Riley discussed a chilly living room with Hannah. They noted a cold patch near the window, corroborated by Owen, and considered whether the issue is the window or the room overall. Riley asked clarifying questions about the cold spots and tea cooling, and both hoped to determine the cause. Action: assess whether the window or heating is causing the chill and address accordingly.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How do things stand with the damp patch this morning?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I think the weather notes are starting to make sense. It doesn't seem to show up with every shower.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. The wall stayed dry during the light rain on November 12.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: But the patch felt damp after the windy rain on November 15.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So maybe it's rain blowing against the window, not just rain in general.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but we can't be sure that's the cause. We can tell Omid what we observed, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll write those weather notes on the back of this envelope, so we have them together.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Thanks. Can you send me your photos of the patch too?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, including the one with the ruler beside it.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Got them. I'll report the leak to Omid now, on November 17.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are you sending the dates too?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yes. I'll say it's beneath the bedroom window in our Ballard apartment, and describe the dry wall on November 12 and the damp patch after November 15.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And that we moved the dresser about a foot away from the wall?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'll include that. I'm sending the description and your photos while my tea cools. At least one of these things is working as intended.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Thanks. I'll put the envelope with the notes somewhere we can find it.

details_in_summary: Riley writes the weather notes on the back of an envelope.
key_facts: The wall stayed dry during the light rain on November 12.
The patch felt damp after the windy rain on November 15.
Maya reports the leak to Omid on November 17.
minor_details: Riley writes the weather notes on the back of an envelope.
Maya sends the message while her tea cools.

summary: Riley discussed the damp patch observations: dry during light rain on Nov 12, damp after windy rain on Nov 15, suggesting weather influence. They planned to inform Omid with dated notes and photos (including a ruler) and to describe the location under the bedroom window in Ballard, and the wallpaper/drywall. They noted moving the dresser about a foot from the wall. Riley would write the notes on the envelope and keep the photos together for Omid.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: You're at your desk already. Morning.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Morning. Just getting settled. How was your weekend?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Good. I found a box of old family photographs while I was looking for a family holiday picture.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, where was it?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: On the top shelf of the hall closet. I don't know how long it'd been up there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Was it an actual photo box, or just a box somebody put photos in?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Just a box, I think. It had a faded blue lid and a loose rubber band wrapped around one corner. Very sophisticated storage system.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: At least it stayed closed. Was the holiday picture in there?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I didn't spot it. I got a little distracted by the rest of them.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Were they all from the same time?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: No, a mix. Some I recognized right away, and some I couldn't place.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's the fun part, though. Until you're trying to remember who somebody is.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right. And then it becomes a very quiet quiz. I've been thinking I want to make a small digital archive the relatives can share.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds nice. Then the pictures aren't just sitting on a shelf.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Exactly. I'd like people to be able to see them without having to come over and dig through the closet.

key_facts: Sam found the box on the top shelf of a hall closet.
Sam was looking for a family holiday picture.
minor_details: The box had a faded blue lid.
A loose rubber band was wrapped around one corner.

summary: Riley and Sam discussed discovering a box of family photographs on the hall closet’s top shelf. They noted the mixed dates, uncertain holiday photo, and a distracting extent of the contents. Riley suggested, and Sam agreed, to create a small digital archive for relatives to view photos without needing to access the closet.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, I got a new exhibit commission. I'm producing an audio piece about Puget Sound ferry commuting.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, that's a good one. Who's the exhibit for?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: It's a small gallery show. Louise Park, the exhibit designer, is working on it with me.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What are you thinking for the audio?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Louise and I want it to center on commuters' own memories, rather than a narrated history.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I like that. More like being on the boat with people than listening to a tour guide.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, exactly. I keep thinking about the little things people remember, not just the big ferry stories.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And how different the same trip might feel to different people.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Right. I sketched an idea on the back of a grocery receipt. It's mostly arrows at the moment.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: College-level diagramming.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Very advanced. I spent longer deciding where the arrows should go than writing the words.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Well, you can explain the arrows over the loaf I brought over. The bottom's slightly burnt, but the rest is good.

details_in_summary: Daniel sketches an idea on the back of a grocery receipt.
key_facts: Daniel is producing an audio piece about Puget Sound ferry commuting.
Exhibit designer Louise Park is working with him on the small gallery show.
They want the piece to center on commuters' own memories rather than a narrated history.
minor_details: Daniel sketches an idea on the back of a grocery receipt.
Riley has brought over a loaf with a slightly burnt bottom.

summary: Riley and Daniel discussed a new audio exhibit about Puget Sound ferry commuting for Louise Park. The concept centers on commuters' memories rather than historical narration, aiming for an intimate, on-board feel. Daniel described a rough diagram of arrows on a grocery receipt as a planning sketch; the idea is to explain the arrows during a future discussion. Riley offered to review or contribute notes, mentioning a loaf as a humorous prop for the conversation.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You're looking at your soup card again.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. Dockside Lunch Counter has punched it 4 times now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: 4 already? It's only November 18.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Apparently I'm very efficient at lunch. Or at soup, anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How did the lemon lentil compare to the mushroom barley I ordered?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I preferred the lemon lentil. The mushroom barley was good, but the lemon gave it a little more bite.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I liked the mushroom barley. I added a packet of crackers to mine, though, so that probably helped.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I remember. They were nearly out of spoons at the counter that visit, too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right, I thought we were going to have to eat it with the crackers.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: A very slow lunch. Luckily, there were still spoons.

details_in_summary: Riley added a packet of crackers to their soup.
The counter was nearly out of spoons when they visited.
key_facts: Sam preferred the lemon lentil soup to the mushroom barley soup Riley ordered.
Sam has collected four punches by November 18.
minor_details: Riley added a packet of crackers to their soup.
The counter was nearly out of spoons when they visited.

summary: Riley Morgan reviewed lunch usage with Sam Okafor. Sam noted the Dockside Lunch Counter punched the soup card four times by November 18. They compared lemon lentil favorably to mushroom barley, with lemon lentil described as having more bite. Riley liked mushroom barley and added crackers, which affected perception. They recalled a shortage of spoons during a slow lunch, and considered eating with crackers. No actionable decisions were made.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Oh, okay, so I just heard the trailer for The Quiet Beacon. That got my attention.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The 6-part one you told me about last week?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, the Soundwave Radio mystery with the missing logbook at the coastal weather station.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What happens in the trailer?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: There's a foghorn that cuts off abruptly. It's a really good little moment.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Just a foghorn? That's your pitch?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: It's a very persuasive foghorn. I may be biased by my entire profession.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You may be. Hang on, I'm folding this dish towel and apparently doing a terrible job of it.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, I'll send you the trailer. It's just under 2 minutes long.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sure, send it over.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Sent. You don't have to listen to it this second.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I see it. All right, you've convinced me. I'll give the series a listen.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Excellent. I was prepared to compare several more foghorns, so you've saved us both an evening.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds like one of your college presentations.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: With fewer slides, but the same amount of unnecessary preparation.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Should we avoid reviews, though? I don't want to stumble across anything while I'm looking it up.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, let's not read any until we've finished the series.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Deal. No reviews until it's over.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Good. I can overthink whether I like it without any outside assistance.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I have absolute faith in your ability to do that.

key_facts: The trailer includes a foghorn that cuts off abruptly.
Riley agrees to listen after Daniel sends them the trailer.
They decide to avoid reviews until the series is over.
minor_details: Riley is folding a dish towel during the conversation.
Daniel mentions that the trailer is just under two minutes long.

summary: Riley Morgan and Daniel Reyes discussed The Quiet Beacon trailer, a 6-part Soundwave Radio mystery about a missing logbook at a coastal weather station. They noted a standout foghorn moment and agreed to listen to the trailer and the series without consulting external reviews. Action items: Daniel will send the trailer to Riley; both will refrain from reading reviews until the series is finished.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The bike's easier to see now, but parking it at the office is apparently the next puzzle.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, did you get lights?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, I bought rechargeable front and rear bike lights. Getting them out of the package was the hardest part.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Really?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: There was this plastic tie that just would not come off. The lights were secure, at least.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good product test. What happened with parking?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I tried the outdoor rack near the office, but it was full when I arrived.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's annoying. Was there anywhere else you could leave it?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I found a spot, but it wasn't very convenient. I don't want to count on that every time.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What about asking if there's another rack we're not seeing?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, that's worth a try. What if I ask around before bringing the bike in again? Saves me doing a little tour with it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And how's the rain situation? Last time you mentioned the spray got your jacket wet.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Still thinking about that. I'm going to look for a rear fender before the next rainy week.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That should help with the stripe up your back, at least.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That's the hope. Sorry, I have an orange at my desk this afternoon, and I'm trying not to get juice on everything.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A noble goal. Maybe finish that before you go looking up fenders.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Good point. Orange first, then fender research. And I'll ask about the rack.

details_in_summary: Sam had an orange at their desk that afternoon.
key_facts: Sam bought rechargeable front and rear bike lights.
The outdoor rack Sam tried near the office was full when they arrived.
Sam plans to look for a rear fender before the next rainy week.
minor_details: The lights came in a package with an unusually stubborn plastic tie.
Sam had an orange at their desk that afternoon.

summary: Riley noted Sam installed rechargeable bike lights. Parking at the office remains tricky due to a full outdoor rack; Sam will ask around for alternative racks before bringing the bike in again. Sam also plans to find a rear fender to improve rain protection. Action items: check for additional racks, pursue rear fender research, and tackle orange-on-desk distraction before fender work.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm at the kitchen table looking at my calendar. Do you have a minute to talk about Crystal Mountain?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I do. We said we'd compare costs before committing, right?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Right. I thought we could pick a day first, so we're looking at the same thing. How about Saturday, January 17, 2026?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: January 17 works for me. A Saturday gives us the whole day.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Good. Now, getting there. I could meet you in Seattle, but that seems a bit backwards.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'll drive from Seattle and pick you up in Tacoma. Then we can go to Crystal Mountain together.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That makes more sense. I was trying to make 2 cars into a sensible plan, and, well.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: We can spare you the exercise. I'll have an ice scraper in the car, too.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: And I'll bring a thermos of coffee. We can at least be awake while we figure out the rest.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Speaking of the rest, neither of us owns any ski gear.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I can compare rental packages for skis, boots and poles. I'll look at what we'd get and what it costs.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll check lift-ticket prices for January 17. Then we can put the numbers together.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Perfect. I haven't skied since that family trip in high school, so I have a little catching up to do. In theory, I'll remember how.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm sure it'll come back. Or we'll spend some quality time on the beginner slopes.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Either way, let's see what it costs before we get too excited.

key_facts: They choose Saturday, January 17, 2026, for the trip.
Riley plans to drive from Seattle and pick Hannah up in Tacoma.
Hannah will compare rental packages for skis, boots and poles.
minor_details: Hannah suggests bringing a thermos of coffee.
Riley mentions keeping an ice scraper in the car.

summary: Riley and Hannah discussed planning a Crystal Mountain trip for Saturday, Jan 17, 2026. They will meet in Seattle, Riley picks up Hannah in Tacoma, then drive together. Riley will check January lift-ticket prices; Hannah will compare ski rental packages (skis, boots, poles). Neither owns ski gear, so rentals considered. They will review costs before committing and may use beginner slopes. Action items: Hannah to compare rentals; Riley to price lift tickets.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Hi, Riley. Have you had lunch yet, or am I interrupting the important work of finding it?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey. I just sat down with it, so your timing's good. How's your day going?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Pretty good. I was looking at the Spokane options over lunch, and I thought I'd call while I could still decipher my notes.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. I checked my work calendar, by the way. I can take Friday off.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That's great. So January 9 to 12 is still what I'm considering. You wouldn't have to come for the whole visit, of course.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I can join you for part of it. What are you thinking for getting there?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Well, I've written the options on the back of an old grocery list, which is a very sound organizational system, in theory.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: As long as you don't accidentally buy a train ticket and a carton of milk.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Right. The train is appealing because we wouldn't have to drive over the pass. But the eastbound train from Seattle reaches Spokane overnight, and that's an awkward schedule.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, arriving in the middle of the night doesn't sound ideal. We'd still have to get to Seattle's station, too.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. And parking near the station would add another expense, if we drove there. It starts to feel less straightforward.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Driving all the way means dealing with the pass, though.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It does. But driving would give me more flexibility while I'm visiting Walter. I wouldn't have to arrange every trip around the train.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That makes sense. I'm glad I can take Friday off, at least. That gives us the option to drive together.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes. Let me keep comparing the two for a bit. I'm leaning toward driving, but I do like the idea of avoiding the pass.

key_facts: The eastbound train from Seattle reaches Spokane overnight.
Driving would give Hannah more flexibility while visiting Walter.
Riley can take Friday off.
minor_details: Hannah has written the options on the back of an old grocery list.
She notes that parking near the station would add another expense.

summary: Riley discussed taking Friday off and possibly joining a Spokane trip with Hannah from January 9–12, joining for part of it if needed. They evaluated travel options: driving vs taking a train from Seattle. Driving offers flexibility but involves the pass; train avoids the pass but has an inconvenient eastbound overnight schedule and station logistics. Hannah will continue comparing options for now, while Riley’s Friday leave remains confirmed.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: And I kept the proposal pretty small. I submitted it just before my lunch break.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. What did you put in?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: 1 trial walk, before scheduling a series. I didn't want to propose a whole calendar before we know what 1 walk takes.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That makes sense. How much time did you ask for?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: A 30-minute program slot, including questions and stops. Not 30 minutes of everyone walking.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. Otherwise someone sees 30 minutes and thinks they have to keep up with a clock.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Exactly. Okay, but I also don't want the description to imply that everyone will cover the same distance.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You could say the slot is 30 minutes, then describe the route separately. The time isn't a required pace.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. And if somebody wants to pause, that's part of the program, not a delay.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A schedule that permits humans. Pretty ambitious.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I know. The paperwork may reject it on principle.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Do you want to make a note about separating the slot from the walking time?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I do. Have you seen my blue pencil?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Here, I found the blue pencil. So, '30 minutes includes questions and stops'?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yes, and no pace requirement. That's the bit I don't want to lose.

key_facts: Maya proposes one trial walk before scheduling a series.
She asks for a 30-minute program slot, including time for questions and stops.
minor_details: She submitted the proposal just before her lunch break.
Riley finds a blue pencil for her notes.

summary: Maya outlined a small proposal: one trial walk before a full series, with a 30-minute slot that includes questions and stops. They agreed to avoid implying a fixed walking pace or distance for all participants. Action items include separating the 30-minute slot from walking time in the description and noting pauses are part of the program; potential paperwork rejection discussed.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Wallingford looks easier for the suite, at least on the bus. Greenwood's tempting too, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How much longer is the trip from Greenwood?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Depends where in Greenwood. Some of the trips I'm seeing have a transfer, and then the walk at the end gets longer.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And Wallingford?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: More options that get me close to the editing suite near the Fremont Cut without a transfer. I'm still checking the actual schedules, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You said you wanted to be closer when we talked about your lease. Is that the main thing you're sorting by?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, mostly. I'm concentrating north of the Ship Canal, and then looking at the bus and the walk from there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Before you fall in love with a listing, you should probably set a rent limit.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. I keep looking at places and thinking, well, maybe that one's worth stretching for.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What's the number where you stop stretching?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: $1,900 a month. That's the ceiling, not including utilities.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay. Put that at the top of the spreadsheet so you can't negotiate with yourself.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I can negotiate with a spreadsheet. I have a column labeled 'walk in rain' now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Honestly, that's a useful column. Have you actually checked the buses, or just put them in the sheet?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I was checking the bus schedules while eating leftover noodles. Very glamorous Friday evening.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Well, at least now you can rule out anything over $1,900 before you spend all night comparing the walks.

details_in_summary: He checks the bus schedules while eating leftover noodles.
key_facts: Daniel sets a rent ceiling of $1,900 a month, not including utilities.
He is concentrating his search north of the Ship Canal.
He compares bus trips from Wallingford and Greenwood to his editing suite.
minor_details: He checks the bus schedules while eating leftover noodles.
His spreadsheet now has a column labeled 'walk in rain.'

summary: Riley and Daniel discussed commuting options to the editing suite, weighing Wallingford vs Greenwood with a preference for fewer transfers and north of the Ship Canal. Riley emphasized proximity and verified schedules; Daniel is checking actual bus times. They set a rent ceiling of $1,900/month (utilities not included) and planned to place it at the top of the spreadsheet to rule out expensive options after schedule verification.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, I took the green bike to a community repair session. It needs a little attention.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How little?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Well, the rear tire is worn and needs replacing. And the brake cables are frayed.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh. I'd put the brakes first, then the tire.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, that seems sensible. Stopping is a fairly important feature.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Big if true. How's the frame?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: It appears sound, at least from what we could see. No obvious damage.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's good. Did you get to check the tires with air in them?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, a volunteer lent me a floor pump. That's when we got a better look at the rear one.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you got grease on your jacket cuff.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I did. Apparently I couldn't inspect a bicycle without putting part of myself in it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So, cables and rear tire first. Then you can see where that leaves you against the $250 replacement.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Right. I still want the repair total below that. I don't want to spend $250 making a worse $250 bike.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Exactly. You don't have to decide on every little thing right now.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, good. Because I was already trying to rank the little things in a spreadsheet in my head.

key_facts: The rear tire is worn and needs replacing.
The brake cables are frayed.
The frame appears sound.
minor_details: A volunteer lent Daniel a floor pump.
He got grease on the cuff of his jacket.

summary: Riley discussed Daniel's green bike repair. The rear tire is worn and brake cables are frayed; brakes are prioritized before the tire. The frame appears sound. Tires were checked with air, revealing the rear tire issue. Daniel stained his jacket while inspecting. They aim to keep total repair costs under $250 and are not finalizing every detail yet; Daniel was mentally ranking items in a spreadsheet.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. How's your Monday afternoon treating you?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey. Not bad. I think lunch helped.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That's a strong argument for lunch. Oh, you remember that box of family photos I found?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, the one on the top shelf when you were looking for the holiday picture.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That's the one. I started sorting it at the kitchen table.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How'd you decide where to start?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I sorted the photos into 3 envelopes by approximate decade. Approximate is doing a lot of work there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you have enough clues to put all of them in an envelope?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: No, 9 photos went into a separate unidentified pile. I couldn't tell where they belonged yet.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds manageable, at least. Did you label the envelopes?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, I wrote on them in pencil. Easier to change if I've got a decade wrong.

details_in_summary: Sam used a pencil to write on the envelopes.
key_facts: Sam sorted the photos into three envelopes by approximate decade.
