Nine photos went into a separate unidentified pile.
minor_details: Sam used a pencil to write on the envelopes.
They did the sorting at the kitchen table.

summary: Riley and Sam discussed sorting a box of family photos into three envelopes by decade, using pencil labels to allow easy changes. Nine photos remained unidentified and undecided about their placement. Action items: review the unidentified photos to determine their correct decade and adjust labels if needed.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: You're looking at dog rescues on the couch?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. I found one with an orange banner at the top of its website. I'm looking at the adult dogs.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Oh, good. I keep picturing one coming along on my Golden Gardens walks.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And I still like the idea of an adult dog more than a puppy. Let's see what we'd actually have to do.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Does it say how much adoption costs?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It lists a $325 adoption fee for adult dogs. I don't see the application yet.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but before we fill anything out, what does our lease say about dogs?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I can pull it up. Give me a second.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'm writing a question on the back of this grocery receipt: 'What does the landlord need from us?'

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Found it. Our lease requires written approval for a dog. So we'd need the landlord's permission before bringing one home.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Written approval, okay. We should ask what information they'd want before we get too far into this.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe whether they need to know which dog we're applying for, or if we can ask in general first.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'll add that to the receipt. A very official filing system.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: At least we have a first step. I'll keep the rescue page open while we figure out what to ask.

key_facts: Their lease requires written approval for a dog.
A rescue they find online lists a $325 adoption fee for adult dogs.
minor_details: The rescue’s website has an orange banner at the top.
Maya writes a question on the back of a grocery receipt.

summary: Riley discussed adopting an adult dog from a rescue (adoption fee $325) and reviewed lease requirements. The lease requires written landlord approval before bringing a dog. They plan to ask the landlord what information is needed and what dog details are required. Action items: confirm landlord’s information needs, obtain written approval, and keep the rescue page open while compiling questions on an official filing system.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, how are things looking with the holds shelf?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: A little clearer, at least. Marisol and I took a closer look at where it gets crowded.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did any particular part stand out?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: The section for surnames beginning with M had the least spare room. It's pretty tight in there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe count the holds before you decide how to divide the space? Just so you're not going by how it looks.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah, that's what we did. Marisol and I counted the holds this Monday morning.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. I was a little late with that suggestion.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Only by a few hours. I wrote the notes on the back of a discarded flyer, so they're very official.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the count backed up what you saw with M?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It helped, yes. Though the amount of room left matters too, not just how many holds are there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. You want to know what's actually crowded, not just which letter has the most.

details_in_summary: Hannah used the back of a discarded flyer for her notes.
key_facts: Hannah and Marisol counted the holds on a Monday morning.
The section for surnames beginning with M had the least spare room.
minor_details: Hannah used the back of a discarded flyer for her notes.

summary: Riley discussed the holds shelf crowding with Hannah Blake. They found the section for surnames starting with M is the tightest area. They decided to count holds to guide space division, counting on Monday morning and documenting notes on the back of a discarded flyer for formality. The count supported the observed crowding, and they noted that remaining available space matters as much as the total number of holds.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Oh, that's useful. I just got off the customer call, and the dispatcher gave me a much clearer picture of how they use the queue.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good timing. I've got the clickable prototype up. What did they say?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: They scan the queue by destination before deciding whom to contact. Not by the problem label, which was my assumption.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Huh. And right now the destination isn't doing much for them in this view.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right. They also wanted the expected arrival time visible in the list.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So they can see where it's going and when it's supposed to get there without opening the delivery.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Exactly. What if we put both on the row? We shouldn't make a dispatcher open each delivery just to understand the problem.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Agreed. I'll put destination and expected arrival time on each prototype row, alongside the status wording.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That should give us something small to test, rather than rearranging the whole screen at once.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. We can still keep the details inside the delivery, just not the things they need for that first scan.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: And we should make the problem clear on the row too. 'Exception' still covers a lot of ground.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll leave space for a more specific status. We can try a few options.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I wrote that down on this yellow sticky note. The tiny truck in the corner is, uh, not part of the recommendation.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I was about to ask if the truck goes on every row.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Only if we want to make the screen less useful. Can we review it here at the end of the long conference table? I can actually see the screen from this end.

details_in_summary: They review the screen at the end of a long conference table.
key_facts: On the call, a dispatcher said they scan the queue by destination before deciding whom to contact.
The dispatcher wanted the expected arrival time visible in the list.
Riley will put destination and arrival time on each prototype row.
minor_details: Sam has a yellow sticky note with a tiny truck drawn in its corner.
They review the screen at the end of a long conference table.

summary: Riley and Sam discussed the clickable prototype: queues are scanned by destination, not problem label. They agreed to show destination and ETA on each row, with status wording, so dispatchers can assess at a glance. Details remain inside the delivery. They’ll add a more specific status placeholder and test a small change before wider layout edits. They noted the tiny truck is not part of the recommendation and planned a quick review at the end of the conference.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I checked that chilly living-room window more closely, the one I told you about.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, did you figure out where the air's coming in?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah. I used a narrow strip of tissue to trace the moving air. It fluttered along the bottom edge of the window sash.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty clear sign. Was it hard to see?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Not once I got the tissue in the right spot. I had to move a small plant off the sill first.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you just held it along the window?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Mm-hmm. I moved it around the edges slowly, and the bottom was where it fluttered.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. So the cold patch Owen noticed was actually near the source.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Seems that way. And I nearly didn't have any tissue to try it with; the box was almost empty.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good thing there was enough left for your experiment.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes, a very sophisticated bit of research. At least now I know where the air's getting in.

details_in_summary: She had to move a small plant off the sill.
key_facts: Hannah used a narrow strip of tissue to trace the moving air.
The tissue fluttered along the bottom edge of the window sash.
minor_details: She had to move a small plant off the sill.
The tissue came from a nearly empty box.

summary: Hannah described locating a living-room window draft by using tissue to trace moving air along the bottom sash. She moved a plant aside to access the sill and confirmed the cold patch Owen noticed was near the source. They noted limited tissue supply but had enough for the test. Next steps imply addressing the identified draft.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Hey. How's your evening going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty good. I'm getting sleepy already, though.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Same. I was just thinking about the laundry.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, our Tuesday plan didn't go very well.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Both washers were occupied again on Tuesday, November 25.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And one machine had a bath mat draped over its lid.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I saw that. A little flag to mark the territory.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: We really thought after dinner might be better than Saturday morning.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but we only tried the one Tuesday. Maybe it's just a popular time.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Could be. I don't really want to keep carrying the basket down to check, though.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Where is it now?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I left the laundry basket by the coat rack.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: All right. What if we try a weekend morning before we make other plans?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Even after both machines were taken that Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. We could try a different morning, and check earlier.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sunday, November 30, in the morning?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That works. Before we decide what else we're doing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay. I'll leave the basket where it is so we don't forget.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Good. It's our very decorative reminder.

details_in_summary: One machine has a bath mat draped over its lid.
Riley leaves the laundry basket by the coat rack.
key_facts: On Tuesday, November 25, both washers are occupied again.
They decide to try Sunday, November 30, in the morning.
minor_details: One machine has a bath mat draped over its lid.
Riley leaves the laundry basket by the coat rack.

summary: Riley and Maya discussed ongoing laundry challenges, noting both washers were occupied on Tuesday, Nov 25, with one machine marked by a bath mat. They agreed to try a weekend morning before other plans. The proposed plan is Sunday, Nov 30, in the morning, with the laundry basket left by the coat rack as a reminder and to be checked earlier. They will use the basket’s current position to avoid forgetfulness.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. Happy Thanksgiving. How's your morning going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, Sam. Pretty quiet so far. Glad we got the call working.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, it connected on the second try. Not bad for a holiday morning.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll take it. What's up?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The pothos, actually. I tried that brighter spot we talked about.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, the one near your desk? How's it doing?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I moved it to the shared west-facing windowsill on November 17. There's definitely more light there than at my desk.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. I wasn't sure how much it would get, so I'm glad you checked.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: And I removed 2 yellow leaves yesterday. A little tidying, not a full renovation.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Ha. Those long vines still looking sparse?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: They are. What if I take cuttings from the longest ones? I'm planning to do that in early December.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds worth trying. You can start with a few and see how it goes.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Exactly. Oh, you've got a pencil tucked behind 1 ear, by the way. Very prepared for a plant consultation.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, I forgot that was there. Thanks. And good luck with the pothos.

key_facts: Sam moved the pothos to the shared west-facing windowsill on November 17.
Sam removed two yellow leaves the day before the call.
Sam plans to take cuttings in early December.
minor_details: Sam's call connects on the second try.
Riley has a pencil tucked behind one ear.

summary: Me and Sam discussed pothos care. Sam moved the plant to a west-facing windowsill on Nov 17 for more light, removed 2 yellow leaves, and noted sparse long vines. Plan to take cuttings from the longest vines in early December; Me advised starting with a few cuttings to test. No other issues noted.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, I'm going to the Seattle ferry terminal on November 29. First outing for the ferry piece.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. Are you just going to walk up to people and ask?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, introduce myself and explain the exhibit first. Then see if anyone actually wants to talk.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And if they do?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I'll ask willing commuters to sign a release before I record their stories. I don't want to spring a form on them afterward.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Makes sense. Are you still going with their memories instead of a narrated history?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: That's the idea Louise and I talked about, yeah. Just give people room to tell it their way.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are you hoping to get anything besides interviews?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: A few short terminal sounds too, if I can. Nothing elaborate.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Have you got your stuff together?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Mostly. I've packed spare batteries in an old pencil case. I'm still deciding whether to bring a thermos of tea, which is apparently a decision I can stretch over several days.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Classic. Bring the tea.

details_in_summary: He has packed spare batteries in an old pencil case.
He is deciding whether to bring a thermos of tea.
key_facts: He plans to visit the Seattle ferry terminal on November 29.
He will ask willing commuters to sign a release before recording their stories.
He hopes to capture a few short terminal sounds as well as interviews.
minor_details: He has packed spare batteries in an old pencil case.
He is deciding whether to bring a thermos of tea.

summary: Riley's colleague Daniel plans a field session at the Seattle ferry terminal on Nov 29 for a piece focused on witnesses’ memories, not a narrated history. He will introduce himself, request consent and a release before recording, and seek brief terminal ambient sounds if possible. Preparations include spare batteries in a pencil case; he’s undecided about bringing a thermos of tea, echoing a light ongoing planning decision.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So where do things stand with The Quiet Beacon? Are we actually doing this?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, I vote yes. None of the 6 parts are out yet, but we could work out how we want to listen.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Separately, maybe? That way we don't have to find a time that works for both of us every time.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. Listen separately, then compare notes afterward. After each part, if we can.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Works for me. And we're still avoiding reviews until it's over?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Definitely. I don't need a stranger telling me what I should have noticed.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You sent me that trailer, and now the foghorn cutting off is stuck in my head.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: It's a good cutoff. Okay, so, first prediction: I think someone moved the logbook before the storm mentioned in the trailer.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Before it? So the storm's just a convenient explanation for it being missing?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: That's my guess. I have very little evidence, which has never stopped me from forming a detailed theory.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I think the apparent haunting is going to have an ordinary explanation. Something at the weather station making a weird noise, maybe.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Reasonable. Also, my cup of mint tea is going cold while I sit here pretending I'm a detective.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And I'm wearing mismatched socks, so we're both clearly prepared for serious investigative work.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Good. We'll listen on our own and see how our guesses hold up. No reviews.

key_facts: They decide to listen separately and compare notes afterward.
Riley predicts the apparent haunting will have an ordinary explanation.
Daniel suspects the missing logbook was moved before the storm mentioned in the trailer.
minor_details: Daniel has a cup of mint tea going cold.
Riley is wearing mismatched socks.

summary: Riley and Daniel discussed The Quiet Beacon. Daniel votes yes; they agree to listen to each of the six parts separately and compare notes afterward, after each part, with no reviews until the project is finished. They note a predicted logbook movement before a mentioned storm and acknowledge possible ordinary explanations for haunting noises (weather station). Action items: listen independently, then exchange notes after each part; avoid external reviews.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Oh, there's a public fast charger near 15th Avenue Northwest. That could work as a backup.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is that on the map you're looking at?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah, I've got the charger map up on my tablet here at the kitchen table. I was wondering what we'd do if the outlet by our space isn't available to us.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: One of the charging-app reviews mentions a broken card reader, though. Doesn't say whether it's fixed now.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but even if it is, would we want to go there every time we need a charge?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Probably not. Our usual driving adds up to roughly 70 miles a week, so we'd have to keep an eye on it and make charging trips.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: And check whether the charger is working before we leave. Our car would have its own social calendar.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. As a backup, sure. But I'd rather not have every charge depend on a separate trip.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The outlet by our space is marked as belonging to the building's common electrical system, right?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. But that doesn't tell us whether we're allowed to use it for a car.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Or what it actually serves. We should find that out before we count on it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Agreed. We said we'd look at charging before getting attached to a car, and I think that's still the right order.

details_in_summary: Riley notices one charging-app review mentions a broken card reader.
key_facts: They find a public fast charger near 15th Avenue Northwest that could serve as a backup.
Their usual driving adds up to roughly 70 miles a week.
The outlet by their space is marked as belonging to the building's common electrical system.
minor_details: Maya checks the charger map on her tablet at the kitchen table.
Riley notices one charging-app review mentions a broken card reader.
meta.storyline_title: A plug in the parking space

summary: Riley discussed backup charging options: a public fast charger near 15th Ave NW and whether it’s on the map. They considered the outlet by their space, unsure of building-ownership and permission to use it for a car. They noted a possibly broken card reader on the charger. Action items: verify charger status, permissions, and how often charging trips would occur; confirm map details.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Oh, good, I caught you! I've got an update on Owen's birthday book.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. Did you find something?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I did. I checked his books first, and there's no copy of The Peregrine by J. A. Baker among them.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Perfect. That seems like a good fit for the nature writing idea.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That's what I thought. I found a used copy at King's Books in Tacoma and bought it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How's the copy?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Pretty good. There's a pencil note on the flyleaf, but it doesn't bother me.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that sounds fine. Was it expensive?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No, it was $12. I spent longer checking the shelves than deciding to buy it, which is probably sensible, in theory.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Especially since he already has that Pacific Northwest bird identification guide.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. I wanted something different, and now I can stop comparing books for a little while.

details_in_summary: The book cost $12.
There is a pencil note on the flyleaf.
key_facts: Hannah found no copy of The Peregrine by J. A. Baker among Owen's books.
She bought a used copy at King's Books in Tacoma.
minor_details: The book cost $12.
There is a pencil note on the flyleaf.

summary: Riley discussed updating Owen's birthday book selection. Hannah confirmed no copy of The Peregrine by J. A. Baker, but found a used copy at King's Books (Tacoma) for $12 with a minor pencil note. Riley noted it fits the nature-writing angle; they already have a Pacific Northwest bird guide. Hannah intends not to compare further and finalize this choice.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Oh, that's a relief. I scanned the first batch of those family photos.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice! How many did you get through?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: 28 photos. I had to wipe the dust off the scanner glass with a microfiber cloth first. Apparently dust also likes family history.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you start with one of the 3 envelopes?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, one of the decade batches. I'm trying a simple naming system for the files.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What does that look like?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: A year, when I know it, and a short subject description. Nothing elaborate.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And if you're not sure about the year?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I leave the date open rather than guess. A confidently wrong filename isn't much help.

details_in_summary: Sam wiped dust off the scanner glass with a microfiber cloth.
key_facts: Sam scanned 28 photos in the first batch.
The filenames use a year when known and a short subject description.
minor_details: Sam wiped dust off the scanner glass with a microfiber cloth.

summary: Riley and Sam discussed scanning the first batch of family photos (28 images). Sam cleaned the scanner glass due to dust. They are using one of three envelopes and applying a simple naming system: year (when known) plus a short subject. If the year is uncertain, the date is left open to avoid incorrect filenames.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How do things stand with Omid and the bedroom window?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I sent him the description and your photos on November 17. Has he replied?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'm reading his reply here at the kitchen table. He proposes inspecting the window on December 4.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but we'll both be out. Does he say how he'll get in?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: He says he can get into the apartment. He just needs access to the bedroom.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That's easy enough. I'll leave the bedroom door open for him.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the dresser's still about a foot away from the wall, so he should be able to see the patch.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Good. No furniture obstacle course for the inspection.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll reply now. 'December 4 works for us. Omid, please let us know what you find.'

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Can you mention that the bedroom door will be open?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yep. Added that, and sent.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'm putting a calendar reminder on my phone for December 4, so I don't shut the door on my way out.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good idea. I'll leave the dresser where it is, too.

details_in_summary: Maya puts a calendar reminder on her phone.
key_facts: Omid proposes an inspection for December 4.
Maya agrees to leave the bedroom door open for him.
Riley asks Omid to let them know what he finds.
minor_details: Riley reads the reply at the kitchen table.
Maya puts a calendar reminder on her phone.

summary: Riley and Maya coordinated Omid's December 4 window inspection. Omid will need access to the bedroom; the bedroom door will be left open and no furniture will block the path. The dresser will remain about a foot from the wall to allow visibility of the patch. Riley drafted and sent a message confirming December 4 and asking Omid to report findings, and noted the door will be open. Maya set a calendar reminder for Dec 4.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Oh, good, Daphne said yes to a temporary trial at the branch.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, for the holds shelf? What are you trying?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Marisol and I made a paper-label prototype. Larger black letters on white card, so people can actually see them.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. Those little labels down along the lower edges weren't exactly helping.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No. And instead of an individual initial on each label, these show surname ranges.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So people look for the range their last name falls into.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Right. We're hoping that makes it easier to find the right spot without having to read every little letter.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you can try it with the shelf you've already got?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That's the idea. No more furniture, just the cards for now. Marisol trimmed them with the library's paper cutter.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Very official.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: In theory. One card came out slightly crooked, so it has a certain handmade authority.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I think patrons will survive.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I hope so. I wanted something we could try before committing to anything more durable.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Especially after you counted and found the M section had the least spare room.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. The count gave us a better sense of what we were dealing with. Now we can see how these labels work in the actual space.

details_in_summary: Marisol trimmed the cards with the library's paper cutter.
One card came out slightly crooked.
key_facts: The prototype uses larger black letters on white card.
The labels show surname ranges rather than individual initials.
Daphne agreed to a temporary trial at the branch.
minor_details: Marisol trimmed the cards with the library's paper cutter.
One card came out slightly crooked.

summary: Riley discussed a temporary branch trial for a holds shelf labeling project. Hannah and Marisol created paper-label prototypes with larger black letters and surname ranges, to replace individual initials. They plan to test the cards on the existing shelf rather than new furniture. Marisol trimmed the cards; one came out crooked. They will evaluate the prototype in the actual space before committing to durable labels, noting the M section has the least spare room.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Oh, good. My mom just told me she's hired Marisol Ibarra for the kitchen.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, she picked a contractor? How's she feeling about it?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Pretty relieved, I think. Okay, so, they've settled on the scope too. The sink stays on its existing wall.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And she's still replacing the peninsula with counter along the wall?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, that's the plan. She really wants the extra prep space.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: When does it all start?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Demolition is scheduled to begin December 15. I'm helping her keep track of the date and the paperwork.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's coming up. Is the estimate straightforward?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Mostly. I circled one line of the printed estimate in pencil so we can make sure we understand it. You know me, I can compare a sentence with itself for 20 minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The classic college method. Did the design consultation help her decide?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: It did. It ran long because she wanted to see a drawer sample.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Honestly, fair. She's going to be opening those drawers a lot.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: That's what she said. I'm just glad there's a plan on paper now.

details_in_summary: Daniel circled one line of the printed estimate in pencil.
key_facts: Teresa hired contractor Marisol Ibarra.
The agreed plan keeps the sink on its existing wall.
Demolition is scheduled to begin on December 15.
minor_details: Daniel circled one line of the printed estimate in pencil.
The consultation ran long because Teresa wanted to see a drawer sample.
unstated_details: The consultation ran long because Teresa wanted to see a drawer sample.

summary: Riley relayed that Daniel’s mom hired Marisol Ibarra for the kitchen. Decision: sink stays on its current wall; peninsula to be replaced with counter along the wall for extra prep space. Demolition is scheduled for December 15, with Daniel tracking dates and paperwork. The estimate line was circled for clarity. Design consultation helped decide after seeing a drawer sample. A plan on paper exists.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, hey. It's really dark for not even 7.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey. Yeah, it feels a lot later.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I did finally replace the rear tire and tube on the green bike.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. Did you take it somewhere?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: No, I installed them myself at home. It took longer than I expected.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What slowed you down?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Getting the tire on was fussier than I thought it'd be. And one tire lever snapped.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh no. Did you lose any of the little parts in the process?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Surprisingly, no. I kept the small parts in a chipped cereal bowl.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The official bike repair bowl.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Exactly. Very specialized equipment. The rear tire and tube were $38, by the way.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So you're still well under the $250 replacement estimate.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. The frayed brake cables are still there, though. At least the frame looked sound at the repair session.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. But the worn rear tire's dealt with, and the cereal bowl earned its keep.

details_in_summary: One tire lever snapped during the job.
He kept the small parts in a chipped cereal bowl.
key_facts: Daniel paid $38 for a rear tire and tube.
He installed them himself at home.
minor_details: One tire lever snapped during the job.
He kept the small parts in a chipped cereal bowl.

summary: Riley noted Daniel replaced the rear tire and tube on the green bike at home, which took longer than expected. A tire lever snapped; no small parts were lost, stored in a chipped cereal bowl. Total cost was $38, well under the $250 replacement estimate. Frayed brake cables remain, though the frame looked sound during the session. Action item: consider addressing the frayed cables in a future maintenance check.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Oh, nice, you've got destination and arrival time on each row now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I put them in the prototype. It feels easier to scan than opening every delivery.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Definitely. I brought 2 wording options for the status. What if we split 'Exception' into 'Delayed' and 'Wrong destination'?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I like that. Let me try them in the list.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The second one's longer, so it might be a little awkward next to the arrival time.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay, I've added both 'Delayed' and 'Wrong destination' to the prototype for testing. The longer one fits.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Good. And that pale gray divider between rows helps keep them apart without shouting at you.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. Though I wonder if 'Wrong destination' is clear enough on its own.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: What if we test both labels without a legend? Just ask people what they think each one means.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Let's do that. If they need an explanation, we can revisit the wording.

details_in_summary: The prototype uses a pale gray divider between rows.
key_facts: Sam proposes “Delayed” and “Wrong destination” as separate status labels.
Riley adds both labels to the prototype for testing.
minor_details: The prototype uses a pale gray divider between rows.

summary: Riley discussed adding destination and arrival time per row to improve scanning. Sam proposed splitting 'Exception' into 'Delayed' and 'Wrong destination'; Riley added both labels for testing, noting 'Delayed' fits better. They approved using a pale gray divider to separate rows. They decided to test both labels without a legend, gathering user feedback to determine clarity and potentially revisit wording later.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: It was better than Tuesday, at least.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, we actually got the laundry done.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: On Sunday, November 30, 1 washer was free when we got there. We still had to wait 20 minutes for the other one.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Which felt longer when I was just standing there looking at the machines.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I had my library book, so I didn't mind the wait as much.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And I found a quarter under the folding table. Big day for both of us.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: A literary morning and a financial windfall.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Still, I'd rather not spend 20 minutes waiting for a washer.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but was the wait worse than coming down and finding both machines occupied?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: No, definitely not. At least we could start one load.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: And we didn't have to go back upstairs with everything.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'd still like to see if there's a time when both are free.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: What about later in the evening? We've tried after dinner, but not that late.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How late are you thinking?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: After 9 p.m. Maybe Wednesday, December 10?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, let's try Wednesday, December 10, after 9 p.m. I can stay up for laundry.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Good. I don't want to start so late that we're regretting it the next morning.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: If they're both occupied, we can just bring it back up.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Deal. No standing guard over the washers all night.

details_in_summary: Riley finds a quarter under the folding table.
key_facts: On November 30, one washer is free when they arrive, and they wait 20 minutes for the other.
They plan to try Wednesday, December 10, after 9 p.m.
minor_details: Maya reads a library book while they wait.
Riley finds a quarter under the folding table.

summary: Riley and Maya discussed laundry logistics. They noted a better day than Tuesday and completed laundry on Sunday, with a 20-minute wait for the second washer and finding a quarter. They agreed to try after 9 p.m. on Wednesday, December 10, with Riley staying up to manage laundry. If both machines are occupied, they will bring loads back up and avoid overnight guarding of washers.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, how did things go with Owen's birthday book?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Really well, actually. He opened The Peregrine at home yesterday, on his birthday, December 3, and he was pleased.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good! Did he already know it?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: He'd heard of J. A. Baker, but he didn't have the book. So checking his shelves paid off.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the used copy from King's Books was a good pick?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It was. He liked that it was a used copy. I'd wrapped it in green tissue paper, which looked nice, in theory. The corners were a bit of a struggle.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Tissue paper is surprisingly unforgiving.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes. I managed to make a book look like an irregularly shaped vegetable.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: But he got through it.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: He did. And he said he wanted to read some passages aloud to me.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty good sign.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I thought so too. He started the first chapter this morning, the morning after his birthday.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Already? He didn't waste any time.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No, he didn't. We had chocolate cake after dinner yesterday, and then he spent a while looking through the book.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm glad he liked it. I was hoping nature writing would be a better bet than another field guide.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It was. Thanks for helping me narrow it down, Riley.

details_in_summary: Hannah wrapped the book in green tissue paper.
key_facts: Owen opened the book at home on his birthday, December 3.
He said he wanted to read some passages aloud to Hannah.
He started the first chapter the following morning.
minor_details: They had chocolate cake after dinner.
Hannah wrapped the book in green tissue paper.

summary: Riley discussed Owen's birthday gift: The Peregrine (nature writing) as a used copy from King's Books. It was wrapped in green tissue paper with awkward corners. Owen opened it on his birthday and began the first chapter the next morning, and expressed interest in reading passages aloud. Nature writing was chosen over a field guide; Riley helped narrow the options; no further action noted.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You're still at your desk? I thought you'd escaped for the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Almost. I'm just putting my soup card back in my work bag.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, how close are you now?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: It's full. I got the 6th punch on December 4, so yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. That's a free soup at Dockside Lunch Counter, right?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yep, after 6 purchased soups. I've been keeping the completed card in the front pocket of my work bag so I don't lose it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Very sensible. Is the free soup worth saving for a particular day?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I think so. My favorite is the roasted squash and ginger soup, so I'm going to use it on a day when that's available.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Better than the lemon lentil?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. I liked the lemon lentil more than the mushroom barley you ordered, but the squash wins.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What's so good about it?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The ginger gives it a little kick, and it came with a swirl of cream. I mean, the cream probably didn't hurt its chances.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How do you know when they'll have it?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The counter posts its daily menu on a small chalkboard. What if I just check that before handing over the card? Revolutionary system.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I support your extremely rigorous soup strategy.

details_in_summary: The counter posts its daily menu on a small chalkboard.
key_facts: Sam got the sixth punch on December 4.
Sam's favorite is the roasted squash and ginger soup.
Sam plans to use the free soup on a day when the squash soup is available.
minor_details: The squash soup came with a swirl of cream.
Sam keeps the completed card in the front pocket of their work bag.
The counter posts its daily menu on a small chalkboard.

summary: Riley discussed Sam's progress on the Dockside soup loyalty card, noting Sam earned the 6th punch on December 4 and will receive a free soup after six purchases. Sam plans to use the free soup on a day when the roasted squash and ginger soup is available, preferring it over lemon lentil. Riley and Sam discussed how the daily menu is posted on a chalkboard, and Riley considered Sam's approach to checking it before redeeming the card. Action: consider using the chalkboard menu to time the redemption.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: You're putting that flyer on the kitchen table?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. I picked up a green flyer from the information table at the Phinney Center.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'm glad we went to the adoption event. It was nice to see the dogs without feeling like we had to pick one.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That dog sleeping under a folding chair seemed pretty happy to ignore everybody.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I liked that one. Did you hear what the volunteer said when I asked about apartments?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Some of it. What did she say?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: She said to look at the individual dog's habits instead of assuming its size determines whether it can live in an apartment.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right, like a small dog could still have a lot of energy.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: And a bigger one might be perfectly content to sleep under your furniture.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: We do have a strong selection of furniture to sleep under.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but we'd need to ask more than where a dog likes to nap. How much exercise does it need? How does it do with noise?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. I still think an adult dog would be a better fit for us than a puppy.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: And I'd love some company on my walks at Golden Gardens.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I was tempted to ask more about the one under the chair, but I didn't want to wake it up just to introduce myself.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: A very considerate first meeting. We'd also need that written approval from the landlord before bringing any dog home.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. For now, I'll keep the flyer. I'm interested, even though we didn't choose a dog today.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Me too. We can look at it together.

key_facts: The adoption event is at the Phinney Center.
A volunteer tells them to consider an individual dog’s habits rather than assuming its size determines whether it can live in an apartment.
minor_details: One dog sleeps under a folding chair.
Riley picks up a green flyer from the information table.

summary: Riley and Maya discussed the information flyer from the Phinney Center and the adoption event. They agree that dog size is less important than individual habits, asking questions about exercise needs and noise tolerance. They note landlord written approval is required before bringing a dog home and prefer an adult dog over a puppy. They planned to review the flyer together and keep it for future consideration.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Oh, yeah! The terminal outing actually went well. I got some usable material.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. Who did you end up talking to?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I recorded 2 commuters waiting for a Bainbridge Island sailing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did they have good stories?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. One of them talked about recognizing the same passengers every morning without knowing their names.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I like that. You know the faces, but that's kind of the whole relationship.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Exactly. That's the kind of thing Louise and I were hoping to get at, instead of someone just telling the history.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How was it trying to do that at the terminal?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, my headphones kept slipping off one ear. A very professional look.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Classic. Did you at least get something to eat afterward?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I bought a cinnamon roll before heading home. Seemed like a reasonable fee for my suffering.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Very reasonable. Are you going back out soon?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, I plan to ride the Bremerton route on December 13, to gather a different set of memories.

details_in_summary: His headphones kept slipping off one ear.
key_facts: He recorded two commuters waiting for a Bainbridge Island sailing.
One described recognizing the same passengers every morning without knowing their names.
He plans to ride the Bremerton route on December 13 to gather a different set of memories.
minor_details: His headphones kept slipping off one ear.
He bought a cinnamon roll before heading home.

summary: Riley described Daniel’s terminal outing, where he interviewed two commuters and collected material focused on recognizable faces and ongoing relationships rather than historical summaries. They noted a desire to capture memory-driven details with Louise. Daniel faced minor equipment issues (headphones slipping) and ate a cinnamon roll. He plans another outing on December 13 along the Bremerton route to gather different memories.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: I wanted to ask you about my mom Isabel's shoebox of old ferry tickets. I think I'd like to make her a small digital album.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, that's a lovely idea. Is it for something in particular?

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: Her birthday, March 15. The box has tickets and other little things from family trips, and the tickets are my favorite part.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You could make it as a PDF. Isabel could open it without needing a special app, and you could keep the pages pretty simple.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: A PDF, yeah. Maybe one ticket per page? I don't want it to feel like a spreadsheet.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: One per page could be nice. You could put a short caption underneath, wherever you know what the trip was.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: That leaves room for the ones I don't know much about. Some of them are just nice to look at.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Exactly. They don't all need a story. Oh, are you ordering?

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: Yes. I'll have a decaf Americano, please. It's a little late for the regular kind.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I probably shouldn't stay too long anyway. I've got a loaf of bread rising at home.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: Then I'll keep my questions to a reasonable number. I was wondering whether the pages should all be the same color.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe a light, neutral background throughout? That way the tickets stand out, even if they're different sizes.

key_facts: Victor is making the album for Isabel's March 15 birthday.
Riley suggests using a PDF for the album.
minor_details: Victor orders a decaf Americano.
Riley has a loaf of bread rising at home.

summary: Victor outlined making a small digital album for his mom Isabel’s ferry-ticket shoebox. They decided on a PDF with one ticket per page, each with a short caption. A light, neutral background will keep pages consistent and tickets prominent, and not all tickets require a story. Victor will proceed with the design; the conversation also briefly touched on ordering a drink and staying processing time.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Hi, Riley. How's your Sunday morning going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty good, actually. How's yours?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Not bad. I've been thinking about that living-room window again.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The one where the tissue fluttered along the bottom of the sash?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That's the one. I contacted Nadiya instead of trying to make a permanent repair myself.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. What did you tell her?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I sent Nadiya a photo of the gap, so she could see what I was talking about.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Could you get a clear picture of it?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah, I took it with the curtains tied back. Otherwise they were rather in the way.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And is she going to come look?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes, she's scheduled to inspect the window on December 12.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's Friday, right?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It is. I wrote the appointment on the paper calendar in the kitchen, so in theory I won't forget it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What made you decide not to tackle it yourself?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Mostly, I don't want to put adhesive on the painted frame without permission. It's a rental, and I'd rather ask than make a mess of it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that seems sensible.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I thought so. The tissue was useful for finding the draft, but it's not exactly a repair strategy.

details_in_summary: Hannah took the photo with the curtains tied back.
key_facts: Hannah sent Nadiya a photo of the gap.
Nadiya is scheduled to inspect the window on December 12.
Hannah wants to avoid putting adhesive on the painted frame without permission.
minor_details: Hannah took the photo with the curtains tied back.
She wrote the appointment on a paper calendar in the kitchen.

summary: Riley discussed a drafty living-room window with Hannah Blake. Hannah contacted Nadiya for a professional assessment, sending a photo of the gap. A clear photo was taken with curtains tied back. Nadiya is scheduled to inspect the window on December 12, with the date noted on the kitchen calendar. Riley and Hannah decided against DIY fixes due to rental restrictions, preferring to obtain permission before any adhesive repairs. The tissue helped locate the draft but was not a repair solution.

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: You're carrying a loaf of bread into the building at this hour. That's a pretty good way to end a Sunday.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'm looking forward to cutting into it. What have you got in your jacket pocket?

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: A roll of painter's tape. I keep forgetting it's in there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It's a little hard to miss.

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: Makes the jacket look more useful than it is. Oh, I was looking at a beginner pottery class for January, but it's full.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, that's too bad. Were you hoping to try the wheel?

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: Yeah, that's the part I'm curious about. Though I expect the clay will win most of the arguments.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are there any other sessions?

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: Let me check. I'm planning to look for a summer pottery session instead.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds good. Hopefully there'll be a spot.

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: I hope so. Anyway, I'll let you get that bread upstairs.

details_in_summary: Omid has a roll of painter's tape in his jacket pocket.
key_facts: The beginner class Omid wanted to take in January is full.
Omid plans to look for a summer pottery session.
minor_details: Omid has a roll of painter's tape in his jacket pocket.
Riley is carrying a loaf of bread.

summary: Riley noted bread and observed Omid’s painter’s tape in his jacket. Omid said the January beginner pottery class is full and expressed interest in trying the wheel; he plans to check for other sessions and look for a summer pottery session. Action: Omid will search for available classes and summer spots.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How are things standing with your mom's kitchen?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, the cabinets are delayed. Delivery moved from December 29 to January 22.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, that's a pretty big jump. Did the supplier call you?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, I took the supplier's call while I was standing outside a pharmacy. Not the most comfortable place to figure out a schedule.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And demolition is still scheduled for December 15?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: That's still the date on the schedule. The question was what to do about the countertop when the cabinets wouldn't be there yet.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Could they measure for it from the plan?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Teresa and Marisol agreed to wait until the cabinets are installed before templating the countertop. That way nobody's guessing at the measurements.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, especially with that new run of counter along the wall.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Right. I spent a while trying to work out whether there was a clever way around it, and then realized I was inventing a problem for myself.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A classic college elective move.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Exactly. Teresa put the revised schedule on the refrigerator with a pear-shaped magnet, so at least we can see what we're working from.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. January 22's a wait, but measuring the actual cabinets sounds a lot better than hoping the plan's exact.

details_in_summary: Teresa kept the revised schedule on the refrigerator with a pear-shaped magnet.
key_facts: The cabinet delivery has moved from December 29 to January 22.
Teresa and Marisol agreed to wait until the cabinets are installed before templating the countertop.
minor_details: Daniel took the supplier's call while standing outside a pharmacy.
Teresa kept the revised schedule on the refrigerator with a pear-shaped magnet.

summary: Riley discussed the kitchen project: cabinet delivery moved from December 29 to January 22, delaying the countertop templating. Demolition remains scheduled for December 15. Teresa and Marisol agreed to wait for cabinet installation before templating to avoid incorrect measurements. A plan-based measurement approach was rejected in favor of actual cabinet measurements. The revised schedule was posted on the refrigerator with a pear-shaped magnet for visibility. Next step: template after cabinets are installed.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The back of my jacket stayed dry this morning, which feels like progress.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, did you get the fender on?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, I installed a rear fender on the bike over the weekend. It made the rainy ride a lot more manageable.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Was it hard to put on?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Not really. I used a small adjustable wrench, fiddled with it a bit, and that was it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. No more stripe up your back.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That's the hope. It's not a full-body rain shield, but it takes care of the road spray.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you've still got the rechargeable lights?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, front and rear. So now I can see, be seen, and arrive without a wet back. A very modest superhero.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How's the parking situation? That rack was full last time you mentioned it.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Better, actually. I talked to the building staff, and they confirmed I can use my badge to access the office bike room.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, that's handy. Have you tried it yet?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I tested the bike room on Monday, December 8, and there was an available locking space.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a relief. Much better than getting here and having to hunt around.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. What if I could just put the bike somewhere and go to work? Revolutionary stuff.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Next you'll be telling me you had a relaxed breakfast.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I had a pear with breakfast, if that counts as relaxed.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It counts. Especially if your jacket was dry afterward.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I'll take it. The fender and the bike room have made the whole train-and-bike thing much easier to deal with.

details_in_summary: Sam used a small adjustable wrench for the installation.
key_facts: Sam installed a rear fender on the bike over the previous weekend.
Building staff confirmed that Sam can use their badge to access the office bike room.
Sam tested the bike room on Monday, December 8, and found an available locking space.
minor_details: Sam used a small adjustable wrench for the installation.
They had a pear with breakfast.

summary: Riley summarized Sam installing a rear fender over the weekend, noting it reduced road spray and that a small adjustable wrench was sufficient. Sam confirmed front and rear rechargeable lights remain. Parking improved after staff granted badge access to the office bike room; a locking space was available on Monday, December 8. Action: continue using the bike room via badge and monitor space availability.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. How's your Tuesday going so far?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, Sam. Pretty good. I just had an early afternoon snack, and apparently most of it ended up on my sweater.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, you've got a few crumbs there. A souvenir of lunch-adjacent time.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Thanks. Oh, you've got a strip of masking tape stuck to your notebook.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Oh, that's from the plant. I was trying to keep track of the cuttings.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You took them, then? How's the pothos doing?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Better, actually. The main plant looks healthier on that west-facing windowsill.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. So that brighter spot seems to be working?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Seems like it. I took 3 cuttings on December 1 and put them in water.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Any roots yet?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: 2 of the cuttings have visible roots. Little ones, but definitely roots.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the third?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I discarded the third cutting after its stem turned mushy. Not much of a recovery plan for that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, probably not. Still, 2 out of 3 isn't bad.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: No, I'll take it. What if I give you 1 once it's got a little more root?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'd love that. I could take it home.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Great. I'll let it stay in the water a bit longer first.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds good. And thanks for thinking of me.

details_in_summary: A strip of masking tape is stuck to Sam's notebook.
key_facts: Sam took three cuttings on December 1 and put them in water.
Two cuttings have visible roots.
Sam discarded the third cutting after its stem turned mushy.
minor_details: A strip of masking tape is stuck to Sam's notebook.
Riley has crumbs on their sweater from an afternoon snack.

summary: Riley discussed a snack mishap and noted masking tape on Sam's notebook used for plant cuttings. Sam reported the pothos improving on a west-facing sill; three cuttings were placed in water on December 1, two have small roots, one was discarded due to a mushy stem. They considered giving Riley one rooted cutting once it matures, with it staying in water a bit longer and Riley potentially taking it home.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Did you find any used electric cars for us to compare?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I scribbled the model names on this yellow sticky note: a 2020 Chevrolet Bolt EV and a 2020 Nissan Leaf.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but how far do they go? Let me get my mint tea out of the way so I can see that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The Bolt's EPA-rated range is about 259 miles. The standard-range Leaf is rated at 150 miles.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That's a pretty big difference. For our usual 70 miles a week, either one could work, at least on paper.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. The Bolt gives us a lot more flexibility for longer drives, though.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: And a little more room for forgetting to charge. Not that we know where we'd be charging yet.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. The outlet by our space is on the building's common electrical system, and we still don't know if we can use it.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The fast charger near 15th Avenue Northwest is a backup, but I don't want every charge to be an outing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Same. I'm not ruling out the Leaf, though. We should keep both on the list.

key_facts: They compare a 2020 Chevrolet Bolt EV with a 2020 Nissan Leaf.
The Bolt's EPA-rated range is about 259 miles, versus 150 miles for the standard-range Leaf.
minor_details: Riley has scribbled the model names on a yellow sticky note.
Maya is drinking mint tea during the comparison.
meta.storyline_title: A plug in the parking space

summary: Riley discussed comparing used EVs: a 2020 Chevy Bolt EV and a 2020 Nissan Leaf. The Bolt has ~259 miles range; Leaf ~150 miles. With about 70 miles/week, both are viable, Bolt offering more long-drive flexibility and charging margin. Riley noted uncertain building outlet access and a backup fast charger on 15th Avenue NW. Decision: keep both vehicles on the list and further verify charging options.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. How's your lunch going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey! Pretty good. I'm taking a break for once. How about you?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Not bad. I had a few minutes, so I thought I'd tell you I reserved our ski equipment.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! What did you end up getting?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: 2 ski, boot and pole packages from a rental shop in Tacoma. One for each of us.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Great. When do we pick them up?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: They're scheduled for pickup on January 16 and return on January 18. So there's time to collect them before we go on the 17th.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Perfect. Did they need our sizes already?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: They asked for our approximate heights. I gave them my best guesses, which is a very scientific system, in theory.

details_in_summary: The shop asked Hannah for their approximate heights.
key_facts: Hannah reserves two ski, boot and pole packages from a Tacoma rental shop.
The equipment is scheduled for pickup on January 16 and return on January 18.
minor_details: The shop asked Hannah for their approximate heights.

summary: Riley and Hannah arranged ski equipment rental: two ski, boot, and pole packages from a Tacoma shop. Pickup is January 16 and return January 18, ahead of their trip on January 17. They provided approximate heights to the rental shop. No further actions recorded beyond confirming pickup/return dates and size information.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm having lunch at the library, so I've got a few minutes. How's your day going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty good. I'm taking a lunch break too. What's up?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I've been asked to put together a small historical photo display for spring, at the Swasey branch of Tacoma Public Library.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, that sounds like your kind of project. How did it come up?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I was putting away a folding table when it came up. Not a very glamorous origin story.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: No, but a good use of table-putting-away time.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Apparently. I made my first note on the back of an old agenda, so it's a very sophisticated operation.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What sort of photos are you thinking about?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'd like them to show everyday life in Tacoma. You know, ordinary places and people, not just the big landmark shots.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I like that. Do you know where it'll go in the branch?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Not yet. I'm interested, but I haven't worked out what we can actually accommodate. I need to have a look at the space before I get too attached to anything.

details_in_summary: The idea came up while Hannah was putting away a folding table.
She made her first note on the back of an old agenda.
key_facts: The display will be at the Swasey branch of Tacoma Public Library.
Hannah wants the photographs to show everyday life in Tacoma.
minor_details: The idea came up while Hannah was putting away a folding table.
She made her first note on the back of an old agenda.

summary: Riley noted Hannah has been asked to assemble a spring photo display for the Swasey branch of Tacoma Public Library. The idea centers on everyday life in Tacoma rather than landmarks. Hannah mentioned origin details (folding table, back of an old agenda) and emphasized needing to view the space at the branch before finalizing concepts or placement.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. Okay, so, how's your lunch going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty good. Better now that I'm away from my desk. How about you?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Good. I went to my first apartment viewing. It was in Wallingford, above a restaurant.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, how was it? You'd been looking at the bus trip from there, right?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. The trip seemed reasonable, but the apartment's off the list. I could hear the kitchen exhaust fan in the bedroom.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, no. Was it loud, or just one of those sounds you can't stop noticing?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: More the second one. A steady hum. I stood there listening long enough that the agent probably thought I was evaluating the acoustics.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I mean, you kind of were.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Fair. The viewing agent arrived carrying a yellow umbrella, by the way. Somehow that's the detail my brain kept, along with the fan.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Well, at least you can cross it off without spending 2 weeks comparing it to every other listing.

details_in_summary: The viewing agent arrived carrying a yellow umbrella.
key_facts: The apartment was above a restaurant in Wallingford.
A kitchen exhaust fan was audible in the bedroom.
minor_details: The viewing agent arrived carrying a yellow umbrella.

summary: Riley discussed her lunch and Daniel Reyes’s first apartment viewing in Wallingford. The apartment was rejected due to a constant kitchen exhaust fan hum in the bedroom. Riley noted Daniel focused on acoustics while the agent carried a yellow umbrella. The listing was crossed off without further comparison to other listings.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: They approved planning the trial, as long as I check the route myself. They specifically want me to check the crossings and resting places.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's good. So is this the loop you're considering?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. My first candidate is a loop from the Ballard library branch, reaching NW 57th Street and 24th Avenue NW.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Can you hold that corner down? The map printout keeps curling up.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'll put my mug of peppermint tea on it. Finally, a practical use for tea.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay, I can see the whole thing now. It looks pretty compact.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but compact on the map doesn't necessarily mean easy to walk. I need to see what the crossings are actually like.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And whether there's anywhere to sit, not just a little green shape that might be a park.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Right. Is there a bench, and can someone get to it? I'd rather say what's there than call the whole route accessible.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The map won't tell you what condition the sidewalk's in, either. It could look continuous here and be cracked or blocked.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Exactly. And I don't want to promise a smooth route just because the line on the page is smooth.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The 30-minute slot includes questions and stops, too, so the loop might take more of that time than it looks like.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. I'll have to see it in person before I know if it's a sensible candidate. The map is a starting point, not a sidewalk inspector.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A sidewalk inspector with a tea mug holding its corner down.

key_facts: The library approves planning the trial but asks Maya to check crossings and resting places.
Her initial candidate is a loop reaching NW 57th Street and 24th Avenue NW.
minor_details: The map printout curls at one corner.
Maya has a mug of peppermint tea.

summary: Riley noted that planning the trial was approved pending Maya’s in-person route checks of crossings and resting places. Maya proposed a loop from Ballard library to NW 57th Street and 24th Avenue NW. They acknowledged the need to assess actual conditions: crossings, benches, accessibility, and sidewalk quality, not just map visuals. The map is a starting point, not a sidewalk inspection. The 30-minute slot includes questions and stops, so the loop’s real duration may exceed the map estimate; Maya will evaluate it in person.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, how are things looking with the pothos cuttings?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Pretty good, actually. The 2 that rooted are still doing well.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the parent plant?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: It's opened a new leaf, and the remaining leaves look firmer. That windowsill seems to be doing the trick.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. It was looking pretty sparse when you found it.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. It's not exactly a jungle now, but it's getting there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you said I could take one of the cuttings home?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yep. Here, this one's yours. It's in a small glass jar.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, thank you! Look at those roots.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I know. Modest, but respectable.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What are you doing with the other cutting?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I'll keep the second cutting in water for now and let it grow on.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Makes sense. I should be able to fit this in my bag.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: What if I wrap the jar in this spare cloth napkin for the trip home? Just in case.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, please. I've got a packet of tissues in here, so I can make room beside it.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: There. It's wrapped. Keep the jar upright if you can.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Got it. It's beside the tissues now. Thanks, Sam.

details_in_summary: Sam wraps the jar in a spare cloth napkin for the trip home.
key_facts: Riley receives one cutting in a small glass jar.
The parent pothos has opened a new leaf and its remaining leaves look firmer.
Sam will keep the second cutting in water for now.
minor_details: Sam wraps the jar in a spare cloth napkin for the trip home.
Riley makes room for it beside a packet of tissues in their bag.

summary: Riley discussed pothos cuttings with Sam. Two cuttings rooted, the parent plant opened a new leaf and looks healthier near the window. Riley will take one cutting home in a glass jar; the second cutting will stay in water to grow. Sam wrapped the jar in a spare cloth napkin for the trip, and Riley should keep the jar upright and fit it in their bag.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How do things stand with the bedroom window? Did Omid say what he found?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. At the December 4 inspection, he found deteriorated sealant on the exterior of the window. He's arranging a repair.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That makes sense with what we noticed. The patch felt damp again after the rain on December 11.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Right. And it stayed dry during the light rain on November 12, but felt damp after the windy rain on November 15.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So it's still not happening every time it rains.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but we don't know exactly how the water's getting in. I'm folding the bedroom curtain back to look at the wall.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Can you see the patch from there?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah, I can. Oh, you've got a pencil tucked behind your ear. Very official leak investigation.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm prepared. Let's leave the dresser where it is while Omid arranges the repair.

details_in_summary: Maya folds the bedroom curtain back to look at the wall.
key_facts: At the December 4 inspection, Omid found deteriorated sealant on the exterior of the window.
The patch felt damp again after rain on December 11.
minor_details: Maya folds the bedroom curtain back to look at the wall.
Riley has a pencil tucked behind one ear.

summary: Riley and Maya discussed the bedroom window leak. Omid found deteriorated exterior sealant during the December 4 inspection and is arranging a repair. Patch remained damp after the December 11 rain, but stayed dry after some previous rains; water ingress is not yet consistent. Riley and Maya planned to inspect the wall behind the curtain. They agreed to leave the dresser in place while Omid schedules the repair.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I've decided to drive to Spokane for the January visit. The train still sounds nice in theory, but getting in overnight is awkward.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, and you'd have more flexibility while you're there.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. I'll drive my car, and I can collect you in Ballard on the way Friday, January 9.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That works. I can take Friday off, like we talked about.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Good. I was thinking we'd head over in the morning, so we're not doing the whole drive in the dark.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds good. I can't stay as long as you, though. I need to be back at work on Monday.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Right. I'm going to stay with Walter until Monday, so we'd need to get you back separately.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I plan to fly back to Seattle on Sunday, January 11. I'll look at flights.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Okay. That gives you a couple of days with Dad, and I can still have Monday morning there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. And I can bring snacks for the drive.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Please do. I want to leave room in the trunk for a small cooler, so we can put anything that needs to stay cold in there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll keep the snacks reasonably compact, then.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
