dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, the cable job was only half a success.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You got one of them on?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, I fitted the new front brake cable. The old rear cable is stuck inside its housing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, that's the one that was sluggish in the courtyard, right?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. I was hoping it would slide out, but it really doesn't want to.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you get much time to work on it this morning?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Enough to make a mess. I was working on a flattened cardboard box, and my hands got cold, so I stopped for toast.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A sensible repair break.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I considered comparing 2 kinds of toast, but somehow made a decision.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Wow. You've changed.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Don't worry, I spent plenty of time staring at the cable first.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So the green bike's still not ready for the commute.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: No. I'm not riding it to work until that rear brake problem is fixed.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, especially after how it felt on that test ride.

key_facts: Daniel fitted the new front brake cable.
The old rear cable is stuck inside its housing.
minor_details: He worked on a flattened cardboard box.
He stopped for toast when his hands got cold.

summary: Riley and Daniel discussed vehicle maintenance: the front brake cable was replaced while the rear cable remains stuck inside its housing and not ready for a test ride. The green bike will not be used for commuting until the rear brake issue is resolved, following a recent test ride that highlighted the problem. They noted a small, inefficient repair session and related, lighthearted interruptions.

dialogue.speaker: Walter
dialogue.text: Oh, hey, I finally got that weatherstripping replaced around my bedroom window.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. How'd it go?

dialogue.speaker: Walter
dialogue.text: Well, the old stuff was worn out, so I pulled it off and put the new strip on. Took me a little longer than it should have.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Was it tricky to get it to stick?

dialogue.speaker: Walter
dialogue.text: No, that part was fine. I cut the first strip too short and had to go back to the hardware store.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh no. By how much?

dialogue.speaker: Walter
dialogue.text: A few inches. Enough that there wasn't any arguing with it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The window won that round.

dialogue.speaker: Walter
dialogue.text: It did. Here in Spokane, I'm apparently no match for a window and a pair of blue-handled scissors.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you get the next strip to fit?

dialogue.speaker: Walter
dialogue.text: I did. Measured it twice that time, which is an excellent system if you actually use it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And can you feel a difference in the room?

dialogue.speaker: Walter
dialogue.text: Yeah, the bedroom feels less drafty now. I had a mug of tea on the dresser while I worked, and I could stand there without feeling that cold air coming in.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a good payoff, even with the extra trip.

dialogue.speaker: Walter
dialogue.text: It is. And the scissors and I are still on speaking terms.

key_facts: Walter replaced the weatherstripping around his bedroom window at his Spokane house.
He cut the first strip too short and returned to the hardware store.
The bedroom feels less drafty now.
minor_details: He used blue-handled scissors for the job.
He had a mug of tea on the dresser while he worked.

summary: Riley discussed Walter replacing his bedroom window weatherstripping in Spokane. The old strip was removed; the first piece was cut too short, requiring a return to the hardware store. Walter then measured twice for the second strip to ensure a proper fit. After installation, the bedroom feels less drafty, and the process left Walter comfortable with the outcome; no further actions were necessary.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So where do you think things stand with my back?

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: Let's work out what's setting it off. When do you notice the lower-back discomfort most?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: After bouldering, mostly. I think it's worse when I drop from the top of a route.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: After the drop itself, or only once you've finished climbing?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sometimes I feel it right after I land. Then it's more noticeable later.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: All right. What if you downclimb on the large holds before stepping onto the mat? Let's see what that does.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Even if they're not part of the route?

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: Absolutely. There's no prize for dropping onto the mat.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I can try that. I get a bit impatient at the top, but it doesn't have to be complicated.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: Exactly. And what do you do before you start climbing?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Not much, honestly. I usually just start on an easy route.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: How about a 5-minute warm-up: some walking, then easy traversing? Just moving across the wall, nothing strenuous.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, 5 minutes sounds doable. I'll try that and the gentler way down.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: Good. Just notice how your back feels afterward. We can see what those changes do.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Will do. Oh, I nearly left my damp knit cap in my coat pocket. Everything in there is going to be wet.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: At least you found it. And watch out for the trolley of resistance bands parked beside the clinic door on your way out.

key_facts: Riley notices more lower-back discomfort after dropping from the top of a route.
Jonas suggests downclimbing on large holds before stepping onto the mat.
They choose a five-minute warm-up of walking and easy traversing.
minor_details: Riley has a damp knit cap in their coat pocket.
A trolley of resistance bands is parked beside the clinic door.

summary: Riley discussed back pain linked to bouldering, especially after drops. Jonas proposed testing triggers by downclimbing on large holds and starting with a gentler approach. They agreed on a 5-minute warm-up (walking and easy traversing) before climbing, and to monitor how the back feels after these changes. Action items: Riley to try downclimb with large holds, implement the warm-up, and report back on back symptoms.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. Okay, so, it's good to be somewhere warm tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey. How did that second apartment viewing go?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: It helped, actually. The apartment's in a 4-unit building on Phinney Ridge. I got a better sense of the place going back.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What did you notice this time?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Footsteps from the unit above. I could hear them during the viewing, even with the windows closed.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Ah. So not the street noise we were talking about, but still noise.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. After that restaurant fan in Wallingford, I think I'd be listening for it all the time. I'm not going to apply.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That seems fair. Was there anything you liked about it?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: There was a red doormat outside the entrance. Very welcoming. Unfortunately, I can't live on the doormat.

details_in_summary: There was a red doormat outside the entrance.
key_facts: The apartment was in a four-unit building on Phinney Ridge.
Daniel could hear footsteps from the unit above during the viewing.
minor_details: There was a red doormat outside the entrance.

summary: Daniel discussed the second apartment viewing in a Phinney Ridge 4-unit building. He noticed upstairs footsteps noise and decided not to apply, citing previous noise sensitivity. He liked a welcoming red doormat but deemed it impractical to live on. Riley noted the noise issue and the overall decision not to pursue this unit.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Oh, that's annoying. I checked for somewhere people could sit, and there's no public bench on the out-and-back stretch we chose.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The one along 22nd Avenue NW to NW 57th Street?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. There is seating at Ballard Commons Park near the library, though, so people could sit there before or after.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: But not along the route itself.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Right. Okay, but I need to say that plainly in the guide, not just mention the park and let people assume there's a bench halfway.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Put it near the distance. Like, 'About 0.3 miles, no public bench along the route.'

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: And then the park seating right after that? So they don't have to hunt through a paragraph for it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. It feels like something you'd want to know before deciding whether to come.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'm trying to make notes while eating this pear, and I keep picking up the wrong thing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I've got the scrap of paper. I'm folding it into a bookmark, so it's no longer available for important library business.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Excellent. Our paperwork department remains efficient. I'll put the seating next to the distance, then.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And keep the before-and-after part separate from what's actually on the walk.

key_facts: Maya notes seating at Ballard Commons Park near the library.
She finds no public bench on the chosen out-and-back stretch.
minor_details: She makes her notes while eating a pear.
Riley folds a scrap of paper into a bookmark.

summary: Riley and Maya planned guide wording about seating: there is no public bench along the chosen route (0.3 miles). Ballard Commons Park seating is nearby but not on the route. They decided to place the seating note next to the distance and keep the before-and-after information separate from the route details. Action items: Maya will include the seating nearest the distance; ensure the note is explicit for readers.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How are things standing with you this morning, Nora?

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: Pretty good, I think. My brain's just been jumping between work and car listings.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, are you thinking about buying a car?

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: Yeah. I'm considering a used electric car, mainly for weekend trips.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That makes sense. Are you looking at anything in particular yet?

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: Not really. I'm comparing listings with what I've saved, trying to work out what I can actually afford.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Do you have a number in mind?

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: I've got $19,000 set aside for a used car. I don't necessarily want to spend every dollar of it on the price in the listing, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, there's more to it than the sticker price.

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: Exactly. I added a column for estimated registration costs to my expense spreadsheet.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Of course you have a spreadsheet.

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: I think it would be irresponsible not to give the car its own spreadsheet. It's a very expensive imaginary car.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are the listings helping you narrow down the price at all?

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: A little. Some are easier to compare than others. One I checked this morning had unusually blurry interior photos.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Like you couldn't see the condition?

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: Yeah. I think there were seats. Probably a steering wheel.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A promising start.

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: I keep wondering how much information is enough to decide what fits the budget. There's always another listing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe start with a range you feel comfortable spending, including those extra costs. Then the listings outside it can wait.

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: Yeah, I think that would help. The spreadsheet can have limits, even if I apparently can't.

key_facts: Nora has $19,000 set aside for a used car.
She is considering an electric car mainly for weekend trips.
minor_details: She has added a column for estimated registration costs to her expense spreadsheet.
A listing she checked that morning had unusually blurry interior photos.

summary: Riley and Nora discussed Nora’s plan to buy a used electric car for weekend trips. Nora has $19,000 set aside and is factoring in registration costs in a dedicated spreadsheet. She’s comparing listings and noting inconsistent photos. They agreed Nora should establish a comfortable spending range including extras to narrow options, with listings outside the range ignored. Action: Nora define budget range and use spreadsheet filters to focus on affordable, well-documented listings.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The labels mostly held up in the dispatcher check. I brought the printed notes, the ones with the blue binder clip.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Great. I've got my notes here too. We had 4 dispatchers review the prototype on January 8, right?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right. 3 understood the status labels without an explanation.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's encouraging. Especially since we wanted 'Delayed' and 'Wrong destination' to work without a legend.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. The link was less clear, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The 'View options' link?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That's the one. 1 dispatcher mistook it for a filter.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, I can see that. 'Options' could sound like ways to narrow the list.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Exactly. What if we call it 'Review delivery' instead?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That tells me what I'm opening, at least. Though I think the placement could be part of the problem too.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, the words can only do so much heavy lifting. They're content, not a forklift.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll change the label and move the link closer to the delivery details in the row.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That sounds worth trying. It should read more like an action on that delivery, not on the whole queue.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm marking the link with a dotted underline in the mockup so I remember to revisit it.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Good. And I'll note the proposed wording alongside the filter confusion, so we don't lose why we're changing it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Perfect. I'll make both changes in the prototype.

details_in_summary: Riley marks the link with a dotted underline in the mockup.
key_facts: Four dispatchers reviewed the prototype on January 8.
Three understood the status labels without an explanation.
One dispatcher mistook the “View options” link for a filter; Sam proposes “Review delivery” instead.
minor_details: The printed notes are held together with a blue binder clip.
Riley marks the link with a dotted underline in the mockup.

summary: Riley and Sam reviewed prototype labels after a January 8 dispatcher check. Three of four understood status labels without a legend; 'Delayed' and 'Wrong destination' were effective. The 'View options' link caused confusion; a rename to 'Review delivery' was proposed, and the link should be placed closer to delivery details. Riley planned a dotted underline for the mockup; both parties will note wording changes and implement them in the prototype.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So, how are we looking for that early-February week if we bring a dog home?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I checked my library schedule, and I can't take leave that week. What about you?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I've got my calendar open on my laptop. I could take Monday and Tuesday off.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, I'm circling those 2 days in pencil. That's all the time we know we'd have at home?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, during the workday. We'd both be home in the evenings, but Wednesday would be that long stretch we talked about.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: About 8:30 to 4:30, right? Okay, but even with a walker in the middle, that's a lot of time alone for a dog that's just arrived.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Especially when we were talking about giving it a quiet first week to settle in.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Could a friend help on Wednesday, or would we just be hoping someone was free?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: We'd be hoping. I don't think we should assume a friend could cover the remaining days.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Agreed. A pencil circle is not a staffing plan.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And even if someone could do Wednesday, we'd still have Thursday and Friday to figure out.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Right. Monday and Tuesday help, but I'd feel better if we had more of that first week covered.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Me too. Let's leave those days circled for now, but not treat them as enough on their own.

details_in_summary: Maya circles the two available days in pencil.
key_facts: Riley could take the Monday and Tuesday of that week off.
Maya cannot take leave that week because of her library schedule.
They decide against assuming a friend could cover the remaining days.
minor_details: Riley has their calendar open on a laptop.
Maya circles the two available days in pencil.

summary: Riley and Maya discussed staffing a first week for bringing a dog home in early February. They can take Monday and Tuesday off; Wednesday is a long stretch with potential mid-day walker needs. They agreed a friend’s help is unlikely and that pencil-circled days are not a full staffing plan. They will keep those days circled for now and plan to seek additional coverage or alternatives for the rest of the week.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm home on the couch, finally getting around to calling you. How are you?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm good. I was just wondering how the rest of your visit with Dad went.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It was nice. After you left on Sunday, Walter and I made vegetable soup for dinner.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, that sounds good. What went in it?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: A bit of everything, but he insisted on adding extra celery. I thought we had enough, apparently not.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Was it good with the extra celery?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It was, actually. I can't even complain properly.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And did you two do anything after dinner?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: We played cribbage that evening. It was a very quiet night, which was just right.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm glad you got that time with him. How was the drive back Monday?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Easy, thankfully. The pass was dry, so after all that worrying about snow, there wasn't much to contend with.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. I kept thinking about that forecast.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Me too. I also found a wool scarf at Walter's that I'd left there on an earlier visit.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a nice bonus. Did you bring it back?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I did. I was pleased we managed an unhurried weekend together, too. We didn't have to squeeze everything in.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I was really glad to be there. And I'm glad you got home easily.

details_in_summary: Walter insisted on adding extra celery to the soup.
Hannah found a wool scarf she had left at Walter's on an earlier visit.
key_facts: After Riley left, Hannah and Walter made vegetable soup for dinner.
Hannah and Walter played cribbage that evening.
The pass was dry on Hannah's drive back on Monday.
minor_details: Walter insisted on adding extra celery to the soup.
Hannah found a wool scarf she had left at Walter's on an earlier visit.

summary: Riley discussed Hannah's visit with Dad, noting they made vegetable soup with extra celery and played cribbage. Riley highlighted the easy drive home due to dry pass and Hannah returning a wool scarf left at Walter's. Riley observed they enjoyed an unhurried weekend together and were glad to be home safely.

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Oh, you're going to like this. I found a box of old movie programs at the Alder Street Cinema.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Really? Where was it?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Tucked behind a stack of folding chairs. A very distinguished archive.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty good hiding place. What were the programs like?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: All different sizes. Some have these lovely little illustrations on the covers. I didn't want to handle them too much, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, especially if the paper's fragile.

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Right. I offered to make a small lobby display using copies, so people could see them without handling the originals.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I love that. It sounds perfect for the lobby.

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Maybe. I just thought it'd be nice to share them instead of leaving them behind the chairs.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Definitely. Oh, am I catching you on your lunch break?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: You are. I've got a cup of mint tea beside me, and somehow we're talking about old paper instead of eating.

details_in_summary: The box was tucked behind a stack of folding chairs.
key_facts: Chloe found a box of old movie programs at the Alder Street Cinema.
She offered to make a small lobby display using copies.
minor_details: The box was tucked behind a stack of folding chairs.
Chloe had a cup of mint tea beside her during the call.

summary: Riley Morgan and Chloe Bennett discussed finding a box of old film programs hidden behind folding chairs at Alder Street Cinema. The programs vary in size and are fragile. Chloe proposed creating a small lobby display using copies to protect the originals, with the goal of sharing the material instead of leaving it hidden. Riley noted Chloe is on lunch break and they briefly mentioned the mint tea.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Oh, good, I caught you at lunch. I wanted to tell you about the window.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did Nadiya get the new weatherstripping in?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: She did. And I can feel less air along the lower edge now, so that's an improvement.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. Is the living room warmer?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It feels better, but there's still a slight draft at the upper right corner. I noticed it on a windy evening.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How'd you find it? More tissue?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No, I used the back of my hand to feel for moving air. I was waiting for pasta water to boil, so I had a minute.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A very efficient inspection.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: In theory. I also got distracted by these little streaks the rain had left on the outside glass.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Have you told Nadiya about the corner?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes, she's scheduled to come back on January 17 to adjust it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay, at least the lower edge is better. Let me know how the corner goes.

details_in_summary: She used the back of her hand to feel for moving air.
Rain had left small streaks on the outside glass.
key_facts: Hannah felt less air along the lower edge after the replacement.
A slight draft remained at the upper right corner on a windy evening.
Nadiya is scheduled to return on January 17 to adjust that corner.
minor_details: Hannah checked the window while waiting for pasta water to boil.
She used the back of her hand to feel for moving air.
Rain had left small streaks on the outside glass.

summary: Riley discussed window updates with Hannah. Weatherstripping by Nadiya reduced drafts along the lower edge and improved warmth, but a draft persists at the upper right corner. Hannah used the back of her hand to detect airflow and noted exterior rain streaks. Nadiya is scheduled to return on January 17 to adjust the corner. Riley asked to be informed about the corner's adjustment progress.

dialogue.speaker: Kevin
dialogue.text: The long runs are the part I'm still trying to fit around work.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Long runs for what?

dialogue.speaker: Kevin
dialogue.text: I signed up for a half-marathon in April 2026.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! How's the training schedule looking?

dialogue.speaker: Kevin
dialogue.text: Very organized in the spreadsheet. I've been using pale blue cells, so it looks remarkably calm.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The spreadsheet's ready, then. What about you?

dialogue.speaker: Kevin
dialogue.text: In theory, I could run before work. But I keep skipping my early alarms, so that's not much of a plan.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I wouldn't build the whole schedule around suddenly loving early alarms.

dialogue.speaker: Kevin
dialogue.text: Exactly. And after work, a long run feels like a pretty ambitious dinner delay.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Especially when there are noodles with mushrooms waiting.

dialogue.speaker: Kevin
dialogue.text: These are good, by the way. Yeah, maybe the weekend makes more sense.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Would Saturday work?

dialogue.speaker: Kevin
dialogue.text: Saturday afternoon could. I meet Brooke for coffee in the morning, so I don't really want to squeeze a long run in before that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What about Sunday morning?

dialogue.speaker: Kevin
dialogue.text: Yeah, I think Sunday mornings should be my regular long-run slot. No work to rush off to.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you could keep Saturday afternoon as a backup.

dialogue.speaker: Kevin
dialogue.text: That's good. Saturday afternoon if Sunday morning doesn't work. I'll put both in the spreadsheet.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pale blue?

details_in_summary: Kevin has been using pale blue cells in his training spreadsheet.
key_facts: Kevin has signed up for an April 2026 half-marathon.
He plans to make Sunday mornings his regular long-run slot.
Saturday afternoon will be his backup long-run slot.
minor_details: They have noodles with mushrooms for dinner.
Kevin has been using pale blue cells in his training spreadsheet.

summary: Riley discussed Kevin's half-marathon training plan for April 2026. They agreed Sunday mornings as the regular long-run slot and Saturday afternoon as a backup. Kevin will update the spreadsheet (noting pale blue cells) to include both slots.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. Is it just me, or is this morning moving at about half speed?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Not just you. I keep thinking it's nearly lunch.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Same. Oh, I finished scanning the selected photos from that family box.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice! How many were left?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: 22 photos in the final batch. Smaller than the holiday batch, thankfully.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And are you still using that filename system?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, a year when I know it and a short description. I'm not making up dates just to make the filenames look tidy.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Probably a good rule. Have you shown anyone the scans yet?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I asked Emeka to test an early album link from Montreal. It worked, but it opened slowly on his phone.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Slow enough to be a problem?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Maybe. What if I try it on my phone too before I decide it's the link? Anyway, he caught something more useful.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What was it?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: One caption named the wrong park. I wrote the correction on a yellow sticky note so I wouldn't forget to fix it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty good test. Slow link and a caption check in one go.

details_in_summary: Sam wrote the correction on a yellow sticky note.
The test link opened slowly on Emeka's phone.
key_facts: Sam scanned 22 photos in the final batch.
Emeka tested the album link from Montreal.
Emeka pointed out that one caption named the wrong park.
minor_details: Sam wrote the correction on a yellow sticky note.
The test link opened slowly on Emeka's phone.

summary: Riley discussed the slowed morning pace and ongoing photo scanning. Sam reported 22 photos left in the final batch and confirmed the existing filename system. Sam tested an early album link with Emeka; it opened slowly and revealed a caption error for the park. Sam noted the correction on a sticky note. Action items: fix the caption, re-test the link on Riley’s phone before finalizing.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, I assembled the first rough cut of the ferry piece. It runs 3 minutes and 42 seconds.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. That's pretty close to your 3 minutes and 30 seconds.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. I'm less worried about the extra 12 seconds than this one transition.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What's happening there?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: There's a long pause between 2 speakers, and it sounds accidental. Like I forgot to put something in.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Does it feel like a pause they need, or just dead space?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: More like dead space. I wanted a little room between the voices, but I think I gave them separate apartments.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Could you put a bit of the ferry underneath it?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: That's what I'm thinking. I've got some deck ambience I can use, just a brief bit to bridge the transition.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds like it'd give the pause a reason to be there.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. Then I can see whether it still needs to be that long. I spent lunch listening to it over and over.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you actually eat lunch?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I did. Leftover lentil soup at the editing suite. And on the bus over, the loose zipper pull on my bag rattled the whole way, which was apparently my warm-up for listening critically.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Very generous of your bag to help.

details_in_summary: He ate leftover lentil soup at the editing suite.
A loose zipper pull on his bag rattled on the bus.
key_facts: The first rough cut runs three minutes and forty-two seconds.
A long pause between two speakers makes the transition sound accidental.
Daniel plans to use a brief deck ambience recording to bridge that transition.
minor_details: He ate leftover lentil soup at the editing suite.
A loose zipper pull on his bag rattled on the bus.

summary: Riley and Daniel discussed the ferry piece, currently 3:42 against a target of 3:30. The main issue is a dead-space pause between two speakers. Daniel plans to bridge the transition with brief deck ambience to give the pause a reason and reassess the length after tweaks. Additionally, Daniel ate leftover lentil soup for lunch and noted distraction from a rattling bag zipper during listening. Action items: insert ambience, recheck duration, and perform another listen.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, how's the box of programs coming along?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: I started sorting them. There are 18 programs in the box.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, that's a nice manageable number.

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Yeah. I'm sorting them by decade, just to get a sense of what's there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Can you tell how old they all are?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Not all of them at a glance. I used an old desk lamp to see some of the smaller print.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Anything you recognized?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: There's one for Singin' in the Rain.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. Is that one in good shape?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: It's holding together. Some of the others are a little more fragile, so I'm being careful with them.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fragile like the paper's brittle?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Yeah, and there's a program near the bottom with a torn fold. I'm trying not to open that one any more than I have to.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you spot the tear before you opened it?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: I did, luckily. It was right along the fold.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good catch. I'd probably have gone straight for it.

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Well, I was going slowly. The box wasn't going anywhere.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Any other hazards in there?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: I set aside a rusty paper clip. Maybe not the most exciting discovery.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Depends how passionate you are about paper clips.

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Mine's a quiet passion. Mostly I prefer them not rusty.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair enough. I'm glad you're getting a look at the programs, anyway.

details_in_summary: She set aside a rusty paper clip.
key_facts: The box contains 18 programs, which Chloe is sorting by decade.
One program is for Singin' in the Rain.
A program near the bottom has a torn fold.
minor_details: Chloe used an old desk lamp to see the smaller print.
She set aside a rusty paper clip.

summary: Riley discussed with Chloe the progress on the box of programs: 18 items, being sorted by decade. Not all ages are readable at a glance; a desk lamp helps view small print. Singin' in the Rain was identified. Some programs are fragile, with a torn fold near the bottom that Chloe is trying not to open further. A rusty paper clip was set aside. Next steps: continue sorting, handle fragile items carefully, and avoid opening the torn program more than necessary.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Morning, Sam. How's the Victoria trip looking?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Morning. A little more organized, but I haven't booked anything.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you get a chance to check your passport?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, it expires in 2028, so that's one less thing to sort out.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you found it without turning the whole place upside down?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Surprisingly, yes. It was in a blue document folder. Past me was briefly competent.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice work, past Sam. Have you heard anything more from Ada about timing?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: She said a long weekend would suit her. So I'm looking at May with that in mind.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds manageable. Are you still leaning toward the direct ferry from Seattle?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I am. The Port Angeles route still looks like a lot of ground travel before I even get on the ferry.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Especially if you're trying not to rent a car.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Exactly. I started looking for the spring ferry schedules, but I want a clearer picture of the May sailings before I buy anything.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So no ferry tickets yet?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: No, not yet. I'd rather check the May schedule first than pick a weekend and find out the crossings don't line up.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, the whole journey, not just the part on the water.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right. What if the sailing times make a long weekend feel like a long commute? I'd like to avoid that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are you going to keep checking?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. I put a reminder on my phone for the end of the month, so I don't have to keep it in my head.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. Passport sorted, and the schedule can wait a bit.

details_in_summary: The passport was in a blue document folder.
Sam put a reminder on their phone for the end of the month.
key_facts: Sam's passport expires in 2028.
Sam hasn't bought ferry tickets yet because they want to check the May sailing schedule first.
Ada has said a long weekend would suit her.
minor_details: The passport was in a blue document folder.
Sam put a reminder on their phone for the end of the month.

summary: Riley and Sam discussed planning a Victoria trip. Sam confirmed passport expires in 2028 and was found in a blue folder. Ada suggested a long weekend in May, influencing timing. Riley preferred the direct Seattle–Port Angeles ferry to minimize ground travel and not rent a car. Sam plans to review the May sailing schedule before buying tickets and set a reminder for end of month.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How's the wall looking after all that rain?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Let's check. That was heavy rain yesterday, January 15, so it should be a decent test.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll use the flashlight to check the lower edge of the wall. Can you feel under the window?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. It's dry. And I don't feel anything damp along the bottom either.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Looks dry down here too. So, January 16, the wall beneath the window is dry.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but let's not declare the window a hero just yet. I'll send Omid an update this evening.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Do you think we can put the dresser back now?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I think so. Let's leave a little space behind it, though, so we can still check the wall.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: All right, I'll take this end. Is that far enough back?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Almost. I'm nudging this dresser leg into place with my foot. There, that's good.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. There's still a little gap behind it.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: And I've just sent Omid the update: the wall's dry after yesterday's heavy rain.

key_facts: Heavy rain fell on January 15.
The wall beneath the window is dry when they check it on January 16.
Maya sends Omid an update that evening.
minor_details: Riley uses a flashlight to check the lower edge of the wall.
Maya nudges one of the dresser legs into place with her foot.

summary: Riley discussed the wall condition after heavy rain. Maya inspected and reported the wall beneath the window remained dry as of January 16; they decided not to declare the window a hero yet. They planned to update Omid that evening. They also repositioned the dresser to create a small clearance for ongoing checks and confirmed the wall remains dry, with Omid already receiving the update.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So, how are things standing with work lately?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, I'm still mostly producing new exhibit audio, but I found something interesting the other day.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh yeah? What kind of thing?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: A part-time audio preservation certificate from the Cascadia Archive Institute.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How'd you find it?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I was clearing out old browser bookmarks and came across the listing. Apparently I save things and then just let them live there forever.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The digital equivalent of that drawer full of mystery cables.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Exactly. Anyway, it got me thinking about archival audio work. I'd like to broaden my freelance work beyond producing new exhibit audio.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What appeals to you about the archival side?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: The idea of helping older recordings survive and stay usable. It's a different way of working with sound than making something new for an exhibit.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that sounds like it could be satisfying. Are you thinking of applying?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I'm interested, but I haven't decided whether to apply. Right now it's mostly just a listing I keep looking at.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair. Hang on, I'm slicing this loaf of bread. Do you want a thick slice or a normal one?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Thick, please. And I promise not to compare the slices for 20 minutes before choosing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You've grown so much since college.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Haven't I? But yeah, the certificate's on my mind. It feels like it might open up a different kind of work.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Well, it sounds worth thinking about. Here's your extremely well-considered slice.

key_facts: The part-time audio preservation certificate is offered by the Cascadia Archive Institute.
Daniel wants to broaden his freelance work beyond producing new exhibit audio.
minor_details: Daniel found the listing while clearing old browser bookmarks.
Riley is slicing a loaf of bread during the conversation.

summary: Riley and Daniel discussed Daniel’s freelance work in audio, noting his ongoing exhibit audio production and a discovery of a part-time audio preservation certificate from the Cascadia Archive Institute. Daniel expressed interest in expanding into archival work to help older recordings survive, but has not decided to apply. The conversation identified potential for broader freelance opportunities and continued consideration of the certificate as a future path.

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: Oh, I just realized Monday's the school holiday. That's coming up fast.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, Monday, January 19. Are you doing something?

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: I'm spending the day with my niece Inez. She's 12, and I'm trying to think of somewhere indoors to take her in Seattle.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What about the Seattle Aquarium?

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: The aquarium. That's a good thought. Is there enough to do there for a few hours?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I think so. You can take your time looking around, and you don't have to worry about the rain.

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: Always a selling point. My folded umbrella is tucked beside my chair, just in case the weather decides to make itself known.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Smart. I'm going to order a coffee with oat milk. Do you want anything?

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: I'm all set, thanks. Do you think the aquarium would be too young for her?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I don't think so. There's a lot to look at, and she can choose what she wants to spend time on.

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: Good. I'll ask Inez what she thinks before I make any plans.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, see if it sounds fun to her.

details_in_summary: Riley orders coffee with oat milk.
key_facts: Naomi plans to spend Monday, January 19, with her twelve-year-old niece Inez.
Riley recommends the Seattle Aquarium as an indoor outing.
minor_details: Naomi has a folded umbrella tucked beside her chair.
Riley orders coffee with oat milk.

summary: Riley noted Monday is a school holiday (Jan 19) and Naomi will spend the day with her niece, Inez, indoors in Seattle. They discussed the Seattle Aquarium as a potential activity; Riley highlighted there is enough to do there, rain won’t be an issue, and the aquarium isn’t deemed too young for Inez. Naomi prepared an umbrella. Riley offered to order coffee. Decision: aquarium is a viable option. Action item: Naomi will check with Inez to see if she’s interested before finalizing plans.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: The signs above the rows are staying put, at least. But I noticed another problem watching people use the holds shelf.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, what happened?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: A patron pointed it out while holding a folded umbrella. The sign for the highest row was difficult to read from a seated position.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Ah, so moving it above the row made it easier to keep attached, but harder for some people to see.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. In theory, I had solved the sign problem. I had solved a sign problem.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Could you put another one lower down?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That's what I'm planning. I'll add a matching sign at eye level, so someone seated can read it without having to look up at that top one.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And keep the one above the row too?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes. Marisol and I agreed we shouldn't rely on that high sign alone. The second one can show the same surname range.

key_facts: The sign for the highest row was difficult to read from a seated position.
Hannah plans to add a matching sign at eye level.
minor_details: A patron pointed out the problem while holding a folded umbrella.

summary: Riley and Hannah discussed sign visibility for rows. The top sign was hard to read from seated positions; moving it up helped but caused accessibility issues. They decided to add a matching sign at eye level while keeping the high sign, so the surname range is shown on both. Marisol is involved, and the plan is to implement the lower sign next.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did that portfolio link I sent you actually come through?

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: Yes, it did. The one you sent on the evening of January 13, right?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that's the one. I just realized I hadn't checked.

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: I've got it. The link works, too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. And you saw what I said about keeping the inquiry quiet?

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: I did. I'll handle it discreetly, Riley.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Thanks. I'm still just considering it, so I don't want it getting around.

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: Of course. You don't have to make a decision just because you sent me a link.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. I think I needed to hear that.

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: The short version is, you're allowed to be curious.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Even on a Sunday morning?

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: Even then. Although I'm mostly waiting for a load of laundry to finish.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I've got my mug of peppermint tea, so this is about as productive as I intended to be.

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: That's a reasonable Sunday standard.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Anyway, I'm glad you got it, and thanks for keeping it quiet.

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: Absolutely. No problem.

key_facts: Riley sent Naomi a portfolio link on the evening of January 13.
Riley asked Naomi to keep the inquiry quiet.
Naomi confirms she will handle the inquiry discreetly.
minor_details: Riley has a mug of peppermint tea.
Naomi is waiting for a load of laundry to finish.

summary: Riley confirmed the portfolio link sent on January 13 works and is keeping an inquiry discreet. Naomi will handle it quietly; Riley is still considering and wants no public discussion. The pair agreed on discretion and that a decision is not required immediately. Light Sunday small talk about tea and chores accompanied the plan.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That practice walk took 11 minutes, including our 1 pause.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's for the out-and-back to NW 57th Street, right?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah, along 22nd Avenue NW. We weren't trying to hurry, either.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I was mostly wondering if my green rain jacket was going to be too warm.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but 11 minutes for us doesn't mean 11 minutes for everyone. I don't want it to sound like a promised pace.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You could call it an estimate, then put it next to the distance.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Maybe: 'About 0.3 miles out and back. Estimated walking time: 11 minutes, including 1 pause.' Does that sound too exact for an estimate?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A little. How about 'around 11 minutes'? And maybe say that's what it took us, so people know where the number came from.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah, I like that. I'll keep the note about no public bench on the stretch nearby, too.

key_facts: Their practice walk takes 11 minutes with one pause.
Maya decides to describe the time as an estimate, not a promised pace.
minor_details: Riley wears a green rain jacket.

summary: Riley discussed a practice walk of about 0.3 miles out and back along 22nd Avenue NW to NW 57th Street, with 11 minutes including one pause. They agreed to frame it as an estimate (e.g., 'around 11 minutes') and to note that pace varies. An action item was to finalize the wording and include a note about no public bench nearby.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, how are things with you?

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: Pretty good. I've been going through a box of old stuff, very slowly.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is that what you've been doing tonight?

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: Yeah. I was looking for a concert ticket, and I found something you might like.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, what was it?

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: A sleeve of film negatives from our old apartment. It was tucked into a shoebox of ticket stubs.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: No way. How many pictures?

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: 24 negative frames. I counted twice, because the first time I got distracted.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: By what?

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: I had a mug of peppermint tea beside the box, and I was trying not to knock it over. A thrilling evening.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds about right. Can you tell what's in the pictures?

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: Not much, just looking at the negatives. But they're definitely from the apartment.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I can't believe you still have them.

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: I can. Keeping things is easy. Finding them again is where I struggle.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: When did we move in there? August 2016, right?

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: Yeah, August 2016. So it'll be 10 years this August. I was thinking I could make a small photo booklet for each of us, to mark it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: One for me and one for you? I'd love that.

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: Exactly. I'm glad. It feels better than putting the sleeve back in the shoebox for another 10 years.

key_facts: The sleeve contains 24 negative frames and was tucked into a shoebox of ticket stubs.
Riley and Gabriel moved into the apartment in August 2016.
Gabriel wants to make one booklet for Riley and one for himself.
minor_details: Gabriel found the sleeve while looking for a concert ticket.
He had a mug of peppermint tea beside the box.

summary: Riley and Gabriel discussed finding 24 film negatives from their August 2016 apartment. Gabriel plans to create a small photo booklet for each of them to mark the 10-year anniversary in August, preferring a booklet over keeping the sleeve in a shoebox. Action item: assemble two photo booklets for Riley and Gabriel.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So, how's the photography project looking after the first meeting?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Good, actually. South End Photo Walks wants the group to document shopfronts as the seasons change.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. That's a pretty clear focus.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. I was wondering whether I could make a series instead of just collecting individual pictures. This gives me somewhere to start.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did they have any advice about where to look?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: They encouraged everyone to pick a manageable walking area. Not, you know, the entire city.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A very modest assignment otherwise.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right. I brought a small notebook to the meeting, so I wrote that down before I could talk myself into covering too much ground.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Have you picked an area yet?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I'm planning to photograph along Rainier Avenue on January 21, tomorrow evening.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: After work? It'll be pretty dark.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, that's partly why I want to try it. I want to see what I can do with the light that's there before our next discussion.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Makes sense. How was the meeting itself?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Relaxed. Someone passed around a tin of ginger biscuits, which helped.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a solid meeting strategy.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: It is. And I left with a smaller area in mind, which is probably more useful than my original instinct to wander everywhere.

key_facts: The group is documenting shopfronts as the seasons change.
Sam plans to photograph along Rainier Avenue on January 21.
The group encouraged participants to pick a manageable walking area.
minor_details: Sam brought a small notebook to the meeting.
Someone passed around a tin of ginger biscuits.

summary: Riley and Sam discussed a South End Photo Walks project to document shopfronts across changing seasons and whether to pursue a cohesive series. They emphasized a manageable walking area. Sam plans a shoot along Rainier Avenue on January 21, after work, to test lighting before the next discussion. He aims for a smaller, focused area rather than wandering broadly. Meeting was relaxed; biscuits were shared.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: That number includes a shipment that was actually delivered on time.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: In the 'Late shipments' summary?

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Yeah. That's what the dashboard calls it on January 20, anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay, show me which one.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: This row here. The expected delivery time was 10:00 a.m.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the delivery scan says 9:50 a.m.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Right. But the scan record arrived in the system at 10:12 a.m.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So the shipment made it, but the record didn't show up until after the deadline?

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Exactly. And that shipment was counted in the summary.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Ah. I'm going to mark that example on my printout with this pencil.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: The distinction is the scan time versus the time the system received the record.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: But if I just see 'Late shipments,' I'd assume the delivery itself was late.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: I would too. In this case, the number is picking up a late-arriving scan record.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Does it tell me that anywhere in the summary?

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Not in the label. It just gives you the count.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty important thing to leave out.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Yeah. The spreadsheet is technically very confident.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is that what you've got written in the little blue notebook beside your monitor?

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: The two timestamps, yes. I wrote them down so I wouldn't confuse which one was which.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good, because 9:50 and 10:12 tell very different stories.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: They do. One says the delivery was on time; the other says the record arrived later.

key_facts: On January 20, the dashboard summary is labeled “Late shipments.”
One shipment’s delivery scan shows 9:50 a.m., before its 10:00 a.m. expected delivery time.
The scan record arrived in the system at 10:12 a.m., and the shipment was counted in the summary.
minor_details: Wei has a small blue notebook open beside the monitor.
Riley marks the example on a printout with a pencil.

summary: Riley discussed a shipment labeled as 'Late shipments' where the delivery was on time but the system record arrived late. Wei identified the issue: the label doesn’t distinguish between scan time and when the system received the record. They reviewed a row with 9:50 a.m. scan vs 10:12 a.m. system receipt, noting the discrepancy. Riley planned to annotate the printout; Wei keeps two timestamps in a notebook to avoid confusion.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How's the apartment search standing now?

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: Better, I think. On January 16, I narrowed it down to apartments I can afford near a bus route.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a good start. What's your budget looking like?

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: My rent ceiling is $1,650 a month. I'm looking along the Route 40 bus corridor, so the commute stays manageable.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are there many options in that range?

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: A few. Enough to compare, anyway. I've marked the promising listings with blue cells in my spreadsheet.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What makes a listing blue?

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: Price, mostly, and how close it is to the bus. Then I look at the photos, though those aren't always helpful.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How so?

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: One listing had photos of a bathroom mirror but not the bathroom.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Just the mirror?

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: Yeah. I think they're renting out a mirror with a mysterious room attached.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: At least the spreadsheet helps you see which ones are worth a closer look.

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.text: It does. I keep comparing the same few, though. At some point I think I have to admit the spreadsheet can't tell me everything.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair. But it sounds like you've got a much clearer search than you did.

details_in_summary: She has marked promising listings with blue cells in her spreadsheet.
One listing had photos of a bathroom mirror but not the bathroom.
key_facts: On January 16, Nora narrowed her search to apartments she could afford near a bus route.
Her rent ceiling is $1,650 a month.
She is looking along the Route 40 bus corridor.
minor_details: She has marked promising listings with blue cells in her spreadsheet.
One listing had photos of a bathroom mirror but not the bathroom.

summary: Riley checked in on Nora Feldman’s apartment search. Nora narrowed choices to units within a $1,650 rent ceiling near Route 40 to maintain a manageable commute. She flags promising listings with blue cells in a spreadsheet, prioritizing price and proximity, then reviews photos, noting some listings have incomplete imagery (e.g., a bathroom mirror). Riley acknowledges the spreadsheet helps, while Nora accepts it won’t capture everything and plans to continue comparing options, aware of its limitations.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, Teresa finally picked the kitchen lighting.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. What did she go with?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: 3000-kelvin LED strips, rather than puck lights.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. And the wiring was okay for them?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. The inspection on January 8 found that the existing wiring could support LED lights.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a relief. Was it a hard choice between the 2?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: For us? Apparently. I spent way too long comparing them with her.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What was the sticking point?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Mostly how the light would spread across the counter. I even used a flashlight and an index card to demonstrate the difference in light spread.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty Daniel approach to a kitchen question.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I know. I can turn any decision into an elective. Teresa brought out a bowl of clementines during the discussion, so at least we had provisions.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And she liked the strips better in the end?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, she did. Marisol ordered the fixtures today, January 20.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. Is Teresa still keen on having the switch near the kitchen doorway?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: She is. It makes sense to her to have it right there when she comes in.

details_in_summary: Daniel used a flashlight and an index card to demonstrate the difference in light spread.
Teresa brought out a bowl of clementines during the discussion.
key_facts: The January 8 inspection found that the existing wiring could support LED lights.
Teresa chose 3000-kelvin LED strips rather than puck lights.
Marisol ordered the fixtures on January 20.
minor_details: Daniel used a flashlight and an index card to demonstrate the difference in light spread.
Teresa brought out a bowl of clementines during the discussion.

summary: Riley and Daniel discussed Teresa’s kitchen lighting decision. Teresa chose 3000K LED strips over puck lights. A January 8 wiring inspection found the existing wiring adequate for LEDs. The decision hinged on light spread across the counter, demonstrated with a flashlight and index card. Fixtures were ordered on January 20, and Teresa still prefers the switch near the kitchen doorway for convenient access.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, how are things standing with the library photo display?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Better than they were. I've started looking through the Tacoma Public Library's Northwest Room collection, and I found some candidates there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. Have you narrowed them down yet?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I've got a shortlist of 12 images. Which is still more than the 8 I was considering for the wall, but at least it's not everything I looked at.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How do you tell which ones you can actually display?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm checking the rights information before I choose the final pictures. I don't want to settle on a set and then find out I can't use half of it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is the rights information easy to find?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Some of it takes a bit of sorting through. I'm trying to keep the details with the right image, which sounds very basic when I say it out loud.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's usually how the fiddly stuff starts.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. I saved the reference numbers in a spreadsheet, so in theory I can find everything again.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: In theory?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Well, 1 catalog entry had a handwritten date on its sleeve. I made a note of that too, so I wouldn't be trying to remember where I'd seen it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, 12 is a lot to keep straight, especially when you're working with 6 feet of wall.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It is. I'm leaving the final selection alone for tonight and working through the rights information first.

details_in_summary: Hannah saved the reference numbers in a spreadsheet.
key_facts: Hannah found candidates in the Tacoma Public Library's Northwest Room collection.
She has made a shortlist of twelve images.
She is checking rights information before choosing the final pictures.
minor_details: One catalog entry had a handwritten date on its sleeve.

summary: Riley discussed progressing the library photo display. Hannah found candidates from the Tacoma Public Library Northwest Room and has a shortlist of 12 images, aiming to display 8. She is verifying rights information to ensure display feasibility, tagging details to the correct image, and maintaining a spreadsheet of reference numbers and notes (including a handwritten date). Next steps: complete rights checks and finalize the selection tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: Oh, you just got in? How was it out there?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Wet. I just came in from a walk in the rain, so I'm still drying off.

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: Well, I'll keep this short. I wanted to check in about what I told you yesterday, January 20. Bluewake's hiring manager wants an introductory call.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I've been thinking about that. I think an introductory conversation could be useful.

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: Good. Are you comfortable with me letting them know you're open to a call?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I am, yeah. I'd like to hear more about the work before I decide anything.

dialogue.speaker: Naomi
dialogue.text: That makes sense. An introductory call is just a conversation, not a marriage proposal.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. And I'd still appreciate you keeping the inquiry quiet.

key_facts: On January 20, Naomi reported that the hiring manager wanted an introductory call.
Riley is open to an introductory call.
minor_details: Riley has just come in from a walk in the rain.

summary: Riley reported returning from a rainy walk. Naomi stated Bluewake's hiring manager wants an introductory call. Riley is open to the call but wants more information about the work before deciding. Naomi will inform them of Riley's openness and keep the inquiry quiet. Action items: Naomi to coordinate the introductory call; Riley to receive more details about the role before deciding.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: The living-room window is finally behaving. Nadiya resecured the weatherstripping at the upper right corner, and the room feels comfortable enough now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. That was the corner that was still drafty, right?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah, the one I noticed on that windy evening. The lower edge was already better after she replaced the weatherstripping.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Have you had a chance to test it properly?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: We have. Owen and I sat on the sofa for about 40 minutes without needing an extra blanket.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty convincing test. Were you just sitting there checking for drafts?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Not entirely. I had a crossword on my lap, and Owen made a bowl of popcorn. Just an ordinary evening, really.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A much more enjoyable experiment than staring at a window.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes. Though, in theory, I was concentrating on the crossword.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you didn't feel that cold patch by the sofa?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No, not like before. I could just sit there and be comfortable, which was the whole point.

details_in_summary: Owen made a bowl of popcorn.
key_facts: Nadiya resecured the weatherstripping at the upper corner.
Hannah and Owen sat on the sofa for about 40 minutes without needing an extra blanket.
minor_details: Hannah had a crossword on her lap.
Owen made a bowl of popcorn.

summary: Riley noted that Hannah report on the living-room window: Nadiya resecured weatherstripping at upper right and improved the lower edge. A 40-minute test with Owen on the sofa showed no need for an extra blanket. They enjoyed a normal evening, with the absence of a cold patch by the sofa. Conclusion: the window feels comfortable and drafts are reduced; no immediate follow-up needed.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How do things stand with the outlet? Did Omid get back to you?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: He did. I spoke to him yesterday, just before leaving for work.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And did the electrician find out what it's connected to?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. Omid said the electrician confirmed it's on a dedicated 120-volt circuit.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. Is he okay with us using it?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: He is, if we use a portable charger set to 12 amps and keep the cord from crossing the walkway.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay, so we wouldn't need to install a new charger.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Right. Okay, but we'd still need to be careful where the cable goes. The walkway isn't a great place for a surprise obstacle course.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm adding a reminder to keep the charger cable off the wet pavement, too.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Good. And Omid and I agreed we'd pay $25 a month toward the electricity.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is that fixed, or does he want to see how much we actually use?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: We'll revisit the amount if our use changes.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds workable. A lot better than counting on the public charger for everything.

details_in_summary: Maya spoke to Omid just before leaving for work.
Riley adds a reminder to keep the charger cable off the wet pavement.
key_facts: Omid says an electrician confirmed the outlet is on a dedicated 120-volt circuit.
He permits them to use a portable charger set to 12 amps, provided the cord doesn't cross the walkway.
They agree to pay $25 a month toward electricity and revisit the amount if their use changes.
minor_details: Maya spoke to Omid just before leaving for work.
Riley adds a reminder to keep the charger cable off the wet pavement.
meta.storyline_title: A plug in the parking space

summary: Riley and Maya reviewed the outlet status. Omid confirmed a dedicated 120-volt circuit; they can use a portable charger set to 12 amps with the cord kept off the walkway. No new charger installation is needed. Action items: keep the charger cable off wet pavement, add a reminder, and monitor electricity usage with a $25/month contribution (to be revised if use changes).

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How did the Rainier Avenue walk go? Have you looked at the pictures yet?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, I went last night. Here, these are a few of the frames.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, I like that shopfront. What happened to the lettering, though?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The brightest window signs lost detail in several frames. They're just these white patches.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the rest looks a little soft. Was it raining?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Drizzling. I had to wipe drizzle off the camera strap. The camera was fine, but I wasn't exactly steady.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Were you shooting handheld?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. The handheld photographs came out blurred at a shutter speed of 1/30 second. I thought I could hold still enough, but apparently not.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Before you dismiss all the blurry ones, what if you compare the settings? See whether the sharper frames have anything in common.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That's fair. I was about to file them under 'hopeless' and move on.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe check the shutter speed and ISO across a few, and see what happened with the signs too.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'll compare them. I want to try a faster shutter speed on the next walk, too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Were you able to get the view you wanted of that corner?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Eventually. A bus briefly blocked one composition. Very considerate of it to leave before I gave up.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Well, at least you've got a few things to compare now.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right. I'll look at the settings first, then try changing one thing at a time.

key_facts: Sam's handheld photographs came out blurred at a shutter speed of 1/30 second.
The brightest window signs lost detail in several frames.
Sam plans to try a faster shutter speed on the next walk.
minor_details: A bus briefly blocked one composition.
Sam had to wipe drizzle off the camera strap.

summary: Riley and Sam discussed the Rainier Avenue walk. Frames showed washed-out window signs and overall softness due to drizzle and handheld shooting at 1/30s. They planned to compare shutter speed and ISO across frames to identify causes, and Sam will try a faster shutter speed on the next walk, adjusting one setting at a time.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: Come on in, Riley. How's your back feeling today?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty good, actually. I stopped for a $4 tea on the way here, so I'm a little more awake too.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: Good investment, hopefully. Did you get a chance to try the changes at the gym?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, on January 19. I did the 5-minute warm-up, walking and easy traversing, and then I tried downclimbing instead of dropping from the top.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: How did you manage the descent?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I used the big holds to get down and then stepped onto the mat. It took a little more attention than just dropping, but it felt fine.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: And the next morning? That's usually useful to check.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: On January 20, I noticed less stiffness in my lower back than I usually get after a session with top drops. That felt pretty encouraging.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: It does. It's still just 1 session, though, so we can't say yet which part helped, or whether it'll be consistent.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. I'm happy to keep trying the warm-up and gentler way down without declaring it a cure.

key_facts: Riley tried the new approach at the gym on January 19.
Riley noticed less stiffness the next morning than after a typical session with top drops.
minor_details: Riley stopped for a $4 tea on the way to the appointment.

summary: Riley reported back improvements after gym changes tried on Jan 19-20: a 5-minute warm-up with walking and easy traversing, and downclimbing using big holds. Riley noted less stiffness the morning after, but acknowledged one session isn’t conclusive. Decision: continue the warm-up and gentler descent approach and monitor for consistency before drawing conclusions.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. That Friday afternoon feeling's really doing its thing, isn't it?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, my brain's already a little ahead of the clock. How's it going?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Pretty good, actually. I finished the family photo album and shared it with the relatives.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! How many photos ended up in it?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: 86 photos. It's a small archive, which was the idea. Small-ish.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And did Emeka's test catch anything else after that park caption?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: No, just that caption. I corrected it before sending the link out.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How did you share it?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Through a link restricted to invited family members. I wanted it to be easy for them to open, but not just open to everyone.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds like a good balance. Did you end up figuring out all the unidentified ones?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: No, and I'm surprisingly okay with that. The unidentified photos are still in the box for a later pass.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Honestly, finishing the album without solving every mystery sounds like the hard part.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. I put a paper label on the outside of the box, so at least the box is identified. And the album cover is a photo of a family picnic table.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I like that. You made something useful without turning it into a forever project.

details_in_summary: Sam put a paper label on the outside of the box.
The album cover is a photo of a family picnic table.
key_facts: The finished album contains 86 photos.
Sam shared it through a link restricted to invited family members.
The unidentified photos remain in the box for a later pass.
minor_details: Sam put a paper label on the outside of the box.
The album cover is a photo of a family picnic table.

summary: Riley noted that Sam finished a family photo album with 86 photos, shared via an invite-only link. Emeka's test yielded no additional findings after the caption correction. Unidentified photos remain in the box for a future pass. A paper label was placed on the box, and the album cover features a family picnic table. Riley acknowledged that completing the album without solving all mysteries is acceptable.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
