Sam replaced cookbooks under his monitor with a bamboo riser ($18) that lifts the monitor 4 inches; he compared three options and chose this, noting a pencil tin now fits beneath. They noted folding table width (32 inches). The lighting is uneven; Riley suggested checking the light source before changes. Sam will assess lighting on his next home-working day.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Oh, okay. I just read the application instructions, and apparently I need to do more than compare course options.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah? What do they want?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: A short statement, a work sample and 1 professional reference. Applications are due April 30, 2026.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So you've got some time, but you can't just keep looking at the course calendar.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Right. I saved the instructions in a folder called 'Maybe school,' which is a very decisive name.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Very on-brand. Do you know what you'd use for the work sample?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Not yet. I should look through my exhibit work instead of spending another week comparing the same options.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the reference might take a little time to arrange.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. I think I'll start gathering the materials, then figure out what I want to say in the statement.

details_in_summary: Daniel has saved the instructions in a folder called “Maybe school.”
key_facts: Applications are due April 30, 2026.
Applicants must provide a short statement, a work sample and one professional reference.
minor_details: Daniel has saved the instructions in a folder called “Maybe school.”
unstated_facts: Applicants must provide a short statement, a work sample and one professional reference.

summary: Riley noted that Daniel must submit a short statement, a work sample, and one professional reference by April 30, 2026. Daniel plans to stop comparing courses and start gathering materials, using the exhibit work as a potential sample. He saved the instructions in a folder named 'Maybe school.' Riley suggested not delaying and emphasized starting the materials and shaping the statement. Action items: Daniel will collect materials, select a work sample, draft the statement, and arrange the reference.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, how do things stand with the Leaf?

dialogue.speaker: Oliver
dialogue.text: I bought it. February 26, for $11,400.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! So you finally made the call.

dialogue.speaker: Oliver
dialogue.text: Yeah. After that battery inspection, I felt a lot better about it. And the landlord saying yes to the driveway outlet helped.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are you all set for charging it?

dialogue.speaker: Oliver
dialogue.text: Mostly. The sale included a portable charging cable, so I'm planning to charge overnight at home.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds pretty straightforward.

dialogue.speaker: Oliver
dialogue.text: I think so, but it depends on how much I drive. I'm still figuring out what kind of routine makes sense.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Still, must be a relief to have the decision made.

dialogue.speaker: Oliver
dialogue.text: Oh, definitely. I can stop comparing listings and start comparing where to put the ice scraper. It's a small one, in the glove compartment.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A very important first customization.

dialogue.speaker: Oliver
dialogue.text: Exactly. The dealer also gave me a plain blue key tag, so the luxury package is complete.

details_in_summary: The dealer gave him a plain blue key tag.
key_facts: Oliver bought the Leaf on February 26 for $11,400.
The sale included a portable charging cable.
He plans to charge overnight at home.
minor_details: He put a small ice scraper in the glove compartment.
The dealer gave him a plain blue key tag.

summary: Riley discussed purchasing a Leaf (Feb 26, $11,400) and a positive battery inspection, plus landlord approval for a driveway outlet. Oliver plans to charge overnight at home with the included portable cable, pending his driving routine. Decisions include finalizing charging setup and choosing where to place the ice scraper; the dealer provided a blue key tag to complete the package.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: I'm eating a pear for lunch, so give me a second if I sound like I'm losing an argument with it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Take your time. How's your lunch break going?

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Pretty good. Marisol and I have been talking about updating the kitchen in our house in Spokane.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, are you doing the whole kitchen?

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: No, definitely not the whole thing. We want to replace the sink cabinet and the countertop, but keep the other cabinets.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds a lot more manageable.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: That's the hope. The sink cabinet's worn out, and the countertop's had a long and not particularly glamorous life.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So you're keeping the layout the same?

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Yeah, that's the plan. We're trying to keep the project at $3,500 or less.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's the cap for the cabinet and counter together?

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Right, $3,500 for the whole project. I don't want to start replacing things just because they're next to the things we're replacing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A dangerous way to renovate, from what I hear.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Exactly. One drawer handle has been loose for months, but I think it can survive without taking the whole kitchen down with it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You could tighten the handle, though.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: I could. I like to leave myself an achievable goal.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Well, I hope the cabinet and counter come in under the cap. And good luck with the handle.

details_in_summary: A drawer handle has been loose for months.
key_facts: The work is for Theo and Marisol's house in Spokane.
They plan to replace the sink cabinet and countertop but keep the other cabinets.
Their budget cap for the project is $3,500.
minor_details: Theo took the call while eating a pear.
A drawer handle has been loose for months.

summary: Riley relays Theo and Marisol planning a kitchen update in Spokane, focusing on replacing the sink cabinet and countertop while keeping existing layout and other cabinets. The target budget is $3,500 total. They discussed not replacing adjacent items and potential minor fixes like tightening a loose drawer handle. Action items include staying under the budget and pursuing the stated scope rather than expanding the project.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So, how's the photo labeling going?

dialogue.speaker: Tessa
dialogue.text: Slowly. I'm getting this scanned family photograph ready to share with the relatives, but I don't know where it was taken.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Let me make us both some peppermint tea, and then I'll have a look.

dialogue.speaker: Tessa
dialogue.text: Thanks. Here's the scan on my phone. The green case makes it easy to find in my bag, at least.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, I recognize that carousel. It's the one in Spokane's Riverfront Park.

dialogue.speaker: Tessa
dialogue.text: Really? I thought it might be, but I didn't want to label it based on a horse and a hunch.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'm pretty sure. That's the Riverfront Park carousel.

dialogue.speaker: Tessa
dialogue.text: Actually, wait. I don't need to guess the year to make the caption useful, do I?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: No, just say it's the carousel in Spokane's Riverfront Park. You can leave the date out.

dialogue.speaker: Tessa
dialogue.text: Perfect. A location is a lot better than 'people near a horse.'

key_facts: Tessa is preparing to share a scanned family photograph with relatives.
Riley identifies the carousel as the one in Spokane's Riverfront Park.
minor_details: Tessa shows Riley the scan on her phone, which has a green case.
Riley makes them both peppermint tea.

summary: Riley discussed progress on photo labeling with Tessa. They reviewed a scanned family photo and identified the Spokane Riverfront Park carousel as the location. Riley confirmed the location, and they decided not to include the year in the caption. Tessa considered the usefulness of a caption versus guessing details, and Riley advised that a location caption suffices. Action: finalize a caption stating 'the carousel in Spokane's Riverfront Park' without a date.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How do things stand with the library walk?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: It's on the calendar. The trial is Saturday, April 11.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. Is that the date you're circling in purple ink?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. I wanted it to stand out from everything else on this page.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Here, I'll clear this stack of mail from the counter so you have room.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Thanks. The mail was making a pretty convincing case for its own program.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So how many people can sign up?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Registration is capped at 8 participants. I think I can keep track of a group that size without rushing everyone.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds manageable, especially with the stops and questions in the 30-minute slot.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but I also want people to have a way to ask questions before they register.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: About the route itself?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. The sign-up notice gives a library contact for questions about the route.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Could you give examples? Like the distance or whether there's somewhere to sit?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I could. The guide already says it's about 0.3 miles and there isn't a public bench on that stretch, but people might want to know more.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And they shouldn't have to explain why they're asking.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Exactly. I don't want the notice to sound like we need someone's medical information to answer a question.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe just say, 'Contact the library with questions about the route.' Then list a couple of examples.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I like that. Conditions and seating, maybe. No 'tell us about your needs' form disguised as an invitation.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. They can ask what they need to know, and you can describe what you've checked.

key_facts: The trial is scheduled for Saturday, April 11.
Registration is capped at eight participants.
The sign-up notice gives a library contact for questions about the route.
minor_details: Maya circles the date in purple ink.
Riley clears a stack of mail from the counter.

summary: Riley and Maya discussed the library walk: the trial is scheduled for Saturday, April 11, with 8 participants maximum in a 30-minute slot. They agreed to clarify the sign-up notice by allowing general questions about the route (e.g., distance, seating) and to state, 'Contact the library with questions about the route.' They decided not to request medical information and to prepare example questions for sign-ups.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, how are things standing with the Astoria hotel search?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Actually, I finally booked it. I reserved a room at Hotel Elliott.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! What made you decide?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I found a rate I was comfortable with, and it's within walking distance of downtown. I kept going back and forth with the Norblad Hotel, but I was getting a little tired of comparing rooms.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A little tired?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: All right, very tired. I think I had compared the same rooms enough times to qualify for a certificate.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you got a private room?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah, a private room for Owen and me. The reservation is refundable until May 15, which makes me feel better about booking it now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's good. Is breakfast included?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No, breakfast isn't included in the rate. I checked that part a couple of times because it wasn't immediately obvious to me.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair enough. Was there anything else you had to figure out?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: The booking page asked for an estimated arrival time, and I had to stop and think about that for a minute. We're still looking at the train and bus connection, so it's an estimate in the loosest sense.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: At least the room's sorted. Did you save the confirmation somewhere?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I did. It's in a folder labeled 'coast.' Now I can stop opening hotel tabs, in theory.

details_in_summary: She saves the confirmation in a folder labeled 'coast.'
The booking page asks for an estimated arrival time.
key_facts: Hannah reserves a room at Hotel Elliott.
The reservation is refundable until May 15.
Breakfast is not included in the rate.
minor_details: She saves the confirmation in a folder labeled 'coast.'
The booking page asks for an estimated arrival time.

summary: Riley’s partner Hannah booked Hotel Elliott for the Astoria search, selecting a refundable private room for Owen and herself. She prioritized the rate and walkable location over the Norblad option; breakfast is not included. The arrival time remains an estimate due to transit concerns. Confirmation was saved in the 'coast' folder, and Riley can stop refreshing hotel tabs for now.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Morning. It's still pretty dim out there, isn't it?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I thought it was earlier when I got up.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I've been looking at the permission form for that neighborhood display I told you about.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is that the draft on the pale green paper?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yep. I printed it on pale green paper because it was in the printer. Very official.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What are you asking people to agree to?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: So far, it asks if they're comfortable being recorded for the project.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay, but agreeing to be recorded isn't necessarily the same as agreeing to have their words in a public display.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Right. The draft separates permission to record from permission to use an excerpt in the display. I don't think I've made that distinction clear enough, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Can I see the sentence?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: This one here. I'm circling it with my blue pen so I remember to rewrite it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, 'take part in the project' is a little vague. Someone could read that either way.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but if I make the questions separate, I should say what happens if they say yes to one and no to the other.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You could just say they can choose whether an excerpt goes on display, even if they're okay with you recording them.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That sounds clearer. And contributors can choose whether their names appear beside their words.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Could they see which words you've picked before you put them up?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yes. I plan to let contributors review their selected excerpts before publication.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. Something might sound different to them once it's pulled out of the conversation.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Exactly. I want them to know what they're saying yes to, not just sign a mysterious green sheet.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The green sheet has a lot of work to do.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: It does. I'll try to give it fewer mysteries.

details_in_summary: The draft is printed on pale green paper.
key_facts: The draft separates permission to record from permission to use an excerpt in the display.
Contributors can choose whether their names appear beside their words.
Maya plans to let contributors review their selected excerpts before publication.
minor_details: The draft is printed on pale green paper.
Maya circles a sentence with a blue pen.

summary: Riley and Maya discussed the neighborhood display permission form on pale green paper. They clarified that consent to be recorded is separate from consent to use an excerpt in the display, and agreed the wording should reflect this. They plan to separate questions, specify outcomes if yes/no, and allow contributors to choose display inclusion and name display. They also intend for contributors to review selected excerpts before publication to avoid misunderstandings. Action: rewrite the form to reduce ambiguity and provide previews.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You're still working on that notebook after the meeting?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Yeah. I ruled a comparison chart in this small spiral notebook. Trying to figure out what I actually need in an apartment.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, are you moving?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: I am. Darius plans to live alone when our Fremont lease ends on May 31, so I'm looking for a place of my own.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Got it. Have you started looking at listings?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: A little. I'm making the requirements list before I schedule any viewings, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What have you got so far?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: A 1-bedroom apartment, for one. And $1,900 a month is my ceiling for rent.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds like a pretty clear starting point.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Yeah, although the bus matters too. I want to stay near a reliable bus route.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So not just near a bus stop, but one with service you can count on.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Exactly. A stop doesn't do me much good if the bus barely comes.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What are the columns in your chart?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Rent, bus route, location. Then I left a little space for notes, because I know I'll think of something else.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You're more organized than I would be.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Well, I borrowed a pen from the office reception desk to make it. So the operation is not entirely self-sufficient.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A promising start anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Fair enough. I'm trying not to get attached to a place just because it looks good in a picture.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, having the list should help you compare them.

key_facts: Darius plans to live alone when their Fremont lease ends on May 31.
Jamal wants a one-bedroom apartment.
His rent ceiling is $1,900 a month.
He wants to stay near a reliable bus route.
minor_details: He has ruled a comparison chart in a small spiral notebook.
He borrowed a pen from the office reception desk.

summary: Riley and Jamal discussed Jamal moving after the Fremont lease ends May 31. Jamal is seeking a 1-bedroom apartment with a rent cap of $1,900 and a reliable bus route. He is compiling a requirements chart (rent, bus route, location) and has started browsing listings, planning to schedule viewings after finalizing criteria. Riley encouraged using the list to compare options and cautioned against getting attached to pictures.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, how are things looking with the shopfront photos?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Pretty good, with a small asterisk. I brought my first prints to the office. The group had a critique last night.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. Are they in that envelope?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. They rode to work in a reused cardboard envelope. The blue ink stain on 1 corner was already there, for the record.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I wasn't going to blame you. How many did you print?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: 6 photographs, at 5 by 7 inches. Small enough to spread out and compare without taking over a whole table.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And what did the group think?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: They said the darkest prints hid too much detail inside the windows. Which, once they pointed it out, was hard to unsee.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is that the same problem as the bright signs losing detail, or sort of the opposite?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Sort of the opposite. The signs were too bright in those frames; here the dark window areas aren't showing enough.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did anyone have a suggestion for fixing the prints?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, 1 member suggested making a lighter test print before ordering a full set. What if I start with the darkest one? Less expensive than discovering the same problem 6 times.

key_facts: Sam printed six photographs at 5 by 7 inches.
The group said the darkest prints hid too much detail inside the windows.
One member suggested making a lighter test print before ordering a full set.
minor_details: The prints rode to work in a reused cardboard envelope.
One corner of the envelope had a blue ink stain.

summary: Riley discussed shopfront photos with Sam. Sam reported a group critique of six 5x7 prints, noting darkest frames hid window detail while bright signs overexposed. They identified a tonal balance issue in opposing areas. A proposed fix: start with a lighter test print of the darkest image before ordering a full set, to reduce costs if the problem persists.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. Nearly made it to the end of Friday.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey. Yeah, the afternoon's dragging a little.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I looked at the Neighborhood Frames schedule and bought my tickets.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. Which ones did you pick?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The Long Way Home and Low Tide Market. I'm passing on A Place for Rain.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How did the timing work out?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The Long Way Home is Saturday evening, and Low Tide Market is a Sunday matinee, March 14 and 15 at the Beacon Hill Screening Room.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a good gap. You won't be spending the whole weekend there.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Exactly. And they were $12 each, so not too bad.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did the tickets come through okay?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: They did, eventually—or, well, they were there all along. I nearly missed the confirmation email because it landed in my promotions folder.

details_in_summary: The tickets cost $12 each.
Sam nearly missed the confirmation email because it landed in a promotions folder.
key_facts: Sam bought tickets for The Long Way Home and Low Tide Market, passing on A Place for Rain.
The first screening is on Saturday evening and the second is a Sunday matinee.
minor_details: The tickets cost $12 each.
Sam nearly missed the confirmation email because it landed in a promotions folder.

summary: Sam bought Neighborhood Frames tickets: The Long Way Home (Sat evening) and Low Tide Market (Sun matinee) for March 14–15 at the Beacon Hill Screening Room, and is skipping A Place for Rain. Tickets were $12 each; confirmation nearly landed in promotions. Riley noted the Friday afternoon drag but no further actions were identified.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. Long week? The elevator seems to think it's Friday too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, Sam. Yeah, I'm pretty ready for the weekend.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Same here. Oh, about that little game group we talked about with Inez.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'd still be up for it.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Good. How does March 21 look for you?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: March 21? That's a Saturday, right? Yeah, I'm free.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Great. Inez is free too. We could use the building's shared lounge, if that works for you.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sure. What time were you thinking?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Maybe 7? Nothing too ambitious.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: 7 works. The lounge table is usually wiped down by evening, at least.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: A clean table. We're already off to a luxurious start.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Do we know what we're playing?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Inez will bring Sushi Go! It's short, so we can try a game without committing to a long evening.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Perfect. That sounds like a good way to start.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Let me write that down on the back of this grocery receipt before I forget.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Go for it. There's enough room after the groceries?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Just about. March 21, 7, shared lounge. The receipt has a second career.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. See you and Inez then.

details_in_summary: Sam writes the plan on the back of a grocery receipt.
key_facts: The first session is planned for March 21 in the building's shared lounge.
Inez will bring Sushi Go!
minor_details: Sam writes the plan on the back of a grocery receipt.
Riley mentions that the lounge table is usually wiped down by evening.

summary: Riley discussed a casual game night with Sam and Inez for March 21 at 7 in the building's shared lounge. Inez will bring Sushi Go!. Sam planned to note the details on a grocery receipt as a reminder. Riley confirmed availability and the lounge is typically cleaned in the evening. Action items: confirm attendees and finalize logistics (time, location, game).

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So, how do things stand with the Fremont apartment?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, I got approved. And I signed the lease on March 4.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You signed it? Daniel, that's huge.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. It's still a little strange to say it out loud.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: After all that waiting, you have a place.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I do. The new lease begins April 1, 2026.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. And was the deposit what you expected?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: The security deposit is $1,200. I kept checking the number like it might change if I stared at it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Very effective negotiating strategy.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, that's what they taught us in that first-year elective, right?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Definitely. Where were you when you signed everything?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: At my kitchen table. Just me and a pile of documents on a screen.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you read every single word.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Almost. The property manager sent a copy of the building rules as a separate PDF, so naturally I spent a while comparing it to the lease.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Of course you did. Does it feel like a relief now?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: It really does. I was trying not to get attached after the second visit, but I did like how quiet it was inside.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And now you don't have to keep looking at listings.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Right. Now I get to look at all the stuff I have to pack instead.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: One problem at a time. You could start with the things you don't use much.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, that sounds manageable. I'm going to enjoy not comparing apartments for at least tonight, though.

details_in_summary: He signed the documents at his kitchen table.
The property manager sent a copy of the building rules as a separate PDF.
key_facts: Daniel signed the new lease on March 4.
The lease begins April 1, 2026.
The security deposit is $1,200.
minor_details: He signed the documents at his kitchen table.
The property manager sent a copy of the building rules as a separate PDF.

summary: Riley and Daniel discussed the Fremont apartment: Daniel's lease was approved and signed on March 4, with the new lease starting April 1, 2026. Security deposit is $1,200. Daniel reviewed the building rules PDF against the lease at his kitchen table. He feels relief and will now focus on packing, starting with items not used often; no longer needs to browse listings tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Oh, for goodness' sake. The wheel on my folding shopping cart just came loose, right here in the lobby.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh no. Did something fall off it?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The little washer did. I saw it roll toward the bench, I think. My cart's apparently trying to take the morning off.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll look under the bench. Oh, there it is. Here's the washer.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Thank you. Let me get the wheel back on. The empty canvas tote in the cart isn't much help holding it steady.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I can hold the cart while you put it back together.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That'd be great, if that works for you. There, the washer's on and the wheel's back in place.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. Does it feel secure?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, it's holding. I'll head out for groceries now. Just onions and oats, so nothing too exciting.

details_in_summary: Sam plans to buy onions and oats.
key_facts: Sam's folding shopping cart has a loose wheel in the apartment lobby.
Riley finds the small washer under a bench, and Sam reattaches the wheel before going grocery shopping.
minor_details: Sam has an empty canvas tote in the cart.
Sam plans to buy onions and oats.

summary: Riley and Sam discussed a loose washer on a folding shopping cart. The washer rolled under a bench; Riley retrieved it while Sam reattached the wheel with Riley holding the cart steady. The wheel is now secure and Sam plans to continue to groceries (onions and oats). No further actions required beyond ensuring the cart remains stable.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Hi, Riley. How's your Saturday evening going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey! Pretty quiet, actually. How's yours?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Quiet here too. I did finally test the flatbed scanner with one of the photographs, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. How did it go?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Well, I wiped the scanner glass with a microfiber cloth first, which felt like a promising start. The test scan is at 600 dpi.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Can you send it to me? I'll have a look.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes, hang on. There, I've sent it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Got it. The detail looks good. Oh, wait, the scanner's automatic crop cut off part of the border.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Oh, you're right. The print has a scalloped edge, and it seems to have decided that bit wasn't worth keeping.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'd rather have the whole edge in there. Could you crop it manually?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I can. I'll crop manually instead. Automatic is convenient in theory.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What format did you save the test in?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: TIFF. It's a pretty big file, though, so I was wondering about JPEG instead.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What if we keep TIFF files as masters and make JPEG copies for sharing? Then we've got the detail but don't have to send huge files around.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That makes sense. TIFF masters, JPEG copies for sharing. And I'll turn off that crop.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Perfect. Thanks for testing it before tackling the 30.

details_in_summary: The test print has a scalloped edge.
key_facts: The test scan is made at 600 dpi.
They decide to keep TIFF files as masters and make JPEG copies for sharing.
Riley notices that the scanner's automatic crop cuts off part of a border, so Hannah will crop manually.

They agreed to turn off automatic cropping and maintain TIFF masters while sharing JPEG versions. Action items: crop manually, disable automatic crop, maintain TIFF masters, generate JPEGs for sharing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How are things standing with the photos after your call with Lian?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Better. She recognized the picnic photo we couldn't place.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, where was it?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Green Lake. And she said I was about 6.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Huh. I wouldn't have guessed Green Lake.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Me neither. Okay, but now we can stop calling it the mysterious picnic.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm making a note in pencil: Green Lake, Maya about 6.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Thanks. That'll be much more useful than 'somewhere with grass.'

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did Lian recognize the others?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Not all of them. I'm putting the unidentified prints in a separate envelope for another call with her.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is that the envelope with the old grocery list on the back?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. It's still an envelope, even if it used to have a career in groceries.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair enough. I'll leave those separate from the ones we can identify.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Perfect. That's enough photo sorting for a Monday morning.

details_in_summary: The envelope has an old grocery list on its back.
key_facts: Lian identifies a picnic photograph as having been taken at Green Lake.
Lian says Maya was about six in the picnic photograph.
Maya puts the unidentified prints in a separate envelope for another call.
minor_details: The envelope has an old grocery list on its back.
Riley uses a pencil to make a note.

summary: Riley and Maya updated Lian on photo sorting. Lian recognized the picnic photo as being Green Lake, with Maya estimated at about 6. They will stop calling it the 'mysterious picnic' and note: Green Lake, Maya about 6. Unidentified prints will go into a separate envelope for a follow-up with Lian; the old grocery list envelope remains distinct from identified items. Plan to revisit the unidentified set on another call; Monday morning photo sorting concluded.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Hi, Riley. How's your lunch going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey! Good, just taking a little break. How's yours?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Pretty good. I thought I'd give you the holds shelf update while I've got a minute.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, yeah. How's the tally looking?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: From March 1 through March 7, staff recorded 3 requests for help finding holds.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a little down from the 4 you had in that February week.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It is. And we made a small clarification to the shelf: I added an arrow showing which way to read within each row, from left to right.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What made you think of that?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Marisol suggested it after she saw a patron start at the right end. We'd labeled the ranges, but, well, the direction wasn't quite as obvious as I thought.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Makes sense. What did you make the arrow out of?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yellow paper. I nearly stuck it on upside down, which would've been a very helpful clarification, in theory.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Glad you caught it. Are you ready to call the layout finished?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Not quite. I want to finish tracking through the end of March before we decide whether it should stay.

details_in_summary: The arrow was cut from yellow paper.
key_facts: Staff recorded three requests for help from March 1 through March 7.
Hannah added an arrow showing the reading direction within each row.
Marisol suggested the arrow after seeing a patron start at the right end.

Riley asked if the layout is ready, and Hannah said she wants to track through the end of March before deciding whether the layout should stay as is.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Oh, nice, it's still available.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What is?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: A cottage in Port Angeles. Okay, so, I was looking for somewhere for our 2 nights away.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. What weekend?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: May 22–24. Friday through Sunday. Does that work for you?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, let's do May 22–24. I could use a couple of quiet days.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Same. And the cottage has 2 separate beds, which seemed worth checking before I got attached to it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Very considerate. How much is it?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: $318 for the stay. That’s the total on the booking page.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds reasonable. Do you like the look of it?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I do. The listing photos include a yellow kettle, which is apparently enough to persuade me I'm a cottage person.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You've compared every kettle on the peninsula, haven't you?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Not yet. I could lose an entire evening to that, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Let's spare you. Go ahead and book it.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay. May 22–24, 2 separate beds, $318. And... booked.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. One actual decision made.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I'm relieved. We can still keep the weekend easy, just like we said, without turning it into a big hiking expedition.

details_in_summary: The cottage costs $318 for the stay.

Daniel books a cottage in Port Angeles.
The cottage has two separate beds.

The listing photos include a yellow kettle.

summary: Riley discussed finding a cottage in Port Angeles for a 2-night weekend (May 22–24) with Daniel. They confirmed dates, 2 separate beds, and a total price of $318. Daniel agreed to book, and the booking was completed. The plan remains a quiet, easy weekend without a hiking-focused agenda.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Riley, can we look at the staged shipment dashboard? I want to check the wording.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sure. It's loading... still loading.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: There it is. That took 2 refreshes to load.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A promising start. Okay, the summary has the label we discussed.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Yes, 'Shipments with delivery scans received after expected delivery time.' That matches the receipt timestamp the count uses.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the explanation still says the count doesn't establish whether the shipment itself arrived late.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Right. But look at the tooltip. On the March 10 staging page, it still says 'Delivered late.'

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, you're right. That makes it sound like we know the shipment was late.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Exactly. We know when the scan record was received, not necessarily when the shipment arrived.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll replace the tooltip text so it describes when the scan record was received.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Good. Something like 'Delivery scan received after expected delivery time' would be more precise.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that keeps it consistent with the summary. I'll use that.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: I'll make a note in the margin with my black pen: tooltip still says 'Delivered late.'

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Thanks for catching it. The long label doesn't help much if the tooltip contradicts it.

key_facts: On March 10, the staged tooltip still says “Delivered late.”
Riley will replace that tooltip text so it describes when the scan record was received.
minor_details: The staging page takes two refreshes to load.
Wei makes a note in the margin with a black pen.

summary: Riley and Wei reviewed the staged shipment dashboard wording. They confirmed the summary label and noted the explanation about late shipments does not imply actual arrival lateness. They identified a misleading tooltip on the March 10 page that said 'Delivered late.' and agreed to replace it with 'Delivery scan received after expected delivery time' for consistency. Action: update tooltip text and annotate the margin note to resolve contradictions.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, how are things standing with the warehouse terms?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Pretty well. Elena has scheduled a moderated session with warehouse staff for March 16. I've put the proposed terms into the screen mockups. Could you review the test setup?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. Are those the mockups I prepared, the picking list and the staging confirmation screen?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Those are the ones. I've used 'pick' on the list and 'stage' on the confirmation. Still proposals, obviously, not commandments.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. What are we asking people to do?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I wrote tasks that ask participants to describe what they would do next. What if we show them each screen without a glossary beside them and see whether they can follow the actions?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that feels closer to how they'd actually encounter the words. Can I see the tasks?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Here. Sorry, the printer left a faint line down one page. It doesn't cover the text, at least.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I can read it. For the picking list, maybe don't say 'pick' in the task itself? Otherwise we're kind of handing them the label.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right. What if we describe the goal instead, and let them tell us what they'd do next?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That works. Same for staging, I think. Give them the situation, not the word we're checking.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Agreed. And we can watch where they hesitate, not just whether they eventually find the button.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Exactly. Oh, can I borrow your charging cable? My battery's nearly gone.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Sure, it's yours for now. I'll revise those task prompts this afternoon, then send them over.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Great. I'll take another look when they come through.

details_in_summary: Riley borrows Sam’s charging cable.
key_facts: Elena has scheduled a moderated session with warehouse staff for March 16.
Riley prepared mockups of a picking list and a staging confirmation screen.
Sam wrote tasks that ask participants to describe what they would do next.
minor_details: The printer leaves a faint line down one page.
Riley borrows Sam’s charging cable.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How's the album coming along? It's March 10 already.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: It's getting there. I have a rough page for the PDF, if you don't mind giving it a look over dinner.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Of course. Oh, that ticket's much clearer than I expected.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: That's one of the faded ones I scanned in January. I think the image is fine, but the layout feels a little crowded.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, the caption's almost touching the ticket. I'd leave a wide margin around the ticket images.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: A wide margin. Maybe that would make the stub feel less like it's being squeezed onto the page.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Exactly. You don't need to fill every bit of space.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: That is difficult advice for a person who makes transit maps.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I know. But this isn't a bus schedule.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: Fair. Oh, I ordered the mushroom noodles, by the way. I was distracted by the menu for a while.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good choice. Also, this table's right beside the fogged-up window. I can barely see outside.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: I think the page has the same problem: too much going on around the edges.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What if you put 1 ticket image on the left of each page and its caption on the right?

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: I like that. With the wide margin around the image, and just a short caption beside it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. For this one, you could keep the Bainbridge Island trip and 1994 together in the caption.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: Right, since Isabel confirmed that date. Let's do it that way: 1 ticket on the left, caption on the right. Simple is probably better.

key_facts: Victor and Riley meet for dinner on March 10.
They decide to put one ticket image on the left of each page and its caption on the right.
Riley suggests leaving a wide margin around the ticket images.

Their table is beside a fogged-up window.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: I booked my first apartment viewing. It's March 14, in Green Lake.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. How does it look?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Good in the photos. Which is, you know, what photos are supposed to do. I'm trying not to make up my mind from those.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What's the rent?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: It's advertised at $1,850 a month, so it's under the $1,900 ceiling. Not by a whole lot, but still.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And it's a one-bedroom?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Yeah. One listing photo has this yellow kettle on the stove, and somehow that's what I keep remembering.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The kettle really sold you on it?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Apparently I can be bought with a kettle. Though I assume it doesn't come with the place.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So what do you want to check in person?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: The size, for one. I'm bringing a tape measure, because the photos make it hard to tell what would actually fit.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, those wide-angle shots can make a room look twice as big.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Exactly. And I want to look at the bus options nearby. A nice apartment's less nice if getting to work is a puzzle every morning.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair enough. You'll get a better sense of it on Saturday.

details_in_summary: Jamal plans to bring a tape measure.
key_facts: The viewing is scheduled for March 14.
The apartment is in Green Lake.
The advertised rent is $1,850 a month.
minor_details: One listing photo shows a yellow kettle on the stove.
Jamal plans to bring a tape measure.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, how are things standing with the kitchen update?

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Better. Marisol and I finally picked a counter: pale gray laminate.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. Are you relieved to be done looking at samples?

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Very. I was starting to think comparing laminate was my new job.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What made that one win?

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: We liked how it looked in the kitchen. I carried one sample home from Finch Hardware in a paper bag, and we compared it with the others under the kitchen light after dinner.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A proper evening of research.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Yeah. Marisol made lentil soup that evening, so at least the research was well catered.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you both agree right away?

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: On the pale gray, yes. Or, well, once we'd looked at everything under that light, we did.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And laminate helps with the budget, I assume?

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: That's the idea. We're still trying to keep the whole thing under $3,500.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Have you got a start date now?

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: We do. Darlene Price is scheduled to start the work on April 8.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's not too far off. Still just the sink cabinet and counter?

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Yep. The other cabinets are staying. They're not invited to the renovation.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Well, I'm glad you can stop bringing samples home.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Me too. The paper bag has served its country.

details_in_summary: He compared samples under the kitchen light after dinner.
Marisol made lentil soup that evening.
key_facts: Theo and Marisol chose a pale gray laminate countertop.
Darlene Price is scheduled to start the work on April 8.
minor_details: Theo carried one sample home in a paper bag from Finch Hardware.

Marisol made lentil soup that evening.

Darlene Price is scheduled to start work on April 8, focusing on the sink cabinet and countertop; other cabinets will stay. Riley notes the ongoing sample process has ended, with the paper bag now retired as a prop.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Hey. How's your evening going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey. Pretty good. I'm glad to be home.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Me too. Did you see the offer from Canal-side Community Garden?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, we got bed 7 through the end of the growing season.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I was checking that it was for the whole season and not just spring. That's nice.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I printed the rules on the back of an old receipt sheet. It's a little cramped.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but it works. I circled one paragraph in blue ink—the one about shared garden work.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, yeah. Each household is expected to contribute 4 hours of shared garden work.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Right. Do you read that as 4 hours for the 2 of us together?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I do. It says per household, not per person.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Good. A rare unit of measurement that includes both of us.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The other thing I noticed is they prohibit synthetic pesticides.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, that's clear. No synthetic pesticides.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll keep the rules somewhere we can find them, even if they do look like a receipt.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Thanks. I'm glad we applied for the bed.

details_in_summary: Riley printed the rules on the back of an old receipt sheet.

Each household is expected to contribute four hours of shared garden work.
The garden prohibits synthetic pesticides.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. Okay, so, how's your evening going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty good. Glad Wednesday's nearly over. How about you?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Better now. The ferry piece cleared its final review.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! What did Louise think?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Louise Park approved the revised mix after a second gallery listen. The voices held up much better against the room noise.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Even the low voice the fan was masking?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. The speech adjustments helped, and pulling back the ambience under the quietest words made a difference too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's such a relief. Did it end up close to your target length?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: 3 minutes and 34 seconds. Four seconds over, which I have decided not to spend the rest of my life debating.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's growth. How'd you celebrate?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I ate a pear from the bottom of my bag. Very glamorous, but honestly, it was a good pear.

key_facts: Louise approved the revised mix after a second gallery listen.
The approved track runs three minutes and thirty-four seconds.
minor_details: Daniel celebrated with a pear from the bottom of his bag.

summary: Riley discussed the ferry piece final review and approval by Louise Park after a second gallery listen. They noted the revised mix improved voice clarity against room noise, with speech adjustments and reduced ambience helping low voices. The piece runs 3 minutes 34 seconds, four seconds over target, a point Riley planned not to dwell on. No further changes were mandated, and Riley marked the moment with a simple pear celebration.

dialogue.speaker: Walter
dialogue.text: I'm sitting here by the kitchen table, and I just remembered I never told you the rest about Mount Spokane.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, from your ski trip with Edith on March 1? You mentioned it Sunday.

dialogue.speaker: Walter
dialogue.text: Yeah. We did get out there, but we completed a shorter loop than we'd planned.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did it still feel like a good outing?

dialogue.speaker: Walter
dialogue.text: It did. And we were both glad we'd brought a thermos. It was nice to stop and have something warm.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's the part I would've remembered too.

dialogue.speaker: Walter
dialogue.text: Well, that and the cinnamon roll I had on the way home. Can't let all that skiing go to waste.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Obviously. Did your boots dry out all right?

dialogue.speaker: Walter
dialogue.text: Yeah, I left them to dry by the back door. They're fine now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. Sounds like a pretty nice day, even with the shorter loop.

details_in_summary: Walter had a cinnamon roll on the way home.
He left his boots to dry by the back door.
key_facts: They completed a shorter loop than they had planned.
They were glad they brought a thermos.
minor_details: Walter had a cinnamon roll on the way home.
He left his boots to dry by the back door.

They completed a shorter loop than planned but still found the outing enjoyable, mentioning a warm thermos and a cinnamon roll on the way home. Boots were drying by the back door afterward, and the overall day was considered pretty nice despite the shorter loop.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm sitting at the kitchen table looking at what's left of my first loaf.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How did it turn out?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Flat, and gummy in the middle. Yours has that nice open texture, and mine is more like a very determined doorstop.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, no. Was any of it edible?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I toasted a slice and had it with sharp cheddar. That was actually pretty good. It did stick to the cooling rack briefly, though, which felt like a review.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Do you remember what you did with the starter before you mixed the dough?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I took it straight from the refrigerator and mixed it in. You said I could keep it in there between baking weeks, so I thought, well, it's ready.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Ah, I should've been clearer. Feed the starter first, then wait for it to rise before you mix the dough.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Right. That first feeding, it doubled in about 7 hours. I suppose it needed a chance to do that again.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. Look for it to get nice and risen rather than going strictly by the clock.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm trying to work out when to feed it around work. I could do it in the evening, in theory, but then I might be waiting up for it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You could feed it in the morning on a day you're home and keep an eye on it. Same equal weights of starter, water and flour.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That makes sense. I'll try that before the next loaf, rather than asking cold starter to do all the work immediately.

key_facts: Hannah's first loaf was flat and gummy in the middle.
She mixed the dough using starter straight from the refrigerator.
Riley suggests feeding the starter and waiting for it to rise before mixing.
minor_details: Hannah ate a toasted slice with sharp cheddar.
The loaf stuck briefly to the cooling rack.

summary: Riley and Hannah discussed bread outcomes: Hannah’s loaf was flat and gummy; Riley’s had an open crumb. They reviewed starter handling: Hannah fed directly from the fridge and mixed, but the starter should be fed first and allowed to rise before mixing dough. Decision: feed starter, wait for a proper rise, not rely on clock time. Action items: Hannah will feed in the morning on days off and monitor until risen; Riley will emphasize proper feeding order for next bake.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I tried a lamp at the home desk. The lighting's a lot better now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. Was that the next thing after the monitor riser?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. I found a used clip-on lamp for $12. The shade's slightly scuffed, but it works.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. What kind of bulb did you put in it?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: A warm LED bulb. I first tested it while I was reviewing a printed document.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Could you see the page without it hitting the screen?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Not at first. Well, I could see the page, but I had to adjust the lamp to keep the light off the screen.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Where did you end up putting it?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Clipping it to the left edge of the table kept glare off the screen. My notes are lit without the monitor turning into a mirror.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty good result for $12.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. The scuffed shade gives it character. Or it just gives it a scuff.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Either way, sounds more useful than a perfectly unscuffed lamp shining straight at your monitor.

details_in_summary: The lamp has a slightly scuffed shade.
Sam first tested it while reviewing a printed document.
key_facts: Sam found a used clip-on lamp for $12.
Sam fitted the lamp with a warm LED bulb.
Clipping the lamp to the left edge of the table kept glare off the screen.
minor_details: The lamp has a slightly scuffed shade.
Sam first tested it while reviewing a printed document.

summary: Riley and Sam improved desk lighting with a used clip-on lamp for $12, using a warm LED. Sam tested it with a printed document and positioned the lamp on the left edge to avoid glare, keeping notes lit without screen reflections. The scuffed shade was noted, and the setup was deemed more useful than a perfectly unscuffed lamp shining at the monitor.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: The album looked mostly fine, but the captions were getting clipped at the edge of the screen.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, on your phone?

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: Yeah. I tested it on my phone today, March 13, and the right side of some captions just disappeared.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Was it the layout we talked about at dinner?

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: Same layout, ticket on the left, caption on the right. I think I'd let the text run too close to the edge.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Were you able to fix it without shrinking the tickets?

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: I was, yeah. I adjusted the captions and checked them again. They're not clipped anymore, and there's still that wide margin around the images.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. Sounds like it's ready, then.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: I think so. It's ready to send. I'm trying not to find another tiny thing to change.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A dangerous moment for a designer. Are you at the office?

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: No, I'm waiting for a bus. I figured I'd give you the quick update while I had a minute.

key_facts: On March 13, Victor tested the album on his phone.
He fixed captions that were being clipped at the edge of the screen.
minor_details: Victor is waiting for a bus when they talk.

summary: Riley discussed a caption clipping issue on the album when viewed on a phone. Victor tested on March 13, found right-side captions disappearing, and adjusted the captions to avoid clipping without shrinking ticket margins. He confirmed there remains a wide image margin. Victor said the project is ready to send and is avoiding further tweaks for now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How are things standing with the Victoria trip?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Much less like a spreadsheet, finally. The sailing schedule is out, and I booked a round trip on the Victoria Clipper.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice! So you're done comparing routes?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yes. No more mentally dragging myself through Port Angeles. The direct ferry from Seattle worked for the dates.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is there still room for a leisurely first day?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I think so. The northbound sailing is in the morning, so I won't be getting in at the very end of the day.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you're not trying to pack the afternoon with things?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: No. I'd rather keep it loose and have some unhurried time with Ada. I can settle into the suite, too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What about the trip back?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The return sailing is in the afternoon on Monday, May 18. The outbound is Friday, May 15.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds like a good amount of breathing room on both ends.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That's the hope. I selected an aisle seat, too. I like being able to get up without negotiating with a stranger.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A very reasonable travel luxury.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Well, the booking page offered me a luggage upgrade. I declined that one.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you get a confirmation you can actually find later?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I did. I saved the confirmation as a PDF. A rare victory for future me.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And with the suite booked, you can stop looking at travel pages for a bit.

details_in_summary: Sam saved the confirmation as a PDF.
The booking page offered a luggage upgrade Sam declined.
key_facts: Sam booked a round trip on the Victoria Clipper.
The northbound sailing is in the morning and the return sailing is in the afternoon.
Sam selected an aisle seat.
minor_details: Sam saved the confirmation as a PDF.
The booking page offered a luggage upgrade Sam declined.

Sam chose an aisle seat, declined a luggage upgrade, and saved the PDF confirmation. Riley noted keeping a relaxed first day to spend time with Ada and avoid further travel-page digging.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How are things looking with the hatchery project?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, Nikhil Sethi and I are scheduled to go to Willow Bend Salmon Hatchery on March 18 to record. First visit.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. Do you know what you want to get while you're there?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: We're planning to cover the water channels and the machinery. I want the working site in there, just not the full factory tour.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. Is that a lot of equipment to haul out there?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: It could be, if I let myself bring every microphone I own. I'm trying to choose a few instead of holding a microphone convention.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How's the choosing going?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Slowly. I have, however, labeled the cable bag with yellow tape, so that's one decisive act.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Look at you. Anything else you need for the site?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: They ask visitors to wear closed-toe shoes. That choice, at least, I can make.

details_in_summary: Daniel has labeled the cable bag with yellow tape.
The site asks visitors to wear closed-toe shoes.
key_facts: Daniel and sound technician Nikhil Sethi are scheduled to record at the hatchery on March 18.
Their recording plan covers both water channels and machinery.
minor_details: Daniel has labeled the cable bag with yellow tape.
The site asks visitors to wear closed-toe shoes.

summary: Riley discussed the hatchery project with Daniel Reyes. They plan a March 18 visit to Willow Bend Salmon Hatchery with Nikhil Sethi to record water channels and machinery, focusing on the working site rather than a full factory tour. Decisions included selecting a limited set of microphones and labeling the cable bag with yellow tape. dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Oh, really? The east corner gets more light?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, quite a bit more than the rest of the balcony. I was watching it this morning.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I checked too, while I was holding a mug of tea. It looked like the sun was coming in around 8:30.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's what I saw. And the direct sun was pretty much gone by 11:30.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but was there still light in the east corner after that, just not direct sun?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, it stayed brighter than the rest for a while. I wouldn't count on full-day sun, though.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: No, 3 hours is a little short of a full day. The balcony is doing its best.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So the east corner might be the place for those cooking herbs we talked about.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I think so. Close enough to the kitchen that we can snip some while we're making dinner, too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And still separate from the community garden bed. Let's keep that corner in mind when we choose the pots.

key_facts: The balcony gets direct sun roughly from 8:30 to 11:30 in the morning.
The east corner receives more light than the rest of the balcony.
minor_details: Maya checked the light while holding a mug of tea.

summary: Riley discussed the balcony’s east corner receiving more light, with direct sun from ~8:30 to ~11:30 and remaining brighter afterward. Conclusion: east corner is suitable for cooking herbs, close to the kitchen for snipping, and kept separate from the community garden bed. Action item: consider this corner when choosing pots for planting.

dialogue.speaker: Beatrice
dialogue.text: Hello, Riley. Are you still awake, or have I caught you on your way to bed?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm still up. It's nice to hear your voice again.

dialogue.speaker: Beatrice
dialogue.text: I was thinking about what I told you this afternoon. Frances and I have signed up to walk the local half-marathon.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a big walk, Grandma. How did you find out about it?

dialogue.speaker: Beatrice
dialogue.text: I first saw it on a flyer at the library. I thought, well, Frances and I are already out walking, aren't we?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How far do you usually go together?

dialogue.speaker: Beatrice
dialogue.text: Our regular walks are 3 miles. I don't intend to go from that straight to a half-marathon and complain about it for a week.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. So you'll build up to it?

dialogue.speaker: Beatrice
dialogue.text: Yes, gradually. A little more distance at a time, and if it feels like too much, we'll adjust.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds sensible. I'm impressed you signed up.

dialogue.speaker: Beatrice
dialogue.text: Well, I've got the registration receipt tucked into a kitchen drawer, so I suppose it's official.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It certainly is. You'll have to keep me posted on how the walks are going.

details_in_summary: She tucked the registration receipt into a kitchen drawer.
key_facts: Beatrice signed up to walk the half-marathon with Frances.
Their regular walks are three miles long.
Beatrice wants to increase their distance gradually.
minor_details: She first saw the event on a flyer at the library.
She tucked the registration receipt into a kitchen drawer.
meta.storyline_title: Thirteen Miles at Her Own Pace

summary: Riley discussed Beatrice and Frances signing up for a local half-marathon after seeing a library flyer. Riley will be kept posted on their progress as training plans proceed.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: I gave Isabel the finished album this morning, March 15. She really enjoyed looking through it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good! Did she recognize all the tickets?

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: Most of them, I think. She spent extra time on the ticket from our family trip to Vashon Island.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What did she say about that one?

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: She mostly just looked at it for a while. Then she started talking about the trip. It was nice to see her take her time.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm so glad. Can I see the finished album?

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: Of course. I brought it up on my phone so I could show you this afternoon. Here, this is the Vashon Island page.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, that looks great. The wide margin really gives the ticket room.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: Yeah, and the caption's on the right, like we decided. I think keeping it simple was the right call.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And nothing's getting clipped now. Also, this cafe table is so wobbly. Sorry, I nearly tipped your tea.

dialogue.speaker: Victor
dialogue.text: The tea's safe, and so is the cinnamon roll. Maybe the table just wants a second opinion.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: My professional opinion is that it needs a napkin under one leg. The album, though, is finished.

details_in_summary: They meet at a cafe with a wobbly table.
key_facts: Victor gave Isabel the finished album on the morning of March 15.
Isabel spent extra time looking at a ticket from a family trip to Vashon Island.
Victor shows Riley the completed album that afternoon.
minor_details: They meet at a cafe with a wobbly table.
Victor has a cinnamon roll with his tea.

summary: Victor delivered the finished album to Isabel on March 15; she recognized most tickets, especially the Vashon Island trip. The Vashon page uses a wide margin and a right-side caption, with no content clipped. Riley will view the finished album this afternoon via Victor's phone. A small note about the wobbling cafe table was mentioned; overall, the album is finished and considered well-presented.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You're making a moving list already?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, I've booked a rental van for April 4. The booking starts at 9 a.m.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Look at you. Actual decisions.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I compared the van sizes for an embarrassing amount of time first. But yes.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you've given notice at your current place?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, I gave notice to my Capitol Hill landlord. That part's done.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. What do you need help with?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Would you be able to help me move my desk and bookcase? They're the 2 things I don't want to wrestle into the van alone.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, absolutely. I can help with both on April 4.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Thank you. I was thinking we could keep it straightforward, just us and the van. No big crew.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds good. Less coordinating, more carrying.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Exactly. I'm saving clean towels to wrap the fragile stuff, so I can pack that ahead.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good use for them. What's the lunch situation?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I'm planning to buy sandwiches for lunch. I figure we can stop when we're hungry instead of scheduling the sandwich down to the minute.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm proud of your restraint.

details_in_summary: The van booking starts at 9 a.m.
Daniel is saving clean towels to wrap fragile items.
He plans to buy sandwiches for lunch.
key_facts: Daniel has booked a rental van for April 4.
Riley agrees to help move his desk and bookcase.
Daniel has given notice to his Capitol Hill landlord.
minor_details: The van booking starts at 9 a.m.
Daniel is saving clean towels to wrap fragile items.
He plans to buy sandwiches for lunch.
