dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I've drafted the captions for the Tacoma photo display and asked Daphne to review them.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. Did you manage to keep them short?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I think so. I'm still aiming for no more than 40 words each, though a couple are right up against it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What did Daphne think?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: She suggested adding locations where they're known, which makes sense. She made her notes in green ink, so at least I can find them.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a considerate choice. Are the locations in the catalog?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Some are. I need to check them as I go rather than assume the caption I've drafted has everything.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did anything else come up?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: The date on the streetcar photograph. I was trying to make the caption sound tidy, and I nearly gave it a specific year.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nearly? You didn't have one?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No. I went back to the catalog, and it's listed only as the 1930s. So I'll use the decade rather than assign it a year.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, a tidy guess is still a guess.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. It's a photograph caption, not a test of my confidence.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you've still got the credit lines to fit in beside those 2 images, right?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Right. I read 1 caption aloud to check its rhythm, and it sounded a little crowded. In theory, 40 words isn't much.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Until you have to make every 1 of them earn its place.

details_in_summary: Daphne made her notes in green ink.
Hannah read one caption aloud to check its rhythm.
key_facts: Daphne suggested adding locations where they are known.
The date of a streetcar photograph is listed only as the 1930s.
Hannah will use that decade rather than assign the photograph a specific year.
minor_details: Daphne made her notes in green ink.
Hannah read one caption aloud to check its rhythm.

summary: Riley noted that Hannah drafted captions for the Tacoma photo display and sent them to Daphne for review. Daphne suggested including known locations; Hannah will verify catalog locations as she goes. For dating, Hannah will use the 1930s decade rather than a specific year. The two captions still need to fit with credit lines for two images. Riley emphasized rhythm by reading one caption aloud; final captions should be concise (about 40 words each) and earn their place.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, where do you want to put the pots we brought home?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: On the balcony floor, I think. Over near that brighter east corner.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: All 3 together?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, if they fit without blocking the way. We got 2 10-inch pots and 1 8-inch pot, so they're not enormous.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but did you still want to hang any of them from the railing?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: No, I looked at the railing-mounted planters and I'd rather not. The floor seems simpler.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Agreed. The railing doesn't need a new job.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And we can move the pots around on the floor if we need to.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Do all 3 have drainage holes?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yep, each pot has drainage holes, and each one has a saucer to catch runoff.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Good. I didn't want water running straight onto the balcony.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Or off the edge. The saucers were included, which was nice.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: How much did they come to altogether?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: $24 altogether.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Not bad. I like the dark green.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I chose that finish. It seemed nicer than the other options.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: It'll look good in the east corner. That's still the spot with the most light, right?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. We figured the balcony gets direct sun roughly from 8:30 to 11:30, and that corner gets more than the rest.

details_in_summary: The pots cost $24 altogether.
Riley chooses a dark green finish.
key_facts: They buy two 10-inch pots and one 8-inch pot.
Each pot has drainage holes and a saucer to catch runoff.
They decide against railing-mounted planters.
minor_details: The pots cost $24 altogether.

summary: Riley and Maya decided to place three pots on the balcony floor near the brighter east corner (two 10-inch and one 8-inch). The east corner receives the most light, roughly 8:30–11:30. Action: arrange/power-position pots without blocking the way and monitor light exposure.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It rose much better this time. I fed the starter first, then baked my second loaf on March 15.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good! Was it less gummy than the first one?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Much less. But I was still handling the dough close to midnight, which isn't really when I want to be doing that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that's a long evening. When did you feed the starter?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Not until later in the day. I kept thinking I had plenty of time, and then, well, the dough had its own opinion.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What if you moved the feeding earlier on the weekend? You'd have more of the day to wait for it to rise before mixing.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That might work. I could feed it in the morning instead of trying to fit everything into the afternoon. In theory, anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you could see how the timing goes before committing to staying up with it.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes. I found a patch of flour on my sleeve the next morning, so apparently I was done paying attention by the end.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: At least you got a better loaf out of it.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I did. Owen liked the crust, too. I'd just like the next one to involve a little less midnight dough handling.

key_facts: Hannah baked her second loaf on March 15 after feeding the starter first.
The loaf rose better, but she was still handling the dough close to midnight.
minor_details: She found a patch of flour on her sleeve the next morning.
Owen liked the crust.

summary: Riley discussed improving bread via earlier starter feeding and weekend timing. Hannah reported a better loaf with less gummy texture but late-night dough handling remained an issue. Suggestions included feeding the starter earlier in the day on weekends to allow rise time, testing the timing before staying up, and observing results. Action: try morning feed, monitor, and adjust schedule to reduce late dough work.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The action words mostly worked in the session, but the staging confirmation screen caused some hesitation.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Was it 'stage' that tripped people up?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Not so much the word. People weren't sure where the goods were supposed to go.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. How many people did we have?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: 4 warehouse staff took part. And 3 participants asked for the staging location to be shown before they confirmed.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Ah, so the confirmation was asking them to say yes without telling them where.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. I've circled that note in orange ink. Very sophisticated analysis system.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It works. The picking list didn't have the same issue?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The action words largely worked there too. I wouldn't call that proof we've solved everything, but they didn't seem to be the main problem.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What if we show the staging location on the confirmation screen, before the button? Then the action and the destination are both clear.

key_facts: Four warehouse staff took part in the session.
Three participants asked for the staging location to be shown before they confirmed.
minor_details: Sam has circled a note in orange ink.

summary: Riley discussed staging confirmation usability issues: participants couldn't identify where goods go. Four warehouse staff participated; three requested the staging location be shown before confirming. Action words were generally effective; the picking list was less problematic. Decision: display the staging location on the confirmation screen before the button to clarify action and destination, then test with additional participants and iterate.

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: Oh, good. Abena and I just got our application in for a community garden plot on Beacon Hill.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! Is it near your place?

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: Yeah, near home. I was going to mention it while I wait for my tea to cool. It's apparently fresh from the center of the sun.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What are you hoping to grow?

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: Greens, mostly. We figured we'd start there and keep it manageable, rather than sign ourselves up for a second job.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That seems wise. Have you picked out which greens?

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: Not really. I made some notes in pencil on the back of a seed catalog, but they're more like a list of possibilities.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A very Kofi approach.

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: Well, a catalog has a lot of possibilities. As far as I can tell, the trick is not trying all of them.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, especially if you and Abena are both fitting it around work.

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: Exactly. We want something we can enjoy without taking on more than we can manage.

details_in_summary: Kofi made notes in pencil on the back of a seed catalog.
key_facts: Kofi and Abena have applied for a plot at a Beacon Hill community garden.
They hope to grow greens without taking on more work than they can manage.
minor_details: Kofi made notes in pencil on the back of a seed catalog.
He mentions the application while waiting for his tea to cool.

summary: Riley discussed with Kofi the recent application for a community garden plot on Beacon Hill, near Kofi’s home. They plan to grow greens but have not selected specific varieties yet, with notes on a seed catalog as possible options. Both want a manageable plot that fits around work commitments. The next step is narrowing down the greens from the catalog and finalizing choices before planting.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Hi, Riley. How's your Wednesday going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, Wei. Pretty good. Nice to take a breath after lunch.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Agreed. My spreadsheet and I needed some time apart.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm sharing my screen from the corner desk. Can you see the updated dashboard?

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Yep. So, for our March 18 check, let's compare the wording with the calculation.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The label now says 'Shipments with delivery scans received after expected delivery time.'

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: And the calculation compares the scan record's receipt timestamp with the expected delivery time, not the delivery scan timestamp.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. The explanation also says the count doesn't establish whether the shipment itself arrived late.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Good. Let's look at the 3 test shipments. The summary count is 2.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Those 2 have scan records received after their expected delivery times. The other 1 doesn't.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Exactly. And a scan can show an on-time delivery but still be received after the expected time. That shipment would be counted.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Here's the tooltip I changed. It says 'Delivery scan record received after expected delivery time,' instead of 'Delivered late.'

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: That's precise. The label and tooltip both describe what the calculation counts.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Great. So the wording checks out against all 3 shipments.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: It does. I'm closing the browser tab now. The spreadsheet can have me back.

details_in_summary: Wei closes a browser tab after the check.
key_facts: On March 18, Riley and Wei verify the updated label and tooltip against the calculation.
Their check uses three test shipments, two of which are included in the summary count.
minor_details: Riley shares the screen from a corner desk.
Wei closes a browser tab after the check.

summary: Riley discussed dashboard wording for March 18: label updated to 'Shipments with delivery scans received after expected delivery time' and tooltip changed to 'Delivery scan record received after expected delivery time.' The calculation compares receipt timestamp to expected time, not delivery scan time. They reviewed 3 test shipments; 2 are counted due to scans after expected times, with one not counted. Clarified that a shipment can be on-time yet received after the expected time. Riley will close the tab; no further actions noted.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Hey. It's nice to finally sit down this evening.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey. Long Wednesday?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: A little. I did get the invitation slips for the library display done, though. I put them at the branch's information desk.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. So people can take one without having to tell you a story right there?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Exactly. The slips ask interested residents to contact me by email or phone. They can think about it first.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That feels a lot less like being cornered at a desk.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but I also want them to know what they'd be saying yes to. I put that the audio sessions would be up to 30 minutes long.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe make it clear that's a maximum, not a quota. They don't have to fill the whole 30 minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Good point. And contacting me doesn't commit them to a session, either. They can just ask questions.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. You could also mention that they get to review any excerpt you select, like you were saying before.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I can add that. I was trying to keep the slips short, but that's worth making room for.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, I just noticed a typo here. 'Neighborhood' is missing an h.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Of course it is. I trimmed all those slips with a paper cutter, too. I'll fix the word and replace them. The paper cutter will be thrilled.

details_in_summary: Riley notices a typo in the word “neighborhood.”
key_facts: Maya puts invitation slips at the branch’s information desk.
The slips ask interested residents to contact her by email or phone.
The proposed recording sessions are up to 30 minutes long.
minor_details: Maya trims the slips with a paper cutter.
Riley notices a typo in the word “neighborhood.”

summary: Riley noted Maya completed invitation slips for the library display and placed them at the branch information desk. The slips invite residents to contact Maya by email or phone, emphasize that audio sessions are a maximum of 30 minutes (not a quota), and that contacting her does not commit them to a session. They can ask questions and review any excerpt. Action items: fix the typo in 'Neighborhood,' replace the slips, and consider adding language about reviewing excerpts. Maya and Riley will finalize wording.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, how are things looking with the apartment search?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Mixed, I guess. I saw that Green Lake place on March 14, and it was too dark for me.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, that's disappointing. You can't always tell from the photos.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Yeah. I was trying to keep an open mind, but once I was there, I couldn't really picture living in it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Have you seen anything else since?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: I did. There was a second apartment in Wallingford that I liked a lot better. It had this wide kitchen counter, which was nice.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds promising. Did you apply?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: I didn't get the chance. I found out on March 19 that it had already been taken.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Ah, that's rough. Especially after the first one.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Yeah. And I was still thinking it over, comparing it with what I need. Apparently the apartment wasn't waiting for my analysis.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did it at least have anything else going for it?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Well, the agent had left a bowl of wrapped mints by the door. Not exactly a reason to rent a place, but I noticed.

details_in_summary: The second apartment had a wide kitchen counter.
The agent had left a bowl of wrapped mints by the door.
key_facts: Jamal found the first apartment too dark.
The appealing second apartment was in Wallingford.
He learned on March 19 that the Wallingford apartment had already been taken.
minor_details: The second apartment had a wide kitchen counter.
The agent had left a bowl of wrapped mints by the door.

summary: Riley discussed the apartment search with Jamal. The Green Lake listing (Mar 14) was too dark; Jamal couldn’t picture living there. A Wallingford listing with a wide kitchen counter was appealing but taken by Mar 19 before he could apply. A mint bowl by the door was noted but not a rental factor. Action items: continue evaluating new listings and prepare for timely applications.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Oh, there it is. I just noticed I cut the awning off in my first photograph of the shoe-repair shop.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh no. Is that one of the prints you brought in?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, one of the 5 by 7s. I'd been looking at the dark window and missed the top edge entirely.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Easy to do when you're trying to see what's inside.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: What if I make a brighter print like the group suggested? Do you think that'd be enough, or would a fresh photograph help?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A brighter print might help with the window, but it won't bring the awning back. I'd take another photograph if you want the whole shopfront.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right. The printer's good, but it's not that good.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are you going back soon?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I'm planning to go back on March 22. I want to try it straight on again, with the full doorway in frame.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe check the frame edges while you're there, before you take the shot. Especially the top.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, a little perimeter check. I can get so focused on the doorway that I forget there's a rest of the picture.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is there anything in the doorway you particularly want to keep?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: There's a brass door handle I like. And I've added a spare battery to my coat pocket, so at least I won't have to rush if I need another try.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds good. You can still make a lighter test print of the first one and compare it with the new photograph.

details_in_summary: The repair shop has a brass door handle.
key_facts: Sam wants to revisit a shoe-repair shop whose awning was cut off in the first photograph.
They plan to go back on March 22.
Riley suggests checking the frame edges on location.
minor_details: Sam has added a spare battery to their coat pocket.
The repair shop has a brass door handle.

summary: Sam noted the awning was cut off in the first shoe-repair shop photo. Riley advised a brighter print helps the window but cannot restore the awning; a fresh photo of the full storefront is preferred. Sam plans to return on March 22 for a straight-on shot including the doorway, with a perimeter/top edge check. He values the brass door handle in the doorway and has a spare battery. They will run a lighter test print of the first image to compare with the new photo.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I think the 30 we picked are manageable, if we do them together instead of me fighting the scanner by myself.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I can come down to Tacoma on Sunday, March 22, and help scan.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That'd be good. After lunch? We can start around 1, if that works.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: 1 works. I'll bring my laptop and a USB drive.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Perfect. I'll prepare a list of the captions we already know, so we're not trying to remember them while the scanner's running.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll handle the files on the laptop, then. You can do the scanning?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes. I'll do the manual cropping too, so we don't lose any more of those borders.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And we'll stick with 600 dpi, TIFF masters and JPEG copies for sharing.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Right. In theory, having a system makes me less likely to muddle it. We'll see.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: We can check a couple as we go. Oh, and for anything we can't caption yet, let's not guess.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Agreed. I'm putting a pack of sticky notes beside the scanner, so we can flag those without writing on the photographs.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds good. See you Sunday after lunch.

details_in_summary: They plan to start after lunch.
key_facts: Riley plans to visit Hannah in Tacoma on Sunday, March 22, to help scan.
Riley will bring a laptop and a USB drive.
Hannah will prepare a list of the captions they already know.
minor_details: They plan to start after lunch.
Hannah puts a pack of sticky notes beside the scanner.

summary: Riley and Hannah plan to scan 30 photos together on Sunday, March 22 in Tacoma, starting around 1 PM after lunch. Riley will bring a laptop and USB; Hannah will prepare known captions, perform manual cropping, and handle scanning. They will use 600 dpi TIFF masters and JPEG copies, avoid guessing uncaptions, and flag such photos with sticky notes. Riley handles laptop files; Hannah scans. They will review a few items during the session.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. Okay, so, how's your Friday evening going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty good. Glad it's Friday. How was the hatchery visit?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Good, actually. On March 18, Nikhil Sethi and I got some lovely water sounds at Willow Bend Salmon Hatchery, near Monroe. We captured the water flowing through the rearing channels.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. Did the machinery cooperate?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Some of it did. But near the intake, a pump's low mechanical hum was really prominent in the audio. It made some of the quieter material hard to use.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Was it that loud everywhere?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Not everywhere. Nikhil and I took notes on where it was strongest. We could hear the difference as we moved around.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: At least you came back with good water sounds. How was it being out there?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: A little muddy. I got mud on one trouser cuff, somehow only the one. Nikhil brought a thermos of black tea, which was a much better decision than any I made about footwear.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: One clean cuff is still a partial victory.

details_in_summary: Nikhil brought a thermos of black tea.
key_facts: The March 18 session captured water flowing through the hatchery's rearing channels.
A pump's low mechanical hum was prominent in the recordings near the intake.
minor_details: Nikhil brought a thermos of black tea.
Daniel got mud on one trouser cuff.

summary: Riley discussed a March 18 visit to Willow Bend Salmon Hatchery with Daniel. Daniel and Nikhil Sethi captured water sounds, noting that a pump near the intake produced a loud hum that affected quieter material. They mapped where the noise was strongest and disagreed about footwear while mud and tea banter occurred. No explicit decisions; notes on noise hotspots were taken.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Hey. It's nice to be home on a Friday night, isn't it?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'm glad the week is over.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but before we get too comfortable, do you want to go through a few more of those photos with Lian? She's on the call.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sure. I can pass you the ones from the unidentified envelope.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Thanks. Lian, can you see this one?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The one with you and Kevin?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. Oh, Lian says, 'Tilt the photograph closer to the camera.' How's that?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: She's nodding. Does she recognize it?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: She does. She says that's Kevin and me outside our childhood home.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, the delivery buzzer. Hang on, Lian, we'll be right back.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, we're back. Sorry about that. Lian, do you remember when the photo was taken?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What did she say?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: She thinks it was the late 1990s, but she can't remember the year. I'll write down 'late 1990s, approximate' and leave the year open.

details_in_summary: Lian asks Maya to tilt the photograph closer to the camera.
key_facts: Lian recognizes a photograph of Maya and Kevin outside their childhood home.
Lian thinks the photograph was taken in the late 1990s but cannot remember the year.
Maya writes down the decade as approximate.
minor_details: Lian asks Maya to tilt the photograph closer to the camera.
The call is briefly interrupted by a delivery buzzer.

summary: Riley discussed reviewing photos with Maya and Lian on the call. They planned to pass along photos from the unidentified envelope. Lian was asked to view a photo of Maya and Kevin outside their childhood home and indicated she could recognize it after tilting the image. Lian identified the scene and recalled the timeframe as late 1990s, but did not remember the exact year. Action item: note the timeframe as 'late 1990s, approximate' and keep the year open.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, I finally picked the work sample. A 2-minute excerpt from an older oral-history edit.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. You sound relieved.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I am. I could've spent another week comparing 2-minute excerpts. A valuable use of my remaining time on earth.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And now you get to write the statement.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. I've started a draft, but the first bit is mostly a list of equipment I've used.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Does that tell them much about how you make decisions?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Not really. It tells them I know the names of things.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe talk about what you're listening for instead. Like when you'd clean something up and when you'd leave it alone.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: That makes sense. I want to focus on making aging recordings usable without erasing their character.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a much better starting point than a gear list.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, I can explain the trade-offs instead of just saying what I used. Maybe connect it to the oral-history excerpt.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. What did you want someone listening to it to be able to hear?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Right. That's the question. Also, I ordered a bowl of tomato soup, so I'd better solve it before the soup gets here.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: We should move it when it does. This table has a wobbling leg.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Good call. I don't need tomato soup making editorial decisions on the draft.

key_facts: Daniel chooses a two-minute excerpt from an older oral-history edit as his work sample.
His statement will focus on making aging recordings usable without erasing their character.
minor_details: They sit at a table with a wobbling leg.
Daniel orders a bowl of tomato soup.

summary: Daniel selected a 2-minute older oral-history excerpt as the work sample and began a draft. The team advised replacing a equipment list with explanations of listening criteria and trade-offs to preserve aging recordings’ character. Action: Daniel to frame the statement around what listeners should hear in the excerpt and how decisions were made, linking to the sample. Also address editorial focus over gear details.

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Hi, Riley. How's your Sunday going? Having a decent lunch?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, Chloe. Yeah, pretty decent. How's yours?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Good, actually. I talked with Fiona Hart at the Alder Street Cinema about those programs.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, the box you were sorting by decade? What did she say?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: She said I can copy the programs for the lobby display. So I don't have to put the originals out where people might handle them.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. Did you figure out where to keep them while you're working on it?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Yeah, they'll stay in the cinema office between my visits. That seemed simpler than taking the whole box home.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And how are you going to make the copies?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: I'm planning to scan my favorites at the Sellwood-Moreland Library. Maybe just a few to start with, so it's manageable.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds sensible. Was the torn one still near the bottom?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Yeah. Oh, and Fiona found a pencil in the bottom of the box. A little bonus from the archives, I guess.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A priceless pencil. Did you go straight home afterward?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: I did, but I walked along the river after Fiona and I talked. It was a nice way to get home.

details_in_summary: Fiona found a pencil in the bottom of the box.
Chloe walked home along the river after their conversation.
key_facts: Fiona Hart gave Chloe permission to copy the programs for the display.
The programs will stay in the cinema office between Chloe's visits.
Chloe plans to scan her favorites at the library.
minor_details: Fiona found a pencil in the bottom of the box.
Chloe walked home along the river after their conversation.

summary: Riley discussed with Chloe the progress on organizing archival programs. Chloe reported that Fiona Hart at Alder Street Cinema approved copying the programs for a lobby display, with originals kept in the cinema office to prevent handling. Chloe will scan a subset at Sellwood-Moreland Library, starting small. The torn program remained near the bottom, and Fiona found a pencil in the box. Chloe planned the storage plan and, after their meeting, walked along the river on her way home.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Morning, Riley. Monday's arrived right on schedule, unfortunately.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Morning. At least we've got a few minutes before the next meeting.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. I talked with Ada about the Victoria weekend, and we sketched out a very loose start.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. Did you pick something to do?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: We're planning to walk in Beacon Hill Park on Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds good. Is it a place Ada likes?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, she mentioned a bench she likes near a flower bed. I think sitting there counts as an itinerary.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A very solid itinerary. What about when you get there on Friday?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Ada suggested keeping the first evening low-key. Which sounds right after the ferry.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Definitely. You don't have to get off the boat and immediately start doing things.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Exactly. What if we just leave the details for that evening open? Well, that's what we agreed to do.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the rest of the weekend?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: We agreed to leave some time unscheduled during the weekend, too. The park walk is the one thing we've picked.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I like that. You can decide what you feel like once you're there.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That's the hope. I wrote the outline in pencil, which feels appropriately noncommittal.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Easy to erase if the bench becomes a 3-hour event.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: A highly demanding bench. We'd need a break afterward.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good thing you've left some room for one.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Exactly. A plan with space in it. I may bring the concept to our next design review.

details_in_summary: Ada mentions a bench she likes near a flower bed.
Sam writes the outline in pencil.
key_facts: Sam and Ada plan to walk in Beacon Hill Park on Saturday.
Ada suggests keeping the first evening low-key.
They agree to leave some unscheduled time during the weekend.
minor_details: Ada mentions a bench she likes near a flower bed.
Sam writes the outline in pencil.

summary: Riley discussed planning a Victoria weekend with Ada, focusing on a Beacon Hill Park walk and a bench by a flower bed as a simple itinerary. They agreed to keep Friday evening low-key and leave parts of the weekend unscheduled, with the park walk being the only fixed activity. Riley noted writing the outline in pencil to allow easy changes. They may bring the concept to the next design review.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: Hi, Riley. Nice to get a little break for lunch, even if the weather's looking a bit, well, Seattle.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, Fatima. You've got a pencil tucked behind your ear, by the way.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: Oh, good. I was wondering where I'd put it. It's March 23 and I've already misplaced it twice today.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's pretty efficient.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: I meant to pass this along: on March 4, Miriam told me she'd reserved Tern Coffee's back table for June 17.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, great. So we have the spot for the A Psalm for the Wild-Built discussion.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: Yes. I'll welcome everyone and get us started, like we said. And you're keeping an eye on the time.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. I can bring sticky notes for us, too, in case we need a discreet reminder of the order of things.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: That would help. Actually, wait, let's keep it to a few notes. We're still leaving room for people to follow their own thoughts.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Definitely. First impressions, then just a reminder to leave a few minutes for final thoughts.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: Perfect. Oh, there's a light drizzle now. We should probably get going.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. See you, Fatima.

key_facts: On March 4, Miriam reported that she had reserved Tern Coffee's back table for June 17.
On March 23, Riley offers to bring sticky notes for the co-leaders.
minor_details: Fatima has a pencil tucked behind one ear.
There is a light drizzle when they part.

summary: Riley Morgan and Fatima Haddad confirmed plans for the A Psalm for the Wild-Built discussion at Tern Coffee on June 17, based on Miriam’s March 4 note. Fatima will welcome attendees and start the session; Riley will monitor time and optionally use a few discreet sticky notes to cue the agenda. They agreed to keep notes minimal to allow participants’ reflections, covering first impressions and a brief final thoughts segment. Weather noted as drizzle; they will proceed.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. Okay, so, how's your evening going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty good. How about yours?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Good. I finally delivered the ferry piece to the exhibit team, so the commission's officially closed out.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! What did you send them in the end?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: A playback WAV and a backup MP3. They confirmed that both files opened correctly.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a relief. After all that work on the voices and the gallery noise.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. I also handed over the written text of the piece for the exhibit's accessibility materials.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So everything's actually out of your hands now.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: It is. I even labeled the delivery folder with a plain black marker. I managed not to spend 20 minutes choosing a pen.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm proud of you. Did you do anything to celebrate?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I stopped for a sesame bagel on my way home. Very restrained, very professional.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Honestly, a solid way to close it out.

details_in_summary: He labeled the delivery folder with a plain black marker.
He stopped for a sesame bagel on his way home.
key_facts: Daniel delivered a playback WAV and a backup MP3 to the exhibit team.
The team confirmed that both files opened correctly.
He also handed over a transcript for the exhibit's accessibility materials.
minor_details: He labeled the delivery folder with a plain black marker.
He stopped for a sesame bagel on his way home.

summary: Riley noted that Daniel delivered the ferry piece to the exhibit team, including a playback WAV and a backup MP3 that opened correctly. The written text for accessibility materials was handed over. The project is now considered closed, with the delivery folder labeled in plain black marker. Riley mentioned a sesame bagel on the way home as a celebration.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm looking at the scan files from yesterday, and I think we did pretty well.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, we got through 18 prints during my visit. Not the whole selection, but that was a good afternoon's work.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Especially since the scanner lid needed a gentle push to close flat. Very sophisticated equipment.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: In theory, it closes on its own.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: In theory. I was looking at the backs we scanned too. There were 4 prints with handwriting on them.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm glad we scanned those backs. Some of the notes would be useful alongside the pictures.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That's what I was thinking. I don't want the front and back images to get separated and leave us guessing which note belongs where.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Could you give each pair matching filenames? Maybe the same number, then 'front' or 'back' at the end.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes, I can do that. Matching filenames for each front and its back. Simple enough that even I can follow it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the ones without writing can just have the front label?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I think so. That way we're not making up a back image when there isn't one.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. And the handwritten notes stay in the scans, rather than us having to squeeze everything into a filename.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. We can still use the captions we know, but the handwriting will be there to check.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I remember looking at one of those after my break. I had a cheese sandwich and then went back to the scanner.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: You did. I think we were both ready for a break by then.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Definitely. I'm happy we took our time with the borders, too.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Me too. The manual cropping was a bit fiddly, but nothing got cut off by that automatic crop.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. And once the front and back filenames match, those notes should be much easier to find.

key_facts: They scanned 18 prints during Riley's visit.
They also scanned the backs of four prints that had handwriting on them.
Hannah will use matching filenames to connect each front image to its back.
minor_details: The scanner lid needed a gentle push to close flat.
Riley had a cheese sandwich during a break.

summary: Riley and Hannah reviewed yesterday's scans, noting 18 prints processed and a need to keep handwriting on backs. They planned matching front/back filenames for each pair, with fronts for unbacked images and backs preserved when present. They agreed to maintain captions and keep notes embedded in scans, avoiding filename-only notes. They also discussed manual cropping accuracy and ensuring front/back images stay paired to facilitate later note matching.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: I'm looking at that little notepad with the ferry estimate on it. I nearly put it away with the grocery list.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, the estimate we talked about on March 11?

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: That's the one. I wrote it in blue ink, which apparently doesn't make it any easier to find.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It was $48 for the scan and the reproduction, right?

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: Yes, $48. Framing would cost extra, so it's not quite as tidy a number as I'd hoped.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: But it's still below your $90 limit, at least before the framing.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: Mm. I don't want to spend so much on the frame that the ferry has to pay rent.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair enough. I was thinking about the original, too. You found it on January 21, didn't you?

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: I did. It was between the pages of an old cookbook. I told you that evening, though I don't think I explained where it was.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I remember you saying you'd found it. So that's where it was hiding.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: And then on February 14, when you were here, we noticed that scratch across the original's sky.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. It's a shame, but the ferry and the bicycle are still clear.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: That's what I thought. The little contact print doesn't show everything as well, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. And you still want the original returned after it's scanned.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: Definitely. I'd rather not fasten it into a frame, scratch or no scratch.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A reproduction makes sense, then. We just have to keep the extra framing cost in mind.

details_in_summary: The original was between the pages of an old cookbook.
key_facts: Lian found the original on January 21.
On February 14, Lian and Riley noticed a scratch across the original's sky.
On March 11, a print shop estimated $48 for scanning and making a reproduction; framing would cost extra.
minor_details: The original was between the pages of an old cookbook.
Lian wrote the estimate in blue ink on a small notepad.

summary: Riley discussed the ferry estimate: $48 for scan and reproduction, framing extra, staying under $90. The original was found January 21 between pages of an old cookbook; a February 14 scratch affected the original's sky but not the ferry or bicycle in photos. Riley preferred a reproduction over framing and insisted the original be returned after scanning, avoiding a frame. Action items: proceed with reproduction, monitor framing costs, and ensure the original is returned.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Oh, these test copies need more room than I thought. The directions are practically squeezed against the map.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Let me see. One of the test sheets came out slightly crooked, too.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah, that one's not helping. But even on the straight one, everything feels crowded.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What size is the text?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The main directions are in 14-point type. I don't want to make them smaller just to fit everything.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Agreed. What can come out instead? The starting point, turnaround and return all need to stay.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but there's that decorative neighborhood history paragraph. It's nice, but it doesn't tell anyone what they need for the walk.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'd cut that before touching the type. You could use the space to give the directions some breathing room.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'll remove the neighborhood history paragraph. I want the distance and the note about there being no bench on the route easy to find, too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the group instructions can stay on the reverse, so you don't have to cram them in here.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Right. I'd rather have a plain guide people can read than a lovely little puzzle.

key_facts: The test copy uses 14-point type for the main directions.
Maya removes a decorative neighborhood history paragraph to make room.
minor_details: One test sheet comes out slightly crooked.

summary: Riley and Maya reviewed crowded test copies. They will not reduce 14-point type. They agreed to remove the decorative neighborhood history paragraph to free space, keep the starting point, turnaround, and return, and place group instructions on the reverse. They also want to include distance and note that there is no bench, aiming for a plain, readable guide.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So is the new sink working yet?

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: It is. It's been working since March 23.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. No more washing dishes in the bathroom?

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: That's the idea. I tested the sink by rinsing a colander, which seemed like a suitably rigorous experiment.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the colander survived?

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: It did. The sink also passed.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is the kitchen all finished now, then?

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Almost. The contractor is due back on March 30 to adjust 1 cabinet door.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Just the 1 door?

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Just 1. A small adjustment.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty short list.

dialogue.speaker: Wei
dialogue.text: Well, there's also a roll of painter's tape left on the windowsill. But I think we can handle that ourselves.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. I was worried you'd need another contractor.

details_in_summary: Wei tested the sink by rinsing a colander.
A roll of painter's tape was left on the windowsill.
key_facts: The new sink has been working since March 23.
The contractor is due back on March 30 to adjust one cabinet door.
minor_details: Wei tested the sink by rinsing a colander.
A roll of painter's tape was left on the windowsill.

summary: Riley noted the new sink has been working since March 23 and passed testing with a colander. The kitchen is almost finished; a contractor is due March 30 to adjust one cabinet door. A roll of painter's tape remained on the windowsill, but Riley/Wei believed they could handle it themselves, avoiding another contractor.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Hey. Okay, so, how's your evening going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, pretty good. Nice to have a little daylight left.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, it makes 5 o'clock feel a lot less final. I was thinking about our May 22–24 weekend.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The Port Angeles cottage weekend. What's up?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: We should figure out how we're getting around once we're on the peninsula. I can bring my car.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That'd be great. Let's split the fuel cost.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, that works. We can fill up and work it out from there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Perfect. I have a paper road atlas in the hall cupboard, too. I could bring it.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Please do. I can spend 40 minutes comparing routes on my phone, or 40 minutes comparing them on paper.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: At least the atlas won't keep suggesting a faster route while you're looking at it.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: True. Okay, car and atlas. That's enough decisions for tonight.

details_in_summary: Riley has a paper road atlas in a hall cupboard.
key_facts: Daniel will bring his car.
Riley and Daniel will split the fuel cost.
minor_details: Riley has a paper road atlas in a hall cupboard.

summary: Riley and Daniel planned the May 22–24 Port Angeles cottage weekend. They decided Daniel will bring his car and split fuel costs; Riley will bring a paper road atlas. Daniel will compare routes (paper vs phone). They will fill up and settle costs, and proceed with car and atlas arrangements; no further decisions tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I finally bought most of the tickets for our Astoria weekend this evening.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. Did you manage to get the train and bus?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Most of it. I booked round-trip Amtrak tickets for Owen and me between Tacoma and Portland. And I booked the outbound POINT bus from Portland to Astoria.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So what's left?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: The return bus from Astoria. I haven't booked that one yet. I'm going to give it a few days while I check the options.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Makes sense. You don't want to pick a bus that gets you back too late for the train.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. I'd rather compare the connections properly than buy something because I'm tired of looking at them. In theory, I'm capable of stopping before that point.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A bold theory. How was booking the rest?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Fine, actually. I paid with the card I keep in my green wallet, and then Owen offered to carry the printed confirmations.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. One less thing for you to keep track of.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes. And it's a relief to have the train tickets sorted for May 29 through May 31, especially after all that room comparing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And Hotel Elliott's already booked, so the return bus is the main thing left.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Right. I'll look at it again in a few days, when I can stand to compare another set of options.

details_in_summary: She pays for the tickets with a card she keeps in a green wallet.
Owen offers to carry the printed confirmations.
key_facts: Hannah books round-trip Amtrak tickets between Tacoma and Portland.
She also books the outbound POINT bus.
She has not yet booked the return bus from Astoria.
minor_details: She pays for the tickets with a card she keeps in a green wallet.
Owen offers to carry the printed confirmations.

summary: Riley summarized that Hannah booked round-trip Amtrak for Owen and herself between Tacoma and Portland and the outbound POINT bus to Astoria. The return bus from Astoria remains unbooked; she plans to compare options in a few days to avoid late connections. Hotel Elliott is booked for May 29–31; payment was via her green-wallet card, with Owen handling printed confirmations. Action: revisit return bus options soon.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How are we looking with the herbs?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Ready to plant, I think. We've got parsley, chives and mint, all nursery plants.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay. I've got the old plastic scoop for the potting mix. Which pot do you want first?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Let's put the parsley in one 10-inch pot and the chives in the other 10-inch pot.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the mint gets the 8-inch pot?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: By itself, please. I don't want it crowding the other plants.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. I'll fill the parsley pot first. Is that enough mix under it?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: A little more, I think. We want the top of the soil to sit below the rim.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Like that? Okay, parsley's in. Chives next.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'm writing labels on strips of masking tape, so we don't have to play herb detective in the dark.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Chives are in their own 10-inch pot. And now the mint gets its own 8-inch pot.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but can we leave a little space between them? I want to reach the pots without knocking one over.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. We can put the parsley and chives toward the east corner, then the mint just beside them, with a gap.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That works. They're all on their saucers, and I can still get a hand in there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. Three herbs, no railing contraptions.

details_in_summary: Maya writes labels on strips of masking tape.
key_facts: Parsley and chives each go into their own 10-inch pot.
Mint goes into the 8-inch pot by itself.
They start all three herbs from nursery plants.
minor_details: Riley uses an old plastic scoop for the potting mix.
Maya writes labels on strips of masking tape.

summary: Riley discussed planting three herbs with Maya: parsley and chives in 10-inch pots, mint in an 8-inch pot. Adjusted soil so the top sits below the rim. Labeled herbs with masking tape. Arranged pots with a gap for access, placing parsley and chives toward the east corner and mint beside them on saucers. No railing contraptions used.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Oh! I nearly forgot to tell you, I made 2 more changes to the home desk.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. How's the lamp working out?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Still good on the left edge. My notes are lit and there's no glare on the screen.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So what did you change this time?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I moved the keyboard 3 inches closer to the front edge of the table.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you actually measure that?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I did. I borrowed the tape measure from the kitchen drawer. Very rigorous operation.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And does it feel better there?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: So far, yeah. I want to use it like that for a while before I decide, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What was the other change?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I gathered the loose cables with reusable hook-and-loop ties. One of the ties is bright orange, so it's not exactly invisible.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: At least you can find it if you need to undo it.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Exactly. What if I leave the whole arrangement unchanged for at least a week? Then I can see how it feels without fiddling with it every day.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A week-long ban on desk adjustments. I support it.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. I'm not calling it done yet, but at least I know where the cables are.

details_in_summary: One cable tie is bright orange.
key_facts: Sam moved the keyboard three inches closer to the front edge.
Sam gathered the loose cables with reusable hook-and-loop ties.
Sam plans to leave the arrangement unchanged for at least a week.
minor_details: One cable tie is bright orange.
Sam used a tape measure borrowed from the kitchen drawer.

summary: Riley noted Sam made two desk adjustments: keyboard moved 3 inches closer to the front edge and cables tidied with reusable ties (one bright orange). Sam confirmed the lamp on the left works and no glare. They agreed to a one-week trial with no further adjustments to assess comfort and usability, aiming to decide if the setup should stay as is.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The return visit went much better. Here's the new frame of the shoe-repair shop.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, you got the whole awning in this time.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. I stepped farther back so I could include the entire awning.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It feels a lot less cramped. Did you check the edges while you were there?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I did. Your suggestion actually saved me from getting home with another half-awning.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a very specific kind of success.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I'll take it. There's a narrow strip of pavement between the shop and the bottom edge of the image now, too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's helping. The doorway has a little room around it instead of feeling like it's going to fall out of the frame.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right. I was trying to keep the full doorway in without making everything else feel squeezed.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And it's still straight on, like the approach you picked for the series.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. What if I show you the other one? I photographed a nearby florist too. They were beginning to put spring plants outside.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, I like those little bits of green against the shopfront.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: And there's a red delivery crate beside the florist's bin. I didn't really notice it until I looked at the frame.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I think it belongs there. It gives the edge a little color without taking over.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Good. I wasn't sure if it was distracting. Also, I bought a sesame roll on the walk home, which was a pretty good end to the outing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A complete awning and a sesame roll. Hard to beat.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: A very productive walk, by my admittedly generous standards.

details_in_summary: A red delivery crate sat beside the florist's bin.
Sam bought a sesame roll on the walk home.
key_facts: Sam stepped farther back to include the entire awning.
A narrow strip of pavement now separates the shop from the bottom edge of the image.
Sam also photographed a nearby florist beginning to put spring plants outside.
minor_details: A red delivery crate sat beside the florist's bin.
Sam bought a sesame roll on the walk home.

summary: Riley discussed improvements to the shoe-repair shop frame, noting the full awning, doorway space, and a straight, balanced perspective. Sam confirmed edges were checked, avoiding a cramped shot and saving from an off-center result. They also reviewed a nearby florist with spring plants and a red delivery crate that added color without overpowering the scene. Riley acknowledged the positive framing adjustments and mentioned a sesame roll from the walk. Overall, they described the outing as productive.

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. How's your evening going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey! Pretty good. Nice to be done with work.

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: Yeah, it's been a long Friday.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: At least we managed to get lunch, even if it wasn't quite what we planned.

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: Right. We met outside Larch Cafe and then found out the kitchen was closed for maintenance.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I was so ready to eat, too.

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: The awkward bit was you needed to get back to work, so we didn't have much time to find somewhere else.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that nearby soup counter was a good save.

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: Quick and practical. My 2 favorite features in a lunch.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I got the lentil soup. It was pretty good, actually.

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: And you made it back to work on time?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I did, just fine. I'm glad we didn't spend ages looking for another place.

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: Me too. I still have the receipt, actually. I saved it in my jacket pocket.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, from the soup counter?

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: Yeah. It's dated March 27, 2026, in case we need a historical record of the detour.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Very important documentation. Friday lunch, rescued by soup.

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: A rare case of a workaround doing exactly what it should.

details_in_summary: Riley ordered lentil soup.
Arjun saved the receipt in his jacket pocket.
key_facts: Riley and Arjun met outside Larch Cafe for lunch on Friday, 27 March 2026.
Larch Cafe's kitchen was closed for maintenance.
They ate at a nearby soup counter because Riley needed to return to work.
minor_details: Riley ordered lentil soup.
Arjun saved the receipt in his jacket pocket.

summary: Riley and Arjun discussed a Friday lunch detour after Larch Cafe was closed for maintenance. They chose a quick, practical option at a nearby soup counter, with Riley having lentil soup and returning to work on time. Arjun noted the receipt was saved as a historical record of the detour (dated March 27, 2026). Action item: preserve the receipt for future reference; no further lunch deviations required.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'm putting a pencil beside the calendar. Can we add the garden workday?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. When is it?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Saturday, April 4, at 10 a.m. It's the first spring workday.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay, I'll write it down. What are we doing there?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Volunteers will prepare the communal paths for spring.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds manageable. Let's go.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but should we bring our own work gloves?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, let's bring them. One of mine has a loose cuff, but it should still be fine.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: As long as it stays on your hand. The path probably doesn't need a glove of its own.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll check it before we go. Are you putting yours by the door?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I can. And I'll put yours there too, if you find them.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Deal. April 4 at 10 is on the calendar.

details_in_summary: One of Riley’s gloves has a loose cuff.
key_facts: The workday is scheduled for April 4 at 10 a.m.
Volunteers will prepare the communal paths for spring.
Maya and Riley plan to bring their own work gloves.
minor_details: One of Riley’s gloves has a loose cuff.
Maya puts a pencil beside the calendar.

summary: Riley discussed adding the garden workday to the calendar: Saturday, April 4 at 10 a.m., first spring workday. Volunteers will prepare communal paths for spring. They decided to bring work gloves; Riley will check a cuff on one of his gloves. Maya will place both pairs by the door. Action items: confirm the date/time on the calendar; bring gloves; ensure gloves are by the door.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Oh, good, it finally went through. I just booked the return POINT bus from Astoria to Portland.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. Was that the last ticket you needed?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah. I was looking at 2 afternoon options, and I went with the earlier one.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So you'll have a bit more room before the train?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. I don't want us getting off the bus and having to rush straight onto the train. That's a little too much excitement for the trip home.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair. And you've already got the train tickets.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Right, and the outbound bus. Both bus tickets are in my email now, so in theory I can find them again.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: In theory?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I've also written the booking reference on a yellow sticky note. Just in case.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Do you need a label for the sticky note?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Very funny. I suppose I could put another sticky note on it that says 'bus.'

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Perfect. Then you'll know exactly what to label the second one.

details_in_summary: She writes the booking reference on a yellow sticky note.
Riley teases her about needing a label for the sticky note.
key_facts: Hannah books the return POINT bus from Astoria to Portland.
She chooses the earlier of the afternoon options she considered.
Both bus tickets are in Hannah's email.
minor_details: She writes the booking reference on a yellow sticky note.
Riley teases her about needing a label for the sticky note.

summary: Riley noted Hannah booked the return POINT bus from Astoria to Portland and chose the earlier afternoon option to allow time before the train. Action items: ensure ticket access remains easy and add clear labels for bus versus train references.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How's the application coming along?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, better than last week. Louise Park agreed to be my professional reference.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, great. The exhibit designer?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. I asked her, and she said she'd be happy to speak to my work.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a good piece to have sorted. How's the statement?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Still a draft, but I'm keeping it focused on making aging audio usable without wiping out its character. Less of the equipment list.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you're still using that 2-minute oral-history edit?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. I prepared a brief note about the condition of the source audio and the edits I made. I'm just not sure how much context it needs.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is the note separate from your statement?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: For now, yeah. I thought it could sit with the excerpt so they know what they're hearing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That makes sense. Enough to understand your choices, but you don't need to walk them through every second.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Right. I have a paragraph and then another paragraph explaining the first paragraph. Very efficient.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe the second one's the bit to cut. Can I see?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Sure. And yes, that's a coffee ring in the corner of the draft. It's my official seal.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It adds character. Here, you can borrow my pencil if you want to mark it up. The eraser's chewed, though.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Thanks. I'll try not to make it worse. So, condition of the source, what I changed, and why?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. And if a detail doesn't help them understand those things, you can probably leave it out.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay. That's shorter than what I've got, which is a promising sign.

Daniel prepares a brief note describing the condition of the source recording and the edits he made.

Daniel's draft has a coffee ring in one corner.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm sorting these prints on a folded dish towel. There are a lot of repeats in here.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah, I noticed a few of the same picture. Are they actually identical?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Same picture, but some copies are sharper than others. This one has a little more detail than that one.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but do we need to scan every copy? That could take a while.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I don't think so. We could pick the sharpest print from each set of duplicates and scan that one.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That makes sense. We can compare them before they go on the scanner.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And what should we do with the ones we don't scan?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Let's keep the unscanned duplicates together in a paper sleeve. There's one with a blue stripe along its edge.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: This one? I'll put them in there as I go.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That's it. The duplicates get their own little waiting room.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: All right. Sharpest one for scanning, the rest in the sleeve.

details_in_summary: One sleeve has a blue stripe along its edge.
key_facts: They choose the sharpest print from each set of duplicates to scan.
They keep the unscanned duplicates together in a paper sleeve.
minor_details: Riley sorts the prints on a folded dish towel.
One sleeve has a blue stripe along its edge.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. How's your Sunday evening going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey! Pretty quiet, actually. How about yours?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Quiet here too, which is nice. I finally worked out the costs for the library photo display.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. Did the 6 pictures fit in Daphne's budget?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: They do. The 6 prints will cost $36, and the mounting supplies will be $18.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So $54 altogether, out of the $70. That's not bad.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No, I'm relieved. I compared prices on a Tuesday break and, well, spent more of it than I meant to looking at mounting options.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What did you end up choosing?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm going to use removable adhesive strips to protect the wall. Those are included in the $18 for supplies.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And no frames?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No, I've decided not to order frames. They'd eat up too much of the budget. The print shop offers a matte finish, though, which I think could look nice on its own.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, especially with the 2 rows of 3. Sounds like a good solution.

details_in_summary: The print shop offers a matte finish.
key_facts: Six prints will cost $36.
Mounting supplies will cost $18.
Hannah plans to use removable adhesive strips to protect the wall.
minor_details: She compared prices on a Tuesday break.
The print shop offers a matte finish.

summary: Riley and Hannah finalized the library photo display budget: six prints at $36 and mounting supplies at $18 total $54 of $70. Riley confirmed no frames to conserve budget; Hannah will use removable adhesive strips included in supplies and rely on a matte finish. Display will be arranged as two rows of three.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Oh, good, they got back to me. I can tour that Greenwood apartment this weekend.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice! When are you going?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Saturday, April 4. I saved the listing during my lunch break and asked about a viewing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What's the rent on this one?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: It's advertised at $1,795 a month. So it's under my $1,900 ceiling, which is a pleasant change from looking at numbers that make me tired.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's promising. How's the location?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: That's what I'm weighing. Greenwood could work, but I need to check the bus options before I get too attached to the rent.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, a cheaper place isn't much help if getting to work is a pain.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Right. I want a reliable route, not just a stop that happens to be nearby.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did the listing give you much of a sense of the building?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: A little. It's got a blue front door, which I remember more clearly than I probably should. I'm trying not to make the photos do all the work, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Especially after the Green Lake place turned out to be so dark.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Exactly. I'll see it for myself, check the bus, and then decide. Fair enough.

details_in_summary: The building has a blue front door.
key_facts: The next apartment is in Greenwood.
The viewing is set for April 4.
The advertised monthly rent is $1,795.
minor_details: The building has a blue front door.
Jamal saved the listing during his lunch break.

Action: Jamal to view, evaluate transit, and decide.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The staging confirmation has the destination area above the action button now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. After 3 people asked where the goods were going, it needed to be there before they confirmed.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. What if we try it in Harborline's internal test build, not just the mockup?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I've got it open. Let me get to the staging screen.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Oh, is that my folded receipt? I've been using it as a bookmark.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It was under my notebook. Here. And sorry, this conference table wobbles when I lean on it.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: It's a very interactive table. Okay, there's the destination, right above the button.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That makes the choice clearer. I'll confirm it.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Wait, the success message still says 'Sent.'

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, and it doesn't say where. Sent could mean just about anywhere.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: What if we change 'Sent' to 'Staged' and include the destination area in the message?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That works. It keeps the action consistent and confirms where the goods went.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I've filed it for revision: 'Staged,' with the destination in the success message.

key_facts: The staging confirmation now displays the destination area above the action button.
Sam and Riley tried the change in Harborline’s internal test build.
A success message still says “Sent,” so Sam files it for revision to “Staged.”
minor_details: The conference table wobbles when Riley leans on it.
Sam uses a folded receipt as a bookmark.
