Riley opened the staging screen and confirmed the destination placement after user inquiries. To reduce ambiguity, Riley and Sam agreed to change the success message from 'Sent' to 'Staged' and include the destination. Action item: Sam filed a revision for 'Staged' with the destination included in the success message.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Oh, I never told you how those 2 films were!

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, right! How was the film series?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Pretty good. I saw The Long Way Home and Low Tide Market like I planned, and I'd recommend Low Tide Market to you.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What made that one stand out?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The scenes of the vendors setting up for the day. They're really patient, and funny without trying too hard. It gives everyone time to be a little bit ridiculous.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds like my kind of movie. What about The Long Way Home?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: It was visually appealing, definitely worth looking at, but the ending felt abrupt. I kept thinking, wait, that's it?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So pretty, but not quite satisfying.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. Low Tide Market felt more complete to me. Oh, and this cup of peppermint tea is hotter than I thought.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Careful. And thanks, I'll keep Low Tide Market in mind.

details_in_summary: Sam had a cup of peppermint tea during the conversation.
key_facts: Sam recommends Low Tide Market for its patient, funny scenes of vendors setting up for the day.
Sam found The Long Way Home visually appealing but thought its ending was abrupt.
minor_details: Sam had a cup of peppermint tea during the conversation.

summary: Riley asked for the film update. Sam reported watching The Long Way Home and Low Tide Market; he recommended Low Tide Market for its vendor setup scenes, patience, and humor. The Long Way Home was visually appealing but had an abrupt ending. Riley expressed interest in Low Tide Market and said she will keep it in mind; a note was made about the peppermint tea being hotter than expected.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I'm just checking my bag for the hatchery trip. I found that cracked foam windscreen at the bottom.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The one you were trying to convince yourself was still fine?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. I'm replacing it before the trip. I've moved on to comparing 2 nearly identical ones, which is progress.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So you're going back out there?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, the second visit to Willow Bend Salmon Hatchery is booked for April 16. I figured going back was better than trying to edit out all that pump hum.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The low hum near the intake? I thought the water in the rearing channels came through pretty well.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: It did. But some of the quieter stuff near the intake was hard to use. The staff expect the intake pump to be off for about 20 minutes during maintenance, so I'm going to use that window.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: 20 minutes isn't much time. Do you know where you want to start?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, Nikhil and I noted where the hum was strongest. I'll start around there and see what the water sounds like without it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you won't have to spend the first 10 minutes figuring out how to get in?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Hopefully not. I wrote the access instructions on an index card. A very advanced system, but it works.

details_in_summary: Daniel is replacing a cracked foam windscreen before the trip.
He has written the access instructions on an index card.
key_facts: The second recording visit is booked for April 16.
Hatchery staff expect the intake pump to be off for about 20 minutes during maintenance.
minor_details: Daniel is replacing a cracked foam windscreen before the trip.
He has written the access instructions on an index card.

summary: Daniel is replacing a cracked windscreen and comparing two nearly identical options. He booked a second visit to Willow Bend Salmon Hatchery for April 16. He plans to operate during a 20-minute maintenance window when the intake pump is off to assess water sound without hum, starting at the area where hum is strongest with Nikhil. He has written access instructions on an index card to simplify entry.

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: Oh, Ellis just asked me to change the meetup schedule again. The awkward bit is, every change has to go through me.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You mean Ellis Brooks can't update the online schedule himself?

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: Not without editing code, no. So he asks me whenever something needs changing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds like a lot of back and forth for a volunteer job.

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: Yeah. I want to make it easier, but I don't want to build something I'll spend all my spare time maintaining.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe just start with the schedule itself. What actually needs to be on the page?

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: The event name, date, time, and a short description. Nothing too elaborate.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm drawing a little box on this paper napkin. Could each event just sit in one of these?

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: Yeah, that makes sense. I'll sketch a page around that, with the goal that Ellis can eventually update it without editing code.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And keep the moving parts to a minimum. How's your lentil sandwich, by the way?

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: Good. Larch Cafe is doing its part, even if it's Wednesday, April 1, and I'm having lunch after 8.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A very efficient lunch. You got a sandwich and a paper-napkin design.

key_facts: At lunch on April 1, Arjun says Ellis currently asks him to make changes to the design meetup's online schedule.
Arjun plans to sketch a page that Ellis can eventually update without editing code.
minor_details: Arjun has a lentil sandwich at Larch Cafe.
Riley draws a small box on a paper napkin while they talk.

summary: Riley discussed with Arjun the bottleneck where Ellis asks Arjun to update the online schedule, since Ellis cannot edit code. They agreed to simplify the process by focusing on essential event fields (name, date, time, description) and to design a basic, napkin-sketch layout where each event sits in a box. The goal is for Ellis to update the schedule without coding. Action item: Arjun will sketch a minimal page structure to support this.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I think the briefing is finally short enough that it won't take longer than the walk.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What are you telling everyone before you leave?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'll describe the route first, including where we turn around, and explain the seating. There's seating at Ballard Commons Park near the library, but no public bench on the out-and-back stretch.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. Can they see that in the guide before deciding whether to come along?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yes, it's right by the distance. I'll hand the guides out before we leave, too, so people have time to look and ask questions.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the directions still stand on their own without the map?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: They do. Start at the branch, go along 22nd Avenue NW to NW 57th Street, then come back the same way.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What if it's pouring on April 11?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: If heavy rain makes the walk unsuitable, we'll stay indoors and discuss the guide instead. I don't want the backup plan to be 'enjoy getting soaked.'

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Does the guide say that before people set out?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yes, I added it to the group instructions on the back. I'll say it in the briefing as well.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And if someone's wondering about the weather that morning?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The finished guide has the branch phone number for last-minute questions. Oh, and I've stapled a spare copy to my planning notes, so I should actually be able to find one.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I found a folder with an intact elastic closure for those. We can put the notes in there before the papers stage an escape.

details_in_summary: Maya staples a spare copy to her planning notes.
key_facts: Maya plans to describe the route and available seating before the group leaves.
If heavy rain makes the walk unsuitable, she will discuss the guide indoors instead.
The finished guide includes the branch phone number for last-minute questions.
minor_details: Maya staples a spare copy to her planning notes.
Riley finds a folder with an intact elastic closure.

A heavy rain contingency keeps the walk indoors and discusses the guide; the weather plan is included on the back and in the briefing. dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, Ben and I are planning a trip to San Juan Island from June 19 to June 22.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. What brought that on?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I first brought it up to Ben over bowls of noodles. We were talking about wanting a few days somewhere near the water.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds good. What do you want to do there?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Mostly walks, good food and time near the water. Nothing too structured. I want enough room to just decide what we feel like doing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A trip where you don't come back needing a recovery day.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Exactly. Though I've already compared 3 kinds of rain jacket, so I'm managing to make it complicated anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You could turn that into a full elective.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. 'Introduction to Waterproofing,' followed by a very long final exam. I'm trying not to do that with the rest of the trip.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Well, walks and food sound like a solid syllabus.

details_in_summary: Daniel first raised the idea with Ben over bowls of noodles.
key_facts: Daniel and Ben are planning to visit San Juan Island from June 19 to June 22.
They want a trip centered on walks, good food and time near the water.
minor_details: Daniel first raised the idea with Ben over bowls of noodles.
He jokes that he has already compared three kinds of rain jacket.

summary: Riley discussed Daniel and Ben's plan to visit San Juan Island from June 19–22. They want a flexible itinerary focusing on walks, good food, and time by the water. Daniel noted prior jacket comparisons and joked about turning the trip into a waterproofing elective. No concrete decisions or action items beyond planning the trip were identified.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: It's May 17. I signed up for my first half-marathon.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, wow. What made you decide to do it?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I've been wanting something to work toward, and a beginner plan seemed less intimidating than just running until I regretted it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair. What's the plan like?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: 3 runs a week. I'm trying to figure out how to fit them around weekends with Leila.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are you thinking one of the runs has to be on the weekend?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, the long run. What if I do those early on Saturdays? Then Sundays can stay open for time with Leila.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds pretty reasonable, as long as early Saturday isn't too painful.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That's the experiment. Early enough that it doesn't take over the whole day, anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Have you put the runs on your calendar yet?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, a paper calendar, in blue pencil. It felt suitably official, but also erasable.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a good combination. Do you eat anything before you go?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Usually a banana before heading out. Nothing complicated.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I like how much thought you've put into keeping it simple.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Well, simple on paper. Blue pencil helps.

details_in_summary: Sam has marked the runs on a paper calendar in blue pencil.
key_facts: The half-marathon is on May 17.
Sam’s beginner plan has three runs a week.
Sam plans to do long runs early on Saturdays, leaving Sundays open for time with Leila.
minor_details: Sam has marked the runs on a paper calendar in blue pencil.
They usually eat a banana before heading out.

summary: Riley noted Sam signed up for a half-marathon and discussed a beginner plan of three runs weekly. They decided the long run will be on Saturdays to keep Sundays free for Leila, with an experiment to start early on Saturdays. Sam has placed the plan on a blue-pencil paper calendar as an erasable record. Pre-run nutrition is a banana. Action items: finalize and keep the calendar updated with the schedule, monitor fit around Leila.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: I'm at the kitchen table with my laptop, and my cup of mint tea is cooling beside it. Could you help me with this ticket page?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sure. What's the concert?

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: A chamber concert on May 2 at the Phinney Center in Seattle. Inez and I would like to go.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay, let's have a look. How much do you want to spend?

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: No more than $65 for both tickets, including whatever fees they come up with.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: All right. This section has 2 seats together, but the total comes to $70 with fees.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: Well, that's an easy decision. Let me put these on so I can check the seating chart.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: There are some seats together in this other section. I'll click on it.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: Oh, it says 1 ticket now. Didn't you select 2?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I did. The page must reset the quantity when you change sections. I'll put it back to 2.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: I can see seats 7 and 8 in row C. They're next to each other, aren't they?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yep. Let's select them and see the total.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: That's $62 including fees. Under budget, and we won't have to sit on each other's laps. What do you think?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I think those look good. Want me to go through to checkout?

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: Yes, please. I'll enter my payment details.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay, everything's filled in. Do you want to press the button?

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: There. Oh, it says the order's confirmed.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Great. You've got seats 7 and 8 in row C, 2 tickets for $62 including fees.

key_facts: The chamber concert is on May 2 at the Phinney Center in Seattle.
Lian wants to spend no more than $65 for both tickets.
They book seats 7 and 8 in row C.
The two tickets cost $62 including fees.

After reviewing sections, Riley found seats 7 and 8 in row C totaling $62 with fees. Riley completed the checkout process and confirmed the order. No further action items; tickets confirmed.

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: Yeah, they gave us a small plot at the Beacon Hill community garden.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! You and Abena applied back in March, right? How small is it?

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: 4 by 8 feet. Which, as far as I can tell, is a sensible amount of garden for 2 people with jobs.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Enough room for the greens you wanted, without turning it into a second job.

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: That's the idea. We're trying to work out watering before we get carried away with anything else.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Have you figured out who goes when?

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: I plan to water on Tuesday and Thursday evenings after work. Abena's taking Sunday mornings.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That fits around both your schedules?

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: Yeah. Evenings work for me, and Sunday morning works for her. We'll keep an eye on whether that's enough water.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is there a hose there, or are you hauling water over?

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: There's a shared hose with a brass nozzle. So, at least we don't have to solve that part.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. And is there somewhere to keep tools?

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: There's a tool shed. The latch sticks a little, but it does open. A very modest security system.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds like you've got the important logistics covered, anyway.

details_in_summary: The garden's shared hose has a brass nozzle.
The latch on the tool shed sticks a little.
key_facts: Their new plot measures four by eight feet.
Kofi plans to water on Tuesday and Thursday evenings after work.
Abena plans to water on Sunday mornings.
minor_details: The garden's shared hose has a brass nozzle.
