dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm just sitting down. I finally reviewed the full March tally for the holds shelf.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, how did it look?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: There were 11 requests for help finding holds in March. And staff recorded 2 holds in the wrong place.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's for the whole month? Seems manageable.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah, I think so. It's not perfect, but patrons and staff can manage it. I've decided we're keeping the layout.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The A through F row on top and everything?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Right. G through M in the middle, N through Z on the bottom. I was tempted to compare another arrangement, but, well, this one works.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you didn't have to squeeze another piece of furniture in there.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. I even filed the completed tally sheet in a gray folder. So it's officially a decision and not just a piece of paper wandering around my desk.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's the highest level of official, I think.

details_in_summary: Hannah filed the completed tally sheet in a gray folder.
key_facts: The March tally showed 11 requests for help finding holds.
Staff recorded two holds in the wrong place during March.
minor_details: Hannah filed the completed tally sheet in a gray folder.

summary: Riley and Hannah discussed the March holds shelf tally. There were 11 help requests and 2 holds placed in the wrong location. Hannah decided to keep the current layout: A–F top, G–M middle, N–Z bottom, and considered no rearrangement. She filed the completed tally in a gray folder, marking it an official decision. No further actions were requested beyond maintaining the established layout.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Hey, you. Are you hungry yet?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I could definitely eat. My arms are a little tired, too.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: 2 hours spreading wood chips on the paths will do that. I think I got almost as many chips in my shoes as on the ground.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Almost? I saw you stop to deal with one.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: One got caught in my sock. It was surprisingly sharp.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I was distracted by the wheelbarrow I borrowed. Its wheel was so squeaky.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but at least nobody had to wonder where you were.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: True. And now we know where the shared tools are stored. I'm glad that garden volunteer showed us.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Me too. We can use those when we start on bed 7.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It still needs the winter weeds removed before we can plant.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. I want to clear those out first, then see what we're working with.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds good. After lunch, though.

details_in_summary: Maya got a wood chip caught in her sock.
Riley borrowed a wheelbarrow with a squeaky wheel.
key_facts: They spent two hours spreading wood chips on the paths.
A garden volunteer showed them where the shared tools are stored.
Their bed still needs its winter weeds removed before planting.
minor_details: Maya got a wood chip caught in her sock.
Riley borrowed a wheelbarrow with a squeaky wheel.

summary: Riley discussed hunger and tired arms after spreading wood chips. Maya joked about chips in shoes and a sock. They referenced a squeaky wheelbarrow and locating shared tools. They plan to use tools for bed 7, identify winter weeds to remove before planting, and settle on starting after lunch.

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Hi, Riley. How's your Saturday going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty good. Nice to have a quiet afternoon. How about yours?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Good, yeah. I did that scanning at the library. I scanned 4 of my favorite programs from the cinema box.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! How did they come out?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Pretty well. I checked the scans, and the text is legible. Even the smaller print.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What resolution did you use?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: 300 dots per inch. It seemed like a reasonable place to start.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the scanner behaved itself?

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Mostly. I wiped a smudge off the scanner glass first. Very glamorous work.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The hidden life of cinema preservation.

dialogue.speaker: Chloe
dialogue.text: Exactly. And then rain started while I was putting on my coat, so that was a nice little finish to the trip.

details_in_summary: Rain started while she was putting on her coat.
key_facts: Chloe scanned four favorite programs.
She used a resolution of 300 dots per inch.
minor_details: She wiped a smudge off the scanner glass first.
Rain started while she was putting on her coat.

summary: Riley and Chloe discussed a quiet Saturday afternoon. Chloe described scanning four cinema programs at the library at 300 dpi, with legible text including smaller print. She noted cleaning the scanner glass before use. The session ended as rain began while she put on her coat, finishing the outing.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm in the kitchen looking at the loaf I baked this morning.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, how did the overnight fridge plan go?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Better, actually. The crumb is more even than before. It's not all gummy in the middle.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice! And were you still dealing with dough at midnight?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No, thank goodness. I fed the starter after work on Friday, April 3.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And then you did the dough on Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah. I mixed it and shaped it on Saturday, then put it in the refrigerator overnight.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And baked it this morning?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Sunday morning, yes. It was much nicer putting it in the oven after I'd slept.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds like a pretty good improvement over the second loaf.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It does. The second one rose better than the first, but I was still handling it close to midnight. I don't want bread to become a late-night hobby.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair. How's the rest of the kitchen looking?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Oh, there's a little flour in the crease of the counter. And I used the blue dish towel to cover the bowl, so that's a bit floury too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A small price to pay for a better crumb.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: In theory. I'll repeat the process before I call it a routine, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sure. But it sounds like this timing was a lot less miserable.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Definitely. And I get to eat the evidence at a reasonable hour.

key_facts: Hannah fed the starter after work on Friday, April 3.
She mixed and shaped the dough on Saturday, then refrigerated it overnight.
She baked the loaf on Sunday morning and found the crumb more even than before.
minor_details: She used a blue dish towel to cover the bowl.
A little flour collected in the crease of the counter.

summary: Riley discussed the overnight fridge plan for sourdough, noting improved crumb and earlier baking with less late-night handling. Hannah confirmed feeding the starter, Saturday dough mixing and refrigeration, and Sunday morning baking. They acknowledged the second loaf rose better but required late-night work. Riley suggested continuing the timed process until it becomes routine, while Hannah reported minor flour residue in the kitchen.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. How's your Monday going so far?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey. Pretty good, actually. How was the Greenwood viewing?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Well, the rent was appealing, but I'm going to pass on it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, what put you off?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Traffic, mostly. You could hear it clearly inside the apartment. I stood there for a bit thinking maybe it'd die down, but it didn't.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that'd be hard to ignore. Anything else?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: There was no secure bike storage in the building either. I was trying to weigh that against the $1,795 rent, but—yeah, not worth it for me.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair enough. Did you at least get a decent walk back?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: A rain shower started just as I left the building, so not quite. The apartment gave me a very clear answer.

details_in_summary: A rain shower started just as he left the building.
key_facts: Traffic noise was clearly audible inside the apartment.
The building had no secure bike storage.
minor_details: A rain shower started just as he left the building.

summary: Riley and Jamal discussed the Greenwood viewing. Jamal will pass on the $1,795 rent due to street traffic noise and lack of secure bike storage. He weighed these factors and concluded the offer wasn't worth it, reinforced by a rain shower as he left. No further actions noted.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So how are things looking now that you're in?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, pretty good. There are still a few boxes, but the essential furniture's in place. And thanks again for helping this weekend.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Of course. Did the desk fit where you wanted it?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, it fits against the wall I chose for it. I measured that wall so many times, it'd have been embarrassing if it didn't.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I was ready to hear you compare 3 other walls anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I did briefly consider a fourth. But no, it's staying there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the bookcase?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: It's in place too. Oh, and I found that missing shelf pin in my jacket pocket.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a good place for it. Very easy to find.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, my filing system remains flawless.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is that your cable box beside the sofa?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. The box of cables is sitting beside the sofa until I can face sorting it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's fair. You've got time.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: And I returned the rental van, so at least that's done.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. What's left at the Capitol Hill apartment?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: The old landlord has scheduled the move-out inspection for April 12.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Next Sunday, then. Good to have it on the calendar.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. For tonight I'm just happy I can sit down without moving a box first.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A pretty solid first Monday in Fremont.

details_in_summary: Daniel found one missing shelf pin in his jacket pocket.
key_facts: Daniel's desk fits against the wall he had chosen for it.
His old landlord has scheduled the Capitol Hill move-out inspection for April 12.
Daniel has returned the rental van.
minor_details: A box of cables is sitting beside the new apartment's sofa.
Daniel found one missing shelf pin in his jacket pocket.

summary: Riley assisted Daniel with settling in Fremont: desk fit on the chosen wall, bookcase placed, shelf pin found, and a note on cable organization. Daniel returned the rental van and confirmed his filing system remains in use. They referenced the Capitol Hill move-out inspection scheduled for April 12, with next Sunday on the calendar. Remaining tasks include unpacking a few boxes, sorting cables, and finalizing the move-in setup.

dialogue.speaker: Elena
dialogue.text: Morning, Riley. Bit early for a proper conversation, isn't it?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Morning. I'm still working on being awake.

dialogue.speaker: Elena
dialogue.text: Fair enough. I wanted to plan that small round of usability interviews. April 20 and 21 work for you?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, both days work. What should we ask participants to do?

dialogue.speaker: Elena
dialogue.text: I was thinking we ask them to identify shipments that need attention.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: In the prototype, right? Just let them look through the shipments and tell us what they'd check?

dialogue.speaker: Elena
dialogue.text: Exactly. Though 'what needs attention' is a little vague. Let me rephrase: which shipments would they look into first, and why?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds better. I'll write the task on this sticky note with my green pen.

dialogue.speaker: Elena
dialogue.text: Green for research. Very official.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It's the pen I could find. Do you want to moderate?

dialogue.speaker: Elena
dialogue.text: Yes, I'll moderate the interviews, and you can observe. That way I can focus on the questions and you can watch how they use the prototype.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Works for me. I'll hold my questions until you're done with the task.

dialogue.speaker: Elena
dialogue.text: Thanks. We can leave a little time at the end if there's something we need to clarify.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds good. Oh, your tea's been sitting there this whole time.

dialogue.speaker: Elena
dialogue.text: And it's gone cold. A productive planning session by every measure.

details_in_summary: Riley writes the task on a sticky note with a green pen.
key_facts: The interviews are scheduled for April 20 and 21.
Participants will be asked to identify shipments that need attention.
Elena will moderate the interviews, and Riley will observe.
minor_details: Riley writes the task on a sticky note with a green pen.
Elena's tea goes cold during the planning conversation.

summary: Riley and Elena planned a small round of usability interviews for April 20–21. They agreed the task is to identify which shipments participants would look at first and why, using the prototype to assess attention. Riley will note the task with a green pen; Elena will moderate while Riley observes, focusing on how participants use the prototype. They’ll reserve time at the end for clarifications and keep questions until the moderator is finished. Tea comment noted.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The trial week went well, actually. I left the setup alone like I said I would, and I'm keeping it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So the separate workspace wins over the dining table?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. I'm staying with the folding table against the living-room wall. The dining table can go back to being a dining table.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What made the biggest difference?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Having room to leave work things in place. I can leave my notebook open beside the keyboard between work sessions, instead of having to clear everything away.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds like a surprisingly big quality-of-life upgrade.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: It is. The riser and the lamp help too, but not having to set up again every time is the part I notice most.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are you still thinking about getting a new desk?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: No, I've decided against it. The folding table works, so a new desk would mostly be a more expensive surface to put things on.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A compelling product pitch.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right? I do keep a coaster at the back corner of the workspace. And the small pad of sticky notes gets tucked into a drawer after work.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds like you've got the whole thing sorted.

details_in_summary: Sam keeps a coaster at the back corner of the workspace.
A small pad of sticky notes is tucked into a drawer after work.
key_facts: Sam has settled on the separate workspace rather than returning to the dining table.
Sam can now leave a notebook open beside the keyboard between work sessions.
Sam has decided against buying a new desk.
minor_details: Sam keeps a coaster at the back corner of the workspace.
A small pad of sticky notes is tucked into a drawer after work.

summary: Riley summarized Sam's report: a trial week with a separate workspace using a folding table against the living-room wall has been kept in place, allowing work items to remain between sessions. The setup, aided by a riser and lamp, reduced re-setup time and improved workflow. Sam has decided against buying a new desk. Ongoing organization includes keeping a coaster in the back corner and tucking sticky notes into a drawer after work. No further actions required.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, how's your evening going?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Pretty good. I'm folding a load of towels while we talk, which is, in theory, a relaxing activity.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: In theory?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I keep finding ones that don't match. Anyway, I was thinking we could have a spring day out on Bainbridge Island, just the 2 of us.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'd love that. A Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah. Let me look at the calendar. How about May 16?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Saturday, May 16, 2026? I'm free.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Me too. Let's do that. I was thinking we could leave the car behind and take the Seattle–Bainbridge ferry as walk-on passengers.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds nice. We can just explore on foot from the terminal.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. We could wander up toward Winslow Way, have a look around, and find somewhere for lunch.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And maybe walk by the water if we feel like it. Nothing too scheduled.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Good. I was starting to compare routes, but we really don't need a spreadsheet for a walk.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: My walking shoes could use a scrub, though. They're looking pretty rough.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Well, you've got time. We can figure out the ferry timing a little closer to May 16.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds good. I'm looking forward to it.

key_facts: The siblings choose Saturday, May 16, 2026, for the trip.
They plan to take the Seattle–Bainbridge ferry as walk-on passengers.
minor_details: Hannah makes the call while folding a load of towels.
Riley mentions that their walking shoes could use a scrub.

summary: Riley discussed planning a relaxed Saturday trip to Bainbridge Island with Hannah on May 16, 2026. They will take the Seattle–Bainbridge ferry as walk-on passengers, explore Winslow Way, and have lunch with no fixed schedule. They will finalize ferry timing closer to the date and confirm calendar availability.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'm still at the laptop, looking at that permission form.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I thought you were done with it for tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Almost. I checked it with a library colleague, and I changed the part about withdrawal. Can I read you the revised paragraph?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, go ahead.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: 'You may withdraw your excerpt before the display files are finalized. Please be aware that we cannot retrieve copies that visitors have already downloaded or photographed.'

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That makes the limit pretty clear. How will they know when the files are finalized?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but that's the part I still need to make clear. I don't want anyone guessing when the deadline is.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And if they have a question about what they're agreeing to?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I added a contact number to the form for questions about permission, so they can call and ask.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. Oh, your pencil just rolled under the sofa.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Of course it did. The sofa's filing system is very thorough.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll get it. You finish the paragraph.

details_in_summary: Maya reads the revised paragraph aloud from her laptop.
key_facts: Contributors may withdraw an excerpt before the display files are finalized.
The form explains that Maya cannot retrieve copies already downloaded or photographed by visitors.
She adds a contact number for questions about permission.
minor_details: Maya reads the revised paragraph aloud from her laptop.
A pencil has rolled under the sofa.
unstated_facts: Contributors may withdraw an excerpt before the display files are finalized.

summary: Riley discussed Maya’s revised permission form clause on withdrawal, noting the need to clearly state when files are finalized. Maya read the updated paragraph: withdrawal before finalization, with no retrieval of previously downloaded or photographed copies. Riley asked how users would know the finalization date, and Maya agreed to clarify the timeline. An additional contact number for questions was added. Riley planned to finish finalizing the paragraph and address any remaining wording.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: I'm looking up the trip now, before I get too attached to the floor plan.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You found another place?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Yeah, it's in Northgate. I'm scheduled to see it on April 11, at 10:30 a.m.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How's it looking for the bus?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Still checking. I want to see how reliable the route is, not just how long the trip is supposed to take.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair. What's the rent?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: It's advertised at $1,820 a month, so it's under my ceiling. Not as low as the Greenwood place, but, well, that one had traffic noise inside.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And no secure bike storage. What do you think of this one so far?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: The floor plan looks practical. There's even a narrow hall closet, which is more exciting to me than it probably should be.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A closet's worth getting excited about. Does the listing say much else?

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.text: Not really. It's light on details, so I'll have to ask about the things I can't tell from the plan.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: At least you'll get a look on Saturday. Hope the trip works out.

details_in_summary: The floor plan shows a narrow hall closet.
The viewing is booked for 10:30 a.m.
key_facts: The apartment is in Northgate.
Jamal is scheduled to view it on April 11.
Its advertised rent is $1,820 a month.
minor_details: The floor plan shows a narrow hall closet.
The viewing is booked for 10:30 a.m.

summary: Jamal is evaluating a Northgate listing, with a viewing scheduled for April 11 at 10:30 a.m. He will assess bus route reliability, not just travel time. Rent is $1,820/month, higher than Greenwood due to fewer issues like traffic noise. The listing lacks details; Jamal will ask about items not visible from the floor plan. Riley noted the practical layout and a narrow hall closet, and they expect a Saturday visit to see the place.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm going to repeat that weekend sourdough schedule over April 18–19, I think.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The one with the overnight rest in the fridge?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah. Feed the starter after work on Friday, then mix and shape on Saturday, refrigerate it overnight and bake Sunday morning.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds good. The crumb was more even last time, right?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It was. I'd like to try it again before I call it a routine, though. In theory, I now have a routine.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you won't be handling dough close to midnight.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That's the hope. Oh, how do I get a cleaner cut on top? Should I use kitchen scissors?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'd try a razor blade instead of kitchen scissors. Make a quick, confident cut before it goes in the oven.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Okay. I have a razor blade I keep in a small tin, so I can use that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Perfect. And it doesn't have to be fancy, just one good slash.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: One slash. I also need to add parchment paper to my shopping list.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Then you're set for April 18 and 19.

details_in_summary: Hannah adds parchment paper to her shopping list.
key_facts: Hannah plans to make her next loaf over April 18–19.
Riley suggests using a razor blade to score the dough instead of kitchen scissors.
minor_details: Hannah adds parchment paper to her shopping list.
She keeps the blade in a small tin.

summary: Riley summarized the weekend sourdough plan for April 18–19: feed starter Friday, mix and shape Saturday, refrigerate overnight, bake Sunday morning. They agreed on not handling dough near midnight and using a razor blade for a clean top slash. Action items: use a razor blade for slashing and add parchment paper to the shopping list. Riley noted the crumb was even previously and they want to try the routine again before formalizing it.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. Okay, so, how's your lunch going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty good. I was ready for a break.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Same. I brought a little printout for the peninsula trip, if you want to look at walks.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. I still want to keep it easy, though. Not turn it into a hiking expedition.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Exactly. I was thinking we could try part of the Spruce Railroad Trail at Lake Crescent.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds good. Just part of it, and we can turn around whenever we've had enough.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, I'm circling this trailhead on the printout. Otherwise I'll compare 6 different places to start until May.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A classic Daniel project. What about something shorter, too?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Madison Falls could be our shorter walking option.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. We don't need to decide which day for either one yet.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Agreed. We can just keep both in mind while we're at the cottage in Port Angeles.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I was also wondering about the Hoh Rain Forest, but that's a lot of driving, isn't it?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, I think a drive to the Hoh Rain Forest would mean too much time in the car. I'd rule that out.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Works for me. I'd rather get out and walk than spend the weekend looking through a windshield.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Especially since the whole point was 2 nights away without a packed itinerary.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: We could pack cheese sandwiches for the walks, too. Nothing elaborate.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Perfect. A manageable number of decisions and a cheese sandwich. That's a solid trip.

details_in_summary: Daniel circles one trailhead on a printout.
Riley suggests packing cheese sandwiches.
key_facts: They want to try part of the Spruce Railroad Trail at Lake Crescent.
Madison Falls is their shorter walking option.
They rule out a drive to the Hoh Rain Forest as too much time in the car.
minor_details: Daniel circles one trailhead on a printout.
Riley suggests packing cheese sandwiches.

summary: Riley discussed planning a short, easy weekend trip with Daniel. They shortlisted two walking options: part of the Spruce Railroad Trail at Lake Crescent and Madison Falls, avoiding the longer drive to Hoh Rain Forest. They will not set dates yet and will keep both options in mind while at the Port Angeles cottage. They prefer a simple itinerary with walking rather than a packed schedule and cheese sandwiches for the walks. Action: Daniel will circle a trailhead on the printout for reference.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. Still here? It's getting pretty quiet for a Thursday.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey. Yeah, I'm just wrapping up. How did the print discussion go?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Pretty useful, actually. This was the second time we talked through prints, and I brought a matte paper sample and a glossy one to compare.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Could people tell much of a difference?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, the group preferred the matte sample. There were fewer distracting reflections, so it was easier to look at the image instead of the room in the image.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty good argument for matte.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: It is. I labeled the paper samples in pencil on the back, so at least I didn't have to rely on my excellent memory.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Always a risky system. How did the photos themselves look?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That's where I noticed something. The color temperatures in my edited images weren't consistent. Some looked warmer than others, and not in a way that felt intentional.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Was it obvious when you put them next to each other?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Much more obvious, yeah. Although the meeting room's folding table wobbled, so keeping them next to each other was a small engineering problem.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What are you going to do before you submit anything for the exhibition?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: What if I revisit the edits together on the same screen? I think that'll make it easier to compare the color without guessing from memory.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds sensible. Get them feeling like a series before you decide what to submit.

details_in_summary: Sam labeled the paper samples in pencil on the back.
key_facts: The group preferred a matte paper sample to a glossy one because reflections were less distracting.
Sam noticed that their edited images had inconsistent color temperatures.
Sam plans to revisit the edits together on the same screen.
minor_details: The meeting room's folding table wobbled.
Sam labeled the paper samples in pencil on the back.

summary: Riley and Sam discussed the print discussion, with the group preferring matte paper due to fewer reflections. Sam had labeled samples on the back to avoid memory reliance. Sam noted inconsistent color temperatures across edited images and suggested revisiting edits on the same screen to compare colors. The goal is to ensure the photos feel like a cohesive series before submitting for the exhibition.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How are we doing on the photos?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: We're down to the last batch: 12 selected prints. I'll check the scans as you go.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay. Can you move the bowl of clementines a little? It's right next to the scanner, and I'm short on room.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Sure. The clementines have been demoted.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: All right, I'm starting with this one. Still using 600 dpi?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah, the test looked clear enough at that setting.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's the last of the 12 scanned. How do they look?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but this one has a cropped edge. Can you rescan that photograph?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yep. There, rescanned. Is the edge in now?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: It is. The rest look good too.

details_in_summary: The scanner sits next to a bowl of clementines.
key_facts: The last batch contains 12 selected prints.
Maya spots one cropped edge, and Riley rescans that photograph.
minor_details: The scanner sits next to a bowl of clementines.

summary: Riley discussed the photo project status with Maya, noting 12 prints in the final batch and confirming 600 dpi for scans. They moved a bowl of clementines away from the scanner. Riley started with one photo, Maya reported a cropped edge on one image and requested a rescan. Riley completed the rescan, and Maya confirmed the edge was included and the remaining images looked good.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Oh, finally. The unofficial academic record I need from the University of Washington came through.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. Did you get a chance to look at it?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, I read it on my phone while I was waiting for a bus. It looks like what they asked for.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So is that the last thing you needed for the application?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Almost. Louise is still going to send her reference directly to the institute. She plans to get it there by April 17.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay, so you're just waiting on that part.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. And I want to proofread the packet once more before I submit it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How's the statement looking?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Pretty good, I think. I marked a typo in the draft with an orange tab, so I at least know where to start.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A whole system. I'm impressed.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, one tab is not a system. Give me time, though, and I can spend an hour comparing tab colors.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Very familiar. Just fix the typo and give it one more read.

details_in_summary: He has marked a typo in his draft with an orange tab.
key_facts: Daniel has received an unofficial transcript from the University of Washington.
Louise plans to send her reference directly to the institute by April 17.
minor_details: Daniel reads the document on his phone while waiting for a bus.
He has marked a typo in his draft with an orange tab.

summary: Daniel reported receiving the UW unofficial academic record. Louise will send her reference to the institute by April 17. Daniel plans to proofread the packet again before submission and has marked a typo with an orange tab. Riley noted the typo and stressed one more read. They discussed a tab-color system briefly. Next steps: fix the typo and perform a final read; await Louise’s reference by the April 17 deadline.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: Morning, Riley. How's your Saturday going so far?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty good. I thought I was late, but the waiting-room clock is 3 minutes fast.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: It is. Gives everyone a little extra excitement before their appointment. How's climbing been?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good, actually. I've been climbing twice a week since mid-March.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: And how's getting down feeling?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm more confident with it. Practicing from halfway up helped, especially on the steeper routes.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: Good. Are you finding places to put your feet more easily?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Usually, yeah. And I can step off from a low hold without feeling like I have to force that last move.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: Any point in a visit where that changes?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Near the end, when I'm tired. The descent feels less controlled, like my feet aren't quite as precise.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: Do you have a sense of roughly how long you've been climbing when that starts?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Not really. I haven't been looking at the time. I just notice it when I'm coming down.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: Could you note roughly how long you've been climbing when the fatigue sets in? It doesn't have to be exact.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I can do that. Maybe I'll put a note on my phone next to my water bottle, the one with the peeling green sticker.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: That'll work. Just a rough time and what you noticed. Let's see what that does.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay. That feels manageable.

details_in_summary: Riley's water bottle has a peeling green sticker.
key_facts: Riley has been climbing twice a week since mid-March.
The descent feels less controlled near the end of a visit.
Jonas asks Riley to note roughly how long they have been climbing when fatigue sets in.
minor_details: Riley's water bottle has a peeling green sticker.
The clinic waiting-room clock is three minutes fast.

summary: Riley discussed climbing progress and descent control with Jonas, noting improved confidence and foothold use, but fatigue affects control near the end. Jonas suggested tracking rough climb duration when fatigue sets in. Riley agreed and planned to place a note on the phone next to the water bottle with the peeling green sticker to capture the approximate time and observations for future review.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Hi, Riley. How's your Sunday been?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty quiet, actually. How about yours?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Not bad. I've been thinking about the photo display, but for once it feels manageable.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. Did the supplies come in?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes, everything's ready. Marisol helped me mount the prints on lightweight backing board.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How did that go? Were they hard to line up?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: A little fiddly. I used a metal ruler to line up the edges, which made me feel very precise, in theory.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And did the removable strips work with the board?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: We tested 1 mounted print on a staff-area wall overnight. It was still up the next day, so that's encouraging.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a relief. It sounds like the pieces are finally coming together.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes. After all that measuring and comparing supplies, it's nice to have something we can actually put on the wall.

key_facts: Marisol helped mount the prints on lightweight backing board.
They tested one mounted print on a staff-area wall overnight.
minor_details: Hannah used a metal ruler to line up the edges.

summary: Riley and Hannah discussed finalizing the photo display. Supplies arrived and Marisol helped mount prints on lightweight backing board. Hannah described precise alignment with a metal ruler, noting it was fiddly. They tested removable strips with a mounted print on a staff-area wall overnight, which remained in place. Riley acknowledged progress and Hannah expressed that the display is finally coming together after measuring and checking supplies.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Hey. It's a pretty quiet Sunday evening, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, nice and slow. Want to get the photo folders organized?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but let's keep it simple. I'm creating 3 subfolders: childhood, gatherings and unidentified photographs.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. I'll read out the filenames while you type. First one: Green Lake picnic, Maya about 6.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Got it. That can go in gatherings. Mom was sure about Green Lake and my age, but we don't have a date.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Next: Maya and Kevin outside childhood home, approx late 1990s.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yes. Let's use 'approx' in filenames whenever a date is uncertain. Mom remembered the decade, not the year.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And that one goes in childhood. Oh, your pen dropped. Hang on, I'll get it.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Thanks. Okay, but for the ones we couldn't identify, let's not guess in the filename. I'll put those in unidentified photographs.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Works for me. I'll read the rest, then. Unidentified photograph 1, unidentified photograph 2.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Typed. I'm adding a short notes file explaining the labels: 'approx' means the date is uncertain, and unidentified means we don't know who's in the photo or where it was taken.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. So the 3 subfolders are set, and the notes make it clear what's known and what isn't.

key_facts: They create subfolders for childhood, gatherings and unidentified photographs.
They use 'approx' in filenames when a date is uncertain.
Maya adds a short notes file explaining the labels.
minor_details: Riley reads out filenames while Maya types.
They stop once to retrieve a dropped pen.

summary: Riley discussed organizing photo folders with Maya, creating three subfolders: childhood, gatherings, unidentified photographs. They planned to title files with location/people and add 'approx' for uncertain dates, avoiding guesses in filenames. A notes file will define labels: 'approx' for uncertain dates and 'unidentified' for unknown subjects. Action items: complete remaining filenames and confirm notes are saved.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: And Ada suggested we cook together at her place on Sunday, while I'm in Victoria.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. Had you two decided what to make?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Vegetable pasta. I offered to buy the ingredients, so she doesn't have to do the shopping as well.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I like that. It's a meal together, but it doesn't turn into a hosting job for her.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, that's what I was hoping for. She suggested adding lemon zest, too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds good. Do you have a list started?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I noted the shopping list on a sticky note. Very sophisticated travel system.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What if you put it somewhere you won't lose it before May?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Fair. I can copy it into my phone. The sticky note's really just for catching things as we think of them.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you still have the rest of the weekend pretty open?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. There's the walk in Beacon Hill Park on Saturday, and we're leaving some time unscheduled. The pasta gives Sunday a little shape without filling the whole day.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds like a good balance. Now, should we get ready for the design review?

details_in_summary: Ada suggests adding lemon zest.
Sam notes the shopping list on a sticky note.
key_facts: Sam and Ada plan to cook at Ada's home on Sunday.
Sam will buy the ingredients for that meal.
They have chosen a vegetable pasta.
minor_details: Ada suggests adding lemon zest.
Sam notes the shopping list on a sticky note.

summary: Riley and Sam discussed cooking with Ada on Sunday (vegetable pasta; Sam to buy ingredients; lemon zest suggested). They noted the shopping list on a sticky note and agreed to copy it into Sam’s phone to avoid losing it before May. Weekend plans include a Beacon Hill Park walk on Saturday and unscheduled time to keep Sunday from being full. Next step: ensure the shopping list is digitized and prepare for the design review.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Oh, good, it's confirmed. Okay, so Ben and I booked a guesthouse in Friday Harbor.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! For the island trip?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, June 19 to June 22. It's within walking distance of the ferry landing, which I like.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's convenient. How much did you end up spending?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: The guesthouse is $450 total for 3 nights. We also set a budget of $400 per person for the trip.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So $225 each for the room, and you've got $175 each for the rest.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Right. It's a modest place, but we weren't looking for anything fancy.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did they make you pay for the whole room upfront?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: No, they take a $60 deposit toward the room. Not an extra fee, thankfully.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. Does it look comfortable?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I think so. It has a small fridge, which I'm disproportionately pleased about.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You can keep your good food in there.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Exactly. I may have compared an embarrassing number of rooms for someone whose main criterion was a fridge.

details_in_summary: The guesthouse takes a $60 deposit toward the room.
Daniel likes that the room has a small fridge.
key_facts: They set a budget of $400 per person for the trip.
They book a Friday Harbor guesthouse for three nights at $450 total.
minor_details: The guesthouse takes a $60 deposit toward the room.
Daniel likes that the room has a small fridge.

summary: Daniel and Riley discussed booking a guesthouse in Friday Harbor for June 19–22. Total cost $450 for 3 nights with a budget of $400 per person. Each person would pay $225 for the room and $175 for other expenses. The guesthouse requires a $60 room deposit. It has a small fridge, which Daniel appreciates. No major issues noted beyond fridge preference.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: The print shop can prepare a proof of the ferry photograph before they make the final print.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. So we can see how the scratch looks?

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: That's what I was thinking. It's right across the sky, and I'd rather check than guess.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Definitely. Did they say what size the print will be?

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: The reproduction will be 8-by-10 inches. That should be enough for the hallway, I think.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, and big enough to see the bicycle at the railing.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: That's the part I don't want to lose. Otherwise it's just a very nice ferry.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: When can we look at the proof?

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: I was hoping you could come with me on April 25. It's a Saturday. What do you think?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: April 25 works. How about 11?

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: 11 is good. We can meet at the shop.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll stop for coffee on the way over. Want one?

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: Yes, please. Just a small coffee.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You got it. And the $48 estimate was for the scan and reproduction, right?

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: Yes, framing is extra. I've clipped the shop's receipt to a calendar, so at least I know where that is.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's better than my system.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: It's not much of a system. The calendar just happened to have a clip.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Still counts. I'll see you at the shop at 11 on April 25.

details_in_summary: Riley offers to stop for coffee on the way over.
key_facts: Lian and Riley plan to check the proof on April 25.
The shop will make an 8-by-10-inch reproduction.
minor_details: Lian has clipped the shop's receipt to a calendar.
Riley offers to stop for coffee on the way over.
unstated_facts: The shop will make an 8-by-10-inch reproduction.

summary: Riley discussed arranging a proof of the ferry photograph before final print. The print will be 8x10 inches; framing is extra. They scheduled to view the proof on April 25 (Saturday) at 11 at the print shop, with Riley stopping for coffee en route. The $48 estimate covers scan and reproduction.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so I think the Edmonds–Kingston ferry makes the most sense for getting over there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'd rather do that than drive all the way around.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Friday morning, then? May 22.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Works for me. What time do we want to get in line?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I'm hoping we can reach the ferry line by 7:30 a.m. That gives us some room if there's a queue.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And if the queue's already long, we just wait. We're not trying to squeeze in a big hike.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Right. This is not one of our college 'we can definitely do all of that' plans.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Thank God. Are you still bringing your car?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yep. I'll pick you up in Ballard, then we'll drive to the terminal in Edmonds.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Perfect. Maybe pick me up around 6:45?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, around 6:45. We can check traffic closer to the day and adjust if we need to.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds early enough for me to require coffee.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: That's a pretty low threshold for you.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll bring a thermos of coffee for the drive.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Excellent. I'm putting a reminder on a blue sticky note: pick up Riley around 6:45, ferry line by 7:30.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Very official. Is the sticky note going to get compared with 4 other sticky notes first?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: No, I already spent too long deciding whether 7:30 was better than 7:15.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Let's keep 7:30 as the hope, not a promise.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Deal. Friday morning, Edmonds to Kingston, and we'll take the queue as it comes.

details_in_summary: Daniel puts a reminder on a blue sticky note.
key_facts: They plan to take the Edmonds–Kingston ferry on Friday morning.
Daniel will pick Riley up in Ballard before driving to the terminal.
They hope to reach the ferry line by 7:30 a.m.
minor_details: Daniel puts a reminder on a blue sticky note.
Riley offers to bring a thermos of coffee.

summary: Riley and Daniel planned a Friday Edmonds–Kingston ferry trip. They preferred the ferry to avoid a longer drive and aimed to reach the line by 7:30 a.m. If the queue is long, they’ll wait, not attempt a big hike. Daniel will drive from Ballard, picking Riley up around 6:45 a.m., then head to the Edmonds terminal, checking traffic closer to the day. A blue sticky note was set as a reminder for pickup and the 7:30 ferry-line goal, treated as hopeful but not guaranteed.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: How are the balcony herbs settling in? The parsley looks a little pale to me.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, those leaves are definitely lighter than they were. The chives look good, though.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: They do. There are several new shoots coming up.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I can see them. The parsley kind of looks like it needs a better spot.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but is there room for it in the brighter east corner?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I think so. Let me move the pot over there.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The leaves look like washed-out lettuce. Not a great advertisement for parsley.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: There, it's in the east corner. Oh, I spilled some soil.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'll move the saucer in closer. Do you want the mint over here too?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I think the mint can stay in the shadier spot. It looks fine where it is.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay. Parsley gets the coveted corner, and mint keeps its privacy.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And I'll brush this spilled soil off the outdoor mat.

details_in_summary: Riley brushes spilled soil off the outdoor mat.
key_facts: The parsley leaves look pale, so they move its pot to the brighter east corner.
The chives have put out several new shoots.
The mint remains in a shadier spot.
minor_details: Riley brushes spilled soil off the outdoor mat.
Maya compares the pale leaves to washed-out lettuce.

summary: Riley discussed balcony herbs with Maya. Observed parsley pale; noted chives healthy and new shoots. Decided to move parsley to the brighter east corner; spilled soil addressed and saucer adjusted. Mint to stay in the shadier spot. Final placements: parsley in the east corner, mint in its current spot; Riley will brush spilled soil from the outdoor mat.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I finished the remaining 12 prints tonight, so that's the whole 30 we picked.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. Did the scanner behave itself?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: More or less. The nearby lamp was catching it, so I used a folded sheet of paper to shade the scanner. A very sophisticated setup.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: As long as it worked. Did you find anything interesting in the last batch?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: A ticket stub tucked behind one print. I nearly missed it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Huh. Is there anything on it that helps with the photograph?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Not anything I'd feel comfortable putting in a caption. But I did want to check a couple of the captions with you.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sure. Which ones?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: There's the photograph of you at a school concert. It has 2001 written on the back.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay, 2001 sounds right. I remember it being a school concert, anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: There's a person standing at the edge of that photograph. Do you know who that is?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I keep thinking I should, but I can't actually make out enough to be sure.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Same here. I had a guess, and then I looked again and wasn't convinced.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Let's leave the name unconfirmed, then. We don't need to turn a guess into a fact.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Agreed. I'll keep the caption to you, the school concert, and 2001, and leave that person's name open.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That works. It's still plenty to help us find the picture.

details_in_summary: She finds a ticket stub tucked behind one print.
key_facts: Hannah scans the remaining 12 prints.
A photograph of Riley at a school concert has 2001 written on its back.
The name of a person standing at the edge of that concert photograph remains unconfirmed.
minor_details: Hannah uses a folded sheet of paper to shade the scanner from a nearby lamp.
She finds a ticket stub tucked behind one print.

summary: Riley and Hannah finished the 30 prints, addressed scanner shading, and found a ticket stub. They reviewed captions for a photo of Riley at a school concert with '2001' on the back and debated an unidentifiable person at the edge. They decided not to confirm the name and to keep the caption as 'the school concert, and 2001,' leaving the name open for now. Action: maintain open caption and verify later.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I've been reviewing the terminology guide, and I think the draft's getting bigger than I can keep current.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is it the number of entries, or how many different areas they cover?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Both, really. Grace suggests leaving transportation terminology out of the initial glossary. I think that's a sensible boundary.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. Let's keep the first release focused on warehouse actions, then. We can make the scope clear in the draft.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I tried narrowing it that way. The draft now contains 12 warehouse action entries.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That feels manageable. Pick and stage are still separate, right?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: They are. And hold has its own definition too, since it affects allocation.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. Oh, that delivery cart squeaking past the meeting room is really announcing itself.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Hard to miss. So, 12 warehouse action entries, no transportation terms in the initial glossary. I'll keep the draft to that scope.

key_facts: Grace suggests leaving transportation terminology out of the initial glossary.
The narrowed draft contains 12 warehouse action entries.
minor_details: A delivery cart squeaks past the meeting room.

summary: Riley and Sam reviewed the terminology guide. They agreed to limit the initial glossary to warehouse actions and exclude transportation terms. The draft will include 12 warehouse action entries; pick and stage remain separate, and hold has its own definition due to allocation effects. They will communicate the scope clearly in the draft and maintain these boundaries for subsequent releases.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, how's the half-marathon training going?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: A little slower than the plan says. My 7-mile run on April 12 was exhausting, more than I expected.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, that rough? Did it feel hard the whole way?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: By the end I was just really tired. And I forgot to charge my headphones before the run, so I had plenty of time to notice.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a long time to be alone with your thoughts.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, they're not all worth 7 miles. Anyway, what if I just eased back instead of trying to push ahead?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds sensible. What are you changing?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I've shortened the next long run, on April 19, to 6 miles, and I'm going to include walk breaks.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds like a good way to make the plan work for you, instead of the other way around.

details_in_summary: Sam forgot to charge their headphones before the tiring run.
key_facts: Sam’s seven-mile run on April 12 felt exhausting.
Sam has shortened the next long run, on April 19, to six miles and plans to include walk breaks.
minor_details: Sam forgot to charge their headphones before the tiring run.

summary: Riley discussed Sam’s half-marathon training progress, noting a 7-mile run on April 12 was exhausting and fatigue plus a missing headphone charge affected the session. Riley suggested adjustments, and Sam decided to ease back by shortening the next long run to 6 miles (April 19) and adding walk breaks to better fit the plan.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Oh, there they are. I left the returned guides in a canvas tote overnight.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: From Saturday's trial? How did it go?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Pretty well. 6 participants came, and the group completed the walk.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's good! Did the guide make sense to people?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Mostly, but 2 participants asked where they could stop before the walk began.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: As in, where they could stop along the route?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. They wanted to know before deciding whether to set out.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm rinsing my breakfast bowl, but I can look at the guide in a second. You did put the seating information in there, didn't you?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I did. But I think I made them work too hard to find it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay. So bring it up earlier?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'm going to move the seating information to the front of the guide. That way it's there when people are deciding.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Next to the distance, maybe? The bit about the park and no bench on the route.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yes. Seating at Ballard Commons Park near the library, and no public bench on the out-and-back stretch.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you were already planning to mention seating before everyone left.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Right. Okay, but it should be easy to find on paper too. The guide shouldn't make people go on a small expedition to find out where they can sit.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Seems like a useful thing to change before another walk.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That's what I'm thinking. I'll make that small revision before offering another one, rather than expand the route right away.

key_facts: Six participants attended the trial, and the group completed the walk.
Two participants asked where they could stop before the walk began.
Maya plans to move the seating information to the front of the guide.
minor_details: She left the returned guides in a canvas tote overnight.
Riley rinses a breakfast bowl while they talk.

summary: Riley and Maya discussed Saturday's trial with 6 participants and a completed walk. Feedback indicated seating information was hard to find; two participants asked for stop locations before starting. Riley suggested adjusting the guide to include seating details earlier. Maya agreed to move seating to the front, near distance, noting seating at Ballard Commons Park and no bench on the out-and-back. The plan is to implement this revision before the next walk, rather than expanding the route.

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: Hi, Riley. Nice to have a little daylight at lunch, isn't it?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, Dolores. Yeah, it makes the middle of the day feel less like a blur.

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: It does. Oh, I meant to tell you how the half-marathon training's going.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How's it been? Last time we talked, you were figuring out the long runs.

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: I got up to 7 miles on March 21. I was pretty pleased with that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: 7 miles! How did it feel?

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: Good, mostly. The wind was strong on the way home, though. Made the last bit feel longer than it was.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds like an unfair way to end a run.

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: The wind didn't seem concerned. Anyway, then I got a cold.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, are you feeling better?

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: I am now. But I missed the week of April 6 through April 12 with it. No running at all.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's frustrating, especially after getting to 7 miles.

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: Yeah. I don't want to just jump straight back in where I left off.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So are you changing the schedule a little?

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: I am. I'm moving this week's long run to Saturday so I can build back gradually. It'll be a shorter one.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Instead of your usual Sunday run?

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: Right. I've got the revised schedule on a yellow sticky note on my fridge. Very official.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Well, it's easy to revise if you need to.

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: Exactly. I can listen to how I feel and move things around again. Worth a try.

details_in_summary: She has a yellow sticky note on her fridge with her revised schedule.
key_facts: Dolores reached seven miles on March 21.
She missed the week of April 6 through April 12 with a cold.
She's moving this week's long run to Saturday so she can build back gradually.
minor_details: She mentions that the wind was strong on the way home from the seven-mile run.
She has a yellow sticky note on her fridge with her revised schedule.

summary: Riley and Dolores discussed Dolores's half-marathon training. Dolores reached 7 miles on March 21, with wind affecting the final stretch, then had a cold and missed the week of April 6–12. She plans to ease back by moving this week's long run to Saturday for a shorter session, with a revised schedule on a yellow sticky note. Riley noted the plan and emphasized listening to how she feels and adjusting the schedule as needed.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Oh, that's better. The 12 warehouse action entries look a lot less intimidating on their own.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, leaving transportation terms out gave them some room. Morning, by the way.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Morning. Now I need to tell people how to suggest changes without putting another glossary above the glossary.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Could you put a couple of sentences at the top of the page?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: What if there's a linked form? Colleagues could submit a proposal with an example and its source.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That makes sense. An example gives you something to check, rather than just 'I don't like this word.'

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Exactly. And I'll review suggested changes on the 1st Wednesday of each month. Not every morning with my tea.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So, 'Suggest a change using the linked form. Include an example and its source.' Then the review schedule?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yes. 'Sam reviews suggestions on the 1st Wednesday of each month.' Short and mildly alarming in the 3rd person.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll add a note too: 'Don't change product copy solely on the strength of a glossary entry.'

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Good. The entry might be useful, but people still need to check what the screen actually does.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, there's a spare highlighter under this chair. I was looking for one.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Nice. And apparently my water bottle's silver lid has a scratch on it. Actually, several scratches. It's had a harder week than I have.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The instructions are still short enough for the top of the page, even with my note.

details_in_summary: Sam’s water bottle has a scratched silver lid.
Riley finds a spare highlighter under a chair.
key_facts: Sam will review suggested changes on the first Wednesday of each month.
Colleagues will submit proposals through a linked form with an example and source.
Riley adds a note asking contributors not to change product copy solely on the strength of a glossary entry.
minor_details: Sam’s water bottle has a scratched silver lid.
Riley finds a spare highlighter under a chair.

summary: Riley and Sam discussed clarifying glossary usage. Riley proposed adding a top-page note with guidance: suggest a change via a linked form, including an example and its source. Sam suggested a linked form proposal process, and a monthly review on the 1st Wednesday (not daily). Riley added a cautionary note: don’t change product copy solely on glossary entries. The page should remain concise, remain useful with examples, and reflect the screen’s actual function. They noted a spare highlighter and a scratched water bottle during the discussion.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How do things stand with the kitchen?

dialogue.speaker: Elena
dialogue.text: The new cabinets are in at our house, which is nice. But the countertop's delayed, so we still don't have a kitchen sink.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, no. How much longer?

dialogue.speaker: Elena
dialogue.text: Looks like another week. That'll be our 2nd week without a sink.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Where are you and Mira washing dishes?

dialogue.speaker: Elena
dialogue.text: In the bathroom. There's a blue checked dish towel in there now, so it almost looks intentional.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And where are you actually making food?

dialogue.speaker: Elena
dialogue.text: We've set up a temporary meal station in the dining room. The electric kettle's plugged in next to a bowl of apples.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's not the worst setup. What have you been eating?

dialogue.speaker: Elena
dialogue.text: Well, I made peanut butter toast for dinner. I wouldn't call it a renovation menu, exactly.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Still, cabinets in is something.

dialogue.speaker: Elena
dialogue.text: It is. I'm trying to focus on that rather than the bathroom full of dishes.

details_in_summary: Elena mentions making peanut butter toast for dinner.
The electric kettle is plugged in next to a bowl of apples.
key_facts: Elena and Mira’s new kitchen cabinets have been installed.
The countertop is delayed, leaving them without a kitchen sink for a second week.
They are washing dishes in the bathroom.
Their temporary meal station is in the dining room.
minor_details: Elena mentions making peanut butter toast for dinner.

Dishes are being washed in the bathroom, with a temporary meal station in the dining room using an electric kettle and apples. Dinner has been peanut butter toast. Next steps: wait for countertop and sink installation, and maintain the temporary setup while focusing on cabinets being in.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Oh, good, I caught you. I've just started a rainy-day list for Astoria.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey! What's on it so far?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: The Columbia River Maritime Museum, for one. I'm interested in the old ship models.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds like a good place to spend a wet afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah. I'm also considering the Flavel House Museum. I don't know if we'd want to do both, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You could just keep them as options and see what you feel like.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That's what I'm thinking. I've got them in this small spiral notebook, which, in theory, will keep me from making 6 different lists.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And then losing 5 of them?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. Anyway, I'll check the museum hours before the trip, but I'm not going to buy advance tickets.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That makes sense. Better to have a couple of options than schedule every hour.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Right. We've already got the train and bus connections to think about. The rest can be a little loose.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And if it's dry, you can just go for a walk instead.

details_in_summary: Hannah makes the list in a small spiral notebook.
key_facts: The Columbia River Maritime Museum is on Hannah's rainy-day list.
She is also considering the Flavel House Museum.
She plans to check museum hours before the trip rather than buy advance tickets.

She is interested in the old ship models.
