summary: Riley discussed the sign text 'Fresh tortillas daily' for Zoe’s grandmother’s grocery in Yakima. They decided to print an 11-by-14 inch image with a narrow border to keep readability, after confirming zoomed-in clarity. The pair noted the bike in the photo and kept expectations modest in size. Greenwood Copy & Print offers the 11-by-14 option for $18, and Zoe placed the order.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Hey. It feels nice to be home this evening.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey. Yeah, I'm glad we got out today, though.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Me too. What did you think of the Island County Historical Museum?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I liked the exhibits on local maritime history. There was a lot to take in.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The display of old ferry photographs was my favorite. Okay, but did we spend longer there than you expected?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A little, yeah. I didn't mind. We still had time for the walk after lunch.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: And we got to do part of the prairie trail at Ebey's Landing instead of the waterfront.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm glad the weather held up enough for that. We would've gone farther on a dry day, though.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah, that brief shower sent us back toward the car sooner than we'd planned.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: My shoelaces got muddy anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The rain jackets did their job, at least. The shoelaces apparently had other priorities.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: They can dry out. I'd still call the day a success.

details_in_summary: Riley's shoelaces got muddy.
key_facts: They visited the museum's exhibits on local maritime history.
They walked part of the prairie trail at Ebey's Landing.
A brief shower sent them back toward the car sooner than planned.
minor_details: Riley's shoelaces got muddy.
Maya liked a display of old ferry photographs.

summary: Riley discussed a day spent visiting the Island County Historical Museum, noting the maritime history exhibits and the ferry photographs as highlights. They spent a bit longer than expected but continued with a walk, including part of the prairie trail at Ebey's Landing. Weather affected plans due to a brief shower, though rain jackets performed well and shoelaces got muddy. Riley considered the day a success and mentioned adapting plans for a drier outing.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: Oh, good. I'm still relieved those library copies came in. We don't have to change our plans for June.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, you told me on May 13 that the remaining copies had come in, right?

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: Right. On April 11, I realized several members were still waiting for library copies of A Psalm for the Wild-Built. I was a little worried about the timing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: But now everyone's had a chance to read it before June 17.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: Exactly. Actually, wait, I don't know who's finished it. But they've had the chance, at least.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair distinction. And we can keep it informal like we talked about.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: Yes. I'll welcome everyone, and you can keep an eye on the time. A very small bureaucracy.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And we'll leave a few minutes for final thoughts. I'll still bring the sticky notes.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: Thank you. Oh, that's Nabil making rice in the kitchen, by the way.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It smells good. I'm glad the book situation worked out, too.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: Me too. I can cross 'worry about library copies' off my list.

details_in_summary: Nabil is making rice in the background while Fatima talks.
key_facts: On April 11, Fatima realized several members were still waiting for library copies.
On May 13, Fatima told Riley that the remaining copies had come in.
minor_details: Nabil is making rice in the background while Fatima talks.

summary: Riley and Fatima discussed library copies of A Psalm for the Wild-Built, confirming copies arrived and that readings were available before June 17. They decided to keep the gathering informal, with Fatima welcoming attendees and Riley monitoring time, leaving room for final thoughts and sticky notes. Fatima noted relief at the book situation and planned to cross off the worry from her list. Other notes: Nabil is cooking rice in the kitchen; no one is sure who’s finished the book yet.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I'm putting this bottle with the blue lid on your desk. Want to help me judge some iced tea?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sure. You made it?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, at home. We've got a few minutes between afternoon meetings, so I thought we could taste it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What's in it?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Black tea and lemon. I brewed the tea for 6 minutes, then added the lemon.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay, let me try it.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Be honest. The bottle's feelings won't be hurt.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It's a little bitter. The lemon's nice, though.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, I get that too. It's a bit stronger than I meant it to be.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe the tea brewed too long?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Could be. What if I try a shorter brew next time? Easier to tell what's making it bitter if I just change that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds good. This first batch needs a little work.

key_facts: Sam brewed black tea for six minutes and added lemon.
Riley finds the tea a little bitter.
minor_details: Sam carries it in a bottle with a blue lid.
They taste it between afternoon meetings.

summary: Riley and Sam evaluated an iced tea from a home brew. They noted black tea with lemon, brewed 6 minutes, resulting in some bitterness but pleasant lemon. They discussed adjusting brew time as the likely cause. Decision: try a shorter brew next batch to isolate bitterness. Action: Sam to brew a shorter batch for comparison; acknowledge that the first batch needs work.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: And the connections were actually manageable, both ways. I spent a lot of time worrying about them for nothing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. How was the train down to Portland?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Fine, and we got the POINT bus from Portland to Astoria without a problem. Having that space between them helped.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And coming home? You picked the earlier bus, right?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I did. The return bus got into Portland about 12 minutes late, but we still caught our train to Tacoma.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty good argument for not making the connection too tight.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes. My gift to myself was 12 minutes of not panicking.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you get the rain they were predicting for Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: We did. So Owen and I went to the Columbia River Maritime Museum on Saturday. It was nice having an indoor option without having to make the whole day into a schedule.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you manage any time by the water?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: We did. Owen found a bench near the water with chipped blue paint. We sat there for a bit.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And how was the food? That's an important part of the report.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I had salmon chowder for lunch, which was very good. And I bought a postcard with a picture of a tugboat, so I was apparently committed to the maritime theme.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds like a good weekend, even with the rain.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It really was. Having a few options instead of a plan for every hour made it much easier to enjoy.

details_in_summary: Hannah had salmon chowder for lunch.
key_facts: The train and bus connections worked in both directions.
Hannah and Owen visited the Columbia River Maritime Museum on the rainy Saturday.
Their return bus arrived in Portland about 12 minutes late, but they still caught their train.
minor_details: Hannah had salmon chowder for lunch.
She bought a postcard with a picture of a tugboat.
Owen found a bench with chipped blue paint near the water.

summary: Riley summarized Hannah’s weekend: travel to Portland and Astoria with manageable connections, opting for an earlier return to avoid tight transfers. Indoor optional activities were used during rainy weather, including a visit to the Columbia River Maritime Museum. Time by the water and a salmon chowder lunch with a maritime-themed postcard complemented a flexible plan rather than a strict schedule, which reduced stress and improved enjoyment.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, the turntable's back. I picked it up from the shop on June 7.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. Did they replace the leads?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, they replaced the RCA leads. And my first test at home was completely free of the hum.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Seriously? Even before the needle hit the record?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. That was the part I was listening for, and there was nothing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's such a relief after all that messing around with the preamp and the ground wire.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: It is. The new plugs have red and white collars, by the way. Very exciting development.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Well, at least you won't have to spend 3 weeks comparing collars.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I appreciate your confidence in me.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So was the cheap turntable worth the trouble?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I think so, yeah. Especially now I can put a record on without listening for that hum.

details_in_summary: The replacement plugs have red and white collars.
key_facts: The shop replaced the RCA leads, and Daniel picked up the turntable on June 7.
His first test at home was free of the hum.
minor_details: The replacement plugs have red and white collars.

summary: Daniel picked up the turntable on June 7 with RCA leads replaced. Riley noted the home test showed no hum even before the needle touched a record. New plugs have red and white collars. Riley concluded the cheap turntable is worth it and that the hum problem is resolved, with no further action planned.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: I'm still working on this mug of ginger tea. Thanks for waiting, by the way. My bus was running late.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: No problem. Did you ever get through that box in the hall closet?

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: I did, actually. I found 2 cassettes from that college radio show on Thursday, April 30.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, the one we listened to when we were roommates?

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Yeah. And I asked you that day which one had the campus-band session. Do you remember now?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I remember the session, but I couldn't tell you which tape it's on.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Fair enough. The labels aren't helping me much either.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Have you been able to play them?

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Yeah. On Tuesday, June 2, I tested both cassettes in a deck I borrowed from Dalia.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And they still work?

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: They both played. One sounded muffled, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's better than neither of them playing, I guess.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Definitely. I still want to make digital copies of both before I return the deck to Dalia.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good idea. Then you can figure out which one has the band without wearing the tapes out.

key_facts: On Thursday 30 April, Marcus found two cassettes and asked Riley which one had the campus-band session.
On Tuesday 2 June, Marcus tested both cassettes in a deck borrowed from Dalia; both played, though one sounded muffled.
Marcus plans to make digital copies before returning the deck.
minor_details: Marcus has a mug of ginger tea.
He mentions that his bus was running late.

summary: Riley discussed Marcus discovering two cassettes from a college radio show on Thursday, April 30, found in the hall closet. They recalled the campus-band session but couldn’t identify which tape it was. Marcus tested both cassettes on June 2 with a borrowed deck; both played, one muffled. They agreed Marcus will digitize both cassettes before returning the deck to Dalia to determine which tape contains the band session.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How are things going with your sourdough lately?

dialogue.speaker: Lucia
dialogue.text: Not brilliantly. My last 2 loaves came out noticeably flat. They spread out in the oven instead of rising up.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Both of them? What did you do for the bulk fermentation?

dialogue.speaker: Lucia
dialogue.text: I gave each dough 4 hours. That's my usual time.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And your kitchen's probably warmer now, isn't it?

dialogue.speaker: Lucia
dialogue.text: Yes. It was about 76°F when I baked the second loaf.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That could make a difference. The dough might be fermenting faster, so 4 hours is too long.

dialogue.speaker: Lucia
dialogue.text: That would explain the way it felt. The second one was quite soft by the end, and it didn't hold its shape very well.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did it still taste okay?

dialogue.speaker: Lucia
dialogue.text: It did. Just made rather short sandwiches.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, you've got flour on the cuff of your cardigan.

dialogue.speaker: Lucia
dialogue.text: Ah. I thought I'd managed to get it all off. Apparently not.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm carrying a paper bag of cherries, so I'm not exactly traveling light either.

dialogue.speaker: Lucia
dialogue.text: At least yours is contained. Mostly.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So the warmer kitchen might be the thing, rather than anything wrong with the flour or starter.

dialogue.speaker: Lucia
dialogue.text: Maybe. I don't know for certain, but 4 hours in a warm kitchen could be more rise than the dough needs.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, sounds worth keeping the temperature in mind.

key_facts: Lucia's last two loaves came out noticeably flat.
She had given each dough a four-hour bulk fermentation.
Her kitchen was about 76°F when she baked the second loaf.
minor_details: Lucia had flour on the cuff of her cardigan.
Riley was carrying a paper bag of cherries.

summary: Riley and Lucia discussed Lucia's flat sourdough loaves. Lucia had 4 hours bulk fermentation in a kitchen around 76°F, which Riley noted could accelerate fermentation and prevent proper rise. They concluded the warmer temperature might be the issue, not flour or starter, and suggested considering shorter fermentation times in warm conditions. Lucia reported the loaves tasted okay but were soft and short; Riley emphasized monitoring kitchen temperature for future batches.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, how do things stand at work this evening?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Not too bad. Daphne asked me to review the event sign-up process at the Swasey branch. Apparently it's giving people some trouble.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What sort of trouble?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Well, staff have noticed patrons hesitating over the field labeled 'Registrant.' I can see why. It's a very official way to say, well, the person signing up.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'd probably pause there too. Are you going to change it?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Not straight away. I want to watch where people get stuck first, rather than rewriting the form and assuming I've fixed it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That makes sense. Have you started keeping notes?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Just the first ones, on the back of a program flyer. A very sophisticated system, in theory. Oh, and I've got a cup of peppermint tea beside me, so I'm properly equipped for this call.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A flyer and peppermint tea. Sounds like a solid start.

details_in_summary: Hannah made her first notes on the back of a program flyer.
key_facts: Daphne asked Hannah to review the event sign-up process at the Swasey branch.
Staff have noticed patrons hesitating over the field labeled 'Registrant.'
minor_details: Hannah made her first notes on the back of a program flyer.
She had a cup of peppermint tea beside her when she called.

summary: Riley discussed the Swasey branch event sign-up issue. Hannah reported that the 'Registrant' field is confusing patrons, causing hesitation. Riley noted the plan to delay changes and observe where users struggle first. Hannah has started collecting notes on the back of a program flyer as a lightweight data-collection method. Action items: continue observation of user interactions, compile notes to inform potential form revisions.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Oh, good, we got the straw down before it got too late.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. I think we got a decent layer around the established plants.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: And we left the carrot row clear. Those little seedlings don't need to fight their way through straw too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hopefully it'll help the soil hold moisture, especially at the far end. That was so much drier than the near end.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but how do we tell how much water it needs now that we can't see all the soil?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: We could just move a bit of straw aside and stick a finger in the soil before we water.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. Let's check with a finger first, then decide how much water each part needs.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Rather than giving the whole bed the same amount and hoping for the best.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Exactly. Our previous irrigation system was mostly optimism.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, I've still got a strand of straw stuck to my sleeve.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Well, at least we brought a tiny bit of the garden home.

details_in_summary: A strand of straw stuck to Riley’s sleeve.
key_facts: They spread straw mulch around the established plants, leaving the carrot row clear.
They agree to check the soil with a finger before deciding how much to water.
minor_details: A strand of straw stuck to Riley’s sleeve.

summary: Riley and Maya discussed mulching with straw to protect established plants and keep the carrot row clear, aiming to improve soil moisture at the dry end. They planned to check soil moisture by inserting a finger before watering, and to water each part based on need rather than a uniform amount, avoiding the previous optimistic irrigation approach. Riley noted straw on a sleeve; they both took the garden home lightly.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I've got the fare comparison open in 2 browser tabs, and I'm already tired of looking at it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: For the October visit to Emeka in Montreal?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. One itinerary connects through Toronto and the other through Chicago.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is there much difference in price?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The Chicago option is about $90 cheaper, but it has a 7-hour layover.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oof. That's a long time to spend in an airport for $90.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. I keep trying to make it sound reasonable. It's only, what, several meals and a complete personality change?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You could get some work done, but then you're starting the visit with a pretty long travel day.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right. And the whole point was to have some ordinary time with Emeka, not turn the trip into an endurance event.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What about the Toronto connection? Is that travel day any better?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: It looks shorter overall. I need to look more closely at the connection, though, not just the total time.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And make sure the dates work with your time off before you get too attached to either one.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Exactly. I haven't booked either option. What if I check the time off first, then compare how much of the day each flight takes?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds sensible. And if Chicago still looks good, you can decide whether 7 hours is worth the $90.

details_in_summary: The cheaper itinerary includes a seven-hour layover.
key_facts: One itinerary connects through Toronto and another through Chicago.
The Chicago option is about $90 cheaper.
Sam has not booked either option.
minor_details: Sam has the fare comparison open in two browser tabs.
The cheaper itinerary includes a seven-hour layover.

summary: Riley discussed fare options for an October visit to Emeka in Montreal. Two itineraries: through Toronto (shorter travel day) and through Chicago (about $90 cheaper but with a 7-hour layover). They agreed to verify dates against time off first, then analyze each option’s layover and total travel time before deciding if Chicago’s savings are worth the long layover.

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.text: Riley, can you help me choose 2 photos for my aunt Farah? I'm visiting her in Tacoma on Sunday, June 14.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, of course. What are the options?

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.text: I've got a few on my phone. Hang on, let me get the tomato soup out of the way first.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, you've got a small crack in the corner of your phone screen.

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.text: I do. It adds character, apparently. Okay, here's Farah in her garden.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I like that one. She's got a really good smile.

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.text: I thought so too. And here's one of Farah and me at a family picnic.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That one's lovely. What else have you got?

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.text: Another garden photo, but Farah isn't in it. Hang on, I think the first 2 are better for her.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Agreed. The garden one with Farah and the picnic one of you both.

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.text: Good. I'll order 2 5-by-7-inch prints for pickup at a photo shop in Fremont.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Can you get the order in before you have to go back to work?

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.text: Yep, just did. Both prints are ordered for pickup. And I still have soup left, so this is a remarkably efficient lunch.

key_facts: Aisha plans to visit Farah in Tacoma on Sunday, June 14.
They choose a photo of Farah in her garden and one of Farah and Aisha at a family picnic.
Aisha orders two 5-by-7-inch prints for pickup at a Fremont photo shop.
minor_details: Aisha has tomato soup for lunch.
Riley notices a small crack in the corner of Aisha's phone screen.

summary: Riley helped Aisha select two photos for her aunt Farah: a garden shot with Farah and a garden/picnic photo of Farah with Aisha. They decided on those two and placed a 2× 5-by-7 inch print order for pickup at a Fremont photo shop, before Riley returned to work. Action item: pickup the ordered prints.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, Maren approved the revised mix on June 10.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. The softer opening worked for them?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, and I brought the feed dispenser up a little, like they asked. It's more noticeable now without taking over.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So you can stop comparing those fades?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: In theory. I checked the mix once more with the suite door closed, just to make sure I wasn't hearing the room along with it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And did you leave it alone after that?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I did. Please note the personal growth.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm proud of you. What's next?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I'm getting the audio ready for a test on the visitor center's actual playback hardware.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What are they playing it through?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: A touch-screen kiosk. So I want to hear what the mix does on that, rather than just in the suite.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is it a different file from the one Maren approved?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Same approved mix. The approved file is a stereo WAV at 48 kHz.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And how are you getting it over there?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I used a silver USB drive for the transfer copy. The export folder also has a text file with version notes, so I don't have to squint at filenames and guess.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A very sensible system, which I assume took you 20 minutes to choose.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, it took a little while. But I only have the 1 silver drive, so that narrowed it down.

details_in_summary: Daniel checked the mix once more with the suite door closed.
He used a silver USB drive for the transfer copy.
key_facts: Maren approved the revised mix on June 10.
The approved file is a stereo WAV at 48 kHz.
The visitor center will play it through a touch-screen kiosk.
minor_details: Daniel checked the mix once more with the suite door closed.
He used a silver USB drive for the transfer copy.
His export folder contains a text file with version notes.

summary: Daniel reports Maren approved the revised mix on June 10. Adjustments: softer opening and increased feed dispenser visibility; fades no longer being compared. He tested with the suite door closed. Next, he will prepare the audio for tests on the visitor center's touch-screen kiosk using the same 48 kHz stereo WAV. Transfer uses a silver USB drive with version notes; selection took about 20 minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Oh, right, the desk! I cleaned it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You did? How'd it go?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Pretty well. Just mild soap and water, nothing fancy. I didn't want to start with anything too harsh.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did that get most of the grime off?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah. There was a paper label stuck on, though. I got it off with a plastic scraper.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And what did you use to clean it?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: A cloth that used to be a pillowcase. Very specialized equipment.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Keeping the $40 desk budget under control.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That's the idea. I've started comparing finishes, too. I tested paste wax and water-based satin polyurethane on separate patches underneath.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Can you see much difference between them?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: A little. I like the softer look of the wax, but I'm not sure it'll protect the top enough.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the polyurethane?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It looks a bit more finished, I guess. In theory it should give the top more protection, which is tempting.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Especially if you're going to be putting things on it.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. But the top has a thin wood veneer, so I intend to avoid heavy sanding. I don't want to go through it trying to make it perfect.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That seems sensible. You can live with a few scuffs.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I can. I'm still weighing the look against the protection, but the test patches helped.

details_in_summary: The cleaning cloth used to be a pillowcase.
key_facts: Hannah cleaned the desk with mild soap and water.
She tested paste wax and water-based satin polyurethane on separate patches underneath.
The top has a thin wood veneer, so she intends to avoid heavy sanding.
minor_details: A stuck-on paper label came off with a plastic scraper.
The cleaning cloth used to be a pillowcase.

summary: Riley discussed cleaning a desk with Hannah (mild soap, label removal, improvised cloth). They kept the $40 budget in mind. Riley and Hannah compared finishes on test patches: paste wax (softer look, less protection) vs water-based satin polyurethane (more protection and finish). Given the thin veneer, they plan to avoid heavy sanding. Action items: continue patch testing and decide on a finish balancing look and protection.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. How's your Friday afternoon treating you?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty well. I'm still waking up from lunch, though.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, my brain's moving at a very reasonable walking speed.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Anything good going on?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Actually, Becca's starting an after-work tabletop-game group. She invited me to come try it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. When's the first one?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: June 18. She texted me about it while I was waiting for the light rail.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Where are you meeting?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Becca arranged to meet at a game shop in the University District. Apparently it has a bright yellow awning, so I should be able to find it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's helpful. Are you going to go?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I think so. I like tabletop games, and it'd be fun to see what she has in mind.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Do you know what you're playing?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Not yet. Or, well, she didn't say in the text. I'm happy to learn something new.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds like a good way to spend an evening.

details_in_summary: The shop has a bright yellow awning.
key_facts: The first gathering is planned for June 18.
Becca has arranged to meet at a game shop in the University District.
minor_details: Sam heard about it in a text while waiting for the light rail.
The shop has a bright yellow awning.

summary: Riley discussed Becca starting an after-work tabletop-game group. The first session is June 18 at a game shop in the University District with a bright yellow awning. Sam is inclined to attend, hoping to learn what games will be played, but no specific game was confirmed yet. No other decisions were made.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. Okay, so, nice morning, huh? Feels like a good slow Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey. Yeah, I'm not in a hurry to do much today.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I've been thinking about growing some cooking herbs in my new apartment. I'm tired of buying a whole bunch for one meal.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, that'd be nice. Do you have a spot for them?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: The kitchen windowsill at my Fremont place gets afternoon light. Seems like a reasonable place to start.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What made you think of it?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I threw away half a bunch of cilantro after making tacos. It just felt silly buying all of that for one meal.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I've done that. Are you thinking seeds or little plants?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Young plants, not seeds. I'd rather start with something already growing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair. Do you know which herbs you want?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Not yet. I'll probably spend an unreasonable amount of time deciding. College-era committee of 1, back in session.

key_facts: Daniel plans to start with young plants rather than seeds.
His Fremont kitchen windowsill gets afternoon light.
minor_details: He mentions throwing away half a bunch of cilantro after making tacos.

summary: Riley and Daniel discussed starting a small herb garden in Daniel's Fremont apartment. They considered using the kitchen windowsill with afternoon light and starting with young plants rather than seeds. Riley noted practicality of avoiding waste. Daniel will decide which herbs to plant, likely spending time choosing, with no concrete purchase plan yet.

dialogue.speaker: Yuki
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. It's a nice afternoon for a walk.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey! Yeah, I'm glad we got out.

dialogue.speaker: Yuki
dialogue.text: It's already June 13. Somehow that feels a little quick.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It really does. How's your corner bed at Canal Street doing?

dialogue.speaker: Yuki
dialogue.text: Better, actually. The replacement radish plants have put out several leaves now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good! After the slugs got the first seedlings, I wasn't sure how the second sowing would do.

dialogue.speaker: Yuki
dialogue.text: Neither was I. I've started checking the bed in the evenings, and I pick off any slugs I find by hand.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You just pick them up? You're braver than I am.

dialogue.speaker: Yuki
dialogue.text: I have an old yogurt container with me. It makes the whole operation feel a little more official.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The Canal Street slug collection department.

dialogue.speaker: Yuki
dialogue.text: Exactly. A very small department, with a very unappealing inventory.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is it helping?

dialogue.speaker: Yuki
dialogue.text: The plants are looking better. I can't say for certain it's all down to me, but I'm going to keep checking.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Any other hazards on slug patrol?

dialogue.speaker: Yuki
dialogue.text: Well, my shoelace came loose and kept catching on my other shoe. I was paying so much attention to the bed that I nearly tripped.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The slugs almost got their revenge.

dialogue.speaker: Yuki
dialogue.text: They did, yes. I'll remember to tie it next time. In theory.

details_in_summary: Yuki uses an old yogurt container while checking the bed.
key_facts: By June 13, the replacement plants have put out several leaves.
Yuki has begun checking the bed in the evenings.
Yuki removes slugs by hand during those checks.
minor_details: Yuki uses an old yogurt container while checking the bed.
A loose shoelace kept catching on Yuki's other shoe.

Yuki is patrolling evenings, removing slugs by hand with a yogurt container. The plants look better, and the effort will continue. A near-trip occurred when Yuki’s shoelace loosened; Riley noted the need to tie it next time. Action item: maintain slug patrol and secure laces.

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: I'm just heading out to pick up my race bib.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, right, the half-marathon's tomorrow. Where do you get the bib?

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: Ballard Community Center. I'm going over there this afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And how are you getting to the start tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: I'm planning to take the bus in the morning. Seems simpler than worrying about parking.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, especially before a long run. Feeling ready?

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: I think so. I've even laid out my running clothes, including a pair of blue socks. Very organized for once.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: After building back from that cold, it must feel good to be this close.

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: It does. I'm trying not to fuss over every little thing now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Well, good luck tomorrow, Dolores.

details_in_summary: She's laid out a pair of blue socks with her running clothes.
key_facts: Dolores plans to pick up her race bib at Ballard Community Center that afternoon.
She intends to take the bus to the start the next morning.
minor_details: She's laid out a pair of blue socks with her running clothes.

summary: Dolores plans to pick up her race bib at Ballard Community Center this afternoon and will take the bus to the half-marathon start tomorrow. She has laid out running clothes and blue socks, indicating readiness after recovering from a cold. She aims not to fuss over minor details. Riley noted the near-race timing and offered luck for the event. Action items: pick up bib; take bus; finalize pre-race prep.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The balcony herbs are looking pretty uneven. I’m going to make some tea with the mint while we take stock.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The mint’s doing great, and so are the chives. The parsley’s growing, just a lot more slowly.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but for our patch of shade, 2 thriving herbs out of 4 isn’t terrible.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Especially since the basil got all long and thin instead of filling out.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Right. And we already said we wouldn’t replace it if it dies. Is the parsley worth keeping, do you think?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I think so, as long as we’re happy waiting longer for it. We did get some for that lemon dressing.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Mm. I’m drinking the mint tea from the blue mug, and I have to say, the mint’s making a strong case for itself.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. If we plant balcony herbs again, I’d prioritize the mint and chives.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Me too. As of June 13, those are definitely the ones thriving out there.

key_facts: By June 13, the chives and mint are thriving, while the parsley is growing more slowly.
Maya and Riley decide they would prioritize chives and mint if they plant balcony herbs again.
minor_details: Maya drinks the mint tea from a blue mug.

summary: Riley and Maya reviewed balcony herbs: mint and chives thriving; parsley growing slowly; basil too elongated. They discussed not replacing basil if it dies and whether parsley is worth keeping. Mint tea was mentioned. For future plantings, they agreed to prioritize mint and chives, with June 13 noting these two as definitely thriving.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: So I got the instructions for the pottery class, and thankfully I don't have to buy a whole set of tools.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. I was wondering what they'd expect you to bring.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: The studio provides the clay and tools. They just ask students to bring an apron.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty manageable list.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah. In theory I can handle remembering 1 apron.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Do you already have one?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I do. I've got a canvas tote set aside by the door, so I'll put it in there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And what are you wearing? Is it going to be messy?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm planning to wear an old pair of sneakers. I figure I won't be too precious about them.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds like you're all set for Thursday.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Pretty much. It's nice not to have to compare 15 little tool sets before I even start.

details_in_summary: Hannah plans to wear an old pair of sneakers.
She has a canvas tote set aside by the door.
key_facts: The studio will provide clay and tools.
Students are asked to bring an apron.
minor_details: Hannah plans to wear an old pair of sneakers.
She has a canvas tote set aside by the door.

Hannah will bring an apron and keep it in a canvas tote by the door. She plans to wear old sneakers to keep them safe from mess. The plan for Thursday is set, avoiding the need to compare multiple tool sets.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: Oh, hello, Riley. It's a nice quiet Sunday afternoon out here.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, Fatima. Hard to believe it's already June 14.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: I know. Oh, hang on. Did you hear that rattle on my bike?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. I think it's coming from the rear fender.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: Actually, wait. There's a loose bolt right here. I've got a multitool in my bag.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Want me to hold the fender steady while you tighten it?

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: Please. There. And just so you know, there are a few dry leaves gathered along the curb behind you.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Got it. I'm holding the fender now. Can you reach the bolt?

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: Yep. It's tight now. And I've got a smudge of grease on my thumb. A souvenir from outside Tern Coffee.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Ha. Let's see if it still rattles. Nope, sounds good.

details_in_summary: A few dry leaves are gathered along the curb.
key_facts: Fatima and Riley stop to talk outside Tern Coffee on the afternoon of June 14.
Riley steadies Fatima’s rear fender while she tightens its loose bolt with the multitool from her bag.
minor_details: A few dry leaves are gathered along the curb.
Fatima gets a smudge of grease on her thumb.

summary: Riley and Fatima discussed a rattling bike noise on June 14. Fatima identified a loose bolt near the rear fender; Riley held the fender while Fatima tightened it with a multitool. They noted leaves along the curb and a grease smear from Tern Coffee. After tightening, Riley tested the ride and found no rattling remains; no further actions required.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I finished the interview with Inez Cole, and I've started putting everyone's words on paper.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How did it go with Inez?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Good. She talked about a small grocery store she remembered. It fits with those everyday places I was hoping people would bring up.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are you going through it now? You've got one earbud in.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'm working with one earbud in while I make dinner. It's not the most efficient arrangement.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And is the ruler for the recipe?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: No, I'm using it to keep my place on the printout. Dinner has enough moving parts without a measuring instrument.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How much do you clean up what people say? I mean, people don't usually talk in neat sentences.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but I don't want to make them sound like they do. I'll remove repeated false starts, but only when taking them out doesn't change the meaning.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So if someone starts over because they're correcting themselves, you'd be careful with that?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Exactly. That might be part of what they mean, not just a stumble. And if I can't make out a word, I mark it as unclear instead of guessing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds readable without making everybody sound like the same person.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That's what I'm aiming for. I want people to recognize their own voices in the words.

key_facts: Inez Cole’s recording includes a memory of a small grocery store.
Maya removes repeated false starts only when doing so doesn’t change the meaning.
She marks unclear words rather than guessing at them.
minor_details: Maya works with one earbud in while making dinner.
She uses a ruler to keep her place on a printout.

summary: Maya finished interviewing Inez Cole and began transcribing. Inez mentioned a small grocery store, aligning with the theme of everyday places. Maya discusses editing approach: keep voice authentic, remove redundant false starts only if meaning stays, mark unclear words, and avoid guessing. Decision: continue transcription with careful handling of corrections and unclear terms; maintain individual voices.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Morning, Grace. How are things standing with the shipment labels?

dialogue.speaker: Grace
dialogue.text: Morning. I wanted to check the wording with you once more before the release.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sure. I've got the review printout here.

dialogue.speaker: Grace
dialogue.text: The one stapled in the top-right corner? That staple always makes me think I'm holding it upside down.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's the one. We reviewed the revised labels together on June 5.

dialogue.speaker: Grace
dialogue.text: Right. We settled on 'Delayed' and 'Awaiting carrier update'.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: 'Delayed' for shipments that are actually delayed, and 'Awaiting carrier update' when we're waiting to hear from the carrier.

dialogue.speaker: Grace
dialogue.text: Exactly. Not 2 kinds of 'Pending' anymore.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. I just wanted to make sure we weren't changing that wording again.

dialogue.speaker: Grace
dialogue.text: What if we keep it as agreed? It makes the distinction without asking people to guess.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Works for me. And they're still slated for the June 18 release?

dialogue.speaker: Grace
dialogue.text: Yes, June 18. Oh, careful, my mug has a chip on the handle.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Ah, I nearly grabbed it by the handle.

dialogue.speaker: Grace
dialogue.text: It's a very minor workplace hazard. So, 'Delayed' and 'Awaiting carrier update' for June 18. Confirmed.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Confirmed. Thanks, Grace.

key_facts: The agreed labels are 'Delayed' and 'Awaiting carrier update'.
Grace and Riley reviewed the revised labels together on June 5.
The labels are slated for the June 18 release.
minor_details: Grace's mug has a chip on the handle.
The review printout is stapled in the top-right corner.

summary: Riley discussed shipment label wording with Grace. They reaffirmed using 'Delayed' and 'Awaiting carrier update' (not 'Pending') and not changing the wording. Both confirmed the June 18 release date with these labels.

dialogue.speaker: Beatrice
dialogue.text: Hello, Riley. Have you managed to get some lunch, or are you living dangerously?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hi, Grandma. I have lunch, thanks. How's your Monday going?

dialogue.speaker: Beatrice
dialogue.text: Quiet enough. I'm still pleased that bedroom window screen is back where it belongs.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You said on Saturday afternoon, June 13, that the patch had fixed the tear. Is it still holding?

dialogue.speaker: Beatrice
dialogue.text: It is. The patch did the trick. Putting the screen back into its frame was the stubborn part.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, was it harder than the actual repair?

dialogue.speaker: Beatrice
dialogue.text: It took longer, certainly. The repair itself was the easy bit.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's always how it goes. The little job turns into the big job.

dialogue.speaker: Beatrice
dialogue.text: The screen and I had a difference of opinion, but I won in the end.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I remember you telling me on May 20 that you'd found a tear in it. I'm glad it's fixed before the warmer nights.

dialogue.speaker: Beatrice
dialogue.text: Me too. I had the radio playing quietly while I worked, which made the whole business a little less irritating.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you leave everything out afterward?

dialogue.speaker: Beatrice
dialogue.text: Just a roll of masking tape on the kitchen table. I noticed it later.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Not bad for a job that put up a fight.

dialogue.speaker: Beatrice
dialogue.text: No, I think I came out ahead. The screen may disagree.

details_in_summary: A roll of masking tape was left on the kitchen table.
key_facts: On May 20, Beatrice told Riley she had found a tear in the screen.
On Saturday afternoon, June 13, Beatrice reported that a patch had fixed the tear.
Getting the screen back into its frame took longer than the repair itself.
minor_details: A roll of masking tape was left on the kitchen table.
Beatrice had the radio playing quietly while she worked.

summary: Riley discussed lunch and daily activities with Beatrice. They reviewed the bedroom window screen repair: the patch fixed the tear and the frame reassembly was the tougher part. Riley noted the work took longer than the repair; Beatrice recalled a difference of opinion but prevailed. They mentioned masking tape left on the kitchen table and plans to fix the screen before warmer nights.

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: Oh, I still can't quite believe I finished that half-marathon yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You did? Congratulations! How did it go?

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: Slower than I'd hoped. I finished in 2 hours and 38 minutes, and my goal was 2 hours and 30 minutes. But I enjoyed it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's great, Dolores. Was there a part you especially liked?

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: The stretch along the water. That was... well, it made the running part feel a little less like work.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A good distraction, then.

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: Yes. And afterward, a volunteer offered me an orange slice. I accepted it without any negotiation.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Probably the best orange slice you've ever had.

dialogue.speaker: Dolores
dialogue.text: It was certainly in the running. Sorry, that was terrible.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll allow it. You earned that one.

details_in_summary: She accepted an orange slice from a volunteer afterward.
key_facts: Dolores finished in 2 hours and 38 minutes, compared with her goal of 2 hours and 30 minutes.
She particularly enjoyed the stretch of the course along the water.
minor_details: She accepted an orange slice from a volunteer afterward.

summary: Riley conveyed congratulations to Dolores on finishing the half-marathon in 2:38, short of the 2:30 goal. Dolores cited the water-side stretch as the highlight and noted accepting an orange slice after the race without negotiation. No follow-up actions or decisions were identified.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How are we looking after the test?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I've been comparing my notes with yours. The main thing is, 2 participants tried to choose an inspection outcome before they'd identified the item.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I wrote that down too. We had those outcomes right there, but they weren't actually ready for them.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I'm circling that note with my purple pen. Very official analysis.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm glad somebody's got a system. My laptop's propped on a folded notebook because I couldn't see the screen properly.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Also a system. So, the outcomes describe the goods, right? Not whether the worker knows what the item is.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. 'Resellable,' 'Damaged' and 'Needs further review' don't really answer the identity question.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: What if we give them a way to say they can't identify it without making that an inspection outcome?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. Otherwise 'Needs further review' could mean two completely different things.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I'll add 'Can't identify item' as a route to a lead, rather than as an inspection outcome.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That gives them somewhere to go if they're stuck. And I'll make the identity confirmation more prominent in the flow.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Good. Not just bigger, though—sorry, I mean, it should be clear that confirming identity comes before recording an outcome.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yes. I'll look at the sequence and how we show that step, not just the size of it.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: And I'll keep the lead route separate from the choices about the goods.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The label condition is still its own field too.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Exactly. Identity, goods condition, label condition. Three different questions, even if the screen would rather they were one.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay. I'll update the flow, and we can compare it with your wording.

key_facts: Two participants tried to choose an inspection outcome before they had identified the item.
Sam will add “Can't identify item” as a route to a lead rather than as an inspection outcome.
Riley will make the identity confirmation more prominent in the flow.
minor_details: Sam circles a note with a purple pen.
Riley's laptop is propped on a folded notebook.

summary: Riley Morgan and Sam Okafor reviewed test outcomes: participants sometimes selected an inspection outcome before identifying the item. They agreed to separate identity confirmation from goods outcomes, add a new lead route 'Can't identify item,' and emphasize identity before recording an outcome. They confirmed three distinct fields—Identity, Goods condition, Label condition—and will update the flow and compare wording. Action: update the flow and align wording.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: Oh, I nearly forgot to tell you! The framed ferry print is home.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good! We collected it on June 13, and I meant to ask where you'd put it.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: It's still wrapped on my dining table. I thought I'd leave it there until I was ready to hang it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Probably safer than leaning it against the wall. How does it look with the mat?

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: That warm ivory mat we chose on May 13 looks just right. And the frame has a narrow dark-brown edge, so it doesn't overwhelm the photograph.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. I'm glad we went with the ivory.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: Me too. Now, I could try hanging it myself, but getting it straight in the hallway might take me until next winter.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I can help. When were you thinking?

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: Would you be free on the evening of June 24? We could figure out the height together. What do you think?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: June 24 in the evening works for me. I'll come over and we'll hang it.

dialogue.speaker: Lian
dialogue.text: Good. I'll keep it wrapped on the table until then.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds good. I'm looking forward to seeing it up.

details_in_summary: The frame has a narrow dark-brown edge.
Lian has left the wrapped frame on her dining table.
key_facts: On May 13, Lian and Riley chose a warm ivory mat.
They collected the framed print on June 13.
Riley will come over on the evening of June 24 to hang it.
minor_details: The frame has a narrow dark-brown edge.
Lian has left the wrapped frame on her dining table.

summary: Riley discussed the framed ferry print arriving on June 13 and its current wrapped state on the dining table. They approved an ivory mat and a narrow dark-brown frame edge. Decision: Riley will help hang the print on the evening of June 24 and determine the hanging height together. Action items: keep the print wrapped on the table until June 24; Riley to visit and assist with installation.

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: Could you share an accessibility tip at an upcoming Harborline design-team meeting?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe. How much preparation are you thinking? I don't have a lot of time to put a presentation together.

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: Not much. It doesn't need to be a presentation. What's one thing you could show the team?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Keyboard navigation, maybe? I could show how to move through an interface without a mouse.

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: That sounds useful. How long would you need?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: 5 minutes, if it's just a quick demonstration. I wouldn't want to make a formal slide deck for it.

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: No slide deck. Just the demonstration is fine.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay. I can show what happens when you tab through controls, and where the focus indicator is.

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: Good. Could you point out what makes it hard to tell where you are?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I can do that. Oh, the office window is open a crack. Is that breeze bothering you?

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: No, it's nice. I'll just move my paper cup of tea away from the edge of the table.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So, 5 minutes of keyboard navigation, no slides. I can manage that.

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: All right, so we have a plan. I'll note that we agreed on it today, Wednesday, June 17, 2026.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Great. Thanks for keeping it short.

key_facts: Priya makes the request on Wednesday, June 17, 2026.
Riley will demonstrate keyboard navigation at an upcoming Harborline design-team meeting.
The demonstration will last five minutes and will not require a formal slide deck.
minor_details: Priya has a paper cup of tea on the table.
Riley mentions that the office window is open a crack.

summary: Riley discussed presenting a quick accessibility tip at the Harborline design-team meeting. The plan is a 5-minute, slide-free demonstration of keyboard navigation, focusing on moving through controls and the focus indicator, plus identifying visibility issues. Priya agreed to the plan and will note it as decided on Wednesday, June 17, 2026.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Oh, hey, I think this is actually working. The little Italian word cards.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You made cards for the course?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. I write new words on index cards and check them the next morning.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Can I see?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Sure. They're held together with a binder clip, which is about as sophisticated as the system gets.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, you have the food words together.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Mm-hm. Cucchiaio means spoon, and forno is oven.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Cucchiaio. I feel like my mouth needs a second to catch up.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Mine too. I keep wanting to add an extra sound in the middle.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And there's olio and sale. Oil and salt, right?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right. Those were 2 of the first ones I learned.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How much time are you spending on this?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: About 5 minutes a day. I do it at the end of breakfast, before I put the cards away.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Do you look at the Italian first?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Usually. I try to say what it means before I turn the card over. Then sometimes I go the other way.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay, test me. What's oven again?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Forno. What if you remember it next to spoon? Cucchiaio, forno. A very small kitchen.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A spoon and an oven. I'll try not to mix those up.

details_in_summary: The cards are held together with a binder clip.
key_facts: Sam has been practicing Italian for about five minutes a day.
Sam learned cucchiaio for spoon and forno for oven.
Sam writes new words on index cards and checks them the next morning.
minor_details: The cards are held together with a binder clip.
Sam practices at the end of breakfast.

summary: Riley discussed learning Italian vocab via handmade index cards created by Sam. Sam uses a binder clip, groups food terms (olio, sale, cucchiaio, forno), and spends about 5 minutes daily. Riley and Sam practice by recalling meanings before flipping cards and testing each other in both directions, focusing on pronunciation and avoiding mix-ups.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: We should figure out what to pack for the peninsula trip. The weather could do just about anything.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, especially for the walk at Salt Creek on Saturday morning.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Have you looked at a forecast yet?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A little, but it's still more than a week away. I don't really trust it yet.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but even if it says sun, can we bring our waterproof shells?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Definitely. And warm layers underneath, in case it's cold by the water.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Good. I'd rather carry a layer than spend the walk wishing I had one.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll put both on the packing list. Shells and warm layers.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: And walking shoes? Also spare dry socks, in case our feet get wet.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yep, walking shoes and spare dry socks. I'll add a small bag of trail mix, too.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but where do we put the wet stuff if it rains?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Do we have a bag we can use for the clothes?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I found a folded tote bag. We can use that for wet clothes.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Perfect. The forecast might look completely different by the time we leave anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'll check it again on Friday morning, June 26, before we head out.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds good. We'll pack for a little uncertainty in the meantime.

details_in_summary: Riley adds a small bag of trail mix to the packing list.
Maya finds a folded tote bag for wet clothes.
key_facts: They decide to bring waterproof shells and warm layers.
They will pack spare dry socks and walking shoes.
Maya plans to check the forecast again on Friday morning.
minor_details: Riley adds a small bag of trail mix to the packing list.
Maya finds a folded tote bag for wet clothes.

summary: Riley and Maya discussed packing for the peninsula trip with weather uncertainty for Salt Creek. They agreed to bring waterproof shells, warm layers, walking shoes, spare dry socks, and a small bag of trail mix, and to use a folded tote bag for wet clothes. The packing list will be updated accordingly. They noted the forecast may change and planned to recheck on Friday morning, June 26, before departure, preparing for potential fluctuations.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. Okay, so, nice evening out, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey. Yeah, it's still light out later than I expect.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I've got a verdict on the turntable, by the way.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. Last I heard, the first test was hum-free.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. I've listened to records on 3 evenings since the repair, and the hum hasn't come back.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty good test. Better than just dropping the needle once and declaring victory.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Which I was tempted to do. But I can overthink a victory as thoroughly as anything else.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So, worth the trouble?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I think so, yeah. Even with the repair, the secondhand purchase was worthwhile. I like listening on it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the new leads did the trick, it sounds like.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. I'm going to keep the Technics and use it rather than shop for an upgrade.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. Where are you keeping the records?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: In a low wooden crate. It's working fine, though 1 listening session ran late because I forgot to turn on a lamp. I just kept listening in the dark.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty solid endorsement, actually.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. The hum was irritating enough that I'd forgotten this was supposed to be fun.

details_in_summary: He has been keeping his records in a low wooden crate.
key_facts: Daniel has listened to records on three evenings since the repair.
He decides to keep the Technics rather than shop for an upgrade.
He considers the secondhand purchase worthwhile despite the repair.
minor_details: He has been keeping his records in a low wooden crate.
One listening session ran late because he forgot to turn on a lamp.

summary: Daniel reported that the turntable repair remains hum-free after three test evenings. Riley noted the improvement and discussed not upgrading, deciding to keep and use the Technics. New leads were effective. Records are stored in a low wooden crate. One long session occurred in darkness due to a forgotten lamp. Overall, a solid endorsement of the repair and ongoing use.

dialogue.speaker: Yuki
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. It's a nice evening, isn't it? Still a bit of light out.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I keep forgetting how late it stays light now. How's your garden bed doing?

dialogue.speaker: Yuki
dialogue.text: Actually, I harvested my first radishes from the Canal Street bed today.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! The ones you replanted after the slugs?

dialogue.speaker: Yuki
dialogue.text: Those are the ones. I carried them home in a paper bag, which felt... appropriately rustic.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Very garden-to-table. What are you going to do with them?

dialogue.speaker: Yuki
dialogue.text: I think I'll eat some with butter and salt. Simple, and in theory, hard to get wrong.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds good. Are the rest of the plants okay while you're away this weekend?

dialogue.speaker: Yuki
dialogue.text: Yes. Miko Sato agreed to water the bed while I'm away. We've worked out when they'll go.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. Your radishes have a whole support system now.

details_in_summary: They plan to eat some with butter and salt.
key_facts: Yuki has harvested the first radishes.
Miko Sato has agreed to water the bed while Yuki is away for the upcoming weekend.
minor_details: Yuki carried the harvest home in a paper bag.
They plan to eat some with butter and salt.

summary: Riley and Yuki discussed garden progress. Yuki harvested the first radishes from the Canal Street bed, replanted after slug damage, and plans to eat some with butter and salt. They arranged for Miko Sato to water the bed this weekend and confirmed the watering schedule. The radish plants now have a support system.

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: Morning, Riley. The light rail was reasonably civilized today, as far as I can tell.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Morning. That's a good start to a Friday.

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: Yeah. Oh, you remember the community garden plot Abena and I got on Beacon Hill?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The 4 by 8 one? How's it going?

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: Pretty well, actually. The watering schedule's been holding through June.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. You were doing Tuesday and Thursday evenings after work, right?

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: Right, and Abena's been doing Sunday mornings. It still fits around our jobs.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And are the greens growing?

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: They are. The first arugula and chard are ready to pick.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, excellent. When are you going to harvest them?

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: Abena and I are planning to do it on Sunday, June 21.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That feels like a pretty good return on a small plot.

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: Yeah, and it hasn't turned into more work than we can manage. That was the hope.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What are you taking to carry everything?

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: I'm going to bring a paper bag. And probably my gloves, although 1 of them has a hole in the thumb.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So 1 thumb gets the full gardening experience.

dialogue.speaker: Kofi
dialogue.text: Exactly. The rest of me remains a cautious observer.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Well, enjoy the harvest. I'm glad the schedule worked out.

details_in_summary: One of Kofi's gardening gloves has a hole in the thumb.
He plans to bring a paper bag for the harvest.
key_facts: The watering schedule has been holding through June.
Their first arugula and chard are ready to pick.
Kofi and Abena plan to harvest the greens on Sunday, June 21.
minor_details: One of Kofi's gardening gloves has a hole in the thumb.
He plans to bring a paper bag for the harvest.

summary: Riley and Kofi discussed their Beacon Hill community garden plot (4x8). The watering schedule has held through June with Tue/Thu evenings and Abena on Sunday mornings. Greens—arugula and chard—are ready to harvest. They plan to harvest on Sunday, June 21. Riley noted they will bring a paper bag and gloves, one of which has a hole. They agreed the arrangement hasn’t become unmanageable and expressed satisfaction with the schedule.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You're looking at flights again?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. My time-off request was approved, so I can finally narrow them down.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! What dates did you get?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: October 21 through October 27. The approval came in while I was on the light rail this morning.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty good commute notification.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Much better than another delay notice. I'm planning to work on October 20 before departing, so I need to check how the flights fit around that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are you still looking at the Toronto and Chicago connections?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. The Chicago option was about $90 cheaper, but it's a longer travel day. Or, sorry, that was the trade-off we were looking at, anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. Now that you know your leave dates, you can see which one actually fits.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: What if I compare the full travel times again before I decide? Cheap is nice, but not if I'm too tired to enjoy being there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Seems sensible. And you still want some time with Emeka that isn't all scheduled.

key_facts: Sam has leave approved for October 21 through October 27.
Sam plans to work on October 20 before departing.
minor_details: The approval arrived while Sam was on the light rail.

summary: Riley reported Sam’s time-off was approved for October 21–27. Sam plans to work on October 20 and then depart, evaluating Toronto and Chicago flight options. The Chicago route is about $90 cheaper but longer travel time. Sam suggested rechecking total travel times before deciding to ensure rest and time with Emeka amid a busy schedule.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I sent each contributor only their own excerpt to review, and Minh got back to me.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, did he want to change something?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. He asked me to omit a sentence about a relative's health.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That makes sense. Was it easy to take out?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: It was. I removed the sentence from both the audio excerpt and the written version.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. I guess even if you got every word right, that doesn't mean he wants all of it on display.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Exactly. It was a useful reminder that the written version isn't neutral just because it's accurate. Choosing what goes in is a choice too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And someone else might be affected by what's in there.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Right. He didn't have to explain the request to me, either. He wanted it out, so it's out.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Have Esther and Inez replied yet?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I haven't checked the rest of my messages yet. I made a cup of peppermint tea before opening them, and Minh's was the first one I read.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A sensible amount of preparation for opening messages on a Friday evening.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but the tea doesn't answer them for me. A serious design flaw.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I can check the page numbers if that would help.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That would be lovely, thanks. I'll look through the rest of these first.

details_in_summary: Riley offers to check the page numbers.
key_facts: Minh asks Maya to omit a sentence about a relative’s health.
Maya removes the sentence from both the audio excerpt and its transcript.
She sends each contributor only their own excerpt for review.
minor_details: Maya makes a cup of peppermint tea before opening her messages.
Riley offers to check the page numbers.

summary: Riley noted Minh's request to omit a sentence about a relative's health; Maya removed it from both audio and written excerpts. Riley highlighted that accuracy alone doesn’t ensure neutrality. They considered responses from Esther and Inez; Maya hadn’t checked them yet and planned to review the rest. Riley offered to check page numbers, and Maya requested them, stating she will skim the remaining messages first.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. Okay, so, how's your Friday evening going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey. Pretty good, actually. Nice to have the week over. How about yours?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Good. I spent a little time on those photo boxes from my mom's house.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, the 3 shoeboxes? Did you start scanning?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Not yet. I made a rough inventory instead, just trying to see what's there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Honestly, sorting first might save you some work. What did you find?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: There are 7 loose envelopes among the photographs. Most of the labels give people or places, but no year.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So you've got some clues, just not much about when.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. And I wrote it all down with a pencil that was missing its eraser, which felt appropriate for a very rough inventory.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A bold choice for someone who likes comparing every option.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I know. I'm trying to grow as a person.

key_facts: Daniel counted seven loose envelopes among the photographs.
Most envelope labels give people or places but no year.
minor_details: Daniel used a pencil with a missing eraser.

summary: Riley discussed Daniel's plan to tackle the photo boxes from his mom's house. Daniel has a rough, pencil-based inventory of seven loose envelopes with labels of people or places but no years. Riley suggested sorting first to save work and consider scanning. Daniel noted the rough inventory and a humorous touch about an eraserless pencil, aiming for personal growth.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: Oh, that discussion really took off, didn't it? I'm still thinking about it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, Wednesday went really well. I was looking back at the questions we compared on June 10.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: The ones about rest and usefulness got everyone talking. I'd expected a pause, at least.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Same. Once we got onto whether rest has to be useful, people had a lot to say.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: Actually, wait, we never got to the question about choice, did we?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: No, and we didn't get to the one about the robots' community either. I kept an eye on the time, but that conversation had its own ideas.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: A very efficient discussion about not needing to be useful. What are you doing, by the way?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, I'm wiping down the kitchen counter while we talk. Sorry, I can stop.

dialogue.speaker: Fatima
dialogue.text: No, you're fine. And I don't mind that we missed those questions. The ones we did reach gave us plenty.

details_in_summary: Riley is wiping down the kitchen counter during the call.
key_facts: The questions about rest and usefulness prompted a lively discussion.
They never got around to the questions about choice and the robots' community.
minor_details: Riley is wiping down the kitchen counter during the call.

summary: Riley discussed Wednesday’s discussion, noting comparison of June 10 questions. Key topics: rest and usefulness, with debate on whether rest must be useful. They acknowledged two questions were not covered: choice and robots’ community. Time management kept the conversation efficient. Riley was wiping the kitchen counter during the call. No explicit actions or follow-up items were stated; participants felt the reached questions were sufficient.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I've been thinking about making a family photo calendar for 2027, for my apartment. Using some of the photographs you and I sorted earlier.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, I like that. A different picture for each month?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah, that's what I had in mind. Would you help me choose the pictures and check the captions? I don't entirely trust myself to remember who's where.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Definitely. We can figure it out together.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Good. I've been making notes on the back of an envelope, which is, in theory, an organizational system.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: As long as you don't throw the envelope away.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
