dialogue.text: That would explain why it looped fine in your editing software. Can they change it?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, they're planning to install a continuous-loop update on July 10. Then I can try the file again.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. Did they give you something to follow up with?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: A support ticket number. I wrote it on a receipt, which is obviously my most reliable filing system.

details_in_summary: Daniel wrote the support ticket number on a receipt.
key_facts: The vendor traced the pause to the kiosk playlist reloading the file at each repeat.
The vendor plans to install a continuous-loop update on July 10.
minor_details: The vendor's reply arrived just before Daniel made dinner.
Daniel wrote the support ticket number on a receipt.

summary: Riley and Daniel discussed a kiosk playback gap causing a 6-second silence. The issue was traced to the kiosk playlist reloading the file on each loop. A continuous-loop update is scheduled for July 10, after which Daniel will retry the file. A follow-up action item is using the provided support ticket number (written on a receipt) to track the fix. Riley noted the pending update and next steps.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: So I did ask Marisol what she hears when I'm not at the desk, and there's another part of that form people aren't sure about.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Not just the 'Contact type' thing?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Right. She's heard patrons ask whether pressing 'Submit' guarantees them a place.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh. And does the form tell them?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Not clearly. The current confirmation screen doesn't mention the waitlist at all.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So someone could see a confirmation and think they're definitely in.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. I jotted down Marisol's comments between shelving carts, and then I went back and looked at the screen.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That seems like a pretty important thing to leave out.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes. In theory, 'Submit' tells you what to do. It doesn't tell you what happens next.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe the wording needs to make that distinction, not just tell people the form went through.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That's what I'm thinking. Whatever wording we settle on should explain what happens after someone submits it, including the possibility of a waitlist.

key_facts: Marisol has heard patrons ask whether pressing 'Submit' guarantees them a place.
The current confirmation screen does not mention the waitlist.
minor_details: Hannah jotted down Marisol's comments between shelving carts.

summary: Riley discussed with Hannah that the form’s confirmation screen does not clearly communicate what happens after submission, including the possibility of a waitlist. They noted patrons may think submission guarantees placement. The plan is to revise wording to differentiate Submit actions from post-submission outcomes and to explicitly explain the waitlist process.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I brought another peach tea sample this morning. I changed one thing from Monday.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. The peach tasted a little cooked last time.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. This time I let the tea cool before adding the peaches.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Can I try it?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Sure. Here, I served it over 2 ice cubes. Very rigorous testing conditions.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Mm. The fruit aroma is fresher this way. It doesn't have that cooked smell.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That's what I noticed too. Or, well, I thought I did, but I wanted a second opinion.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: No, I think cooling it helped. The peach comes through better.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Good. One small victory for letting things sit there.

details_in_summary: Sam serves the sample over two ice cubes.
key_facts: Sam let the tea cool before adding the peaches.
Riley thinks the fruit aroma is fresher this way.
minor_details: Sam serves the sample over two ice cubes.

summary: Riley and Sam compared a peach tea sample. Sam adjusted by cooling the tea before adding peaches and served it over two ice cubes for testing. Riley noted the peach aroma improved and flavors weren’t cooked. They agreed cooling helped and referenced a small success from allowing the mixture to sit; next steps: consider maintaining the cooling step in future tests.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You're really studying that kitchen windowsill. How are the herbs doing?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, the basil gave me a scare. Its soil dried out over 3 days, and it drooped.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh no. Is it still droopy?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: No, I watered it and it perked up. Apparently it was just thirsty, which I did eventually deduce.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A triumphant piece of detective work.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Thank you. I even clipped a few basil leaves for pasta.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. And is that parsley next to the thyme?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, I added a parsley plant to the sill. I found it while I was buying dish soap.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a good shopping trip. Are the basil and thyme still in their nursery pots?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: They are. I wanted to see how they did before buying larger pots, but they're looking pretty crowded now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe give the crowded ones a little more room?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: That's the plan. I'm going to repot the most crowded plants on Sunday, July 12.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You don't have to compare every pot in Seattle first.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I mean, I could. But Sunday might actually arrive before I finish.

details_in_summary: He clipped a few basil leaves for pasta.
key_facts: The basil drooped after its soil dried out over three days, then perked up when Daniel watered it.
Daniel has added a parsley plant to the sill.
He plans to repot the most crowded plants on July 12.
minor_details: He clipped a few basil leaves for pasta.
He found the parsley while buying dish soap.

summary: Riley and Daniel discussed the kitchen herb sill, noting basil recovered after its soil dried out and was watered. Daniel cut basil leaves for pasta and added a parsley plant found while shopping. The basil and thyme remain in nursery pots and are crowded. They plan to repot the most crowded plants on Sunday, July 12, acknowledging that completing this before then may be tight.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, Omid, how do things stand with that missing Cascadia tile?

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: Still missing, I'm afraid. I told you about it on June 13, and a further search hasn't turned it up.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Ah, the copy your group bought, right?

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: That's the one. It's a forest-and-mountain habitat tile.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Where have you looked so far?

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: I've checked the game box and the area under the sofa. Nothing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Those seem like the obvious places.

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: Yes. The box was particularly disappointing. It seemed like a good place for a game piece.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are you going to try to replace it?

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: I'm looking into a replacement. Let me check what's available before I say any more than that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair enough. I hope it's not too much trouble.

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: We'll see. It's only 1 tile, but I'd like to have the complete set.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that makes sense.

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: You've got your climbing bag with you. Coming back from the gym?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yep, just on my way back from the climbing gym. What's that folded grocery receipt you're holding?

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: Just a grocery receipt. I folded it up and apparently forgot to put it away.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: At least you know where that is.

dialogue.speaker: Omid
dialogue.text: For now. Anyway, have a good evening, Riley.

key_facts: On June 13, Omid told Riley that a tile was missing from the copy the group bought.
The missing piece is a forest-and-mountain habitat tile.
Omid has checked the game box and the area under the sofa without finding it.
minor_details: Omid is holding a folded grocery receipt.
Riley is on the way back from the climbing gym.

summary: Riley and Omid discussed the missing Cascadia forest-and-mountain habitat tile from a copied set. Searches so far include the game box and area under the sofa; nothing found. Omid is investigating replacement options and will check availability before commenting further. Riley noted returning from the gym and asked about the receipt. Action item: Omid to confirm possible replacement options and availability.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How's the rest of July looking for us?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I was just looking at something for Saturday, July 25. I saw a listing on the library bulletin board.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, what was it?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: An outdoor screening of Kiki's Delivery Service.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, I'd love to see that. Where is it?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Salmon Bay Park. Admission is free.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's pretty good. What time does it start?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: 9 p.m. We could make an evening of it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'm into that. Is July 25 definitely a Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yep, Saturday the 25th.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay, let's put it on the calendar before I forget.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The shared one?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, please. Do you have the listing there?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I do. Okay, but should I put the film title in the event name or just 'outdoor film'?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Put Kiki's Delivery Service. That'll be easier to spot.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Fair. Otherwise we'll have a very mysterious calendar entry.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: With an actual location and time, at least.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: True. Okay, it's on there for 9 p.m. at Salmon Bay Park.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. I'm looking forward to it.

details_in_summary: The film is scheduled to start at 9 p.m.
key_facts: The screening is on Saturday, July 25.
The film is Kiki's Delivery Service.
The screening is at Salmon Bay Park and admission is free.
minor_details: Maya noticed the listing on a library bulletin board.
The film is scheduled to start at 9 p.m.

summary: Riley discussed planning an outdoor film night for Saturday, July 25: Kiki's Delivery Service at Salmon Bay Park, starting at 9 p.m. Admission is free. They agreed to add the event to the shared calendar with the film title in the event name. Action item: create the calendar entry for 9 p.m., Salmon Bay Park, on July 25.

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: Picking up a cheddar biscuit this late?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, if you've got one left.

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: I do. Here you go.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Thanks. Oh, you moved the board under the awning.

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: I did. I tried the spot you suggested.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How's it looking?

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: Pretty good, actually. It's quiet right now, so I can stand back and get a decent look at it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The iced drinks are much easier to see from here.

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: That's what I thought. The glare isn't hitting it the same way.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you didn't have to buy a new sign.

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: My favorite part of the arrangement.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are you keeping it there?

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: For now. I want to leave it there through lunch next Wednesday, July 15, and see how it does when we're busier.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that'll give you a better idea than a quiet evening.

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: Exactly. Right now it's doing a very good job of being a board.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is that a blue pencil behind your ear?

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: It is. I was looking for it, too. Well, there's that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Glad I could help. Thanks for the biscuit.

key_facts: Rosa has tried the awning position.
She plans to assess it during the following Wednesday’s lunch service.
minor_details: Rosa has a blue pencil tucked behind her ear.
Riley picks up a cheddar biscuit.

summary: Riley and Rosa discussed optimizing the sign board. Rosa moved the board under the awning to improve visibility, noting iced drinks are easier to see and no new sign was needed. They decided to keep the board in place through lunch next Wednesday, July 15, to evaluate performance during a busier period. Riley acknowledged the biscuit and equipment noted (blue pencil).

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: It's a shoreline cleanup. I saw the notice on a community bulletin board and thought we could try it together.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, where is it?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Golden Gardens. Volunteers are meeting at the south parking lot.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds good. When?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: July 18, from 9 to 11 a.m. So, next Saturday morning.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I like that. Something practical outdoors, instead of just talking about doing something.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but can I finish telling you about it before you get toast crumbs all over the notice?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'm eating toast, not demolishing a building.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The group running it is called Ballard Shoreline Stewards.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Do we need to bring anything?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'm not sure. I'll check the notice again. For now, are you in?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'm in. Let's give it a try.

key_facts: The cleanup is on July 18, from 9 to 11 a.m.
Volunteers are meeting at the south parking lot at Golden Gardens.
The event is run by a local group called Ballard Shoreline Stewards.
minor_details: Maya found the notice on a community bulletin board.
Riley is eating toast while they discuss it.

summary: Riley discussed a shoreline cleanup at Golden Gardens organized by Ballard Shoreline Stewards. The volunteer event is July 18, 9–11 a.m., meeting at the south parking lot. Riley agreed to participate. Maya will recheck the notice for any required items; Riley will follow up if needed to confirm specifics. No other commitments were made.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That was a good game of Qwirkle. Inez won by 6 points, right?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, 6. I thought I was closer until we added everything up.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Same. And I think the 3 of us are working pretty well as a group.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I do too. It's easier to concentrate up here than it was in the lounge.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Definitely. Apart from that chair squeaking whenever anyone leaned back.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I kept forgetting and making it squeak again. At least you put out a bowl of pretzels to distract us.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: A very sophisticated solution. Anyway, Inez seemed happy to keep playing, and I was thinking roughly once a month, if that works for you.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, once a month sounds good. I'd rather not lock it to the same date every time, though.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Me neither. We can just arrange each date as we go. Inez was good with that too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Perfect. That leaves room for people to change their minds if a month gets busy.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Exactly. No fixed recurring date, just the 3 of us checking in.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds like a plan. Thanks for having us up here.

key_facts: Inez won the game by six points.
The group agreed to meet roughly once a month rather than set a fixed recurring date.
minor_details: Sam put out a bowl of pretzels.
One of the chairs squeaked whenever anyone leaned back.

summary: Riley discussed the recent Qwirkle game and Inez’s 6-point win. The group noted good collaboration and preferred the up-here setting over the lounge, despite a squeaky chair. Pretzels helped distract them. They agreed to meet roughly once a month with flexible dates, not a fixed schedule, coordinating dates as needed with Inez.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, the update actually worked.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The kiosk loop? No more weird pause?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Not in the bench test. On July 10, the updated player completed 5 consecutive repeats without an audible gap.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. You must be relieved.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Very. I was sitting there with a mug of peppermint tea, listening to the end over and over.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you start doubting whether you could hear a gap at all?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: By the fourth repeat, yes. I thought, maybe silence is a matter of opinion.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's your professional assessment?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Only after sufficient tea. The player was sitting on a folded towel on the workbench, which made the whole setup look very serious.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And it just kept going, no 6-second wait?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Right. But I still want to hear it running in the visitor center. A bench test isn't quite the same as the actual setup.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Do you know when you'll get to try it there?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: The on-site installation is scheduled for August 1.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are you bringing your own copy of the audio, just in case?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'll bring a backup copy of the approved audio. I'd rather carry it and not need it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. And maybe make sure your laptop's charged.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Funny you say that. I nearly forgot to charge it afterward. Solved the loop, almost defeated by a battery.

key_facts: The updated player completed five consecutive repeats without an audible gap in the July 10 bench test.
The on-site installation is scheduled for August 1.
Daniel will bring a backup copy of the approved audio to the installation.
minor_details: He watched the test with a mug of peppermint tea.
The player sat on a folded towel on the workbench.
He nearly forgot to charge his laptop afterward.

summary: Daniel reported the update succeeded; bench tests showed 5 consecutive repeats with no audible gap as of July 10. Riley and Daniel discussed the need for on-site testing at the visitor center. Installation is scheduled for August 1. Action items: Daniel will bring a backup copy of the approved audio and ensure his laptop is charged for on-site setup.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. How's your Sunday going so far?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty good, just having a quiet lunch. How about you?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Quiet here too, in theory. I've got tea going cold while I sort through calendar pictures.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, for the 2027 calendar? Did you start putting them in months?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I did. Well, the first 3, anyway. Can I run them by you?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, go ahead.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: For January, I'm thinking of that picture of you and me skating at a Spokane rink. The one with a red mitten in one corner.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, I know the one. That feels right for January.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Good. Then February could be the family kitchen baking photograph. It's cozy, which is about as much logic as I've applied.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I like that. We don't actually have to know if it was taken in February, right?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No, I think looking seasonal is enough. March is the picture of us in our childhood backyard. What do you think?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that works for March. Even if we have no idea what month it really was.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. All right, that's the first 3 settled. Now I should drink my tea before it's completely cold.

details_in_summary: The skating picture has a red mitten in one corner.
key_facts: January will show Hannah and Riley skating at a Spokane rink.
February will use a family kitchen baking photograph.
March will show the siblings in their childhood backyard.
minor_details: The skating picture has a red mitten in one corner.
Hannah has tea going cold while she sorts.

summary: Riley discussed the 2027 calendar photo lineup with Hannah Blake. They agreed on January: the skating photo with a red mitten; February: the family kitchen baking photo; March: the childhood backyard photo. They plan to use seasonal logic rather than exact dates. Action items: finalize and confirm these three selections for the calendar.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How's Italian going now that the course is nearly over?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Pretty well, I think. For the July 16 class, I have to describe a simple meal in Italian. It's the final exercise.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What meal did you pick?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Beans on toast. I figured I should keep the meal simple if the sentences are going to be hard.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair. Have you tried saying it yet?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. I'm taping myself rehearsing on my phone so I can hear where I hesitate.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And how was the first attempt?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: A bus went past during the first attempt, so it was a little hard to hear me. Probably for the best.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, come on. Was it worse than the market exercise?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Fewer quantities to freeze on, at least. Would you listen to a rough rehearsal?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, go for it.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Okay. 'Preparo fagioli sul pane tostato. Scaldo i fagioli con un po' d'olio e sale. Poi metto i fagioli sul pane.'

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I caught the olio and sale. You paused a little before the last bit.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, I was trying to remember metto. I know what I want to say, and then the word just takes the long way around.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Want to try that bit again?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: 'Poi metto i fagioli sul pane.' Better, I think. What if I practice just that sentence a few times before I do the whole thing again?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Sounds good. And now I want beans on toast.

details_in_summary: A bus went past during the first attempt.
key_facts: For the July 16 class, Sam must describe a simple meal in Italian.
Sam chose to describe beans on toast.
Sam is recording a rehearsal to hear where they hesitate.
minor_details: The recording was made on Sam's phone.
A bus went past during the first attempt.

summary: Riley discussed Sam’s Italian final exercise describing a simple meal. Sam chose beans on toast and is recording rehearsals to identify hesitations. A noise issue from a bus affected the first attempt, but Sam noted fewer quantities to memorize than the market exercise. Riley and Sam agreed to practice the phrase 'Poi metto i fagioli sul pane' several times before re-running the full description.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So how are things standing with the tapes?

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Better, actually. On Thursday, July 9, I transferred the clearer tape and sent you the file.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I got it. Is the campus-band session on that one?

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: It is. It's near the end of the file.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. I haven't gotten that far yet.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: I listened to the transfer through headphones. I wanted to make sure I hadn't somehow copied 40 minutes of silence.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That would have been a pretty experimental radio show.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Yeah. And, uh, probably my most technically accomplished work.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll listen through to the end. Thanks for sending it.

details_in_summary: Marcus listened to the transfer through headphones.
key_facts: On Thursday 9 July, Marcus transferred the clearer tape and sent Riley the recording.
The campus-band session is near the end of the recording.
minor_details: Marcus listened to the transfer through headphones.

summary: Riley discussed tape status with Marcus. Marcus transferred the clearer tape on Thursday, July 9 and sent the file, which includes the campus-band session near the end. Marcus listened to the transfer to confirm it wasn’t silent. Riley plans to listen through to the end. Marcus noted the session as possibly his most technically accomplished work.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How's the desk coming along?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm getting it ready for the polyurethane, but the drawer's being difficult. It doesn't want to slide smoothly.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Does it stick the whole way, or just at one point?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Mostly as it gets toward the back. I pulled it out and had a look, and it rubs along the right-hand wooden runner.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is there something on the runner, or does it look out of place?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Well, I noticed the runner's rear screw is loose. I think that might be letting the runner shift a little.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That could explain why it catches near the back. Can you get a screwdriver in there?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I think so. It's a bit awkward, but not impossible. In theory, anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe try tightening it gently and see if the drawer moves any better.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'll start there. Oh, and I found a forgotten blue rubber band behind the drawer. Not the source of the problem, apparently.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: At least the desk came with an accessory.

details_in_summary: She found a forgotten blue rubber band behind the drawer.
key_facts: The drawer rubs along its right-hand wooden runner.
Hannah noticed that the runner's rear screw is loose.
minor_details: She found a forgotten blue rubber band behind the drawer.

summary: Riley discussed desk progress with Hannah, focusing on a drawer that sticks toward the back. The right-hand wooden runner rubs, likely due to a loose rear screw. Decision: tighten the rear screw gently to test improvement. A blue rubber band was found behind the drawer but not related to the issue. Action item: Hannah to tighten the screw and recheck drawer movement.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The bedroom's still holding all that heat from today.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, and it's only 7:30. Maybe we could use the fan once the air outside cools down.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but which way would you point it? The fan made the living room more comfortable, but the thermometer didn't budge.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Out the bedroom window, I think. Try to push the warm air out instead of just blowing it around.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Let's wait until it's cooler outside, then. Otherwise we're just sending the heat on a scenic tour.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I can get it plugged in. I just have to move this laundry basket to reach the outlet.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, it's 9 p.m. My phone says it's 68°F outside, and the bedroom thermometer says 76°F.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's enough of a difference. I'm pointing the fan outward at the bedroom window now.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Can we leave the door open too, so air has somewhere to come from?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. Let's give it a while and see what the thermometer does.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'm ready for bed. The bedroom thermometer reads 74°F now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: 2 degrees down. Not bad. It feels better in here, too.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. I think this evening setup is worth trying again when it's hot.

details_in_summary: Riley has to move a laundry basket to reach the outlet.
key_facts: At 9 p.m., it is 68°F outside and 76°F in the bedroom.
Riley points the fan outward at the bedroom window.
By bedtime, the bedroom thermometer reads 74°F.
minor_details: Maya checks the outdoor reading on her phone.
Riley has to move a laundry basket to reach the outlet.

summary: Riley discussed cooling the bedroom using a fan, aiming to vent warm air outward rather than circulate it. They considered leaving the door open to improve airflow and planned to plug in the fan after moving a laundry basket to reach the outlet. They noted outside temperature around 68°F and indoor readings from 76°F down to 74°F, concluding the evening setup is worth trying again when temperatures rise further.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Oh, right! The repotting. Okay, so, I finally did it on July 12.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How'd it go? Did the basil get more room?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: It did. I moved the basil into a terracotta pot with a drainage hole.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. Especially after it got so droopy.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, I'm hoping a little more space helps. The parsley got a larger plastic pot, also with drainage.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And the thyme?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I kept the thyme in its original pot. I checked the roots, and they still had room.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So not everything had to move.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Nope. Just those 2. I did spend an embarrassing amount of time choosing containers, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How embarrassing?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Long enough that I started comparing drainage holes like it was my job. I have a gift for making small decisions large.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The classic college group-project method.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Exactly. Except this time the group was me and 3 plants.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you get soil all over the kitchen?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I spread old newspaper over the kitchen floor to catch it. A teaspoon turned out to be handy for filling the gaps around the roots.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A teaspoon? That's actually pretty clever.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Thanks. I'd like that noted as the 1 efficient part of the operation.

key_facts: On July 12, Daniel moved the basil into a terracotta pot with a drainage hole.
He repotted the parsley in a larger plastic pot, also with drainage.
He kept the thyme in its original pot because its roots had room.
minor_details: He spread old newspaper over the kitchen floor to catch soil.
A teaspoon proved handy for filling gaps around the roots.

summary: Daniel reports completing repotting on July 12. Basil moved to a terracotta pot with drainage; parsley to a larger plastic pot with drainage; thyme remained in its original pot. Only two plants were moved. He reflects on spending time choosing containers and notes using a teaspoon to fill gaps and newspaper to protect the kitchen floor as efficient steps.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I booked a second usability session for the revised returns flow: July 22, with 3 warehouse staff.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Great. I want to check whether it's clear when they should print a replacement label.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. What if we give them a case where the item can't be confidently matched to a return? See whether they try to print anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That works. They should confirm the item's identity before they get to printing.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right. And if they can't identify it, the route is to set it aside for a lead, not pick an inspection outcome.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: We can leave the identifying marks note optional in the scenario and see if they notice it.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Or let them decide whether it's useful. I don't want the task to tell them which field to use.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good point. I'll keep the prompt about the item, not the screen. And I'm adding a paper-clip symbol to the test notes so I can find that scenario.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The very high-tech filing system. We should also have a scenario where they can confirm the identity, so we see the printing path.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yes, including the confirmation before they send the label to the printer. I'll put both scenarios in the notes.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Perfect. I'll review the prompts with you before July 22, then.

details_in_summary: Riley adds a paper-clip symbol to the test notes.
key_facts: A second usability session is booked for July 22 with three warehouse staff.
The test includes a scenario in which the item cannot be confidently matched to a return.
minor_details: Riley adds a paper-clip symbol to the test notes.

summary: Riley discussed a July 22 usability session for the revised returns flow (3 warehouse staff). They outlined scenarios: (1) item cannot be confidently matched; require identity confirmation before printing; if unidentified, route to lead rather than an inspection outcome; optional identifying marks note. (2) scenario where identity is confirmed before printing. Add a paper-clip symbol to test notes. Sam will review prompts before July 22.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How are things standing with the garden after that warm spell?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The soil's been drying out again, especially at the far end. I checked below the surface, not just the top.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Okay. I can take the watering can over and reach that corner better.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but let's not wait until it looks dry on top. What if we alternate checks every 2 days during dry weather?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Works for me. You check tomorrow, July 16, and I'll check on July 18?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah. And whoever checks can feel the soil and water if it needs it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: After 6 p.m. if we need the shared hose, right?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Right, or before 9 a.m. The hose has office hours.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How are the peas looking, by the way?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: They've started flowering, but there aren't any pods ready to pick.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. And we finished our shared-work hours on July 11, didn't we?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: We did. We spent 2 hours pulling weeds from the communal herb area, so that's our household's commitment for the season done.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Your hat kept sliding over 1 eye the whole shift. Oh, and there was a red bucket left beside the compost bins.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That hat was determined to make me weed with 1 eye. Anyway, I'll check the bed tomorrow.

key_facts: On July 11 they spent two hours pulling weeds from the communal herb area.
That shift completed their household’s shared-work commitment for the season.
They decide to alternate garden checks every two days during dry weather.
The pea plants have begun flowering but have no pods ready to pick.
minor_details: Maya’s hat kept sliding over one eye during the work shift.
A red bucket was left beside the compost bins.

summary: Riley and Maya reviewed garden status: soil drying, especially at the far end; plan to alternate checks every 2 days during dry weather. Scheduling: Maya will check July 16; Riley July 18; both will test soil by feel and water as needed. Hose usage: after 6pm or before 9am due to office hours. Peas flowering but no pods yet. Shared-work hours completed on July 11 (2 hours weeding). Maya will check the herb bed tomorrow; a red bucket and hat issue noted.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Oh, finally. I bought the flights to Montreal.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You did? You've been watching those fares for a while.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: A few weeks, yeah. I'm leaving Seattle on the evening of October 20 and coming back October 27.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So you can still work on October 20 before you go.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Exactly. And the outbound flight connects in Toronto.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You went with Toronto instead of the cheaper Chicago option?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. Not the absolute cheapest, but the connection seemed more manageable. I didn't want to start the visit already exhausted.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Fair. What did the ticket come to?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: $729 round trip. I paid with the card I keep for travel purchases.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's nice to have settled. Did the confirmation come through?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: It did. I even saved the confirmation email in a folder instead of leaving it in my inbox. A rare administrative triumph.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I was going to ask if you'd be able to find it again.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: What if I try being organized just this once? But yeah, Emeka's working those first few weekdays, so I'll still have some time to explore on my own.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you don't have to make every hour into an activity. That sounds like the trip you wanted.

details_in_summary: Sam paid with a card they keep for travel purchases.
key_facts: Sam will depart Seattle on the evening of October 20 and return on October 27.
The outbound flight connects in Toronto.
The round-trip ticket cost $729.
minor_details: Sam paid with a card they keep for travel purchases.
They saved the confirmation email in a folder rather than leaving it in their inbox.

summary: Sam booked flights to Montreal for Oct 20–27, with an outbound connection in Toronto, chosen for a more manageable layover over a Chicago option. The round-trip cost was $729, paid with a travel card, and the confirmation email was saved. Emeka will cover the first weekdays, allowing Riley some solo exploration time, and the plan avoids packing every hour with activities.

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: I'm just wiping down this tray. You grabbing lunch?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, if you're not too busy. How did the board do under the awning on Wednesday?

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: Easier to read, actually. The glare wasn't nearly as bad.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. Did it hold up through the lunch rush?

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: Well, there’s that. Customers waiting for pickup had to squeeze past the board.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Ah. So it worked until people actually showed up.

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: Exactly. A very successful menu for an empty cafe.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is that it inside, by the counter?

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: Yep. I brought it back inside for now while I think about what else to do.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Makes sense. Sorry my suggestion turned into an obstacle course.

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: It was worth trying. Oh, you've got a receipt stuck to the sole of your shoe.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, I was wondering what that was. There, got it.

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: Thanks. I'll take that off your hands. Now, what can I get you for lunch?

details_in_summary: A receipt is stuck to the sole of Riley’s shoe.
key_facts: Customers waiting for pickup had to squeeze past the board.
Rosa has temporarily put the board inside the cafe.
minor_details: A receipt is stuck to the sole of Riley’s shoe.
Rosa is wiping down a tray.

summary: Riley discussed testing a menu board under the awning. Rosa noted glare improved readability but customers had to squeeze past the board, causing congestion. The board was brought back inside while considering other placements. Riley apologized for the obstacle; Rosa acknowledged the attempt. A receipt was found on Riley’s shoe and removed. Rosa asked about lunch options.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Oh, finally! The desk drawer actually works.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. What did you end up doing?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I tightened the rear screw on the right-hand runner. It was loose, just like I thought.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And that stopped it catching?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It helped, but it was still a little sticky. So I rubbed a little candle wax along the drawer's contact points.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you have to buy a candle for the desk?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No, it was a stub from the kitchen drawer. A very sophisticated repair kit.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, if it works. Does it slide all the way out now?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It opens without me needing a second hand to brace the desk. That's a pretty big improvement.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's great. I was wondering if the runner was going to need replacing.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Me too. I'm relieved I didn't have to replace any hardware.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Was the wax messy?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: A little crumbly. I used a folded grocery flyer to catch the wax crumbs, which worked, mostly.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Mostly is good enough for a flyer.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. And the drawer opens, so I'm calling it a success.

details_in_summary: The candle was a stub from a kitchen drawer.
She used a folded grocery flyer to catch the wax crumbs.
key_facts: Hannah tightened the rear screw on the runner.
She rubbed a little candle wax along the drawer's contact points.
The drawer now opens without needing a second hand to brace the desk.
minor_details: The candle was a stub from a kitchen drawer.
She used a folded grocery flyer to catch the wax crumbs.

summary: Riley discussed with Hannah a repair of a sticking desk drawer. Actions: tighten the rear screw on the right-hand runner, apply candle wax to contact points, and use a folded grocery flyer to catch wax crumbs. Result: drawer now opens fully, no hardware replacement needed; wax cleanup was minor.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, I thought we'd spend the first lesson actually drumming. Marisol spent so much time on how I was holding the sticks.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: After all those years of saying you wanted to play, was that a letdown?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Not really. I was just surprised how much there was to it. She taught me matched grip.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What's matched about it?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Both hands hold the sticks the same way, more or less. She kept having me loosen my grip instead of squeezing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds harder than it should be.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. Apparently I can overthink holding 2 sticks. Here's what I bought to practice on at home.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, the gray rubber surface is the part you hit?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Exactly. It's a quiet practice pad for my Fremont apartment. No full kit for the neighbors to endure.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Can I try it?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Sure. I carried the sticks home in a canvas grocery bag, by the way. Very rock and roll.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hang on, am I squeezing too hard?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Probably. I say that with the authority of someone who's had 1 lesson.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll take it. So did it feel any less awkward by the end?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: A little. Then I'd think about my hands again and lose it. But it was good to finally do the lesson.

details_in_summary: He carried his sticks home in a canvas grocery bag.
key_facts: Daniel bought a quiet practice pad for his Fremont apartment.
His first lesson covered matched grip.
minor_details: The pad has a gray rubber surface.
He carried his sticks home in a canvas grocery bag.

summary: Riley and Daniel discussed Daniel’s first drumming lesson, focusing on matched grip and loosening the grip. Daniel found it straightforward but noted overthinking hand positioning. He bought a quiet practice pad for home use in his Fremont apartment and mentioned carrying sticks home in a canvas bag. Riley asked to try the pad, and Daniel agreed. The lesson progressed to a positive, though initial, sense of achievement with practice continuing as the next step.

dialogue.speaker: Carmen
dialogue.text: Did you bring the test card for the window?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I printed it on matte white paper, with the dark lettering and the left-aligned layout you liked.

dialogue.speaker: Carmen
dialogue.text: Oh, good. The phone number's easy to spot. Is the web address all there?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yep. 206-555-0148 and junipercut.example/carmen.

dialogue.speaker: Carmen
dialogue.text: And it's 6 inches by 8 inches?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Pretty close. Actually, I left one edge a little uneven. Can I borrow your salon scissors?

dialogue.speaker: Carmen
dialogue.text: Sure. What if we just trim that edge before we put it up?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: There. Much better. Sorry, I nudged your water bottle.

dialogue.speaker: Carmen
dialogue.text: It's fine. That dent near the base of my water bottle was already there. It has a more exciting life than I do.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So, inside the window, in that clear patch we measured?

dialogue.speaker: Carmen
dialogue.text: That's the spot. I'll attach the test print with small loops of low-tack tape, so it stays removable.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Want me to hold it while you stick it up?

dialogue.speaker: Carmen
dialogue.text: Please. A little to the left. There, I think that's straight.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll step outside and look. Oh, I can read it from here, even with some reflection.

dialogue.speaker: Carmen
dialogue.text: Good. I'll watch how legible it is at different times of day, though. The light changes a lot on that window.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, this is just one evening. At least the matte paper seems to be helping right now.

key_facts: The temporary card is printed on matte white paper.
Carmen attaches the test print with small loops of low-tack tape.
minor_details: Riley trims one uneven edge with salon scissors.
Carmen’s water bottle has a dent near the base.

summary: Riley and Carmen prepared a window test card on matte white paper, confirmed contact details (phone and web address), and discussed dimensions with minor edge trimming. They planned removable placement using low-tack tape, adjusted position for straightness, and noted a dent unrelated to the task. Riley will observe readability under varying light, and both will evaluate legibility at different times of day. No further actions beyond placement and testing were specified.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It's still light out. This is a pretty good evening for a walk.

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: Yeah. I was just thinking about that coffee we had on May 16, during the day. When I tried telling you about my week in Italian.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Your first attempt at the whole account, right? How do you feel about it now?

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: Better than I did while I was doing it. I got through it with a few notes, including the bit about a bus delay.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I remember you unfolding the notes. They were tiny by the time you were done with them.

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: I'd folded them into quarters. Very compact, not very easy to read.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And your coffee cup had that chipped handle. I kept wondering if it was going to fall off.

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: It held on. A useful example for me, really.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You'd been aiming for 5 sentences. Did having the notes make it easier to keep going?

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: It did, though I kept wanting to check every word. I could recognize some of the past-tense forms, but choosing one on the spot was different.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are you still mixing up essere and avere?

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: Sometimes. Less on a worksheet than when I'm trying to say something aloud.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Do you think you'd want to try talking with Francesca soon?

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: I'm considering it. Maybe a 10-minute call would be a manageable first try.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Would you use notes for that too?

dialogue.speaker: Amara
dialogue.text: Probably a few. I'd rather manage a short call imperfectly than wait until I feel fluent. That could be a very long wait.

key_facts: Amara tried her short account with Riley over daytime coffee on May 16.
She got through it using a few notes, including a description of a bus delay.
She is considering a ten-minute call as a manageable first try.
minor_details: Her coffee cup that day had a chipped handle.
She had folded her notes into quarters.

summary: Riley discussed an evening walk with Amara while recounting their Italian study: May 16 coffee, using notes, and compact formatting. Amara noted benefits of notes for a five-sentence target, but read-through remained challenging, especially choosing past-tense forms and ess ere vs avere. They considered a brief practice with Francesca, suggesting a 10-minute call and using a few notes. Action items: explore a short call with Francesca and continue note-supported speaking.

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.text: I'm looking at this lamp here. The cream-colored shade is nice.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It's pretty small. Is that what you wanted for your desk?

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.text: Yeah, the desk by my living-room window. It's so crowded that anything bigger would need its own apartment.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How much space have you got?

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.text: Hang on, I brought my notebook. I marked the space on the cover.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The base fits inside the marks, with a little room to spare.

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.text: Good. I even dated the page Sunday, July 19, 2026. Very official market research.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And here we are at the Fremont Sunday Market, putting it to use. Can we check the switch?

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.text: The seller says we can plug it in here. There, it turns on. And off. A promising start.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What's the seller asking for it?

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.text: $18. I'll take it. It's light enough for us to carry home.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The seller's wrapping the cord in newspaper for you. I'll hold the shade while you pay.

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.text: Thanks. And thanks for carrying it home with me. Here, let's put it on the desk.

details_in_summary: The lamp has a cream-colored shade.
The seller asks $18 for it.
key_facts: Aisha and Riley visit the Fremont Sunday Market on July 19, 2026.
Aisha wants a small lamp for the desk by her living-room window.
They check the lamp’s switch and measure its base against Aisha’s notebook.
Aisha buys the lamp, and they carry it home.
minor_details: The lamp has a cream-colored shade.
The seller asks $18 for it.
The seller wraps the cord in newspaper.

summary: Riley discussed choosing a cream-shade lamp for a desk by the living-room window, confirming space via a notebook-marked measurement, and testing the switch at Fremont Sunday Market. The seller quoted $18; Riley agreed to buy and will carry the lamp home with the shade handled by Riley. The plan is to place the lamp on the desk.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How are things standing with your mom's photo boxes?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, Teresa and I sorted a group of loose pictures into broad piles. Nothing too elaborate yet.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What kinds of piles?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Mostly by people or places when we could tell. She recognized a group of pictures from a Spokane picnic.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. Did she know when the picnic was?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Not for sure. We're leaving dates open when we don't know, instead of guessing.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Probably better than giving everybody a wrong year to remember.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Exactly. I put 24 undated photographs in a separate pile for later review.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are the Spokane ones in there?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: The ones we couldn't date, yeah. One picnic picture has a thumb partly covering a corner, which feels like a pretty authentic family photo.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It's not a family picnic unless somebody's thumb shows up.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Right. I also bought acid-free paper sleeves for the most fragile prints.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Were they easy to find?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. They came in a brown paper packet. I spent longer comparing sleeves than I care to admit, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: We both know you care at least a little.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Fair. But at least now we can sort without having to invent dates for everything.

key_facts: Teresa recognized a group of pictures taken at a Spokane picnic.
Daniel put 24 undated photographs into a separate pile for later review.
He bought acid-free paper sleeves for the most fragile prints.
minor_details: One picnic picture has a thumb partly covering a corner.
The sleeves came in a brown paper packet.

summary: Riley discussed the status of mom's photo boxes. Daniel and Teresa sorted photos into broad piles by people or places, including Spokane picnic images with dates left open. 24 undated photos were set aside for later review. A photo with a partial thumb was noted as authentic. Daniel bought acid-free sleeves and compared options. The team agreed to continue sorting without guessing dates, with a plan to revisit the undated pile later.

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. How's your lunch break going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey! Pretty good. I'm taking a little break from my screen.

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: Good plan. So, I'm thinking ahead to January. Would you want to join me for a ski weekend at White Pass?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that sounds fun. What weekend are you thinking?

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: How about January 16–17, 2027? I found a cabin listing, but the cancellation policy is strict, so I don't want to book it until we agree.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: January 16–17 works for me. I'd love to go.

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: Great. I'll send you the cabin listing before I book it, so you can take a look too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Thanks. Anything I should know about it?

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: Well, the listing mentions a boot rack by the door. And I was thinking we could bring a thermos of coffee for the drive. I'm only planning 6 months ahead, which is restrained for me.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Very restrained. Send me the listing and I'll check it out.

details_in_summary: Owen suggests bringing a thermos of coffee for the drive.
The cabin listing mentions a boot rack by the door.
key_facts: They settle on January 16–17, 2027, for skiing at White Pass.
Owen will send Riley the cabin listing before booking because its cancellation policy is strict.
minor_details: Owen suggests bringing a thermos of coffee for the drive.
The cabin listing mentions a boot rack by the door.
meta.storyline_title: A January Weekend at White Pass

summary: Owen proposed a ski weekend at White Pass for January 16–17, 2027. Riley agreed. Owen will send the cabin listing before booking due to a strict cancellation policy; Riley will review it. They discussed a boot rack at the door and bringing a thermos of coffee. Riley noted the plan is a cautious six-month horizon.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The first week of Neighborhood Voices went pretty well. Someone had a useful comment about the display today.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hang on, I'm drying the dishes. What was the comment?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: A visitor said the printed text was difficult to read while standing back from the display.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh. Could they get closer to it?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I didn't ask. But either way, it seems worth making the words easier to read.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are you going to redo the whole display?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but I don't think I need to. I'm planning to add a large-print copy that visitors can hold.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds simpler. They could bring it closer instead of leaning over the table.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Exactly. I'd rather not make leaning a required part of the exhibit.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A very demanding library activity.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: And I found a paper bookmark left on the display table. I kept wondering whether someone meant to come back for it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The display has already acquired its own lost property.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Apparently. Still, it's nice to have it up, and to have one small thing I can improve.

details_in_summary: Maya describes finding a paper bookmark left on the display table.
key_facts: The exhibit is titled “Neighborhood Voices.”
A visitor says the transcript text is difficult to read while standing back from the display.
Maya plans to add a large-print copy visitors can hold.
minor_details: Maya describes finding a paper bookmark left on the display table.
Riley asks about the comment while drying dishes.

summary: Riley reported on Maya’s update: feedback from Neighborhood Voices noted display text was hard to read from a distance. Maya plans to add a large-print copy for closer viewing rather than redesigning the whole display. Action items: create a large-print version and place it with the exhibit. Also noted a left bookmark found on the display table; potential lost property.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How's the calendar coming along?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Pretty well. I've got 2 garden shots for April, and I'm having trouble choosing. Can you see both of them?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. They're really similar. Is that Walter in the background of the first one?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It is. I like that one better, I think. It's got the crooked watering can.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I like that one too. The daffodils stand out more, and it's nice having Walter back there.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Okay, then April will be the daffodils with Walter in the background. That's settled.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What about May?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I'm thinking May should be Beatrice sitting on the porch. It feels like a good one after the garden.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I like that for May. Are you keeping the choices together somewhere?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: In theory, yes. I've labeled my working folder with a green dot, so at least I can find that part.

details_in_summary: Hannah prefers the garden shot with the crooked watering can.
She has labeled her working folder with a green dot.
key_facts: April will use a photograph of daffodils with Walter in the background.
May will show Beatrice sitting on a porch.
minor_details: Hannah prefers the garden shot with the crooked watering can.
She has labeled her working folder with a green dot.

summary: Riley discussed the calendar. For April, Hannah will use the daffodils with Walter in the background (the other option was rejected). Beatrice sitting on the porch is planned for May. They noted the two similar garden shots, Walter's presence, and a crooked watering can as distinguishing elements. An action item: Hannah will keep the working folder organized, labeled with a green dot for easy access.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Oh, come on. The parsley's got brown edges on its leaves now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh no. Didn't you just give it a bigger pot?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, on July 12. I noticed the edges while I was waiting for my kettle to boil.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Do you think it's getting too much sun?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, it was right against the hot window. I think that did it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you move it?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, I moved it back from the glass onto the kitchen table.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hopefully that gives it a little break.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. I spent all that time comparing pots, and the window was the problem. Very efficient.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Your usual approach: carefully solve 1 problem at a time.

key_facts: The parsley developed brown leaf edges against the hot window.
Daniel moved it back from the glass onto the kitchen table.
minor_details: He noticed the damage while waiting for his kettle to boil.

summary: Riley discussed a parsley plant with brown-edged leaves. Daniel noted a larger pot was used in July, but sun exposure near a hot window seemed to cause the issue. He moved the plant away from the glass to the kitchen table to provide a break. Riley praised the approach of solving one problem at a time and suggested continuing to avoid direct heat from the window and monitor the plant for improvement.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. How's your afternoon going? Mine's been mostly meetings with tiny gaps between them.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Same. I keep thinking I have time to start something, and then I don't.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. Oh, remember how we were wondering about the bigger game night?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The July 16 one? How did it go?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: It ran later than we expected. The July session ended at 9:15 p.m., which felt pretty late for a work night.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oof. Was the bigger table part of it?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I think so. More people means more turns to get through, and more explaining. Or, well, more chances for the explaining to take a while.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is Becca thinking of keeping it smaller next time?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, Becca's proposed a 4-player cap for the next few gatherings. What if we try that and see how the timing works? Seems easier than declaring a perfect number now.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Makes sense. Did you at least get something to eat on the way home?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I ate a granola bar on the way home. Very glamorous end to the evening.

details_in_summary: Sam ate a granola bar on the way home.
key_facts: The July session ended at 9:15 p.m.
Becca has proposed a four-player cap for the next few gatherings.
minor_details: Sam ate a granola bar on the way home.

summary: Riley discussed the July game night, noting the session ran until 9:15 p.m. with a larger table causing longer turns and more explanations. Becca proposed a 4-player cap for upcoming gatherings to simplify timing. They considered testing the cap rather than deciding on a perfect number now. Riley mentioned a quick meal on the way home (granola bar).

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So, where do you stand on the shoreline cleanup now that we've had a couple of days?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'd like to go again. It was a good way to spend a Saturday morning. What about you?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I would too. It felt good to do something practical outside.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I was surprised we filled a whole bucket with bottle caps and pieces of fishing line.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The fishing line was tricky to pick up. I was glad the organizers lent us litter grabbers for the morning.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Me too. Though the grabbers didn't do much for the sand.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nope. I got sand in one shoe, and I didn't notice until we were done.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Just the one? That's a fairly efficient beach trip.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I thought so. What was your favorite part?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I liked the view from the northern end of the beach. I kept stopping to look at it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that was nice. Do you know how we sign up for the next one?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: The next volunteer message will include a sign-up link.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. I was wondering if we'd missed it.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: No, not yet. I can keep an eye on the group's volunteer messages and let you know when it comes.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Thanks. I'd like to do another one with you.

details_in_summary: Riley got sand in one shoe.
key_facts: Riley and Maya filled a bucket with bottle caps and pieces of fishing line.
The organizers lent them litter grabbers for the morning.
The next volunteer message will include a sign-up link.
minor_details: Riley got sand in one shoe.
Maya liked the view from the northern end of the beach.

summary: Riley and Maya discussed continuing shoreline cleanup. They plan to participate again, noting bucket-filled bottle caps and fishing line as notable finds; litter grabbers helped with litter but not sand. They will await the next volunteer message containing a sign-up link, and Maya will monitor group messages to inform Riley when it’s available. Riley expressed interest in doing another cleanup together.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Oh, good, I finally get to tell you: my lamp's fixed!

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! Was it something other than the bulb?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It was. Tacoma Lamp & Shade found a worn socket and replaced it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So the new bulb was fine all along.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Apparently. I picked the lamp up on July 17 and brought it home.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And no flickering?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: None. The light stayed steady through an evening of reading after I brought it home.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty good test.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah, I kept expecting it to start again. But it just stayed on, like a lamp is supposed to.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Was the repair expensive?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: It was $28.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, that's not bad.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No, and I'm so relieved I don't have to shop for another one. I could've spent an absurd amount of time comparing lamps.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You'd have a spreadsheet by the end.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: In theory, a very efficient spreadsheet.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Is it back beside your reading chair?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yep. I put a felt pad under the base before setting it back down.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Look at that, a working lamp and a felt pad.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I know. It's a very satisfying little corner again.

details_in_summary: The repair cost $28.
Hannah put a felt pad under the base before setting it back down.
key_facts: The repair shop found a worn socket and replaced it.
Hannah picked up the lamp on July 17.
The light stayed steady through an evening of reading after she brought it home.
minor_details: The repair cost $28.
Hannah put a felt pad under the base before setting it back down.

summary: Riley discussed Hannah's lamp repair: Tacoma Lamp & Shade replaced a worn socket; the new bulb was fine. The repair cost $28, and the lamp tested well during an evening of reading with no flicker. It was placed back beside the reading chair with a felt pad, restoring a satisfactory setup. No follow-up actions noted.

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: I kept looking at that wet railing, and it finally clicked.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The close-up we couldn't place?

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: Yeah. It's the railing on the apartment's back steps. I recognized the wood.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, the back steps! I was trying to make it into something much more interesting.

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: I spent a surprising amount of time staring at wet wood.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So what do we call it? 'The back steps, after rain.'

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: That's good. Just 'The back steps, after rain.' I'll use that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And we're keeping 'Basil that somehow survived' for the kitchen window?

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: Definitely. That one stays.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Wait, look at the lampshade in this picture. It's crooked.

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: Oh, it is. Somehow I missed that every time I looked at it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I kind of love it. Don't straighten it in the picture.

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: I won't. Actually, wait, that was the last caption we needed, wasn't it? The railing?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, I think we've got them all now. Did you settle on a title?

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: I did. 'First Place, 2016–2018.'

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Perfect. Did you get the printing arranged?

dialogue.speaker: Gabriel
dialogue.text: I did. The print shop promised the order will be ready on August 14. I also paid an extra $3 for a matte cover.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. Matte feels right for it.

details_in_summary: Gabriel pays an extra $3 for a matte cover.
Riley notices a crooked lampshade in one of the pictures.
key_facts: Gabriel recognizes the wet railing as the one on the apartment's back steps.
They caption that picture “The back steps, after rain.”
The booklet title is “First Place, 2016–2018.”
The print shop has promised the order will be ready on August 14.
minor_details: Gabriel pays an extra $3 for a matte cover.
Riley notices a crooked lampshade in one of the pictures.

summary: Riley and Gabriel finalized project pieces: captions settled on ‘The back steps, after rain,’ and ‘Basil that somehow survived.’ The crooked lampshade would stay as is, not straightened. They confirmed the title, ‘First Place, 2016–2018,’ and arranged printing, with an August 14 readiness date and an extra $3 paid for a matte cover. Riley noted they’ve captured all captions, and Gabriel confirmed the print order is in place.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The Italian meal description went better than my rehearsal.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good! How did the beans on toast go?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I got through the whole description without reading from notes. Which felt like a small miracle.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. What helped?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I wrote down 3 prompts beforehand, just to remember the order. Once I had that in my head, it was easier to keep going.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So you weren't trying to remember every sentence exactly?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right. Just what came next. I still hesitated a little, but not nearly as much as in the rehearsal.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty good way to finish the course.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. The classroom chairs were stacked after the session, and I was standing there thinking, well, that's that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you do anything to celebrate?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I got a pastry on the way home. A very practical reward.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I think getting through it without notes earned you a pastry.

details_in_summary: Sam celebrated with a pastry on the way home.
The classroom chairs were stacked after the session.
key_facts: Sam completed the meal description without reading from notes.
Writing down three prompts beforehand helped Sam remember the order.
minor_details: Sam celebrated with a pastry on the way home.
The classroom chairs were stacked after the session.

summary: Riley noted Sam’s Italian meal description went better than the rehearsal. Sam used 3 prompts to remember the order, avoiding full sentence recall and reducing hesitation. They discussed finishing the course without notes, the classroom chairs being stacked, and Sam celebrating with a pastry on the way home. Action items: consider continuing practice with prompt-based recall and reinforce notetaking avoidance as a learning strategy.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Hi, Riley. How's your evening going?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, Hannah. Pretty quiet, which is nice. How's yours?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Good. I just got out of the final pottery class, and I spent an embarrassing amount of it looking at glaze samples.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, the bowls were ready to glaze?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yeah, they'd been bisque-fired. The little crack near the rim of the third one held up, too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice! So what did you choose?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Speckled cream for 2 bowls, and dark green for the remaining bowl.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds like a good set. Did you know right away?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No. The studio displays the glaze samples on small clay tiles, and I kept going back and forth between them. Very decisive of me.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Were you trying to match them exactly, or did you give up on that?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I gave up, like you suggested. The walls aren't identical anyway, so a different color on one seemed fine.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And do the glazes look like the tiles when you put them on?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Not really. The finished colors may look different from the samples, too, so we'll see. I also got glaze on the cuff of my shirt, which wasn't part of the design.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Ha. At least you remembered your apron. Did you get a chance to eat before class?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I did. I brought a sandwich and ate it before class. So, in theory, I had plenty of energy for all that very difficult tile comparison.

details_in_summary: Hannah got glaze on the cuff of her shirt.
She brought a sandwich to eat before class.
key_facts: Hannah chose a speckled cream glaze for two bowls.
She used a dark green glaze on the remaining bowl.
The studio's glaze samples are displayed on small clay tiles.
minor_details: Hannah got glaze on the cuff of her shirt.
She brought a sandwich to eat before class.

summary: Riley and Hannah discussed Hannah’s pottery class. Hannah reported choosing glaze colors—speckled cream for two bowls and dark green for the third—after comparing options on tiles, deciding not to match tiles exactly. The bowls had bisque firing and a minor crack near the rim held up. Riley noted glaze behavior may differ from samples; Hannah accidentally got glaze on her shirt cuff. She had a sandwich before class to maintain energy for tile comparisons.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Oh, wow, there's more to getting an audience seated than I thought.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Was that from the shadow shift you were talking about?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. I shadowed an usher at the Gull House screening on July 18. Okay, so, I mostly watched how they guided people into the auditorium.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What did you notice?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: That you can't just point everyone toward the doors and call it done. People stop to get their bearings, and then the people behind them stop too.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The classic doorway conference.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
