They considered mounting paper as a large souvenir and discussed finalizing the exhibit materials and display decisions.

dialogue.speaker: Ingrid
dialogue.text: A quick update on the Routewise case study draft: I marked that section we discussed, but I haven't revised it yet.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: The route-planning part?

dialogue.speaker: Ingrid
dialogue.text: Yes. When we reviewed it on March 18, 2026, we identified that section as needing a clearer account of what I contributed.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. It wasn't clear what you'd actually worked on in the app's route-planning flow.

dialogue.speaker: Ingrid
dialogue.text: Exactly. I've put a yellow sticky note on it, which is a very efficient way of not rewriting it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: At least you can find it.

dialogue.speaker: Ingrid
dialogue.text: That's the hope. I'm still trying to keep the whole case study concise.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Maybe that section doesn't need to be longer. Just more specific about your part.

dialogue.speaker: Ingrid
dialogue.text: Yes. I keep looking at it and thinking, 'That's a description of the project, not my contribution.'

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds like the distinction we were trying to get at.

dialogue.speaker: Ingrid
dialogue.text: It is. For now, the sticky note is doing all the work.

details_in_summary: Ingrid has marked the section with a yellow sticky note.
key_facts: On March 18, 2026, Riley and Ingrid identified a section that needed a clearer account of Ingrid's contribution.
The section concerns Ingrid's work on the app's route-planning flow.
minor_details: Ingrid has marked the section with a yellow sticky note.

summary: Riley discussed the Routewise case study draft with Ingrid. Ingrid has marked the route-planning section but has not revised it; a March 18 review identified the need to clarify Ingrid's contributions to the route-planning flow. Ingrid placed a yellow sticky note to avoid rewriting, aiming for conciseness. The plan is to make the section specify Ingrid's contributions rather than the project description; action item is to produce a clearer account of her work.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So, how do things stand with the graduation photos?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so, Teresa found something that settles the year. A graduation program, dated June 1987.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. So her memory was right, not the envelope.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. The envelope said 1986. She found the program tucked inside an old cookbook, of all places.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a pretty good place to hide a graduation program from yourself.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Apparently. I wouldn't have thought to look there.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you change the files, then?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I did. I updated the graduation files to use 1987 as the event year.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And did you keep a note about the envelope?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, I noted that the original envelope was labeled 1986. Just so the different date doesn't look like it came out of nowhere.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. I'm glad you didn't have to make a guess.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Me too. I was fully prepared to spend an unreasonable amount of time staring at those 2 numbers.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A classic Daniel comparison project.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Exactly. Oh, and if I sound a little distracted, I'm having toast with apricot jam.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: No, you're fine. That's a solid Sunday morning setup.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: It is. And now I can eat it without wondering which year to put on those files.

details_in_summary: Daniel had toast with apricot jam during the call.
key_facts: A graduation program Teresa found is dated June 1987.
Daniel updated the graduation files to use 1987 as the event year.
He noted that the original envelope was labeled 1986.
minor_details: The program was tucked inside an old cookbook.
Daniel had toast with apricot jam during the call.

summary: Riley discussed graduation photos: Teresa found a 1987 graduation program, while the envelope dated 1986. Daniel updated the files to 1987 and kept a note about the envelope to avoid guessing. They agreed this clarifies the date discrepancy. Daniel mentioned being distracted by toast with apricot jam, but confirmed the file updates and documentation are in place.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: I asked Daphne about starting later on Thursdays for that swim class.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, good. What did she say?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: She's open to a trial, if we can work out the hours and the coverage.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So not an immediate no.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: No, which was a relief. She does want me to keep the same total weekly hours, though.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. You'd need to make up that hour somewhere.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Yes. The class is at 8:00 in Tacoma, so I'd need to start at 10:00 instead of 9:00 on Thursdays.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And what happens with your opening duties?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: That's the other condition. Another staff member would have to cover them if I start later.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Makes sense. Did you get a chance to talk it through properly?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: A little. I brought it up after a staff meeting. I'd written my questions on the back of an old envelope, which made me look very organized, in theory.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey, you had the questions written down. That's organized.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: The envelope was doing its best. Anyway, Daphne was willing to discuss it, but the hours and opening coverage both need to work.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It's good she didn't rule it out. Sounds like those are the 2 things to figure out.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Exactly. I was mostly worried she'd think I hadn't considered the opening at all, so I'm glad we talked about it.

key_facts: Daphne wants Hannah to keep the same total weekly hours.
Any later start depends on another staff member covering Hannah's opening duties.
minor_details: Hannah brought the subject up after a staff meeting.
She had written her questions on the back of an old envelope.

The plan: keep total weekly hours, start at 10:00 instead of 9:00, and arrange coverage for opening duties. The two conditions—hours and opening coverage—must be resolved for any reversal. Riley noted Daphne’s willingness but emphasized these points need confirmation.

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: You're staring at the board from all the way over there. Can you read it?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, actually. The navy lettering stands out a lot better against the ivory.

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: Good. The repainting's finished, it's dry, and the board's back in use inside Plover Coffee.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It definitely looks easier to read in here.

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: It does. Outside in the sun is still the question.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Right. And the awning spot made the pickup line pretty tight.

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: People could read the menu, but they had to squeeze past the board. Well, there's that.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: So you're not putting it back there?

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: Not for now. I need to test some outdoor positions when the sun's out, see what actually works.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Makes sense. Oh, your jar of wooden stirrers is nearly empty.

dialogue.speaker: Rosa
dialogue.text: Thanks, I'll refill it. How's your bread going, by the way?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good, although the dough rose faster than I expected. I had to move things along a little.

details_in_summary: A jar of wooden stirrers is nearly empty.
Riley mentions that their bread dough rose faster than expected.
key_facts: The repainted board is dry and back in use inside Plover Coffee.
Rosa plans to test outdoor positions when the sun is out.
minor_details: A jar of wooden stirrers is nearly empty.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Morning, Sam. How are things standing with the iced tea trials?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Morning. I brought in what I hope is the final batch. Peach and black tea again.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. What did you change this time?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I steeped the tea for 5 minutes. Still 1 sliced peach per liter, and I let the tea cool before adding it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And you poured the samples from that glass jar?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. Here, try yours. I'm hoping the extra minute gives the tea a little more presence.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Mm. I had a piece of toast with mine, so let me try another sip. Yeah, that's really good.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The peach still comes through? I didn't want to lose it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: It does, and the tea doesn't taste bitter. I think this is the one to keep.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I agree. Peach and black tea is my favorite combination of the ones we tried.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Mine too. Are you going to add any sweetener?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: No, I plan to keep the recipe unsweetened. And I think I'm happy to stop running tea trials for now. My work here is done.

details_in_summary: Sam poured the samples from a glass jar.
key_facts: Sam and Riley settle on peach and black tea as their favorite combination.
For the final batch, Sam steeped the tea for five minutes.
Sam plans to keep the recipe unsweetened.
minor_details: Sam poured the samples from a glass jar.
Riley had a piece of toast with theirs.

summary: Riley discussed iced tea trials with Sam, focusing on peach and black tea. Sam kept 1 sliced peach per liter, steeped 5 minutes, and cooled before adding; samples were poured from a glass jar. They agreed the tea is unsweetened and retains peach flavor without bitterness. Sam will stop trials, and they conclude the peach and black tea is the final recipe.

dialogue.speaker: Andre
dialogue.text: Hang on, I'm tying my climbing shoes. This lace keeps slipping.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Take your time. I'm not racing you to the wall.

dialogue.speaker: Andre
dialogue.text: Good, because I'd lose that one. Oh, I had an idea I wanted to mention.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah? What's the idea?

dialogue.speaker: Andre
dialogue.text: A little photo booklet about my aunt Nadine's old stationery shop in Beacon Hill.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, that sounds lovely. Is it for her?

dialogue.speaker: Andre
dialogue.text: Yeah. I want to have it ready for her birthday in October.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a really nice gift.

dialogue.speaker: Andre
dialogue.text: I'm hoping to keep the cost low, though. So, small and simple, probably.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Makes sense. Do you have anything in mind for how you want it to look?

dialogue.speaker: Andre
dialogue.text: Not yet. I wrote the idea on the back of a grocery list, so that's about how far I've got.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's a perfectly good place to start.

dialogue.speaker: Andre
dialogue.text: I was going to ask you for some layout advice on August 12, if you're around.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Wednesday? Yeah, ask me then. I'd be happy to help.

dialogue.speaker: Andre
dialogue.text: Great. I'll think about what I want to ask before then. Worth a try.

details_in_summary: Andre has the idea written on the back of a grocery list.
key_facts: Nadine's stationery shop was in Beacon Hill.
Andre wants the booklet ready for Nadine's October birthday.
He hopes to keep the cost low.
Andre plans to ask Riley for layout advice on August 12.
minor_details: Andre has the idea written on the back of a grocery list.
He mentions it while tying his climbing shoes.

summary: Riley and Andre discussed creating a small, inexpensive photo booklet about Andre’s aunt Nadine’s old Beacon Hill stationery shop as a gift for her October birthday. They agreed to keep it simple and start from ideas written on a grocery list. Andre plans to ask Riley for layout advice on August 12 and will prepare questions beforehand, with Riley available to assist then.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Okay, so the thyme has a replacement. I bought a chive plant at the neighborhood garden shop.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice. Is it on the sill with the basil?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah, the chives are on the kitchen sill, in a pot with their own saucer.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you spend an hour choosing the pot this time?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: No, but I did have 2 chive plants to choose from. I picked the shorter one because it fit in my tote.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A very practical selection process.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I know. I barely recognized myself. The saucer's an odd pale blue one I already had, so no comparison shopping there either.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And how's the reminder system going?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Well, today being Monday, I got the reminder to check the pots. I think I need to use those to feel the soil, though, not automatically water every pot.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Especially after the thyme.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yeah. Its soil stayed wet, and I suspect I was watering it too often. So Monday and Thursday can just be check days.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds less like a watering schedule and more like an inspection.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Exactly. I'll try not to make a spreadsheet about it.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I give you until Thursday.

key_facts: Daniel bought a chive plant from a neighborhood garden shop.
He will use the reminders to feel the soil, not automatically water every pot.
He placed the chives on the sill in a pot with its own saucer.
minor_details: He chose the shorter of two plants because it fit in his tote.
The saucer is an odd pale blue one he already had.

summary: Riley discussed Daniel replacing thyme with a chive plant on the kitchen sill. They noted practical pot choice and avoiding comparison shopping. They decided to use Monday and Thursday as soil-check days rather than automatic watering, since the thyme stayed wet. Riley will avoid making a spreadsheet and focus on feeling soil moisture for watering decisions.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I'm having toast with plum jam. Do you want the last piece?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: No, you have it. I'm still waking up.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Fair. I was thinking we could go to Spokane this autumn and visit Walter.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, yeah. I'd like that. Could we make a weekend of it instead of squeezing in a quick visit?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That's what I was thinking. Okay, but which weekend works for you?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: How about October 16–18?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That's Friday through Sunday, right?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. I'll take Friday, October 16, off work so we don't have to rush after work.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Good. Then we can leave enough time to actually sit with Walter, not just say hello and turn around.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Exactly. I'd rather have most of the weekend free for visiting than try to fit in a bunch of sightseeing.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Same. We don't need an itinerary with 15-minute visiting slots.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Let me write the dates down before I forget. I'm making a note on the back of the grocery list.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Okay, but leave the groceries visible. I don't want to come home with a bag full of October.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: I'll fold it the other way. Spokane, October 16–18, and Friday off.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Perfect. We can keep the rest of the weekend pretty open.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah. A proper visit sounds really nice.

details_in_summary: Riley makes a note on the back of a grocery list.
key_facts: They choose October 16–18 for the Spokane trip.
Riley plans to take Friday, October 16, off work.
They want most of the weekend free for visiting rather than sightseeing.
minor_details: Riley makes a note on the back of a grocery list.
Maya is having toast with plum jam.

summary: Riley and Maya discussed a Spokane trip to visit Walter in October. They agreed on October 16–18 (Friday–Sunday) and Riley will take Friday off to avoid rush. They plan to keep the weekend open for visits rather than sightseeing, and they decided to write the dates on the back of the grocery list. They also noted leaving groceries visible and avoiding a tight itinerary.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Hi, Riley. Are you getting a proper lunch, or is it one of those lunch-at-your-desk days?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: At my desk, but I did actually bring food. How's your day going?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Not bad. I tried that sign-up wording with a few volunteers, like we talked about.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, how did it go?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: 4 volunteers worked through my printed sample screens. Mostly they seemed comfortable with the wording, but 1 phrase caught a couple of them.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Which phrase?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: 'Number attending.' 2 volunteers read it as the number of seats still available, rather than the number of people they were signing up.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, I can see that. It's not really clear whose number it is.

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: Right. I'm thinking 'How many people are you signing up, including yourself?' It's longer, but at least it asks an actual question. I'll adjust it and test it again.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds worth trying. Did they write their answers on the printouts?

dialogue.speaker: Hannah
dialogue.text: They did. I offered them a choice of blue or black pens, which was the 1 part of the process nobody had trouble with.

details_in_summary: Hannah offered the volunteers a choice of blue or black pens.
key_facts: Four volunteers worked through Hannah's printed sample screens.
Two volunteers read 'number attending' as the number of seats still available.
minor_details: Hannah offered the volunteers a choice of blue or black pens.

summary: Riley discussed lunch at the desk while Hannah tested volunteer sign-up wording. Four volunteers evaluated printed sample screens; most were comfortable, but the phrase 'Number attending' caused confusion, interpreted as seats available by two volunteers. Hannah decided to change the phrasing to 'How many people are you signing up, including yourself?' and will retest. Volunteers wrote their answers on printouts, with a choice of blue or black pens. Action: revise wording and conduct a follow-up test.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Hey, Riley. How's your afternoon going so far?

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Hey. Pretty good. I'm still waking up from lunch, though.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Same. My brain's taking the scenic route back to work.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Anything fun going on this week?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I'm getting ready to host Becca's game group. Well, not this week. I'm hosting on August 20, at my home in Columbia City.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! Is this the smaller table Becca was talking about?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah, we're trying that 4-player cap for the next few gatherings. After July ran until 9:15, a work-night game needs a little more supervision.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: What are you thinking of playing?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I plan to put out Splendor. It should fit comfortably into an evening, and the turns are pretty straightforward.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds good. Are you going to explain it, or just hand everyone the rules?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I'll explain the basics, I think. What if I leave the details until they actually come up? Less of a lecture that way.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, and people can start playing sooner. What time are they coming?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The invitation asks everyone to arrive at 6:30 p.m. That gives us a bit of room to settle in before we start.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: And hopefully get home at a reasonable hour.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That's the dream. I also need to clear a stack of mail off the dining table. Very glamorous hosting preparations.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: You could make sorting the mail the opening game.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: The scoring would be brutal. I'm also considering putting a pitcher of water on the counter, so people can just help themselves.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's easy. And you could keep the rules nearby in case something comes up.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Good idea. I'll have them handy, but try not to read every last bit aloud.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Your guests will thank you.

details_in_summary: Sam wants to clear a stack of mail off the dining table.
key_facts: Sam will host on August 20 at their home in Columbia City.
Sam plans to put out Splendor.
The invitation asks guests to arrive at 6:30 p.m.
minor_details: Sam wants to clear a stack of mail off the dining table.
They are considering putting a pitcher of water on the counter.

summary: Riley discussed hosting Becca's game group on Aug 20 at her home in Columbia City with a 4-player cap. They plan to play Splendor, with Riley planning to explain the basics while leaving detailed rules optional. Guests are asked to arrive at 6:30 p.m., aiming for an early end to the evening. Practical tasks include clearing the dining-table mail, having a pitcher of water available, and keeping the rules handy without reading them aloud in full. Action items: prep hosting space, brief players on basics, and have reference rules ready.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Morning, Riley. It's nice to get a quiet minute before the day starts.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Morning. Yeah, I'm enjoying it while it lasts.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I tried that Italian practice on the light rail, by the way.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Oh, how'd it go?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Pretty well, actually. I practiced on 3 commutes using notes I'd saved on my phone.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That's better than trying to remember after dinner.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yeah. Having the notes right there helped. Though my phone was nearly out of battery on Tuesday.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Did you get to practice?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I did, just briefly. I keep a charger in my canvas bag, so it wasn't a disaster.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Good. Were you saying the words out loud too?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I tried, but speaking aloud felt awkward on a crowded train. Not quite the audience I had in mind.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah, that's a tough place to practice pronunciation.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: What if I split it up? Reading on the commute, pronunciation at home.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: That sounds easier. You'd still get some practice in on the train.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Right. And I can look at the food words without quietly performing them for everyone.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Are the notes mostly vocabulary?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Mostly, yes. Words and a few short bits to read. Nothing I need to spread out across a seat.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: A considerate study plan.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That's the goal. So I'll save pronunciation practice for home and use the commute for reading.

details_in_summary: They keep a charger in a canvas bag.
key_facts: Sam practiced on three commutes using notes saved on their phone.
Speaking aloud felt awkward on a crowded train.
Sam will save pronunciation practice for home and use the commute for reading.
minor_details: Sam's phone was nearly out of battery on Tuesday.
They keep a charger in a canvas bag.

summary: Riley discussed practicing Italian on the train, using phone notes saved for vocabulary and short phrases. She noted battery concerns but kept a charger in her bag. Riley found speaking aloud on a crowded train awkward, so she planned to split practice: reading on commutes and pronunciation at home, with notes primarily covering vocabulary. The goal is a practical, less disruptive study routine.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Oh, that's much better! I tried the shade halfway down this afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Yeah? Was there enough light to read?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: There was. I could read on the sofa without turning on a lamp.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Nice. When did you lower it?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: When the sun reached the living-room rug, I lowered the shade halfway. It blocked the direct sun without making everything gloomy.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Much better than having it all the way down, then.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Definitely. Okay, but I don't know if halfway will be enough on a hotter day.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: We can see. Oh, I brought you a glass of iced tea.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Thank you. Could you hand me my book too? The one with the blue bookmark.

dialogue.speaker: Me
dialogue.text: Here. Were you able to read the whole time without the sun in your eyes?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Yeah, from that spot on the sofa. It's a nice middle ground so far.

details_in_summary: The book she is reading has a blue bookmark.
Riley brings her a glass of iced tea.
key_facts: Maya lowers the shade halfway when the sun reaches the living-room rug.
She can read on the sofa without turning on a lamp.
